cn: 视频挑战赛不会让个别学生处于尴尬境地——所以它在设计上不那么令人生畏。

en: It also adds the element of artistic creativity to attract a new pool of students who may not see themselves as 'math people'. (23 words)
cn: 它还增加了艺术创造力的元素，以吸引那些可能不认为自己是‘数学人’的新学生群体。

en: We live today indebted to McCardell, Cashin, Hawes, Wilkins, and Maxwell, and other women who liberated American fashion from the confines of Parisian design. (24 words)
cn: 我们今天的生活要感谢麦卡德尔、卡申、霍斯、威尔金斯、麦克斯韦和其他将美国时尚从巴黎设计的束缚中解放出来的女性。

en: Independence came in tying, wrapping, storing, harmonizing, and rationalizing that wardrobe. (11 words)
cn: 独立性体现在对衣橱的系带、包裹、收纳、协调和合理化中。

en: These designers established the modern dress code, letting playsuits and other active wear outfits suffice for casual clothing, allowing pants to enter the wardrobe, and prizing rationalism and versatility in dress, in contradiction to dressing for an occasion or allotment of the day. (43 words)
cn: 这些设计师确立了现代着装规范，让运动套装和其他运动装足以作为休闲服装，让裤子进入衣橱，并重视着装中的理性主义和多功能性，这与为特定场合或一天中的某个时段着装形成对比。

en: Fashion in America was logical and answerable to the will of the women who wore it. (16 words)
cn: 美国的时尚是合乎逻辑的，并服从于穿着它的女性的意愿。

en: Implicitly or explicitly, American fashion addressed a democracy, whereas traditional Paris-based fashion was prescriptive and imposed on women, willing or not. (21 words)
cn: 或明或暗地，美国时尚体现了民主，而传统的巴黎时尚是规定性的，无论愿意与否都强加于女性。

en: In an earlier time, American fashion had also followed the dictates of Paris, or even copied and pirated specific French designs. (21 words)
cn: 在更早的时期，美国时尚也遵循巴黎的指令，甚至复制和盗版特定的法国设计。

en: Designer sportswear was not modeled on that of Europe, as 'modern art' would later be; it was genuinely invented and developed in America. (23 words)
cn: 设计师运动装并非像后来的‘现代艺术’那样模仿欧洲；它是在美国真正发明和发展起来的。

en: Its designers were not high-end with supplementary lines. (8 words)
cn: 其设计师并非高端且附带产品线的。

en: The design objective and the business commitment were to sportswear, and the distinctive traits were problem-solving ingenuity and realistic lifestyle applications. (21 words)
cn: 设计目标和商业承诺都面向运动装，其显著特点是解决问题的创造力和现实生活应用的实用性。

en: Ease of care was most important: summer dresses and outfits, in particular, were chiefly cotton, readily capable of being washed and pressed at home. (24 words)
cn: 易于护理最为重要：尤其是夏装和套装，主要是棉质的，便于在家洗涤和熨烫。

en: Closings were simple, practical, and accessible, as the modern woman depended on no personal maid to dress her. (18 words)
cn: 闭合件简单、实用且易于使用，因为现代女性不依赖个人女仆来穿衣。

en: American designers prized resourcefulness and the freedom of women who wore the clothing. (13 words)
cn: 美国设计师重视穿着这些服装的女性的机智和自由。

en: Many have argued that the women designers of this time were able to project their own clothing values into a new style. (22 words)
cn: 许多人认为，当时的女性设计师能够将她们自己的服装价值观投射到一种新风格中。

en: Of course, much of this argument in the 1930s-40s was advanced because there was little or no experience in justifying apparel on the basis of utility. (26 words)
cn: 当然，20世纪30-40年代的这种论点之所以被提出，很大程度上是因为几乎没有或根本没有基于实用性来论证服装的经验。

en: If Paris was cast aside, the tradition of beauty was also to some degree slighted. (15 words)
cn: 如果巴黎被抛在一边，美的传统也在某种程度上被轻视了。

en: Designer sportswear would have to be verified by a standard other than that of pure beauty; the emulation of a designer's life in designer sportswear was a crude version of this relationship. (32 words)
cn: 设计师运动装必须由纯美之外的标准来验证；在设计师运动装中模仿设计师的生活是这种关系的粗略版本。

en: The consumer was ultimately to be mentioned as well, especially by the likes of Dorothy Shaver, who could point to the sales figures at Lord & Taylor. (27 words)
cn: 消费者最终也被提及，尤其是像多萝西·谢弗这样的人，她可以引用洛德泰勒的销售数据。

en: Could utility alone justify the new ideas of the American designers? (11 words)
cn: 仅凭实用性就能证明美国设计师的新理念是合理的吗？

en: Fashion is often regarded as a pursuit of beauty, and some cherished fashion's trivial relationship to the fine arts. (19 words)
cn: 时尚通常被视为对美的追求，一些人珍视时尚与美术之间的微妙关系。

en: What the designers of the American sportswear proved was that fashion is a genuine design art, answering to the demanding needs of service. (23 words)
cn: 美国运动装设计师所证明的是，时尚是一种真正的设计艺术，回应着服务的严格要求。

en: Of course these practical, insightful designers have determined the course of late twentieth-century fashion. (14 words)
cn: 当然，这些实用、有洞察力的设计师决定了20世纪后期时尚的走向。

en: They were the pioneers of gender equity, in their useful, adaptable clothing, which was both made for the masses and capable of self-expression. (23 words)
cn: 她们是性别平等的先驱，她们实用、适应性强的服装既为大众制作，又能实现自我表达。

en: Massive rubbish dumps and sprawling landfills constitute one of the more uncomfortable impacts that humans have on wildlife. (18 words)
cn: 大量垃圾堆和蔓延的垃圾填埋场构成了人类对野生动物更令人不安的影响之一。

en: They have led some birds to give up on migration. (10 words)
cn: 它们导致一些鸟类放弃了迁徙。

en: Instead of flying thousands of miles in search of food, they make the waste sites their winter feeding grounds. (19 words)
cn: 它们不再飞行数千英里寻找食物，而是将垃圾场作为冬季觅食地。

en: Researchers in Germany used miniature GPS tags to track the migrations of 70 white storks from different sites across Europe and Asia during the first five months of their lives. (30 words)
cn: 德国的研究人员使用微型GPS标签追踪了70只白鹳在生命的前五个月里从欧洲和亚洲不同地点的迁徙情况。

en: While many birds travelled along well-known routes to warmer climates, others stopped short and spent the winter on landfills, feeding on food waste, and the multitudes of insects that thrive on the dumps. (33 words)
cn: 虽然许多鸟类沿着众所周知的路线飞到更温暖的气候，但其他鸟类中途停下，在垃圾填埋场过冬，以食物垃圾和在垃圾场上大量繁衍生息的昆虫为食。

en: In the short-term, the birds seem to benefit from overwintering on rubbish dumps. (13 words)
cn: 短期内，这些鸟类似乎从在垃圾堆上过冬中受益。

en: Andrea Flack of the Max Planck Institute found that birds following traditional migration routes were more likely to die than German storks that flew only as far as northern Morocco, and spent the winter there on rubbish dumps. (38 words)
cn: 马克斯·普朗克研究所的安德烈娅·弗拉克发现，遵循传统迁徙路线的鸟类比那些只飞到摩洛哥北部并在那里的垃圾堆上过冬的德国鹳更可能死亡。

en: 'For the birds it's a very convenient way to get food. (11 words)
cn: ‘对鸟类来说，这是一种非常方便的获取食物的方式。’

en: There are huge clusters of organic waste they can feed on,' said Flack. (13 words)
cn: 弗拉克说：‘有大量的有机废物供它们食用。’

en: The meals are not particularly appetising, or even safe. (9 words)
cn: 这些食物不是特别开胃，甚至不安全。

en: Much of the waste is discarded rotten meat, mixed in with other human debris such as plastic bags and old toys. (21 words)
cn: 大部分废物是丢弃的腐肉，混有塑料袋和旧玩具等其他人类废弃物。

en: 'It's very risky. (3 words)
cn: ‘这非常危险。’

en: The birds can easily eat pieces of plastic or rubber bands and they can die,' said Flack. (17 words)
cn: 弗拉克说：‘鸟类很容易吃到塑料碎片或橡皮筋，它们会死。’

en: 'And we don't know about the long-term consequences. (8 words)
cn: ‘我们不知道长期后果。’

en: They might eat something toxic and damage their health. (9 words)
cn: ‘它们可能吃到有毒的东西，损害健康。’

en: We cannot estimate that yet.' (5 words)
cn: ‘我们还无法估计。’

en: The scientists tracked white storks from different colonies in Europe and Africa. (12 words)
cn: 科学家追踪了来自欧洲和非洲不同种群的白鹳。

en: The Russian, Greek and Polish storks flew as far as South Africa, while those from Spain, Tunisia and Germany flew only as far as the Sahel. (26 words)
cn: 俄罗斯、希腊和波兰的鹳飞到了南非，而来自西班牙、突尼斯和德国的鹳只飞到了萨赫勒地区。

en: Landfill sites on the Iberian peninsula have long attracted local white storks, but all of the Spanish birds tagged in the study flew across the Sahara desert to the western Sahel. (31 words)
cn: 伊比利亚半岛的垃圾填埋场长期以来一直吸引着当地的白鹳，但研究中标记的所有西班牙鹳都飞越了撒哈拉沙漠到达西萨赫勒。

en: Writing in the journal, the scientists describe how the storks from Germany were clearly affected by the presence of waste sites, with four out of six birds that survived for at least five months overwintering on rubbish dumps in northern Morocco, instead of migrating to the Sahel. (47 words)
cn: 科学家在期刊中写道，来自德国的鹳明显受到垃圾场存在的影响，六只存活至少五个月的鸟中有四只在摩洛哥北部的垃圾堆上过冬，而不是迁徙到萨赫勒。

en: Flack said it was too early to know whether the benefits of plentiful food outweighed the risks of feeding on landfills. (21 words)
cn: 弗拉克说，现在判断充足食物的好处是否超过在垃圾填埋场觅食的风险还为时过早。

en: But that's not the only uncertainty. (6 words)
cn: 但这并不是唯一的不确定性。

en: Migrating birds affect ecosystems both at home and at their winter destinations, and disrupting the traditional routes could have unexpected side effects. (22 words)
cn: 候鸟既影响它们家乡的生态系统，也影响它们冬季目的地的生态系统，扰乱传统路线可能会产生意想不到的副作用。

en: White storks feed on locusts and other insects that can become pests if their numbers get out of hand. (19 words)
cn: 白鹳以蝗虫和其他昆虫为食，如果它们的数量失控，就会成为害虫。

en: 'They provide a useful service,' said Flack. (7 words)
cn: 弗拉克说：‘它们提供了一种有用的服务。’

en: Let's all stop judging people who talk to themselves. (9 words)
cn: 让我们都别再评判那些自言自语的人了。

en: New research says that those who can't seem to keep their inner monologues in are actually more likely to stay on task, remain focused better and show improved perception capabilities. (30 words)
cn: 新的研究表明，那些似乎无法抑制内心独白的人实际上更有可能专注于任务、保持更专注并表现出更好的感知能力。

en: Not bad, really, for some extra muttering. (7 words)
cn: 对于额外的一些自言自语来说，这确实不错。

en: According to a series of experiments published in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology by professors Gary Lupyan and Daniel Swignley, the act of using verbal clues to trigger mental pictures helps people function quicker. (35 words)
cn: 根据加里·卢皮扬和丹尼尔·斯威格尼教授发表在《实验心理学季刊》上的一系列实验，使用语言线索触发心理图像的行为有助于人们更快地运作。

en: In one experiment, they showed pictures of various objects to twenty volunteers and asked them to find just one of those, a banana. (23 words)
cn: 在一项实验中，他们向20名志愿者展示了各种物体的图片，并要求他们只找到其中一样——一根香蕉。

en: Half were instructed to repeat out loud what they were looking for and the other half kept their lips sealed. (20 words)
cn: 一半人被指示大声重复他们正在寻找的东西，另一半人则紧闭嘴唇。

en: Those who talked to themselves found the banana slightly faster than those who didn't, the researchers say. (17 words)
cn: 研究人员说，那些自言自语的人比那些没有自言自语的人稍快找到香蕉。

en: In other experiments, Lupyan and Swignley found that uttering the name of a common product when on the hunt for it helped quicken someone's pace, but talking about uncommon items showed no advantage and slowed you down. (37 words)
cn: 在其他实验中，卢皮扬和斯威格尼发现，在寻找常见产品时说出其名称有助于加快速度，但谈论不常见的物品则没有优势，反而会减慢速度。

en: Common research has long held that talking themselves through a task helps children learn, although doing so when you've apparently matured is not a great sign of brilliance. (28 words)
cn: 常见的研究长期以来一直认为，在完成任务时自言自语有助于儿童学习，尽管当你明显成熟后这样做并不是聪明的表现。

en: The two professors hope to refute that idea, claiming that just as when kids walk themselves through a process, adults can benefit from using language not just to communicate, but also to help 'augment thinking'. (35 words)
cn: 两位教授希望反驳这一观点，声称正如孩子们在完成一个过程时自言自语一样，成年人也可以从使用语言中受益，不仅是为了交流，也是为了帮助‘增强思维’。

en: Of course, you are still encouraged to keep the talking at library tones and, whatever you do, keep the information you share simple, like a grocery list. (27 words)
cn: 当然，仍然鼓励你保持图书馆般的说话音量，并且无论做什么，都要保持你分享的信息简单，就像购物清单一样。

en: At any volume, there's still such a thing as too much information. (12 words)
cn: 无论音量大小，仍然存在信息过量的情况。

en: The lives of children from rich and poor American families look more different than ever before. (16 words)
cn: 美国富裕家庭和贫困家庭孩子的生活看起来比以往任何时候都更加不同。

en: Well-off families are ruled by calendars, with children enrolled in ballet, soccer and after-school programs, according to a new Pew Research Center survey. (23 words)
cn: 根据皮尤研究中心的一项新调查，富裕家庭受日程表支配，孩子们参加芭蕾、足球和课后活动。

en: There are usually two parents, who spend a lot of time reading to children and worrying about their anxiety levels and hectic schedules. (23 words)
cn: 通常有双亲，他们花大量时间给孩子读书，并担心他们的焦虑程度和繁忙的日程。

en: In poor families, meanwhile, children tend to spend their time at home or with extended family. (16 words)
cn: 与此同时，在贫困家庭中，孩子们往往在家里或与大家庭成员一起度过时间。

en: They are more likely to grow up in neighborhoods that their parents say aren't great for raising children, and their parents worry about them getting shot, beaten up or in trouble with the law. (34 words)
cn: 他们更有可能在父母认为不适合抚养孩子的社区长大，他们的父母担心他们会遭枪击、被殴打或惹上法律麻烦。

en: The class differences in child rearing are growing—a symptom of widening inequality with far-reaching consequences. (15 words)
cn: 育儿方面的阶级差异正在扩大——这是不平等加剧的一个征兆，会产生深远的影响。

en: Different upbringings set children on different paths and can deepen socioeconomic divisions, especially because education is strongly linked to earnings. (20 words)
cn: 不同的成长环境使孩子走上不同的道路，并可能加深社会经济分化，尤其是因为教育与收入密切相关。

en: Children grow up learning the skills to succeed in their socioeconomic stratum, but not necessarily others. (16 words)
cn: 孩子们在成长过程中学习在其社会经济阶层中取得成功的技能，但不一定能学习其他技能。

en: 'Early childhood experiences can be very consequential for children's long-term social, emotional and cognitive development,' said Sean Reardon, professor of poverty and inequality in education at Stanford University. (28 words)
cn: 斯坦福大学贫困与教育不平等教授肖恩·里尔登说：‘早期童年经历对儿童的长期社交、情感和认知发展可能非常重要。’

en: 'And because those influence educational success and later earnings, early childhood experiences cast a lifelong shadow.' (16 words)
cn: ‘因为这些影响教育成功和未来收入，早期童年经历投射出一生的阴影。’

en: The cycle continues: Poorer parents have less time and fewer resources to invest in their children, which can leave children less prepared for school and work, which leads to lower earnings. (31 words)
cn: 这个循环持续着：较贫困的父母有更少的时间和资源投入到孩子身上，这可能导致孩子为学校和工作做的准备更少，从而导致收入更低。

en: American parents want similar things for their children, the Pew report and past research have found: for them to be healthy and happy, honest and ethical, caring and compassionate. (29 words)
cn: 皮尤报告和过去的研究发现，美国父母对他们的孩子有相似的期望：希望他们健康快乐、诚实正直、关心他人、富有同情心。

en: There is no best parenting style or philosophy, researchers say, and across income groups, 92% of parents say they are doing a good job at raising their children. (28 words)
cn: 研究人员说，没有最好的育儿风格或理念，在各收入群体中，92%的父母表示他们在抚养孩子方面做得很好。

en: Yet they are doing it quite differently. (7 words)
cn: 然而，他们做的方式却大相径庭。

en: Middle-class and higher-income parents see their children as projects in need of careful cultivation, says Annette Lareau, whose groundbreaking research on the topic was published in her book Unequal Childhoods: Class, Race and Family Life. (35 words)
cn: 安妮特·拉罗说，中产阶级和较高收入的父母将他们的孩子视为需要精心培养的项目，她关于这一主题的开创性研究发表在她的《不平等的童年：阶级、种族与家庭生活》一书中。

en: They try to develop their skills through close supervision and organized activities, and teach children to question authority figures and navigate elite institutions. (23 words)
cn: 他们试图通过密切监督和有组织的活动来发展孩子的技能，并教导孩子质疑权威人物和应对精英机构。

en: Working-class parents, meanwhile, believe their children will naturally thrive, and give them far greater independence and time for free play. (20 words)
cn: 与此同时，工薪阶层父母相信他们的孩子会自然成长，并给予他们更大的独立性和自由玩耍的时间。

en: They are taught to be compliant and respectful to adults. (10 words)
cn: 他们被教导要顺从并尊重成年人。

en: There are benefits to both approaches. (6 words)
cn: 两种方法都有好处。

en: Working-class children are happier, more independent, complain less and are closer with family members, Ms. Lareau found. (17 words)
cn: 拉罗女士发现，工薪阶层的孩子更快乐、更独立、抱怨更少，与家庭成员更亲近。

en: Higher-income children are more likely to declare boredom and expect their parents to solve their problems. (16 words)
cn: 较高收入的孩子更可能声称无聊，并期望父母解决他们的问题。

en: Yet later on, the more affluent children end up in college and on the way to the middle class, while working-class children tend to struggle. (25 words)
cn: 然而后来，较富裕的孩子最终上了大学并走向中产阶级，而工薪阶层的孩子则往往挣扎。

en: Children from higher-income families are likely to have the skills to navigate bureaucracies and succeed in schools and workplaces, Ms. Lareau said. (22 words)
cn: 拉罗女士说，来自较高收入家庭的孩子很可能具备应对官僚体制并在学校和工作场所取得成功的技能。

en: 'Do all parents want the most success for their children? Absolutely,' she said. (13 words)
cn: 她说：‘所有父母都希望孩子取得最大的成功吗？当然。’

en: 'Do some strategies give children more advantages than others in institutions? Probably they do. (14 words)
cn: ‘某些策略是否在体制内比其他策略给孩子更多优势？可能是的。’

en: Will parents be damaging children if they have one fewer organized activity? No, I really doubt it.' (17 words)
cn: ‘如果孩子少参加一个组织活动，父母会伤害孩子吗？不，我真的怀疑。’

en: Social scientists say the differences arise in part because low-income parents have less money to spend on music class or preschool, and less flexible schedules to take children to museums or attend school events. (34 words)
cn: 社会科学家说，这些差异部分源于低收入父母没有那么多钱花在音乐课或学前教育上，也没有那么灵活的时间带孩子去博物馆或参加学校活动。

en: Extracurricular activities reflect the differences in child rearing in the Pew survey, which was of a nationally representative sample of 1,807 parents. (22 words)
cn: 课外活动反映了皮尤调查中育儿方式的差异，该调查对1807名父母进行了全国代表性抽样。

en: Of families earning more than $75,000 a year, 84% say their children have participated in organized sports over the past year, 64% have done volunteer work and 62% have taken lessons in music, dance or art. (36 words)
cn: 在年收入超过75000美元的家庭中，84%表示他们的孩子在过去一年参加了有组织的体育活动，64%做过志愿者工作，62%上过音乐、舞蹈或艺术课。

en: Of families earning less than $30,000, 59% of children have done sports, 37% have volunteered and 41% have taken arts classes. (21 words)
cn: 在收入低于30000美元的家庭中，59%的孩子参加过体育活动，37%做过志愿者，41%上过艺术课。

en: Especially in affluent families, children start young. (7 words)
cn: 特别是在富裕家庭中，孩子很早就开始。

en: Nearly half of high-earning, college-graduate parents enrolled their children in arts classes before they were 5, compared with one-fifth of low-income, less-educated parents. (23 words)
cn: 近半数高收入、大学毕业的父母在孩子5岁前就让他们参加艺术课，相比之下，低收入、教育程度较低的父母中只有五分之一这样做。

en: Nonetheless, 20% of well-off parents say their children's schedules are too hectic, compared with 8% of poorer parents. (18 words)
cn: 尽管如此，20%的富裕父母表示孩子的日程过于繁忙，而贫困父母中只有8%如此认为。

en: Another example is reading aloud, which studies have shown gives children bigger vocabularies and better reading comprehension in school. (19 words)
cn: 另一个例子是大声朗读，研究表明这能让孩子拥有更大的词汇量和更好的阅读理解能力。

en: 71% of parents with a college degree say they do it every day, compared with 33% of those with a high school diploma or less. (25 words)
cn: 71%拥有大学学位的父母表示他们每天都这样做，而高中文凭或更低学历的父母中只有33%这样做。

en: White parents are more likely than others to read to their children daily, as are married parents. (17 words)
cn: 白人父母比其他人更可能每天给孩子读书，已婚父母也是如此。

en: Most affluent parents enroll their children in preschool or day care, while low-income parents are more likely to depend on family members. (22 words)
cn: 大多数富裕父母让孩子上幼儿园或日托，而低收入父母更可能依赖家庭成员。

en: Discipline techniques vary by education level: 8% of those with a postgraduate degree say they often beat their children, compared with 22% of those with a high school degree or less. (31 words)
cn: 管教方式因教育水平而异：拥有研究生学历的人中有8%表示他们经常打孩子，而高中学历或更低的人中有22%如此。

en: The survey also probed attitudes and anxieties. (7 words)
cn: 调查还探究了态度和焦虑。

en: Interestingly, parents' attitudes toward education do not seem to reflect their own educational background as much as a belief in the importance of education for upward mobility. (27 words)
cn: 有趣的是，父母对教育的态度似乎并不像对教育对社会阶层向上流动重要性的信念那样反映他们自己的教育背景。

en: Most American parents say they are not concerned about their children's grades as long as they work hard. (18 words)
cn: 大多数美国父母表示，只要孩子努力学习，他们就不担心孩子的成绩。

en: But 50% of poor parents say it is extremely important to them that their children earn a college degree, compared with 39% of wealthier parents. (25 words)
cn: 但50%的贫困父母表示，孩子获得大学学位对他们来说极其重要，而富裕父母中只有39%如此认为。

en: Less-educated parents, and poorer and black and Latino parents are more likely to believe that there is no such thing as too much involvement in a child's education. (28 words)
cn: 受教育程度较低的父母、较贫困的父母以及黑人和拉丁裔父母更可能认为对孩子教育的参与再多也不为过。

en: Parents who are white, wealthy or college-educated say too much involvement can be bad. (14 words)
cn: 白人、富裕或受过大学教育的父母表示过度参与可能有害。

en: Parental anxieties reflect their circumstances. (5 words)
cn: 父母的焦虑反映了他们的处境。

en: High-earning parents are much more likely to say they live in a good neighborhood for raising children. (17 words)
cn: 高收入父母更可能表示他们住在适合养育孩子的好社区。

en: While bullying is parents' greatest concern over all, nearly half of low-income parents worry their child will get shot, compared with one-fifth of high-income parents. (25 words)
cn: 虽然欺凌是父母最普遍的担忧，但近半数低收入父母担心孩子会遭枪击，而高收入父母中只有五分之一如此。

en: They are more worried about their children being depressed or anxious. (11 words)
cn: 他们更担心孩子抑郁或焦虑。

en: In the Pew survey, middle-class families earning between $30,000 and $75,000 a year fell right between working-class and high-earning parents on issues like the quality of their neighborhood for raising children, participation in extracurricular activities and involvement in their children's education. (41 words)
cn: 在皮尤调查中，年收入在30000至75000美元之间的中产阶级家庭在社区质量、课外活动参与和对孩子教育参与等问题上正好处于工薪阶层和高收入父母之间。

en: Children were not always raised so differently. (7 words)
cn: 孩子并不总是被如此不同地抚养。

en: The achievement gap between children from high- and low-income families is 30-40% larger among children born in 2001 than those born 25 years earlier, according to Mr. Reardon's research. (29 words)
cn: 根据里尔登先生的研究，2001年出生的孩子与25年前出生的孩子相比，高收入和低收入家庭孩子之间的成绩差距扩大了30-40%。

en: People used to live near people of different income levels; neighborhoods are now more segregated by income. (17 words)
cn: 人们过去常住在不同收入水平的人附近；现在社区更多地按收入隔离。

en: More than a quarter of children live in single-parent households—a historic high, according to Pew—and these children are three times as likely to live in poverty as those who live with married parents. (33 words)
cn: 超过四分之一的孩子生活在单亲家庭——据皮尤称，这是历史新高——这些孩子生活在贫困中的可能性是与已婚父母同住的孩子的三倍。

en: Meanwhile, growing income inequality has coincided with the increasing importance of a college degree for earning a middle-class wage. (19 words)
cn: 与此同时，日益加剧的收入不平等与大学学位对挣取中产阶级工资的重要性日益增加同时发生。

en: Yet there are recent signs that the gap could be starting to shrink. (13 words)
cn: 然而，最近有迹象表明差距可能开始缩小。

en: In the past decade, even as income inequality has grown, some of the socioeconomic differences in parenting, like reading to children and going to libraries, have narrowed. (27 words)
cn: 在过去十年中，即使收入不平等加剧，育儿方面的一些社会经济差异，如给孩子读书和去图书馆，已经缩小。

en: Public policies aimed at young children have helped, including public preschool programs and reading initiatives. (15 words)
cn: 针对幼儿的公共政策有所帮助，包括公共学前项目和阅读倡议。

en: Addressing differences in the earliest years, it seems, could reduce inequality in the next generation. (15 words)
cn: 解决生命最初几年的差异，似乎可以减少下一代的不平等。

en: Tennessee's technical and community colleges will not outsource management of their facilities to a private company, a decision one leader said was bolstered by an analysis of spending at each campus. (31 words)
cn: 田纳西州的理工和社区学院不会将设施管理外包给私营公司，一位领导人表示，这一决定得到了对各校区支出分析的支持。

en: In an email sent Monday to college presidents in the Tennessee Board of Regents system, outgoing Chancellor John Morgan said an internal analysis showed that each campus' spending on facilities management fell well below the industry standards identified by the state. (41 words)
cn: 在周一发送给田纳西州董事会系统中各大学校长的电子邮件中，即将离任的校长约翰·摩根表示，内部分析显示，各校区在设施管理上的支出远低于州确定的行业标准。

en: Morgan said those findings—which included data from the system's 13 community colleges, 27 technical colleges and six universities—were part of the decision not to move forward with Governor Bill Haslam's proposal to privatize management of state buildings in an effort to save money. (43 words)
cn: 摩根表示，这些发现——包括该系统13所社区学院、27所技术学院和6所大学的数据——是决定不推进州长比尔·哈斯拉姆为省钱而将州建筑管理私有化提议的部分原因。

en: 'While these numbers are still being validated by the state, we feel any adjustments they might suggest will be immaterial,' Morgan wrote to the presidents. (25 words)
cn: 摩根在给校长们的信中写道：‘虽然这些数字仍在由州政府验证，但我们认为它们可能建议的任何调整都将无关紧要。’

en: 'System institutions are operating very efficiently based on this analysis, raising the question of the value of pursuing a broad scale outsourcing initiative.' (23 words)
cn: ‘基于这一分析，系统各机构运行非常高效，这引发了对推行大规模外包举措价值的质疑。’

en: Workers' advocates have criticized Haslam's plan, saying it would mean some campus workers would lose their jobs or benefits. (19 words)
cn: 工人权益倡导者批评了哈斯拉姆的计划，称这将意味着一些校园工人将失去工作或福利。

en: Haslam has said colleges would be free to opt in or out of the outsourcing plan, which has not been finalized. (21 words)
cn: 哈斯拉姆表示，大学可以自由选择加入或退出尚未最终确定的外包计划。

en: Morgan notified the Haslam administration of his decision to opt out in a letter sent last week. (17 words)
cn: 摩根在上周发出的一封信中通知哈斯拉姆政府他选择退出的决定。

en: That letter, which includes several concerns Morgan has with the plan, was originally obtained by The Commercial Appeal in Memphis. (20 words)
cn: 这封信包含了摩根对该计划的几个担忧，最初由孟菲斯的《商业呼吁报》获得。

en: In an email statement from the state's Office of Customer Focused Government, which is examining the possibility of outsourcing, spokeswoman Michelle R. Martin said officials were still working to analyze the data from the Board of Regents. (37 words)
cn: 在州政府客户导向政府办公室的一封电子邮件声明中，发言人米歇尔·R·马丁表示，官员们仍在努力分析来自董事会的相关数据。该办公室正在研究外包的可能性。

en: Data on management expenses at the college system and in other state departments will be part of a 'business justification' the state will use as officials deliberate the specifics of an outsourcing plan. (33 words)
cn: 大学系统和其他州部门的管理费用数据将是州政府在官员审议外包计划细节时使用的‘商业论证’的一部分。

en: 'The state's facilities management project team is still in the process of developing its business justification and expects to have that completed and available to the public at the end of February,' Martin said. (34 words)
cn: 马丁说：‘州政府的设施管理项目团队仍在制定其商业论证，预计将在2月底完成并向公众公开。’

en: 'At this time there is nothing to take action on since the analysis has yet to be completed.' (18 words)
cn: ‘目前还没有什么可采取行动的，因为分析尚未完成。’

en: Morgan's comments on outsourcing mark the second time this month that he has come out against one of Haslam's plans for higher education in Tennessee. (25 words)
cn: 摩根关于外包的评论标志着本月他第二次公开反对哈斯拉姆关于田纳西州高等教育的计划之一。

en: Morgan said last week that he would retire at the end of January because of the governor's proposal to split off six universities of the Board of Regents system and create separate governing boards for each of them. (38 words)
cn: 摩根上周表示，他将在1月底退休，因为州长提议将董事会系统中的六所大学分离出来，并为每所大学设立独立的理事会。

en: In his resignation letter, Morgan called the reorganization 'unworkable'. (9 words)
cn: 在他的辞职信中，摩根称这次重组‘不可行’。

en: Beginning in the late sixteenth century, it became fashionable for young aristocrats to visit Paris, Venice, Florence, and above all, Rome, as the culmination of their classical education. (28 words)
cn: 从16世纪末开始，年轻贵族访问巴黎、威尼斯、佛罗伦萨，尤其是罗马，作为他们古典教育的高潮，成为一种时尚。

en: Thus was born the idea of the Grand Tour, a practice which introduced Englishmen, Germans, Scandinavians, and also Americans to the art and culture of France and Italy for the next 300 years. (33 words)
cn: ‘大旅行’的想法由此诞生，这一做法在接下来的300年里向英国人、德国人、斯堪的纳维亚人以及美国人介绍了法国和意大利的艺术与文化。

en: Travel was arduous and costly throughout the period, possible only for a privileged class—the same that produced gentlemen scientists, authors, antique experts, and patrons of the arts. (27 words)
cn: 在整个时期，旅行艰辛且昂贵，只有特权阶级才能负担——就是那些产生了绅士科学家、作家、古董专家和艺术赞助人的阶级。

en: The Grand Tourist was typically a young man with a thorough grounding in Greek and Latin literature as well as some leisure time, some means, and some interest in art. (30 words)
cn: 大旅行者通常是一个年轻男子，具备扎实的希腊和拉丁文学基础，并有一些闲暇时间、一些财力和一些对艺术的兴趣。

en: The German traveler Johann Winckelmann pioneered the field of art history with his comprehensive study of Greek and Roman sculpture; he was portrayed by his friend Anton Raphael Mengs at the beginning of his long residence in Rome. (38 words)
cn: 德国旅行家约翰·温克尔曼以他对希腊和罗马雕塑的全面研究开创了艺术史领域；他的朋友安东·拉斐尔·门斯在他长期居住在罗马之初为他画了肖像。

en: Most Grand Tourists, however, stayed for briefer periods and set out with less scholarly intentions, accompanied by a teacher or guardian, and expected to return home with souvenirs of their travels as well as an understanding of art and architecture formed by exposure to great masterpieces. (46 words)
cn: 然而，大多数大旅行者停留的时间较短，学术意图较弱，由教师或监护人陪同，并期望在回家时带回旅行纪念品以及通过接触伟大杰作而形成的对艺术和建筑的理解。

en: London was a frequent starting point for Grand Tourists, and Paris a compulsory destination; many traveled to the Netherlands, some to Switzerland and Germany, and a very few adventurers to Spain, Greece, or Turkey. (34 words)
cn: 伦敦是大旅行者频繁的起点，巴黎是必经之地；许多人前往荷兰，一些人前往瑞士和德国，极少数冒险者前往西班牙、希腊或土耳其。

en: The essential place to visit, however, was Italy. (8 words)
cn: 然而，必去之地是意大利。

en: The British traveler Charles Thompson spoke for many Grand Tourists when in 1744 he described himself as 'being impatiently desirous of viewing a country so famous in history, a country which once gave laws to the world, and which is at present the greatest school of music and painting, contains the noblest productions of sculpture and architecture, and is filled with cabinets of rarities, and collections of all kinds of historical relics'. (72 words)
cn: 英国旅行者查尔斯·汤普森在1744年描述自己‘急切地渴望看到一个在历史上如此著名的国家，一个曾经为世界制定法律的国家，一个目前是音乐和绘画最伟大的学校，拥有最崇高的雕塑和建筑作品，并充满了珍奇柜和各种历史文物收藏’，这代表了许多大旅行者的心声。

en: Within Italy, the great focus was Rome, whose ancient ruins and more recent achievements were shown to every Grand Tourist. (20 words)
cn: 在意大利内部，焦点是罗马，每位大旅行者都能看到其古代遗址和更近期的成就。

en: Panini's Ancient Rome and Modern Rome represent the sights most prized, including celebrated Greco-Roman statues and views of famous ruins, fountains, and churches. (23 words)
cn: 帕尼尼的《古罗马》和《现代罗马》代表了最受珍视的景观，包括著名的希腊罗马雕像和著名废墟、喷泉和教堂的景色。

en: Since there were few museums anywhere in Europe before the close of the eighteenth century, Grand Tourists often saw paintings and sculptures by gaining admission to private collections, and many were eager to acquire examples of Greco-Roman and Italian art for their own collections. (44 words)
cn: 由于18世纪末之前欧洲几乎没有博物馆，大旅行者通常通过进入私人收藏来观看绘画和雕塑，许多人渴望为他们的收藏获得希腊罗马和意大利艺术的典范。

en: In England, where architecture was increasingly seen as an aristocratic pursuit, noblemen often applied what they learned from the villas of Palladio in the Veneto and the evocative ruins of Rome to their own country houses and gardens. (38 words)
cn: 在英国，建筑日益被视为贵族追求，贵族们经常将他们从威尼托的帕拉迪奥别墅和罗马令人回味的废墟中学到的东西应用到他们自己的乡间别墅和花园中。

en: In the past 12 months, Nigeria has suffered from a shrinking economy, a sliding currency, and a prolonged fuel shortage. (20 words)
cn: 在过去的12个月里，尼日利亚遭受了经济萎缩、货币贬值和持续的燃料短缺。

en: Now, Africa's largest economy is facing a food crisis as major tomato fields have been destroyed by an insect, leading to a nationwide shortage and escalating prices. (27 words)
cn: 如今，非洲最大的经济体正面临粮食危机，主要番茄田被一种昆虫摧毁，导致全国范围内短缺和价格飙升。

en: The insect, Tuta absoluta, has destroyed 80% of farms in Kaduna, Nigeria's largest tomato producing state, leading the government there to declare a state of emergency. (26 words)
cn: 这种名为番茄潜叶蛾的昆虫已经摧毁了尼日利亚最大番茄生产州卡杜纳州80%的农场，导致当地政府宣布进入紧急状态。

en: The insect, also known as the tomato leaf miner, devastates crops by feeding on fruits and digging into and moving through stalks. (22 words)
cn: 这种昆虫也被称为番茄潜叶虫，它通过取食果实并在茎秆中钻蛀和移动来破坏作物。

en: It reproduces incredibly quickly, breeding up to 12 generations per year if conditions are favorable. (15 words)
cn: 它的繁殖速度惊人，在条件有利的情况下每年可繁殖多达12代。

en: It is believed to have originated in South America in the early 1900s, and later spread to Europe before crossing over to sub-Saharan Africa. (24 words)
cn: 据信它于20世纪初起源于南美洲，后来传播到欧洲，然后蔓延到撒哈拉以南非洲。

en: In Nigeria, where tomatoes are a staple of local diets, the insect's effects are devastating. (15 words)
cn: 在番茄是当地主食的尼日利亚，这种昆虫的影响是毁灭性的。

en: Retail prices for a handful of tomatoes at local markets have risen from $0.50 to $2.50. (16 words)
cn: 当地市场上一小把番茄的零售价已从0.50美元涨到2.50美元。

en: Farmers are reporting steep losses and a new $20 million tomato-paste factory has halted production due to the shortages. (19 words)
cn: 农民报告了严重损失，一家价值2000万美元的新番茄酱工厂因短缺而停产。

en: Given the moth's ability also to attack crops like pepper and potatoes, Audu Ogbeh, Nigeria's minister of agriculture, has warned that the pest may 'create serious problems for food security' in the country. (33 words)
cn: 鉴于这种蛾子还能攻击辣椒和土豆等作物，尼日利亚农业部长奥杜·奥贝警告说，这种害虫可能‘给该国的粮食安全带来严重问题’。

en: Ogbeh says experts are investigating how to control the pest's damage and prevent its spread, which has gone largely unchecked until now. (22 words)
cn: 奥贝表示，专家们正在研究如何控制这种害虫的损害并防止其传播，迄今为止这种传播基本上没有得到控制。

en: Despite being the continent's second-largest producer of tomatoes, Nigeria is dependent on $1 billion worth of tomato-paste imports every year, as around 75% of the local harvest goes to waste thanks to a lack of proper storage facilities. (38 words)
cn: 尽管尼日利亚是非洲大陆第二大番茄生产国，但由于缺乏适当的储存设施，约75%的当地收成被浪费，因此每年依赖价值10亿美元的番茄酱进口。

en: A further reduction in local supplies is yet another unwelcome setback to the industry. (14 words)
cn: 本地供应的进一步减少对该行业来说又是一个不受欢迎的挫折。

en: 'Nearly everyone I know is addicted in some measure to the internet,' wrote Tony Schwartz in The New York Times. (20 words)
cn: 托尼·施瓦茨在《纽约时报》上写道：‘我认识的几乎每个人都在某种程度上对互联网上瘾。’

en: It's a common complaint these days. (6 words)
cn: 这是当下常见的抱怨。

en: A steady stream of similar headlines accuse the net and its offspring apps, social media sites and online games of addicting us to distraction. (24 words)
cn: 源源不断的类似头条新闻指责互联网及其衍生的应用程序、社交媒体网站和在线游戏让我们沉迷于分心。

en: There's little doubt that nearly everyone who comes in contact with the Net has difficulty disconnecting. (16 words)
cn: 毫无疑问，几乎每个接触互联网的人都难以断开连接。

en: Many of us, like Schwartz, struggle to stay focused on tasks that require more concentration than it takes to post a status update. (23 words)
cn: 我们中的许多人，像施瓦茨一样，努力专注于那些需要比发布状态更新更多专注力的任务。

en: As one person ironically put it in the comments section of Schwartz's online article, 'As I was reading this very excellent article, I stopped at least half a dozen times to check my email.' (34 words)
cn: 正如有人在施瓦茨在线文章的评论区讽刺地说的那样：‘当我正在读这篇非常优秀的文章时，我至少停下来五六次去查看我的电子邮件。’

en: There's something different about this technology: it is both invasive and persuasive. (12 words)
cn: 这项技术有一些不同之处：它既具有侵入性又具有说服力。

en: But who's at fault for its overuse? (7 words)
cn: 但过度使用它该怪谁呢？

en: To find solutions, it's important to understand what we're dealing with. (11 words)
cn: 要找到解决方案，重要的是要了解我们正在应对的是什么。

en: There are four parties conspiring to keep you connected: the tech, your boss, your friends and you. (17 words)
cn: 有四方合谋让你保持连接：技术、你的老板、你的朋友和你自己。

en: The technologies themselves and their makers are the easiest suspects to blame for our diminishing attention spans. (17 words)
cn: 技术本身及其制造者是我们注意力持续时间缩短最容易被指责的对象。

en: Nicholas Carr, author of The Shallows: What the Internet Is Doing to Our Brains, wrote, 'The net is designed to be an interruption system, a machine geared to dividing attention.' (30 words)
cn: 《浅薄：互联网如何改变我们的大脑》一书的作者尼古拉斯·卡尔写道：‘互联网被设计成一个中断系统，一台旨在分散注意力的机器。’

en: Online services like Facebook, Twitter and the like are called out for manipulation—making products so good that people can't stop using them. (22 words)
cn: Facebook、Twitter等在线服务被指责为操纵——把产品做得太好，以至于人们无法停止使用它们。

en: After studying these products for several years, I wrote a book about how they do it. (16 words)
cn: 在研究了这些产品几年之后，我写了一本书，讲述它们是如何做到这一点的。

en: I learned it all starts with the business model. (9 words)
cn: 我了解到这一切都始于商业模式。

en: Since these services rely on advertising revenue, the more frequently you use them, the more money they make. (18 words)
cn: 由于这些服务依赖广告收入，你使用得越频繁，它们赚的钱就越多。

en: It's no wonder these companies employ teams of people focused on engineering their services to be as engaging as possible. (20 words)
cn: 难怪这些公司雇佣团队专注于设计他们的服务，使其尽可能吸引人。

en: These products aren't habit-forming by chance; it's by design. (9 words)
cn: 这些产品不是偶然形成习惯的；它们是设计使然。

en: They have an incentive to keep us hooked. (8 words)
cn: 他们有动机让我们上瘾。

en: However, as good as these services are, there are simple steps we can take to keep them at bay. (19 words)
cn: 然而，尽管这些服务很好，我们还是可以采取简单的步骤来限制它们。

en: For example, we can change how often we receive the distracting notifications that trigger our urge to check. (18 words)
cn: 例如，我们可以改变接收触发我们查看冲动的干扰通知的频率。

en: According to Adam Marchick, CEO of mobile marketing company Kahuna, less than 15 percent of smartphone users ever bother to adjust their notification settings—meaning the remaining 85 percent of us default to the app makers' every preset trigger. (38 words)
cn: 据移动营销公司Kahuna的首席执行官亚当·马奇克称，只有不到15%的智能手机用户会费心调整他们的通知设置——这意味着我们其余85%的人默认接受应用制造商的每一个预设触发。

en: Google and Apple have made it far too difficult to adjust these settings, so it's up to us to take steps to ensure we set these triggers to suit our own needs, not the needs of the app makers. (39 words)
cn: 谷歌和苹果使调整这些设置变得过于困难，所以我们要采取措施，确保我们将这些触发设置为适合我们自己的需求，而不是应用制造商的需求。

en: While companies like Facebook harvest attention to generate revenue from advertisers, other technologies have no such agenda. (17 words)
cn: 虽然像Facebook这样的公司通过获取注意力来从广告商那里产生收入，但其他技术没有这样的目的。

en: Take email, for example. (4 words)
cn: 以电子邮件为例。

en: This system couldn't care less how often you use it. (10 words)
cn: 这个系统根本不在乎你使用它的频率。

en: Yet to many, email is the most habit-forming medium of all. (11 words)
cn: 然而对许多人来说，电子邮件是最容易让人上瘾的媒介。

en: We check email at all hours of the day—we're obsessed, but why? (12 words)
cn: 我们全天候查看电子邮件——我们痴迷于此，但为什么呢？

en: Because that's what the boss wants. (6 words)
cn: 因为那是老板想要的。

en: For almost all white-collar jobs, email is the primary tool of corporate communication. (13 words)
cn: 对于几乎所有白领工作来说，电子邮件是企业沟通的主要工具。

en: A slow response to a message could hurt not only your reputation but also your livelihood. (16 words)
cn: 对消息的迟缓回应不仅可能损害你的声誉，还可能影响你的生计。

en: Your friends are also responsible. (5 words)
cn: 你的朋友也有责任。

en: Think about this familiar scene. (5 words)
cn: 想想这个熟悉的场景。

en: People gathered around a table, enjoying food and each other's company. (11 words)
cn: 人们围坐在桌旁，享受美食和彼此的陪伴。

en: There's laughter and a bit of kidding. (7 words)
cn: 有笑声和一点玩笑。

en: Then, during an interval in the conversation, someone takes out their phone to check who knows what. (17 words)
cn: 然后，在谈话间隙，有人拿出手机查看谁也不知道是什么的内容。

en: Barely anyone notices and no one says a thing. (9 words)
cn: 几乎没有人注意到，也没有人说什么。

en: Now imagine the same dinner, but instead of checking their phone, the person belches loudly. (15 words)
cn: 现在想象同样的晚餐，但不是看手机，而是那个人大声打嗝。

en: Everyone notices. (2 words)
cn: 每个人都注意到了。

en: Unless the meal takes place in a beer house, this is considered bad manners. (14 words)
cn: 除非这顿饭是在啤酒屋进行的，否则这被认为是不礼貌的。

en: The impolite act violates the basic rules of etiquette. (9 words)
cn: 这种不礼貌的行为违反了基本的礼仪规则。

en: One has to wonder why we don't apply the same social norms to checking phones during meals, meetings and conversations as we do to other antisocial behaviors. (27 words)
cn: 人们不禁要问，为什么我们不把同样的社交规范应用于吃饭、开会和谈话时查看手机，就像我们对待其他反社会行为一样。

en: Somehow, we accept it and say nothing when someone offends. (10 words)
cn: 不知何故，当有人冒犯时，我们接受它，什么也不说。

en: The reality is taking one's phone out at the wrong time is worse than belching because, unlike other minor offenses, checking tech is contagious. (24 words)
cn: 现实是在错误的时间拿出手机比打嗝更糟糕，因为与其他小过失不同，查看技术具有传染性。

en: Once one person looks at their phone, other people feel compelled to do the same, starting a chain reaction. (19 words)
cn: 一旦一个人看手机，其他人就会觉得有必要也这样做，引发连锁反应。

en: The more people are on their phones, the fewer people are talking until finally you are the only one left not reading email or checking Twitter. (26 words)
cn: 看手机的人越多，说话的人就越少，直到最后你是唯一一个没有看邮件或刷Twitter的人。

en: From a societal perspective, phone checking is less like belching in public and more like another bad habit. (18 words)
cn: 从社会角度来看，查看手机不像在公共场合打嗝，而更像是另一种坏习惯。

en: Our phones are like cigarettes—something to do when we're bored or when our fingers need something to toy with. (19 words)
cn: 我们的手机就像香烟——当我们无聊或手指需要摆弄什么东西时的一种消遣。

en: Seeing others enjoy a smoke, or sneak a quick glance, is too tempting to resist and soon everyone is doing it. (21 words)
cn: 看到别人在抽烟，或者偷偷看一眼，太诱人了，难以抗拒，很快每个人都在这样做。

en: The technology, your boss, and your friends all influence how often you find yourself using (or overusing) these gadgets. (19 words)
cn: 技术、你的老板和你的朋友都影响你使用（或过度使用）这些小工具的频率。

en: But there's still someone who deserves scrutiny—the person holding the phone. (11 words)
cn: 但仍然有一个人值得审视——拿着手机的人。

en: I have a confession. (4 words)
cn: 我有一个坦白。

en: Even though I study habit-forming technology for a living, disconnecting is not easy for me. (15 words)
cn: 尽管我以研究习惯形成技术为生，但断开连接对我来说并不容易。

en: I'm online far more than I'd like. (7 words)
cn: 我在线的时间远远超过我想要的。

en: Like Schwartz and so many others, I often find myself distracted and off track. (14 words)
cn: 像施瓦茨和许多其他人一样，我经常发现自己分心和偏离轨道。

en: I wanted to know why, so I began self-monitoring to try to understand my behavior. (15 words)
cn: 我想知道为什么，所以我开始自我监控，试图理解我的行为。

en: That's when I discovered an uncomfortable truth. (7 words)
cn: 就在那时我发现了一个令人不安的事实。

en: I use technology as an escape. (6 words)
cn: 我把技术当作逃避的手段。

en: When I'm doing something I'd rather not do, or when I'm someplace I'd rather not be, I use my phone to port myself elsewhere. (24 words)
cn: 当我在做我不想做的事情时，或者当我在我不想待的地方时，我就用手机把自己传送到别处。

en: Sometimes this distraction was often a good thing, like when passing time on public transportation, but frequently my tech use was not so benign. (24 words)
cn: 有时这种分心往往是好事，比如在公共交通上消磨时间时，但经常我的技术使用并不那么良性。

en: When I faced difficult work, like thinking through an article idea or editing the same draft for the hundredth time, for example, a more sinister screen would draw me in. (30 words)
cn: 当我面对困难的工作时，比如思考一篇文章的思路或第一百次编辑同一份草稿时，一个更邪恶的屏幕会把我吸引进去。

en: I could easily escape discomfort, temporarily, by answering email or browsing the web under the pretense of so-called 'research.' (19 words)
cn: 我可以很容易地暂时逃避不适，通过回复电子邮件或在所谓的‘研究’幌子下浏览网页。

en: Though I desperately wanted to lay blame elsewhere, I finally had to admit that my bad habits had less to do with new-age technology and more to do with old-fashioned procrastination. (31 words)
cn: 尽管我非常想把责任归咎于别处，但我最终不得不承认，我的坏习惯与新时代技术关系不大，而与老式的拖延症关系更大。

en: It's easy to blame technology for being so distracting, but distraction is nothing new. (14 words)
cn: 把分心归咎于技术很容易，但分心并不是什么新鲜事。

en: Aristotle and Socrates debated the nature of 'akrasia'—our tendency to do things against our interests. (15 words)
cn: 亚里士多德和苏格拉底曾争论过‘akrasia’——即我们做违背自己利益的事情的倾向。

en: If we're honest with ourselves, tech is just another way to occupy our time and minds. (16 words)
cn: 如果我们对自己诚实，技术只是另一种占据我们时间和思想的方式。

en: If we weren't on our devices, we'd likely do similarly unproductive things. (12 words)
cn: 如果我们不在设备上，我们很可能会做类似的非生产性的事情。

en: Personal technology is indeed more engaging than ever, and there's no doubt companies are engineering their products and services to be more compelling and attractive. (25 words)
cn: 个人技术确实比以往任何时候都更吸引人，毫无疑问，公司正在设计他们的产品和服务，使其更具吸引力和诱惑力。

en: But would we want it any other way? (8 words)
cn: 但我们想要别的样子吗？

en: The intended result of making something better is that people use it more. (13 words)
cn: 把东西做得更好的预期结果是人们更多地使用它。

en: That's not necessarily a problem; that's progress. (7 words)
cn: 那不一定是个问题；那是进步。

en: These improvements don't mean we shouldn't attempt to control our use of technology. (13 words)
cn: 这些改进并不意味着我们不应该尝试控制我们对技术的使用。

en: In order to make sure it doesn't control us, we should come to terms with the fact that it's more than the technology itself that's responsible for our habits. (29 words)
cn: 为了确保它不控制我们，我们应该接受这样一个事实：对我们的习惯负责的不仅仅是技术本身。

en: Our workplace culture, social norms and individual behaviors all play a part. (12 words)
cn: 我们的职场文化、社会规范和个人行为都在起作用。

en: To put technology in its place, we must be conscious not only of how technology is changing, but also of how it is changing us. (25 words)
cn: 要让技术恰如其分，我们不仅必须意识到技术是如何变化的，还必须意识到它是如何改变我们的。

en: You may have heard that Coca-Cola once contained an ingredient capable of sparking particular devotion in consumers: cocaine. (18 words)
cn: 你可能听说过可口可乐曾经含有一种能够激发消费者特别喜爱的成分：可卡因。

en: The 'Coca' in the name referred to the extracts of coca leaf that the drink's originator, chemist John Pemberton, mixed with his sugary syrup. (24 words)
cn: 名字中的‘Coca’指的是这种饮料的创始人、化学家约翰·彭伯顿与他含糖糖浆混合的古柯叶提取物。

en: At the time, coca leaf extract mixed with wine was a common tonic, and Pemberton's sweet brew was a way to get around local laws prohibiting the sale of alcohol. (30 words)
cn: 当时，古柯叶提取物与葡萄酒混合是一种常见的滋补品，彭伯顿的甜饮料是一种规避当地禁止销售酒精法律的方式。

en: But the other half of the name presents another ingredient, less infamous, perhaps, but also strangely potent: the kola nut. (20 words)
cn: 但名字的另一半呈现了另一种成分，也许不那么臭名昭著，但也同样具有奇特的效力：可乐果。

en: In West Africa, people have long chewed kola nuts as stimulants, because they contain caffeine that also occurs naturally in tea, coffee, and chocolate. (24 words)
cn: 在西非，人们长期以来把可乐果当作兴奋剂咀嚼，因为它们含有咖啡因，这种物质也天然存在于茶、咖啡和巧克力中。

en: They also have heart stimulants. (5 words)
cn: 它们也含有心脏兴奋剂。

en: Historian Paul Lovejoy relates that the cultivation of kola nuts in West Africa is hundreds of years old. (18 words)
cn: 历史学家保罗·洛夫乔伊指出，西非种植可乐果已有数百年历史。

en: The leafy, spreading trees were planted on graves and as part of traditional rituals. (14 words)
cn: 这些枝叶茂盛、树冠展开的树木被种植在坟墓上，并作为传统仪式的一部分。

en: Even though the nuts, which need to stay moist, can be somewhat delicate to transport, traders carried them hundreds of miles throughout the forests and grasslands. (26 words)
cn: 尽管需要保持湿润的可乐果运输起来有些娇贵，但商人们还是把它们运到了数百英里外的森林和草原。

en: Europeans did not know of them until the 1500s, when Portuguese ships arrived on the coast of what is now Sierra Leone. (22 words)
cn: 欧洲人直到16世纪才知道它们，当时葡萄牙船只抵达了现在塞拉利昂的海岸。

en: And while the Portuguese took part in the trade, ferrying nuts down the coast along with other goods, by 1620, when English explorer Richard Jobson made his way up the Gambia, the nuts were still peculiar to his eyes. (39 words)
cn: 虽然葡萄牙人参与了贸易，将可乐果和其他货物一起运往沿海地区，但到了1620年，当英国探险家理查德·乔布森沿着冈比亚河向上航行时，这些坚果在他眼中仍然很奇特。

en: By the late 19th century, kola nuts were being shipped by the tonne to Europe and the US. (18 words)
cn: 到19世纪末，可乐果正以吨为单位运往欧洲和美国。

en: Many made their way into medicines, intended as a kind of energy boost. (13 words)
cn: 许多可乐果被用于药物，作为一种能量补充剂。

en: One such popular medicinal drink was Vin Mariani, a French product consisting of coca extract mixed with red wine. (19 words)
cn: 其中一种流行的药用饮料是Vin Mariani，一种由古柯提取物与红酒混合的法国产品。

en: It was created by a French chemist, Angelo Mariani, in 1863. (11 words)
cn: 它于1863年由法国化学家安吉洛·马里亚尼创造。

en: So when Pemberton created his drink, it represented an ongoing trend. (11 words)
cn: 因此，当彭伯顿创造他的饮料时，它代表了一种持续的潮流。

en: When cocaine eventually fell from grace as a beverage ingredient, kola-extract colas became popular. (14 words)
cn: 当可卡因最终作为饮料成分失宠时，可乐果提取物的可乐变得流行起来。

en: The first year it was available, Coca-Cola averaged nine servings a day across all the Atlanta soda fountains where it was sold. (22 words)
cn: 在上市的第一年，可口可乐在所有亚特兰大的汽水售卖机平均每天售出9杯。

en: As it grew more popular, the company sold rights to bottle the soda, so it could travel easily. (18 words)
cn: 随着它越来越受欢迎，该公司出售了瓶装这种汽水的权利，以便它能轻松运输。

en: Today about 1.9 billion Cokes are purchased daily. (8 words)
cn: 如今每天约售出19亿瓶可口可乐。

en: It's become so iconic that attempts to change its taste in 1985—sweetening it in a move projected to boost sales—proved disastrous, with widespread anger from consumers. (26 words)
cn: 它已经变得如此具有标志性，以至于1985年改变其口味的尝试——通过增加甜味来促进销售——被证明是灾难性的，引发了消费者的广泛愤怒。

en: 'Coca-Cola Classic' returned to store shelves just three months after the 'New Coke' was released. (15 words)
cn: 在‘新可乐’发布仅三个月后，‘经典可口可乐’就回到了商店货架上。

en: These days, the Coca-Cola recipe is a closely guarded secret. (10 words)
cn: 如今，可口可乐的配方是一个严格保守的秘密。

en: But it's said to no longer contain kola nut extract, relying instead on artificial imitations to achieve the flavour. (19 words)
cn: 但据说它不再含有可乐果提取物，而是依靠人工仿制品来实现这种风味。

en: Twenty years ago, the Urban Land Institute defined the two types of cities that dominated the US landscape: smaller cities that operated around standard 9-5 business hours and large metropolitan areas that ran all 24 hours of the day. (39 words)
cn: 二十年前，城市土地学会定义了主导美国城市景观的两种城市类型：按照标准朝九晚五工作时间运行的小城市和全天24小时运转的大都市区。

en: Analyzing and comparing cities using the lens of this basic divide gives interesting context to how investment capital flows and housing prices have shifted. (24 words)
cn: 用这种基本分化的视角来分析和比较城市，为投资资本的流动和房价的变动提供了有趣的背景。

en: In recent years, many mid-sized cities have begun to adopt a middle-of-the-road approach incorporating the excitement and opportunity of large cities with small cities' quiet after midnight. (27 words)
cn: 近年来，许多中等城市开始采取一种中间路线，将大城市的刺激和机遇与小城市午夜后的宁静结合起来。

en: These 18-hour cities are beginning to make waves in real estate rankings and attract more real estate investment. (18 words)
cn: 这些‘18小时城市’开始在房地产排名中崭露头角，并吸引更多的房地产投资。

en: What is underlying this new movement in real estate, and why do these cities have so much appeal? (18 words)
cn: 房地产这一新运动的背后是什么，为什么这些城市有如此大的吸引力？

en: 18-hour cities combine the best of 24-hour and 9-5 cities, which contributes to downtown revitalization. (15 words)
cn: 18小时城市结合了24小时城市和9-5城市的最佳特点，这有助于市中心的复兴。

en: For decades, many downtown cores in small to mid-sized cities were abandoned after work hours by workers who lived in the suburbs. (22 words)
cn: 几十年来，中小城市的许多市中心核心区在非工作时间被住在郊区的工人所遗弃。

en: Movement out of city centers was widespread, and downtown tenants were predominantly made up of the working poor. (18 words)
cn: 迁出市中心很普遍，市中心的租户主要是贫穷的工薪阶层。

en: This generated little commerce for downtown businesses in the evenings, which made business and generating tax revenue for municipal upkeep difficult. (21 words)
cn: 这在晚上为市中心的企业带来的商业活动很少，这使得营商和为市政维护创造税收变得困难。

en: With the rise of a new concept in urban planning that aims to make life easier and more convenient, however, increasing popularity for urban areas that eased the real estate pushes, in major cities like San Francisco or New York, has inspired a type of forward-thinking urbanity and in smaller cities. (51 words)
cn: 然而，随着城市规划中旨在让生活更轻松便捷的新概念的兴起，旧金山或纽约等主要城市对缓解房地产压力的城区的日益青睐，激发了一种前瞻性的城市风格，在小城市也是如此。

en: Transforming downtown areas so that they incorporate modern housing and improved walkability to local restaurants, retail, and entertainment—especially when combined with improved infrastructure for cyclists and public transit—makes them appeal to a more affluent demographic. (35 words)
cn: 改造市中心区域，使其融合现代住房和改善的步行便利性，方便前往当地餐馆、零售和娱乐场所——尤其是当与改善的自行车和公共交通基础设施相结合时——使它们吸引了更富裕的人群。

en: These adjustments encourage employers in the knowledge and talent industries to keep their offices downtown. (15 words)
cn: 这些调整鼓励知识和人才行业的雇主将办公室留在市中心。

en: Access to foot traffic and proximity to transit allow the type of entertainment-oriented businesses such as bars and restaurants to stay open later, which attracts both younger, creative workers and baby boomers nearing retirement alike. (35 words)
cn: 便捷的人流和靠近交通枢纽使酒吧和餐馆等以娱乐为导向的企业能够营业到更晚，这既吸引了年轻、有创造力的工作者，也吸引了接近退休的婴儿潮一代。

en: Because of their smaller size, most keep hours that allow people to enjoy themselves, then have some quiet after midnight, as opposed to large major cities like New York, where the buzz of activity is ongoing. (36 words)
cn: 由于它们的规模较小，大多数城市的时间安排让人们能够尽情享受，然后在午夜后享受一些宁静，这与纽约等大都市不同，那里的活动喧嚣持续不断。

en: These 18-hour cities are rapidly on the rise and offer great opportunities for homeowner investment. (15 words)
cn: 这些18小时城市正在迅速崛起，为房主投资提供了巨大的机会。

en: In many of these cities such as Denver, a diverse and vigorous economy attracted to the urban core has offered stable employment for residents. (24 words)
cn: 在丹佛等许多这样的城市中，被城市核心所吸引的多样化和充满活力的经济为居民提供了稳定的就业。

en: The right urban mix has propped up home occupancy, increased property values, and attracted significant investment capital. (17 words)
cn: 正确的城市组合支撑了房屋入住率，提高了房产价值，并吸引了大量投资资本。

en: The Pacific island nation of Palau has become home to the sixth largest marine sanctuary in the world. (18 words)
cn: 太平洋岛国帕劳已成为世界第六大海洋保护区的所在地。

en: The new marine reserve, now the largest in the Pacific, will permit no fishing or mining. (16 words)
cn: 这个新的海洋保护区目前是太平洋地区最大的，将不允许捕鱼或采矿。

en: Palau also established the world's first shark sanctuary in 2009. (10 words)
cn: 帕劳还在2009年建立了世界上第一个鲨鱼保护区。

en: The tiny island nation has set aside 500,000 square kilometres—80 percent—of its maritime territory for full protection. (17 words)
cn: 这个小小的岛国已将50万平方公里——占其海洋领土的80%——用于全面保护。

en: That's the highest percentage of an exclusive economic zone devoted to marine conservation by any country in the world. (19 words)
cn: 这是世界上任何国家专属经济区用于海洋保护的最高比例。

en: The remaining 20 percent of the Palau seas will be reserved for local fishing by individuals and small-scale commercial fishing businesses with limited exports. (24 words)
cn: 帕劳海域剩余的20%将留给个人和小规模商业捕鱼企业进行当地捕鱼，出口有限。

en: 'Island communities have been among the hardest hit by the threats facing the ocean,' said President Tommy Remengesau Jr. in a statement. (22 words)
cn: 总统汤米·雷蒙杰索在一份声明中说：‘岛屿社区是海洋面临威胁中受灾最严重的地区之一。’

en: 'Creating this sanctuary is a bold move that the people of Palau recognise as essential to our survival. (18 words)
cn: ‘建立这个保护区是一个大胆的举动，帕劳人民认为这对我们的生存至关重要。’

en: We want to lead the way in restoring the health of the ocean for future generations.' (16 words)
cn: ‘我们希望引领恢复海洋健康，造福子孙后代。’

en: Palau has only been an independent nation for twenty years and has a strong history of environmental protection. (18 words)
cn: 帕劳成为一个独立国家才二十年，但有着悠久的环保历史。

en: It is home to one of the world's finest marine ecosystems, with more than 1,300 species of fish and 700 species of coral. (23 words)
cn: 它拥有世界上最优良的海洋生态系统之一，有1300多种鱼类和700多种珊瑚。

en: Senator Hokkons Baules, lead sponsor of the Palau National Marine Sanctuary Act, said the sanctuary will 'help build a secure future for the Palauan people by honoring the conservation traditions of our past'. (33 words)
cn: 参议员霍肯斯·鲍勒斯是帕劳国家海洋保护区法案的主要发起人，他说该保护区将‘通过尊重我们过去的保护传统，帮助为帕劳人民建立一个安全的未来’。

en: These include the centuries-old custom of 'bul', where leaders would call a temporary stop to fishing for key species in order to give fish stocks an opportunity to replenish. (29 words)
cn: 其中包括有着数百年历史的‘bul’习俗，即领导人会暂时停止捕捞关键物种，以便让鱼类种群有机会补充。

en: It is a movement building steady momentum: a call to make research data, software code and experimental methods publicly available and transparent. (22 words)
cn: 这是一场正在稳步增强势头的运动：呼吁使研究数据、软件代码和实验方法公开透明。

en: A spirit of openness is gaining acceptance in the science community, and is the only way, say advocates, to address a 'crisis' in science whereby too few findings are successfully reproduced. (31 words)
cn: 倡导者说，开放精神正在科学界获得认可，并且是解决科学‘危机’的唯一途径，即成功重现的研究成果太少。

en: Furthermore, they say, it is the best way for researchers to gather the range of observations that are necessary to speed up discoveries or to identify large-scale trends. (28 words)
cn: 此外，他们说，这是研究人员收集加速发现或识别大规模趋势所需的各种观测数据的最佳方式。

en: The open-data shift poses a confusing problem for junior researchers. (10 words)
cn: 数据开放的转变给初级研究人员带来了一个令人困惑的问题。

en: On the one hand, the drive to share is gathering official steam. (12 words)
cn: 一方面，分享的驱动力正在获得官方的支持。

en: Since 2013, global scientific bodies have begun to back policies that support increased public access to research. (17 words)
cn: 自2013年以来，全球科学机构开始支持增加公众获取研究机会的政策。

en: On the other hand, scientists disagree about how much and when they should share data, and they debate whether sharing it is more likely to accelerate science and make it more robust, or to introduce vulnerabilities and problems. (38 words)
cn: 另一方面，科学家们对分享数据的程度和时机存在分歧，他们争论分享数据是否更可能加速科学进展并使其更稳健，或者引入漏洞和问题。

en: As more journals and funders adopt data-sharing requirements, and as a growing number of enthusiasts call for more openness, junior researchers must find their place between adopters and those who continue to hold out, even as they strive to launch their own careers. (43 words)
cn: 随着越来越多的期刊和资助者采用数据共享要求，以及越来越多的爱好者呼吁更加开放，初级研究人员必须在支持者和坚持不分享者之间找到自己的位置，即使他们正努力开创自己的职业生涯。

en: One key challenge facing young scientists is how to be open without becoming scientifically vulnerable. (15 words)
cn: 年轻科学家面临的一个关键挑战是如何保持开放而不陷入科学上的脆弱境地。

en: They must determine the risk of jeopardizing a job offer or a collaboration proposal from those who are wary of—or unfamiliar with—open science. (23 words)
cn: 他们必须确定可能危及工作机会或合作提议的风险，这些风险来自那些对开放科学持谨慎态度或不熟悉的人。

en: And they must learn how to capitalize on the movement's benefits, such as opportunities for more citations and a way to build a reputation without the need for conventional metrics, such as publication in high-impact journals. (36 words)
cn: 他们还必须学会如何利用这场运动的好处，例如获得更多引用的机会，以及无需依赖传统指标（如在影响因子高的期刊上发表论文）来建立声誉的方式。

en: Some fields have embraced open data more than others. (9 words)
cn: 一些领域比其他领域更欢迎开放数据。

en: Researchers in psychology, a field rocked by findings of irreproducibility in the past few years, have been especially vocal supporters of the drive for more-open science. (26 words)
cn: 心理学领域的研究人员在过去几年中因研究结果不可重现而受到冲击，他们一直是推动更开放科学的特别积极的支持者。

en: A few psychology journals have created incentives to increase interest in reproducible science—for example, by affixing an 'open-data' badge to articles that clearly state where data are available. (28 words)
cn: 一些心理学期刊已经创设了激励机制来提高人们对可重复科学研究的兴趣——例如，在明确注明数据可用位置的论文上贴上‘开放数据’徽章。

en: According to social psychologist Brian Nosek, executive director of the Center for Open Science, the average data-sharing rate for the journal Psychological Science, which uses the badges, increased tenfold to 38% from 2013 to 2015. (35 words)
cn: 据开放科学中心执行主任、社会心理学家布莱恩·诺塞克称，使用徽章的《心理科学》期刊的平均数据共享率在2013年至2015年间增长了十倍，达到38%。

en: Funders, too, are increasingly adopting an open-data policy. (8 words)
cn: 资助者也越来越多地采用开放数据政策。

en: Several strongly encourage, and some require, a data-management plan that makes data available. (13 words)
cn: 几家机构强烈鼓励，有些则要求制定数据管理计划，使数据可用。

en: The US National Science Foundation is among these, some philanthropic funders, including the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation in Seattle, Washington, and the Wellcome Trust in London, also mandate open data from their grant recipients. (35 words)
cn: 美国国家科学基金会就在其中，一些慈善资助机构，包括华盛顿州西雅图的比尔及梅琳达·盖茨基金会和伦敦的惠康信托基金会，也要求其受助人开放数据。

en: But many young researchers, especially those who have not been mentored in open science, are uncertain about whether to share or to stay private. (24 words)
cn: 但许多年轻研究人员，尤其是那些没有接受过开放科学指导的人，对于是分享还是保持私密感到不确定。

en: Graduate students and postdocs, who often are working on their lab head's grant, may have no choice if their supervisor or another senior colleague opposes sharing. (26 words)
cn: 研究生和博士后通常是在实验室负责人的资助下工作，如果他们的导师或其他资深同事反对分享，他们可能别无选择。

en: Some fear that the potential impact of sharing is too high, especially at the early stages of a career. (19 words)
cn: 一些人担心分享的潜在影响太大，尤其是在职业生涯的早期阶段。

en: 'Everybody has a scary story about someone getting scooped,' says New York University astronomer David Hogg. (16 words)
cn: 纽约大学天文学家大卫·霍格说：‘每个人都有一个关于某人被抢先的恐怖故事。’

en: Those fears may be a factor in a lingering hesitation to share data even when publishing in journals that mandate it. (21 words)
cn: 这些担忧可能是即使发表在有强制要求的期刊上时，人们仍对分享数据犹豫不决的一个因素。

en: Researchers at small labs or at institutions focused on teaching arguably have the most to lose when sharing hard-won data. (20 words)
cn: 小型实验室或教学型机构的研究人员在分享来之不易的数据时，可以说是损失最大的。

en: 'With my institution and teaching load, I don't have postdocs and grad students,' says Terry McGlynn, a tropical biologist at California State University, Dominguez Hills. (25 words)
cn: 加州州立大学多明格斯山分校的热带生物学家特里·麦格林说：‘考虑到我的机构和教学负担，我没有博士后和研究生。’

en: 'The stakes are higher to share data because it's a bigger fraction of what's happening in my lab.' (18 words)
cn: ‘分享数据的风险更高，因为数据在我的实验室工作中占更大比例。’

en: Researchers also point to the time sink that is involved in preparing data for others to view. (17 words)
cn: 研究人员还指出了将数据准备给别人查看所涉及的时间消耗。

en: Once the data and associated materials appear in a repository, answering questions and handling complaints can take many hours. (19 words)
cn: 一旦数据和相关材料出现在存储库中，回答问题和处理投诉可能需要很多个小时。

en: The time investment can present other problems. (7 words)
cn: 时间投入可能带来其他问题。

en: In some cases, says data scientist Karthik Ram, it may be difficult for junior researchers to embrace openness when senior colleagues—many of whom head selection and promotion committees—might ridicule what they may view as misplaced energies. (36 words)
cn: 数据科学家卡西克·拉姆说，在某些情况下，当资深同事——其中许多人是遴选和晋升委员会的负责人——可能会嘲笑他们认为用错精力的行为时，初级研究人员可能很难接受开放。

en: 'I've heard this recently—that embracing the idea of open data and code makes traditional academics uncomfortable,' says Ram. (18 words)
cn: 拉姆说：‘我最近听到这种说法——接受开放数据和代码的理念会让传统学者感到不安。’

en: 'The concern seems to be that open advocates don't spend their time being as productive as possible.' (17 words)
cn: ‘担忧似乎是开放倡导者没有把时间花在尽可能提高效率上。’

en: An open-science stance can also add complexity to a collaboration. (10 words)
cn: 开放科学的立场也可能增加合作的复杂性。

en: Kate Ratliff, who studies social attitudes at the University of Florida, Gainesville, says that it can seem as if there are two camps in a field—those who care about open science and those who don't. (35 words)
cn: 在佛罗里达大学盖恩斯维尔分校研究社会态度的凯特·拉特利夫说，在一个领域中，似乎有两个阵营——关心开放科学的和不关心的。

en: 'There's a new area to navigate—'Are you cool with the fact that I'll want to make the data open?'—when talking with somebody about an interesting research idea,' she says. (29 words)
cn: 她说：‘当与某人谈论一个有趣的研究想法时，有一个新的领域需要应对——“你介不介意我想公开数据？”’

en: Despite complications and concerns, the upsides of sharing can be significant. (11 words)
cn: 尽管存在复杂性和担忧，分享的好处可能是巨大的。

en: For example, when information is uploaded to a repository, a digital object identifier (DOI) is assigned. (16 words)
cn: 例如，当信息上传到存储库时，会分配一个数字对象标识符（DOI）。

en: Scientists can use a DOI to publish each step of the research life cycle, not just the final paper. (19 words)
cn: 科学家可以使用DOI来发布研究生命周期的每个步骤，而不仅仅是最终的论文。

en: In so doing, they can potentially get three citations—one each for the data and software, in addition to the paper itself. (21 words)
cn: 这样做，他们有可能获得三次引用——除了论文本身外，数据和软件各一次。

en: And although some say that citations for software or data have little currency in academia, they can have other benefits. (20 words)
cn: 虽然有些人说软件或数据的引用在学术界价值不高，但它们可能有其他好处。

en: Many advocates think that transparent data procedures with a date and time stamp will protect scientists from being scooped. (19 words)
cn: 许多倡导者认为，带有日期和时间戳的透明数据程序将保护科学家不被抢先发表。

en: 'This is the sweet spot between sharing and getting credit for it, while discouraging plagiarism,' says Ivo Grigorov, a project coordinator at the National Institute of Aquatic Resources Research Secretariat in Charlottenlund, Denmark. (33 words)
cn: 丹麦夏洛滕隆国家水生资源研究秘书处的项目协调员伊沃·格里戈罗夫说：‘这是分享和获得认可之间的最佳平衡点，同时还能防止剽窃。’

en: Hogg says that scooping is less of a problem than many think. (12 words)
cn: 霍格说，抢先发表问题没有许多人想象的那么严重。

en: 'The two cases I'm familiar with didn't involve open data or code,' he says. (14 words)
cn: 他说：‘我熟悉的两个案例都不涉及开放数据或代码。’

en: Open science also offers junior researchers the chance to level the playing field by gaining better access to crucial data. (20 words)
cn: 开放科学也为初级研究人员提供了通过更好地获取关键数据来公平竞争的机会。

en: Ross Mounce, a postdoc studying evolutionary biology at the University of Cambridge, UK, is a vocal champion of open science, partly because his fossil-based research depends on access to others' data. (31 words)
cn: 英国剑桥大学研究进化生物学的博士后罗斯·蒙斯是开放科学的积极倡导者，部分原因是他以化石为基础的研究依赖于获取他人的数据。

en: He says that more openness in science could help to discourage what some perceive as a common practice of shutting out early-career scientists' requests for data. (26 words)
cn: 他说，科学领域更加开放有助于阻止一些人认为的常见做法，即拒绝早期职业科学家的数据请求。

en: Communication also helps for those who worry about jeopardizing a collaboration, he says. (13 words)
cn: 他说，对于担心危及合作的人来说，沟通也有帮助。

en: Concerns about open science should be discussed at the outset of a study. (13 words)
cn: 对开放科学的担忧应在研究开始时进行讨论。

en: 'Whenever you start a project with someone, you have to establish a clear understanding of expectations for who owns the data, at what point they go public and who can do what with them,' he says. (36 words)
cn: 他说：‘每当你与某人开始一个项目时，你必须对数据的所有权、何时公开以及谁可以用数据做什么等期望有清晰的了解。’

en: In the end, sharing data, software and materials with colleagues can help an early-career researcher to gain recognition—a crucial component of success. (22 words)
cn: 最终，与同事分享数据、软件和材料可以帮助早期职业研究人员获得认可——这是成功的关键组成部分。

en: 'The thing you are searching for is reputation,' says Titus Brown, a genomics researcher at the University of California, Davis. (20 words)
cn: 加州大学戴维斯分校的基因组学研究员泰特斯·布朗说：‘你在寻找的东西就是声誉。’

en: 'To get grants and jobs, you have to be relevant and achieve some level of public recognition. (17 words)
cn: ‘为了获得资助和工作，你必须具有相关性并达到一定水平的公众认可。’

en: Anything you do that advances your presence—especially in a larger sphere, outside the communities you know—is a net win.' (19 words)
cn: ‘你所做的任何能提升你存在感的事情——尤其是在你熟悉的圈子之外的更大范围——都是净赢。’

en: In the beginning of the movie I, Robot, a robot has to decide whom to save after two cars plunge into the water—Del Spooner or a child. (27 words)
cn: 在电影《我，机器人》的开头，两辆汽车坠入水中后，一个机器人必须决定拯救谁——戴尔·斯普纳还是一个孩子。

en: Even though Spooner screams 'Save her! Save her!' the robot rescues him because it calculates that he has a 45 percent chance of survival compared to Sarah's 11 percent. (29 words)
cn: 尽管斯普纳喊道‘救她！救她！’但机器人还是救了他，因为它计算得出他有45%的存活几率，而萨拉只有11%。

en: The robot's decision and its calculated approach raise an important question: would humans make the same choice? (17 words)
cn: 机器人的决定及其计算方式提出了一个重要的问题：人类会做出同样的选择吗？

en: And which choice would we want our robotic counterparts to make? (11 words)
cn: 我们希望我们的机器人伙伴做出哪个选择？

en: Isaac Asimov evaded the whole notion of morality in devising his three laws of robotics, which hold that: 1. Robots cannot harm humans or allow humans to come to harm; 2. Robots must obey humans, except where the order would conflict with law 1; and 3. Robots must act in self-preservation, unless doing so conflicts with laws 1 or 2. (60 words)
cn: 艾萨克·阿西莫夫在设计他的机器人三定律时回避了道德这一概念。三定律规定：1. 机器人不得伤害人类，或坐视人类受到伤害；2. 机器人必须服从人类的命令，除非该命令与第一定律冲突；3. 机器人必须保护自身的存在，除非保护自身与第一或第二定律冲突。

en: These laws are programmed into Asimov's robots—they don't have to think, judge, or value. (14 words)
cn: 这些定律被编程到阿西莫夫的机器人中——它们不需要思考、判断或评价。

en: They don't have to like humans or believe that hurting them is wrong or bad. (15 words)
cn: 它们不需要喜欢人类，也不需要相信伤害他们是错误或不好的。

en: They simply don't do it. (5 words)
cn: 它们只是不去做。

en: The robot who rescues Spooner's life in I, Robot follows Asimov's zeroth law: robots cannot harm humanity (as opposed to individual humans) or allow humanity to come to harm—an expansion of the first law that allows robots to determine what's in the greater good. (44 words)
cn: 在《我，机器人》中拯救斯普纳生命的机器人遵循阿西莫夫的“第零定律”：机器人不得伤害人类整体（而非个体人类），或坐视人类整体受到伤害——这是第一定律的延伸，允许机器人判断什么是更大的利益。

en: Under the first law, a robot could not harm a dangerous gunman, but under the zeroth law, a robot could kill the gunman to save others. (26 words)
cn: 根据第一定律，机器人不能伤害危险的持枪歹徒，但根据第零定律，机器人可以杀死持枪歹徒以拯救他人。

en: Whether it's possible to program a robot with safeguards such as Asimov's laws is debatable. (15 words)
cn: 是否能够对机器人进行编程使其具有如阿西莫夫定律那样的安全防护措施，这是有争议的。

en: A word such as 'harm' is vague (what about emotional harm? (11 words)
cn: 像‘伤害’这样的词是模糊的（情感伤害呢？

en: Is replacing a human employee harm?), and abstract concepts present coding problems. (12 words)
cn: 替换人类员工算是伤害吗？），抽象概念带来了编程问题。

en: The robots in Asimov's fiction expose complications and loopholes in the three laws, and even when the laws work, robots still have to assess situations. (25 words)
cn: 阿西莫夫小说中的机器人暴露了三定律中的复杂性和漏洞，即使定律起作用，机器人仍然需要评估情况。

en: Assessing situations can be complicated. (5 words)
cn: 评估情况可能很复杂。

en: A robot has to identify the players, conditions, and possible outcomes for various scenarios. (14 words)
cn: 机器人必须识别各种场景中的参与者、条件和可能的结果。

en: It's doubtful that a computer program can do that—at least, not without some undesirable results. (15 words)
cn: 计算机程序能否做到这一点是值得怀疑的——至少，不会没有一些不良结果。

en: A roboticist at the Bristol Robotics Laboratory programmed a robot to save human proxies called 'H-bots' from danger. (18 words)
cn: 布里斯托机器人实验室的一位机器人专家对机器人进行了编程，使其拯救名为‘H-bot’的人类替身免受危险。

en: When one H-bot headed for danger, the robot successfully pushed it out of the way. (15 words)
cn: 当一个H-bot走向危险时，机器人成功把它推开了。

en: But when two H-bots became imperiled, the robot choked 42 percent of the time, unable to decide which to save and letting them both 'die.' (25 words)
cn: 但当两个H-bot陷入危险时，机器人在42%的情况下卡住了，无法决定救哪一个，让它们都‘死去’。

en: The experiment highlights the importance of morality: without it, how can a robot decide whom to save or what's best for humanity, especially if it can't calculate survival odds? (29 words)
cn: 这个实验突出了道德的重要性：没有道德，机器人如何决定拯救谁或什么对人类最好，尤其是当它无法计算生存几率时？

en: Our world now moves so fast that we seldom stop to see just how far we have come in just a few years. (23 words)
cn: 当今世界变化如此之快，我们很少停下来看看短短几年内我们取得了多大的进步。

en: The latest iPhone 6s, for example, has a dual-core processor and fits nicely into your pocket. (16 words)
cn: 例如，最新的iPhone 6s配备了双核处理器，而且可以轻松放进口袋。

en: By comparison, you would expect to find a technological specification like this on your standard laptop in an office anywhere in the world. (23 words)
cn: 相比之下，你可能会期望在世界各地办公室的标准笔记本电脑上看到这样的技术规格。

en: It's no wonder that new applications for the Internet of Things are moving ahead fast when almost every new device we buy has a plug on the end of it or a wireless connection to the internet. (37 words)
cn: 几乎我们购买的每一台新设备都带有插头或无线网络连接，难怪物联网的新应用正在飞速发展。

en: Soon, our current smartphone lifestyle will expand to create our own smart home lifestyle too. (15 words)
cn: 很快，我们当前的智能手机生活方式将扩展，创造我们自己的智能家居生活方式。

en: All researches agree that close to 25 billion devices, things and sensors will be connected by 2020, which incidentally is also the moment that Millennials are expected to make up 75 percent of our overall workforce, and the fully connected home will become a reality for large numbers of people worldwide. (51 words)
cn: 所有研究都一致认为，到2020年将有近250亿台设备、物品和传感器实现互联，巧合的是，届时千禧一代预计将占全球劳动力的75%，全互联家庭将成为全球大量人群的现实。

en: However, this is just the tip of the proverbial iceberg as smart buildings and even cities increasingly become the norm as leaders and business owners begin to wake up to the massive savings that technology can deliver through connected sensors and new forms of automation coupled with intelligent energy and facilities management. (52 words)
cn: 然而，这只是冰山一角，因为智能建筑甚至智能城市日益成为常态，领导者和企业主开始意识到技术通过互联传感器和新型自动化，结合智能能源和设施管理所能带来的巨大节省。

en: Online security cameras, intelligent lighting and a wealth of sensors that control both temperature and air quality are offering an unprecedented level of control, efficiency, and improvements to what were once classed necessary costs when running a business or managing a large building. (43 words)
cn: 在线安全摄像头、智能照明以及大量控制温度和空气质量的传感器，正在为经营企业或管理大型建筑时一度被视为必要成本的项目提供前所未有的控制水平、效率和改进。

en: We can expect that the ever-growing list of devices, systems and environments remain connected, always online and talking to each other. (21 words)
cn: 我们可以预期，不断增长的设备、系统和环境列表将保持互联，始终在线并相互通信。

en: The big benefit will not only be in the housing of this enormous and rapidly growing amount of data, but will also be in the ability to run real time data analytics to extract actionable and ongoing knowledge. (38 words)
cn: 巨大的好处不仅在于容纳这些庞大且快速增长的数据量，还在于能够运行实时数据分析以提取可操作和持续的知识。

en: The biggest and most exciting challenge of this technology is how to creatively leverage this ever-growing amount of data to deliver cost savings, improvements and tangible benefits to both businesses and citizens of these smart cities. (36 words)
cn: 这项技术最大、最令人兴奋的挑战是如何创造性地利用这不断增长的数据量为企业和这些智慧城市的公民带来成本节约、改进和实实在在的利益。

en: The good news is that most of this technology is already invented. (12 words)
cn: 好消息是，这项技术的大部分已经发明了。

en: Let's face it, it wasn't too long ago that the idea of working from anywhere and at anytime was some form of a distant Utopian dream, and yet now we can perform almost any office-based task from any location in the world as long as we have access to the internet. (51 words)
cn: 让我们面对现实吧，不久以前，随时随地工作的想法还是一种遥远的乌托邦式的梦想，而现在，只要我们能上网，就可以在世界任何地方完成几乎任何办公室的工作。

en: It's time to wake up to the fact that making smart buildings, cities and homes will dramatically improve our quality of life in the years ahead. (26 words)
cn: 是时候清醒地认识到，建造智能建筑、城市和家庭将在未来几年极大地改善我们的生活质量。

en: Many European countries have been making the shift to electric vehicles and Germany has just stated that they plan to ban the sale of vehicles using gasoline and diesel as fuel by 2030. (33 words)
cn: 许多欧洲国家一直在向电动汽车转型，德国刚刚宣布计划到2030年禁止销售使用汽油和柴油作为燃料的车辆。

en: The country is also planning to reduce its carbon footprint by 80-95% by 2050, sparking a shift to green energy in the country. (23 words)
cn: 该国还计划到2050年将碳足迹减少80-95%，从而引发向绿色能源的转变。

en: Effectively, the ban will include the registration of new cars in the country as they will not allow any gasoline powered vehicle to be registered after 2030. (27 words)
cn: 实际上，该禁令将包括该国新车的注册，因为2030年后他们将不再允许任何汽油动力车辆注册。

en: Part of the reason this ban is being discussed and implemented is because energy officials see that they will not reach their emissions goals by 2050 if they do not eliminate a large portion of vehicle emissions. (37 words)
cn: 这一禁令被讨论和实施的部分原因是能源官员看到，如果他们不消除大部分车辆排放，就无法在2050年前实现排放目标。

en: The country is still hopeful that it will meet its emissions goals, like reducing emissions by 40% by 2020, but the acceptance of electric cars in the country has not occurred as fast as expected. (35 words)
cn: 该国仍然对实现其排放目标抱有希望，比如到2020年减排40%，但该国对电动汽车的接受程度并未如预期般迅速。

en: Other efforts to increase the use of electric vehicles include plans to build over 1 million hybrid and electric car battery changing stations across the country. (26 words)
cn: 增加电动汽车使用的其他努力包括计划在全国建设超过100万个混合动力和电动汽车电池更换站。

en: By 2030, Germany plans on having over 6 million charging stations installed. (12 words)
cn: 到2030年，德国计划安装超过600万个充电站。

en: According to the International Business Times, electric car sales are expected to increase as Volkswagen is still recovering from its emissions scandal. (22 words)
cn: 据《国际商业时报》报道，随着大众汽车仍在从排放丑闻中恢复，电动汽车的销量预计将增加。

en: There are currently around 155,000 registered hybrid and electric vehicles on German roads, dwarfed by the 45 million gasoline and diesel cars driving there now. (25 words)
cn: 目前德国道路上约有15.5万辆注册的混合动力和电动汽车，与目前行驶的4500万辆汽油和柴油汽车相比相形见绌。

en: As countries continue setting goals of reducing emissions, greater steps need to be taken to have a noticeable effect on the surrounding environment. (23 words)
cn: 随着各国继续设定减排目标，需要采取更大的措施来对周围环境产生显著影响。

en: While the efforts are certainly not futile, the results of such bans will likely only start to be seen by generations down the line, bettering the world for the future. (30 words)
cn: 虽然这些努力当然不是徒劳的，但此类禁令的效果可能只有子孙后代才能看到，为未来改善世界。

en: The battle between Apple and law enforcement officials over unlocking a terrorist's smartphone is the culmination of a slow turning of the tables between the technology industry and the United States government. (32 words)
cn: 苹果公司与执法官员之间关于解锁恐怖分子智能手机的争端，是科技行业与美国政府之间角色缓慢转换的高潮。

en: After revelations by the former National Security Agency contractor Edward J. Snowden in 2013 that the government both cozied up to certain tech companies and hacked into others to gain access to private data on an enormous scale, tech giants began to recognize the United States government as a hostile actor. (51 words)
cn: 2013年前国家安全局承包商爱德华·J·斯诺登揭露政府既讨好某些科技公司又入侵其他公司以大规模获取私人数据之后，科技巨头开始将美国政府视为敌对行为者。

en: But if the confrontation has crystallized in this latest battle, it may already be heading toward a predictable conclusion: In the long run, the tech companies are destined to emerge victorious. (31 words)
cn: 但如果对抗在这场最新战役中已经变得明确，它可能已经在走向一个可预测的结局：从长远来看，科技公司注定会取得胜利。

en: It may not seem that way at the moment. (9 words)
cn: 目前看来可能并非如此。

en: On the one side, you have the United States government's mighty legal and security apparatus fighting for data of the most sympathetic sort: the secrets buried in a dead mass murderer's phone. (32 words)
cn: 一方面，美国政府强大的法律和安全机构正在为获取最令人同情的类型的数据而战：一个已故大规模杀人犯手机中埋藏的秘密。

en: The action stems from a federal court order issued on Tuesday requiring Apple to help the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to unlock an iPhone used by one of the two attackers who killed 14 people in San Bernardino, California, in December. (42 words)
cn: 该行动源于周二发布的联邦法院命令，要求苹果公司帮助联邦调查局解锁2015年12月在加利福尼亚州圣贝纳迪诺杀害14人的两名袭击者之一使用的iPhone。

en: In the other corner is the world's most valuable company, whose chief executive, Timothy Cook, has said he will appeal the court's order. (23 words)
cn: 另一角是世界上最有价值的公司，其首席执行官蒂莫西·库克表示他将对法院命令提出上诉。

en: Apple argues that it is fighting to preserve a principle that most of us who are addicted to our smartphones can defend: Weaken a single iPhone so that its contents can be viewed by the American government and you risk weakening all iPhones for any government intruder, anywhere. (48 words)
cn: 苹果辩称，它正在为捍卫我们大多数沉迷于智能手机的人都能捍卫的原则而战：削弱一部iPhone以便美国政府查看其内容，你就冒着为任何地方的任何政府入侵者削弱所有iPhone的风险。

en: There will probably be months of legal confrontation, and it is not at all clear which side will prevail in court, nor in the battle for public opinion and legislative favor. (31 words)
cn: 可能会有数月的法律对抗，目前尚不清楚哪一方将在法庭上获胜，也不清楚在争取公众舆论和立法支持方面的胜负。

en: Yet underlying all of this is a simple dynamic: Apple, Google, Facebook and other companies hold most of the cards in this confrontation. (23 words)
cn: 然而，这一切背后的简单动态是：苹果、谷歌、Facebook和其他公司在这场对抗中掌握着大部分牌。

en: They have our data, and their businesses depend on the global public's collective belief that they will do everything they can to protect that data. (25 words)
cn: 他们拥有我们的数据，他们的业务依赖于全球公众的集体信念，即他们将尽一切努力保护这些数据。

en: Any crack in that front could be fatal for tech companies that must operate worldwide. (15 words)
cn: 前线任何裂痕对必须在全球运营的科技公司来说都可能是致命的。

en: If Apple is forced to open up an iPhone for an American law enforcement investigation, what is to prevent it from doing so for a request from the Russians or the Iranians? (32 words)
cn: 如果苹果被迫为美国执法调查开放iPhone，有什么能阻止它为俄罗斯人或伊朗人的请求这样做呢？

en: If Apple is forced to write code that lets the FBI get into the Phone 5c used by Syed Rizwan Farook, the male attacker in the San Bernardino attack, who would be responsible if some hacker got hold of that code and broke into its other devices? (47 words)
cn: 如果苹果被强迫编写代码让联邦调查局进入圣贝纳迪诺袭击中的男性袭击者赛义德·里兹万·法鲁克使用的Phone 5c，如果某个黑客拿到了该代码并闯入其其他设备，谁将负责？

en: Apple's stance on these issues emerged post-Snowden, when the company started putting in place a series of technologies that, by default, make use of encryption to limit access to people's data. (31 words)
cn: 苹果在这些问题上的立场是在斯诺登事件后出现的，当时该公司开始实施一系列技术，这些技术默认利用加密来限制对人们数据的访问。

en: More than that, Apple—and, in different ways, other tech companies, including Google, Facebook, Twitter and Microsoft—have made their opposition to the government's claims a point of corporate pride. (28 words)
cn: 不仅如此，苹果——以及以不同方式包括谷歌、Facebook、Twitter和微软在内的其他科技公司——已将反对政府的主张作为公司自豪感的体现。

en: Apple's emerging global brand is privacy; it has staked its corporate reputation, not to mention the investment of considerable technical and financial resources, on limiting the sort of mass surveillance that was uncovered by Mr. Snowden. (36 words)
cn: 苹果新兴的全球品牌是隐私；它将公司声誉——更不用说大量的技术和财务资源投资——押注于限制斯诺登所揭露的那种大规模监控。

en: So now, for many cases involving governmental intrusions into data, once-lonely privacy advocates find themselves fighting alongside the most powerful company in the world. (24 words)
cn: 所以现在，在许多涉及政府入侵数据的案件中，曾经孤独的隐私倡导者发现自己正与世界上最强大的公司并肩作战。

en: 'A comparison point is in the 1990s battles over encryption,' said Kurt Opsahl, general counsel of the Electronic Frontier Foundation, a privacy watchdog group. (24 words)
cn: 隐私监督组织电子前沿基金会的总法律顾问库尔特·奥普萨尔说：‘一个可比较的点是20世纪90年代围绕加密的斗争。’

en: 'Then you had a few companies involved, but not one of the largest companies in the world coming out with a lengthy and impassioned post, like we saw yesterday from Timothy Cook. (32 words)
cn: ‘那时有少数公司参与，但没有一家世界最大的公司像我们昨天看到蒂莫西·库克那样发出冗长而慷慨激昂的帖子。’

en: Its profile has really been raised.' (6 words)
cn: ‘它的形象确实得到了提升。’

en: Apple and other tech companies hold another ace: the technical means to keep making their devices more and more inaccessible. (20 words)
cn: 苹果和其他科技公司还持有另一张王牌：使他们的设备越来越难以访问的技术手段。

en: Note that Apple's public opposition to the government's request is itself a hindrance to mass government intrusion. (17 words)
cn: 注意，苹果对政府要求的公开反对本身就是对政府大规模入侵的障碍。
