en: And to get at the contents of a single iPhone, the government says it needs a court order and Apple's help to write new code; in earlier versions of the iPhone, ones that were created before Apple found religion on privacy, the FBI might have been able to break into the device by itself. (54 words)
cn: 而要获取一部iPhone的内容，政府表示需要法院命令和苹果帮助编写新代码；在更早版本的iPhone中，即在苹果热衷隐私之前创建的版本中，FBI可能能够自行破解该设备。

en: You can expect that noose to continue to tighten. (9 words)
cn: 你可以预期这种束缚将继续收紧。

en: Experts said that whether or not Apple loses this specific case, measures that it could put into place in the future will almost certainly be able to further limit the government's reach. (32 words)
cn: 专家表示，无论苹果是否输掉这一具体案件，它未来可能采取的措施几乎肯定能够进一步限制政府的触及范围。

en: That is not to say that the outcome of the San Bernardino case is insignificant. (15 words)
cn: 这并不是说圣贝纳迪诺案件的结果无关紧要。

en: As Apple and several security experts have argued, an order compelling Apple to write software that gives the FBI access to the iPhone in question would establish an unsettling precedent. (30 words)
cn: 正如苹果和几位安全专家所言，强迫苹果编写让FBI访问涉案iPhone的软件的命令将确立一个令人不安的先例。

en: The order essentially asks Apple to hack its own devices, and once it is in place, the precedent could be used to justify law enforcement efforts to get around encryption technologies in other investigations far removed from national security threats. (40 words)
cn: 该命令本质上要求苹果攻击自己的设备，一旦确立，该先例可用于证明执法部门在与国家安全威胁相去甚远的其他调查中绕过加密技术的行为是正当的。

en: Once armed with a method for gaining access to iPhones, the government could ask to use it proactively, before a suspected terrorist attack—leaving Apple in a bind as to whether to comply or risk an attack and suffer a public-relations nightmare. (41 words)
cn: 一旦掌握了获取iPhone内容的方法，政府可以在疑似恐怖袭击发生前要求主动使用它——让苹果陷入两难境地：是服从还是冒着发生袭击的风险并遭受公关噩梦。

en: 'This is a brand new move in the war against encryption,' Mr. Opsahl said. (14 words)
cn: 奥普萨尔先生说：‘这是对抗加密战争中的全新举措。’

en: 'We have had plenty of debates in Congress and the media over whether the government should have a backdoor, and this is an end run around that—here they come with an order to create that backdoor.' (36 words)
cn: ‘我们在国会和媒体上就政府是否应该拥有后门进行了大量辩论，而这是绕过辩论的迂回战术——他们带着创建后门的命令来了。’

en: Yet it is worth noting that even if Apple ultimately loses this case, it has plenty of technical means to close a backdoor over time. (25 words)
cn: 然而值得注意的是，即使苹果最终输掉了这个案子，它也有足够的技术手段随着时间的推移关闭后门。

en: 'If they are anywhere near worth their salt as engineers, I bet they are rethinking their threat model as we speak,' said Jonathan Zdziarski, a digital expert who studies the iPhone and its vulnerabilities. (34 words)
cn: 研究iPhone及其漏洞的数字专家乔纳森·兹贾尔斯基说：‘如果他们作为工程师还算称职的话，我敢打赌他们正在我们说话时重新思考他们的威胁模型。’

en: One relatively simple fix, Mr. Zdziarski said, would be for Apple to modify future versions of the iPhone to require a user to enter a passcode before the phone will accept the sort of modified operating system that the FBI wants Apple to create. (44 words)
cn: 兹贾尔斯基先生说，一个相对简单的修复方法是苹果修改未来版本的iPhone，要求用户在手机接受FBI想要苹果创建的那种修改过的操作系统之前输入密码。

en: That way, Apple could not unilaterally introduce a code that weakens the iPhone—a user would have to consent to it. (20 words)
cn: 这样一来，苹果就不能单方面引入削弱iPhone的代码——用户必须同意才行。

en: 'Nothing is 100 percent hacker-proof,' Mr. Zdziarski said, but he pointed out that the judge's order in this case required Apple to provide 'reasonable security assistance' to unlock Mr. Farook's phone. (31 words)
cn: 兹贾尔斯基先生说：‘没有100%防黑客的东西’，但他指出，本案中法官的命令要求苹果提供‘合理的安全协助’来解锁法鲁克先生的手机。

en: If Apple alters the security model of future iPhones so that even its own engineers' 'reasonable assistance' will not be able to crack a given device when compelled by the government, a precedent set in this case might lose its lasting force. (42 words)
cn: 如果苹果改变未来iPhone的安全模型，使其自己的工程师在政府强迫下也无法破解特定设备，那么本案中确立的先例可能会失去其持久效力。

en: In other words, even if the FBI wins this case, in the long run, it loses. (16 words)
cn: 换句话说，即使FBI赢了这场官司，从长远来看，它还是输了。

en: At the base of a mountain in Tanzania's Gregory Rift, Lake Natron burns bright red, surrounded by the remains of animals that were unfortunate enough to fall into the salty water. (31 words)
cn: 在坦桑尼亚格雷戈里裂谷的一座山脚下，纳特龙湖燃烧着鲜红色，周围是那些不幸落入咸水中的动物的遗骸。

en: Bats, swallows and more are chemically preserved in the pose in which they perished, sealed in the deposits of sodium carbonate in the water. (24 words)
cn: 蝙蝠、燕子等以它们死亡时的姿势被化学保存，封存在水中碳酸钠的沉积物中。

en: The lake's landscape is bizarre and deadly—and made even more so by the fact that it's the place where nearly 75 percent of the world's flamingos are born. (28 words)
cn: 湖的景观奇异而致命——更因其是近75%的世界火烈鸟的出生地而显得如此。

en: The water is so corrosive that it can burn the skin and eyes of unadapted animals. (16 words)
cn: 湖水具有如此强的腐蚀性，以至于能灼伤不适应的动物的皮肤和眼睛。

en: Flamingos, however, are the only species that actually makes life in the midst of all that death. (17 words)
cn: 然而，火烈鸟是唯一真正在这片死亡之地中生存的物种。

en: Once every three or four years, when conditions are right, the lake is covered with the pink birds as they stop flight to breed. (24 words)
cn: 每隔三四年，当条件适宜时，湖面上覆盖着粉色鸟儿，它们停下飞行来繁殖。

en: Three-quarters of the world's flamingos fly over from other salt lakes in the Rift Valley and nest on salt-crystal islands that appear when the water is at a specific level—too high and the birds can't build their nests, too low and predators can move briskly across the lake bed and attack. (51 words)
cn: 世界上四分之三的火烈鸟从裂谷的其他盐湖飞来，在水位达到特定水平时出现在盐晶岛上筑巢——水位太高鸟儿无法筑巢，水位太低捕食者可以迅速穿过湖床发起攻击。

en: When the water hits the right level, the baby birds are kept safe from predators by a corrosive ditch. (19 words)
cn: 当水位达到合适水平时，幼鸟被一条腐蚀性的沟渠保护起来，免受捕食者的侵害。

en: 'Flamingos have evolved very leathery skin on their legs so they can tolerate the salt water,' says David Harper, a professor at the University of Leicester. (26 words)
cn: 莱斯特大学教授戴维·哈珀说：‘火烈鸟的腿进化出了非常坚韧的皮肤，所以它们能耐受盐水。’

en: 'Humans cannot, and would die if their legs were exposed for any length of time.' (15 words)
cn: ‘人类不能，如果双腿暴露在盐水中任何一段时间都会死亡。’

en: So far this year, water levels have been too high for the flamingos to nest. (15 words)
cn: 今年到目前为止，水位太高，火烈鸟无法筑巢。

en: Some fish, too, have had limited success vacationing at the lake as less salty lagoons form on the outer edges from hot springs flowing into Lake Natron. (27 words)
cn: 一些鱼类也在湖中取得了有限的生存成功，因为流入纳特龙湖的温泉在外缘形成了盐度较低的泻湖。

en: Three species of tilapia thrive there part-time. (7 words)
cn: 三种罗非鱼在那里部分时间繁衍生息。

en: 'Fish have a refuge in the streams and can expand into the lagoons when the lake is low and the lagoons are separate,' Harper said. (25 words)
cn: 哈珀说：‘鱼类在溪流中有避难所，当湖水下降且泻湖分离时，它们可以扩展到泻湖中。’

en: 'All the lagoons join when the lake is high and fish must retreat to their stream refuges or die.' (19 words)
cn: ‘当湖水上涨时，所有泻湖连成一片，鱼类必须撤退到溪流避难所，否则就会死亡。’

en: Otherwise, no fish are able to survive in the naturally toxic lake. (12 words)
cn: 否则，没有鱼能在这个天然有毒的湖泊中生存。

en: This unique ecosystem may soon be under pressure. (8 words)
cn: 这个独特的生态系统可能很快就会面临压力。

en: The Tanzanian government has once again started mining the lake for soda ash, used for making chemicals, glass and detergents. (20 words)
cn: 坦桑尼亚政府再次开始在该湖开采纯碱，用于制造化学品、玻璃和洗涤剂。

en: Although the planned operation will be located more than 40 miles away, drawing the soda ash in through pipelines, conservationists worry it could still upset the natural water cycle and breeding grounds. (32 words)
cn: 尽管计划中的作业将位于40多英里外，通过管道输送纯碱，但环保人士担心它仍可能扰乱自然水循环和繁殖地。

en: For now, though, life prevails—even in a lake that kills almost everything it touches. (14 words)
cn: 不过目前，生命仍在延续——即使是在一个几乎杀死它所接触到的一切的湖泊中。

en: It is the season for some frantic last-minute math—across the country, employees of all stripes are counting backward in an attempt to figure out just how much paid time-off they have left in their reserves. (35 words)
cn: 这是一年中进行疯狂最后时刻计算的季节——全国各地的各种员工都在倒数，试图弄清楚他们的带薪休假还有多少剩余。

en: More of them, though, will skip those calculations altogether and just power through the holidays into 2017: More than half of American workers don't use up all of their allotted vacation days each year. (34 words)
cn: 然而，更多的人会完全跳过这些计算，直接度过假期进入2017年：超过一半的美国工人每年没有用完所有分配的年假。

en: Not so long ago, people would have turned up their noses at that kind of dedication to the job. (19 words)
cn: 不久以前，人们还会对这种对工作的奉献嗤之以鼻。

en: As marketing professors Silvia Bellezza, Neeru Paharia, and Anat Keinan recently explained in Harvard Business Review (HBR), leisure time was once seen as an indicator of high social status, something attainable only for those at the top. (37 words)
cn: 正如市场营销学教授西尔维亚·贝莱扎、尼鲁·帕哈里亚和阿纳特·凯南最近在《哈佛商业评论》中解释的那样，休闲时间曾被视为高社会地位的标志，只有顶层人士才能获得。

en: Since the middle of the 20th century, though, things have turned the opposite way—these days, punishing hours at your desk, rather than days off, are seen as the mark of someone important. (32 words)
cn: 然而，自20世纪中叶以来，情况发生了逆转——如今，长时间伏案工作而非休假被视为重要人物的标志。

en: In a series of several experiments, the researchers illustrated just how much we've come to admire busyness, or at least the appearance of it. (24 words)
cn: 在一系列实验中，研究人员展示了我们有多么欣赏忙碌，或至少是忙碌的表象。

en: Volunteers read two passages, one about a man who led a life of leisure and another about a man who was over-worked and over-scheduled; when asked to determine which of the two had a higher social status, the majority of the participants said the latter. (45 words)
cn: 志愿者阅读了两篇文章，一篇关于一个过着休闲生活的男人，另一篇关于一个过度工作和日程过满的男人；当被要求判断两者中谁的社会地位更高时，大多数参与者说是后者。

en: The same held true for people who used products that implied they were short on time: In one experiment, for example, customers of the grocery-delivery service Peapod were seen as of higher status than people who shopped at grocery stores that were equally expensive; in another, people wearing wireless headphones were considered further up on the social ladder than those wearing regular headphones, even when both were just used to listen to music. (73 words)
cn: 同样的情况也适用于使用暗示时间紧迫的产品的用户：例如，在一项实验中，食品配送服务Peapod的顾客被认为比在同样昂贵的杂货店购物的人地位更高；在另一项实验中，佩戴无线耳机的人被认为比佩戴普通耳机的人社会阶层更高，即使两者都只是用来听音乐。

en: In part, the authors wrote in HBR, this pattern may have to do with the way work itself has changed over the past several decades. (25 words)
cn: 作者在《哈佛商业评论》中写道，这种模式在某种程度上可能与过去几十年工作本身的变化方式有关。

en: We think that the shift from leisure-as-status to busyness-as-status may be linked to the development of knowledge-intensive economies. (18 words)
cn: 我们认为，从休闲即地位的转变到忙碌即地位的转变可能与知识密集型经济的发展有关。

en: In such economies, individuals who possess the human capital characteristics that employers or clients value (e.g., competence and ambition) are expected to be in high demand and short supply on the job market. (33 words)
cn: 在这样的经济体中，拥有雇主或客户重视的人力资本特征（如能力和抱负）的个体，预计在就业市场上会供不应求。

en: Thus, by telling others that we are busy and working all the time, we are implicitly suggesting that we are sought after, which enhances our perceived status. (27 words)
cn: 因此，通过告诉别人我们很忙、一直在工作，我们在暗示我们是抢手货，这提升了我们的感知地位。

en: Even if you feel tempted to sacrifice your own vacation days for fake busyness, though, at least consider leaving your weekends unscheduled. (22 words)
cn: 然而，即使你受到诱惑为了虚假的忙碌而牺牲自己的假期，至少考虑让你的周末不被安排。

en: It's for your own good. (5 words)
cn: 这是为了你好。

en: Scientists scanning and mapping the Giza pyramids say they've discovered that the Great Pyramid of Giza is not exactly even. (20 words)
cn: 扫描和绘制吉萨金字塔的科学家表示，他们发现胡夫金字塔并非完全对称。

en: But really not by much. (5 words)
cn: 但差距其实并不大。

en: This pyramid is the oldest of the world's Seven Wonders. (10 words)
cn: 这座金字塔是世界七大奇迹中最古老的一座。

en: The pyramid's exact size has puzzled experts for centuries, as the 'more than 21 acres of hard, white casing stones' that originally covered it were removed long ago. (28 words)
cn: 几个世纪以来，金字塔的确切尺寸一直困扰着专家们，因为最初覆盖它的‘超过21英亩的坚硬白色外壳石料’早已被移除。

en: Reporting in the most recent issue of the newsletter 'AERAGRAM,' which chronicles the work of the Ancient Egypt Research Associates, engineer Glen Dash says his team used a new measuring approach that involved finding any surviving remnants of the casing in order to determine where the original edge was. (49 words)
cn: 工程师格伦·达什在最新一期的通讯《AERAGRAM》中报告说，他的团队使用了一种新的测量方法，包括寻找任何残存的外壳遗迹，以确定原始边缘的位置。该通讯记录了古埃及研究协会的工作。

en: They found the east side of the pyramid to be a maximum of 5.5 inches shorter than the west side. (20 words)
cn: 他们发现金字塔东侧比西侧最多短5.5英寸。

en: The question that most fascinates him, however, isn't how the Egyptians who designed and built the pyramid got it wrong 4,500 years ago, but how they got it so close to perfect. (32 words)
cn: 然而，最让他感兴趣的问题不是4500年前设计和建造金字塔的埃及人是如何出错的，而是他们如何做到如此接近完美。

en: 'We can only speculate as to how the Egyptians could have laid out these lines with such precision using only the tools they had,' Dash writes. (26 words)
cn: 达什写道：‘我们只能推测埃及人是如何仅凭他们拥有的工具就能以如此高的精度布置这些线条的。’

en: He says his hypothesis is that the Egyptians laid out their design on a grid, noting that the great pyramid is oriented only slightly away from the cardinal directions (its north-south axis runs 3 minutes 54 seconds west of due north, while its east-west axis runs 3 minutes 51 seconds north of due east) — an amount that's 'tiny, but similar,' archeologist Atlas Obscura points out. (66 words)
cn: 他说他的假设是埃及人在网格上布置了他们的设计，并指出大金字塔的方向仅略微偏离基本方向（其南北轴位于正北以西3分54秒，而其东西轴位于正东以北3分51秒）——考古学家Atlas Obscura指出，这个偏差‘微小，但相似’。

en: Parents of teenagers often view their children's friends with something like suspicion. (12 words)
cn: 青少年的父母通常对孩子的朋友抱有某种怀疑的态度。

en: They worry that the adolescent peer group has the power to push its members into behavior that is foolish and even dangerous. (22 words)
cn: 他们担心青少年同伴群体有能力促使其成员做出愚蠢甚至危险的行为。

en: Such wariness is well founded: statistics show, for example, that a teenage driver with a same-age passenger in the car is at higher risk of a fatal crash than an adolescent driving alone or with an adult. (37 words)
cn: 这种警惕是有充分根据的：例如，统计数据显示，车内有同龄乘客的青少年司机发生致命车祸的风险高于独自驾驶或与成人同行的青少年。

en: In a 2005 study, psychologist Laurence Steinberg of Temple University and his co-author, psychologist Margo Gardner, then at Temple, divided 306 people into three age groups: young adolescents, with a mean age of 14; older adolescents, with a mean age of 19; and adults, aged 24 and older. (48 words)
cn: 在2005年的一项研究中，天普大学的心理学家劳伦斯·斯坦伯格和他的合著者、当时也在天普大学的心理学家玛戈·加德纳将306人分为三个年龄组：平均年龄14岁的青少年；平均年龄19岁的青少年；以及24岁及以上的成年人。

en: Subjects played a computerized driving game in which the player must avoid crashing into a wall that materializes, without warning, on the roadway. (23 words)
cn: 受试者玩一个电脑驾驶游戏，游戏者必须避免撞到突然出现在道路上的墙壁。

en: Steinberg and Gardner randomly assigned some participants to play alone or with two same-age peers looking on. (17 words)
cn: 斯坦伯格和加德纳随机分配一些参与者独自玩游戏，或让两个同龄同伴旁观。

en: Older adolescents scored about 50 percent higher on an index of risky driving when their peers were in the room—and the driving of early adolescents was fully twice as reckless when other young teens were around. (36 words)
cn: 当有同龄人在场时，年龄较大的青少年在危险驾驶指数上的得分高出约50%，而当有其他年轻青少年在场时，年龄较小青少年的驾驶鲁莽程度则完全是其两倍。

en: In contrast, adults behaved in similar ways regardless of whether they were on their own or observed by others. (19 words)
cn: 相比之下，成年人的行为无论独自一人还是被他人观察都表现相似。

en: 'The presence of peers makes adolescents and youth, but not adults, more likely to take risks,' Steinberg and Gardner concluded. (20 words)
cn: 斯坦伯格和加德纳总结道：‘同伴的存在使青少年和年轻人更倾向于冒险，但成年人则不然。’

en: Yet in the years following the publication of this study, Steinberg began to believe that this interpretation did not capture the whole picture. (23 words)
cn: 然而，在这项研究发表后的几年里，斯坦伯格开始相信这种解释并没有反映全貌。

en: As he and other researchers examined the question of why teens were more apt to take risks in the company of other teenagers, they came to suspect that a crowd's influence need not always be negative. (36 words)
cn: 当他和其他研究人员研究为什么青少年在与其他青少年相处时更容易冒险时，他们开始怀疑群体的影响不一定总是负面的。

en: Now some experts are proposing that we should take advantage of the teen brain's keen sensitivity to the presence of friends and leverage it to improve education. (27 words)
cn: 现在，一些专家提议我们应该利用青少年大脑对朋友在场的敏锐敏感性，并利用它来改善教育。

en: In a 2011 study, Steinberg and his colleagues turned to functional MRI to investigate how the presence of peers affects the activity in the adolescent brain. (26 words)
cn: 在2011年的一项研究中，斯坦伯格和他的同事使用功能性磁共振成像来研究同伴的存在如何影响青少年大脑的活动。

en: They scanned the brains of 40 teens and adults who were playing a virtual driving game designed to test whether players would brake at a yellow light or speed on through the crossroad. (33 words)
cn: 他们扫描了40名青少年和成年人的大脑，他们正在玩一个虚拟驾驶游戏，旨在测试玩家是否会在黄灯时刹车还是加速通过十字路口。

en: The brains of teenagers, but not adults, showed greater activity in two regions associated with rewards when they were being observed by same-age peers than when alone. (27 words)
cn: 青少年的大脑在与奖励相关的两个区域表现出更大的活动，当他们被同龄人观察时比独自一人时更活跃，而成年人则没有。

en: In other words, rewards are more intense for teens when they are with peers, which motivates them to pursue higher-risk experiences that might bring a big payoff (such as the thrill of just making the light before it turns red). (40 words)
cn: 换句话说，青少年与同伴在一起时奖励感更强烈，这激励他们追求可能带来巨大回报的高风险体验（例如在红灯亮起前刚好通过的刺激感）。

en: But Steinberg suspected this tendency could also have its advantages. (10 words)
cn: 但斯坦伯格怀疑这种倾向也可能有其优势。

en: In his latest experiment, published online in August, Steinberg and his colleagues used a computerized version of a card game called the Iowa Gambling Task to investigate how the presence of peers affects the way young people gather and apply information. (41 words)
cn: 在他最新发表于8月的在线实验中，斯坦伯格和他的同事使用了一种名为爱荷华赌博任务的纸牌游戏的电脑版，来研究同伴的存在如何影响年轻人收集和应用信息的方式。

en: The results: Teens who played the Iowa Gambling Task under the eyes of fellow adolescents engaged in more exploratory behavior, learned faster from both positive and negative outcomes, and achieved better performance on the task than those who played in solitude. (41 words)
cn: 结果：在同伴注视下玩爱荷华赌博任务的青少年表现出更多的探索行为，从积极和消极结果中学得更快，并在任务中表现得比独自玩耍的青少年更好。

en: 'What our study suggests is that teenagers learn more quickly and more effectively when their peers are present than when they're on their own,' Steinberg says. (26 words)
cn: 斯坦伯格说：‘我们的研究表明，青少年在有同伴在场时比独自一人时学得更快、更有效。’

en: And this finding could have important implications for how we think about educating adolescents. (14 words)
cn: 这一发现可能对我们如何思考青少年教育产生重要影响。

en: Matthew D. Lieberman, a social cognitive neuroscientist at the University of California, Los Angeles, and author of the 2013 book Social: Why Our Brains Are Wired to Connect, suspects that the human brain is especially skillful at learning socially significant information. (41 words)
cn: 加州大学洛杉矶分校的社会认知神经科学家马修·D·利伯曼是2013年出版的《社交：为什么我们的大脑天生会连接》一书的作者，他怀疑人脑特别擅长学习具有社会意义的信息。

en: He points to a classic 2004 study in which psychologists at Dartmouth College and Harvard University used functional MRI to track brain activity in 17 young men as they listened to descriptions of people while concentrating on either socially relevant cues (for example, trying to form an impression of a person based on the description) or more socially neutral information (such as noting the order of details in the description). (70 words)
cn: 他引用了2004年的一项经典研究，在该研究中，达特茅斯学院和哈佛大学的心理学家使用功能性磁共振成像追踪17名年轻男性的大脑活动，他们一边听关于人的描述，一边专注于社会相关线索（例如，试图根据描述形成对一个人的印象）或更中立的社会信息（例如，注意描述中细节的顺序）。

en: The descriptions were the same in each condition, but people could better remember these statements when given a social motivation. (20 words)
cn: 每种情况下的描述都相同，但当给予社会动机时，人们能更好地记住这些陈述。

en: The study also found that when subjects thought about and later recalled descriptions in terms of their informational content, regions associated with factual memory, such as the medial temporal lobe, became active. (32 words)
cn: 研究还发现，当受试者根据信息内容思考和回忆描述时，与事实记忆相关的区域，如内侧颞叶，变得活跃。

en: But thinking about or remembering descriptions in terms of their social meaning activated the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex—part of the brain's social network—even as traditional memory regions registered low levels of activity. (31 words)
cn: 但根据社会意义思考或回忆描述激活了背内侧前额叶皮层——大脑社交网络的一部分——即使传统记忆区域的活动水平较低。

en: More recently, as he reported in a 2012 review, Lieberman has discovered that this region may be part of a distinct network involved in socially motivated learning and memory. (29 words)
cn: 最近，正如他在2012年的一篇综述中所报道的那样，利伯曼发现这一区域可能是一个独特的网络的一部分，该网络参与社会动机的学习和记忆。

en: Such findings, he says, suggest that 'this network can be called on to process and store the kind of information taught in school—potentially giving students access to a range of untapped mental powers.' (33 words)
cn: 他说，这些发现表明：‘可以利用这一网络来处理和存储学校教授的那种信息——从而有可能让学生获得一系列未开发的心理能力。’

en: If humans are generally geared to recall details about one another, this pattern is probably even more powerful among teenagers who are very attentive to social details: who is in, who is out, who likes whom, who is mad at whom. (41 words)
cn: 如果人类通常倾向于回忆彼此的细节，那么这种模式在青少年中可能更强大，他们非常关注社交细节：谁受欢迎，谁被冷落，谁喜欢谁，谁生谁的气。

en: Their desire for social drama is not—or not only—a way of distracting themselves from their schoolwork or of driving adults crazy. (21 words)
cn: 他们对社交戏剧的渴望不是——或不只是——分散自己学业注意力或让成年人抓狂的方式。

en: It is actually a neurological sensitivity, initiated by hormonal changes. (10 words)
cn: 它实际上是由荷尔蒙变化引发的一种神经敏感性。

en: Evolutionarily speaking, people in this age group are at a stage in which they can prepare to find a mate and start their own family while separating from parents and striking out on their own. (35 words)
cn: 从进化角度来说，这个年龄段的人处于一个阶段，他们可以准备寻找伴侣、组建自己的家庭，同时离开父母独立生活。

en: To do this successfully, their brain prompts them to think and even obsess about others. (15 words)
cn: 为了成功做到这一点，他们的大脑促使他们思考甚至痴迷于他人。

en: Yet our schools focus primarily on students as individual entities. (10 words)
cn: 然而，我们的学校主要将学生视为个体。

en: What would happen if educators instead took advantage of the fact that teens are powerfully compelled to think in social terms? (21 words)
cn: 如果教育者利用青少年强烈倾向于社交思维这一事实，会发生什么？

en: In Social, Lieberman lays out a number of ways to do so. (12 words)
cn: 在《社交》一书中，利伯曼列出了几种方法。

en: History and English could be presented through the lens of the psychological drives of the people involved. (17 words)
cn: 历史和英语可以通过相关人物的心理驱动力来呈现。

en: One could therefore present Napoleon in terms of his desire to impress or Churchill in terms of his lonely gloom. (20 words)
cn: 因此，可以从拿破仑渴望给人留下深刻印象的角度来呈现他，或从丘吉尔孤独忧郁的角度来呈现他。

en: Less inherently interpersonal subjects, such as math, could acquire a social aspect through team problem solving and peer tutoring. (19 words)
cn: 本身不太需要人际交往的科目，如数学，可以通过团队解决问题和同伴辅导获得社交属性。

en: Research shows that when we absorb information in order to teach it to someone else, we learn it more accurately and deeply, perhaps in part because we are engaging our social cognition. (32 words)
cn: 研究表明，当我们为了教给别人而吸收信息时，我们会学得更准确、更深入，部分原因可能是我们正在调动我们的社会认知。

en: And although anxious parents may not welcome the notion, educators could turn adolescent recklessness to academic ends. (17 words)
cn: 尽管焦虑的父母可能不欢迎这个观点，但教育者可以将青少年的鲁莽行为用于学术目的。

en: 'Risk taking in an educational context is a vital skill that enables progress and creativity,' wrote Sarah-Jayne Blakemore, a cognitive neuroscientist at University College London, in a review published last year. (31 words)
cn: 伦敦大学学院的认知神经科学家萨拉-杰恩·布莱克莫尔在去年发表的一篇综述中写道：‘在教育情境中冒险是促进进步和创造力的重要技能。’

en: Yet, she noted, many young people are especially unwilling to take risks at school—afraid that one low test score or poor grade could cost them a spot at a selective university. (31 words)
cn: 然而，她指出，许多年轻人特别不愿意在学校冒险——担心一次低分或糟糕的成绩会让他们失去在精英大学的入学名额。

en: We should assure such students that risk, and even peer pressure, can be a good thing—as long as it happens in the classroom and not in the car. (28 words)
cn: 我们应该让这些学生放心，冒险，甚至同伴压力，都可以是好事——只要它发生在教室里，而不是在车里。

en: The Ebro Delta, in Spain, famous as a battleground during the Spanish Civil War, is now the setting for a different contest, one that is pitting rice farmers against two enemies: the rice-eating giant apple snail, and rising sea levels. (40 words)
cn: 西班牙的埃布罗三角洲因西班牙内战期间的战场而闻名，现在正上演一场不同的较量，水稻种植者面临两个敌人：食稻的巨型苹果螺和上升的海平面。

en: What happens here will have a bearing on the future of European rice production and the overall health of southern European wetlands. (22 words)
cn: 这里发生的事情将对欧洲水稻生产的未来和南欧湿地的整体健康产生影响。

en: Located on the Mediterranean just two hours south of Barcelona, the Ebro Delta produces 120 million kilograms of rice a year, making it one of the continent's most important rice-growing areas. (31 words)
cn: 埃布罗三角洲位于地中海沿岸，距巴塞罗那以南仅两小时车程，年产大米1.2亿公斤，使其成为欧洲大陆最重要的大米产区之一。

en: As the sea creeps into these fresh-water marshes, however, rising salinity is hampering rice production. (15 words)
cn: 然而，随着海水侵入这些淡水沼泽，不断上升的盐度正在阻碍水稻生产。

en: At the same time, this sea-water also kills off the greedy giant apple snail, an introduced pest that feeds on young rice plants. (23 words)
cn: 同时，这种海水也杀死了贪婪的巨型苹果螺——一种以水稻幼苗为食的外来害虫。

en: The most promising strategy has become to harness one foe against the other. (13 words)
cn: 最有希望的策略已成为利用一个敌人对付另一个敌人。

en: The battle is currently being waged on land, in greenhouses at the University of Barcelona. (15 words)
cn: 这场战斗目前正在陆地上进行，在巴塞罗那大学的温室里。

en: Scientists working under the banner 'Project Neurice' are seeking varieties of rice that can withstand the increasing salinity without losing the absorbency that makes European rice ideal for traditional Spanish and Italian dishes. (33 words)
cn: 以‘Neurice项目’为旗帜的科学家们正在寻找能够抵抗盐度增加而不失去吸水性的水稻品种，正是这种吸水性使欧洲大米成为传统西班牙和意大利菜肴的理想选择。

en: 'The project has two sides,' says Xavier Serrat, Neurice project manager and researcher at the University of Barcelona, 'the short-term fight against the snail, and a mid- to long-term fight against climate change. (33 words)
cn: 巴塞罗那大学的Neurice项目经理兼研究员泽维尔·塞拉特说：‘该项目有两个方面：短期对抗蜗牛，中期到长期对抗气候变化。’

en: But the snail has given the project greater urgency.' (9 words)
cn: ‘但蜗牛给项目带来了更大的紧迫性。’

en: Originally from South America, the snails were accidentally introduced into the Ebro Delta by Global Aquatic Technologies, a company that raised the snails for fresh-water aquariums, but failed to prevent their escape. (32 words)
cn: 这些蜗牛原产于南美洲，被Global Aquatic Technologies公司意外引入埃布罗三角洲，该公司饲养蜗牛用于淡水水族馆，但未能防止它们逃逸。

en: For now, the giant apple snail's presence in Europe is limited to the Ebro Delta. (15 words)
cn: 目前，巨型苹果螺在欧洲的存在仅限于埃布罗三角洲。

en: But the snail continues its march to new territory, says Serrat. (11 words)
cn: 但塞拉特说，蜗牛继续向新领地进军。

en: 'The question is not whether it will reach other rice-growing areas of Europe, but when.' (15 words)
cn: ‘问题不是它是否会到达欧洲其他水稻种植区，而是何时。’

en: Over the next year and a half investigators will test the various strains of salt-tolerant rice they've bred. (18 words)
cn: 在接下来的一年半里，研究人员将测试他们培育的各种耐盐水稻品种。

en: In 2018, farmers will plant the varieties with the most promise in the Ebro Delta and Europe's other two main rice-growing regions—along the Po in Italy, and France's Rhone. (29 words)
cn: 2018年，农民将在埃布罗三角洲和欧洲其他两个主要水稻种植区——意大利的波河流域和法国的罗讷河流域——种植最有希望的品种。

en: A season in the field will help determine which, if any, of the varieties are ready for commercialization. (18 words)
cn: 一季的田间种植将有助于确定哪些品种（如果有的话）已准备好商业化。

en: As an EU-funded effort, the search for salt-tolerant varieties of rice is taking place in all three countries. (18 words)
cn: 作为欧盟资助的项目，寻找耐盐水稻品种的工作正在这三个国家进行。

en: Each team is crossbreeding a local European short-grain rice with a long-grain Asian variety that carries the salt-resistant gene. (19 words)
cn: 每个团队都在将当地的欧洲短粒水稻与携带耐盐基因的亚洲长粒品种进行杂交。

en: The scientists are breeding successive generations to arrive at varieties that incorporate salt tolerance but retain about 97 percent of the European rice genome. (24 words)
cn: 科学家们正在培育连续世代，以获得既具有耐盐性又保留约97%欧洲水稻基因组的品种。

en: Photography was once an expensive, laborious ordeal reserved for life's greatest milestones. (12 words)
cn: 摄影曾经是一种昂贵、费力的考验，只用于人生最重要的里程碑。

en: Now, the only apparent cost to taking infinite photos of something as common as a meal is the space on your hard drive and your dining companion's patience. (28 words)
cn: 如今，对像一顿饭这样普通的东西拍无数张照片，唯一明显的成本就是硬盘空间和你用餐同伴的耐心。

en: But is there another cost, a deeper cost, to documenting a life experience instead of simply enjoying it? (18 words)
cn: 但是，记录生活经历而不是简单地享受它，是否有另一种成本，一种更深的成本？

en: 'You hear that you shouldn't take all these photos and interrupt the experience, and it's bad for you, and we're not living in the present moment,' says Kristin Diehl, associate professor of marketing at the University of Southern California Marshall School of Business. (43 words)
cn: 南加州大学马歇尔商学院市场营销学副教授克里斯汀·迪尔说：‘你听说你不应该拍这么多照片并打断体验，这对你不好，我们没有活在当下。’

en: Diehl and her fellow researchers wanted to find out if that was true, so they embarked on a series of nine experiments in the lab and in the field testing people's enjoyment in the presence or absence of a camera. (40 words)
cn: 迪尔和她的同事想弄清楚这是否属实，于是他们在实验室和现场进行了一系列九项实验，测试人们在有相机或没有相机的情况下的享受程度。

en: The results, published in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, surprised them. (13 words)
cn: 发表在《人格与社会心理学杂志》上的结果让他们感到惊讶。

en: Taking photos actually makes people enjoy what they're doing more, not less. (12 words)
cn: 拍照实际上让人们更享受他们正在做的事情，而不是更少。

en: 'What we find is you actually look at the world slightly differently, because you're looking for things you want to capture, that you may want to hang onto,' Diehl explains. (30 words)
cn: 迪尔解释说：‘我们发现你实际上以略微不同的方式看世界，因为你在寻找你想要捕捉、你可能想要保留的东西。’

en: 'That gets people more engaged in the experience, and they tend to enjoy it more.' (15 words)
cn: ‘这让人更投入到体验中，他们往往更享受。’

en: Take sightseeing. (2 words)
cn: 以观光为例。

en: In one experiment, nearly 200 participants boarded a double-decker bus for a tour of Philadelphia. (15 words)
cn: 在一项实验中，近200名参与者登上一辆双层巴士游览费城。

en: Both bus tours forbade the use of cell phones but one tour provided digital cameras and encouraged people to take photos. (21 words)
cn: 两次巴士游览都禁止使用手机，但其中一次提供了数码相机并鼓励人们拍照。

en: The people who took photos enjoyed the experience significantly more, and said they were more engaged, than those who didn't. (20 words)
cn: 拍照的人比不拍照的人明显更享受体验，并表示他们更投入。

en: Snapping a photo directs attention, which heightens the pleasure you get from whatever you're looking at, Diehl says. (18 words)
cn: 迪尔说，拍照会引导注意力，从而增加你从所看之物中获得的愉悦感。

en: It works for things as boring as archaeological museums, where people were given eye-tracking glasses and instructed either to take photos or not. (23 words)
cn: 这同样适用于考古博物馆等无聊的场所，在那里，人们被戴上眼球追踪眼镜，并被指示拍照或不拍照。

en: 'People look longer at things they want to photograph,' Diehl says. (11 words)
cn: 迪尔说：‘人们看他们想拍的东西时间更长。’

en: They report liking the exhibits more, too. (7 words)
cn: 他们也报告更喜欢展品。

en: To the relief of Instagrammers everywhere, it can even make meals more enjoyable. (13 words)
cn: 让世界各地的Instagram用户松了一口气的是，这甚至能让用餐更愉快。

en: When people were encouraged to take at least three photos while they ate lunch, they were more immersed in their meals than those who weren't told to take photos. (29 words)
cn: 当人们被鼓励在吃午餐时至少拍三张照片时，他们比没有被要求拍照的人更沉浸在用餐中。

en: Was it the satisfying click of the camera? (8 words)
cn: 是相机令人满意的咔哒声吗？

en: The physical act of the snap? (6 words)
cn: 是按下快门的物理动作吗？

en: No, they found; just the act of planning to take a photo—and not actually taking it—had the same joy-boosting effect. (20 words)
cn: 不，他们发现；仅仅是计划拍照的行为——而不是实际拍照——也有同样的提升快乐的效果。

en: 'If you want to take mental photos, that works the same way,' Diehl says. (14 words)
cn: 迪尔说：‘如果你想拍心理照片，那也有同样的效果。’

en: 'Thinking about what you would want to photograph also gets you more engaged.' (13 words)
cn: ‘思考你想拍什么也会让你更投入。’

en: Did Sarah Josepha Hale write 'Mary's Little Lamb,' the eternal nursery rhyme about a girl named Mary with a stubborn lamb? (21 words)
cn: 莎拉·约瑟法·黑尔是《玛丽的小羊羔》的作者吗？这首永恒的童谣讲述了一个名叫玛丽的女孩和她那固执的小羊羔的故事。

en: This is still disputed, but it's clear that the woman reputed for writing it was one of America's most fascinating characters. (21 words)
cn: 这一点仍有争议，但很明显，这位因创作这首童谣而闻名的女性是美国最引人注目的人物之一。

en: In honor of the poem's publication on May 24, 1830, here's more about the supposed author's life. (17 words)
cn: 为纪念这首诗于1830年5月24日发表，以下关于这位所谓作者的更多生平信息。

en: Hale wasn't just a writer, she was also a fierce social advocate, and she was particularly obsessed with an ideal New England, which she associated with abundant Thanksgiving meals that she claimed had 'a deep moral influence.' (37 words)
cn: 黑尔不仅是一位作家，她还是一位激烈的社会倡导者，她尤其痴迷于理想化的新英格兰，她将其与丰盛的感恩节大餐联系在一起，并声称这些大餐具有‘深刻的道德影响’。

en: She began a nationwide campaign to have a national holiday declared that would bring families together while celebrating the traditional festivals. (21 words)
cn: 她发起了一场全国性的运动，要求宣布一个全国性节日，让家人团聚在一起庆祝传统节日。

en: In 1863, after 17 years of advocacy including letters to five presidents, Hale got it. (15 words)
cn: 1863年，经过17年的倡导，包括给五位总统写信，黑尔成功了。

en: President Abraham Lincoln, during the Civil War, issued a proclamation setting aside the last Thursday in November for the holiday. (20 words)
cn: 在内战期间，亚伯拉罕·林肯总统发布了一项公告，将11月的最后一个星期四定为这个节日。

en: The true authorship of 'Mary's Little Lamb' is disputed. (9 words)
cn: 《玛丽的小羊羔》的真正作者身份存在争议。

en: According to the New England Historical Society, Hale wrote only part of the poem, but claimed authorship. (17 words)
cn: 据新英格兰历史学会称，黑尔只写了这首诗的一部分，但声称自己是作者。

en: Regardless of the author, it seems that the poem was inspired by a real event. (15 words)
cn: 无论作者是谁，这首诗似乎是受一个真实事件启发的。

en: When young Mary Sawyer was followed to school by a lamb in 1816, it caused some problems. (17 words)
cn: 1816年，年幼的玛丽·索耶被一只小羊羔跟着去学校，这引起了一些麻烦。

en: A bystander named John Roulstone wrote a poem about the event, then, at some point, Hale herself seems to have helped write it. (23 words)
cn: 一个名叫约翰·鲁尔斯通的旁观者写了一首关于这件事的诗，然后，在某个时候，黑尔本人似乎帮忙写了这首诗。

en: However, if a 1916 piece by her great-niece is to be trusted, Hale claimed for the rest of her life that 'some other people pretended that someone else wrote the poem'. (31 words)
cn: 然而，如果她侄孙女在1916年的一篇文章可信的话，黑尔在余生中一直声称‘有些其他人假装是别人写了这首诗’。

en: Ever since humanity began to farm our own food, we've faced the unpredictable rain that is both friend and enemy. (20 words)
cn: 自从人类开始种植自己的食物以来，我们就面临着变幻莫测的雨水，它既是朋友也是敌人。

en: It comes and goes without much warning, and a field of lush leafy greens one year can dry up and blow away the next. (24 words)
cn: 它来去无常，前一年还是一片茂盛的绿叶菜地，第二年就可能干枯并被风吹走。

en: Food security and fortunes depend on sufficient rain, and nowhere more so than in Africa, where 96% of farmland depends on rain instead of the irrigation common in more developed places. (31 words)
cn: 粮食安全和财富依赖于充足的雨水，这一点在非洲最为突出，那里96%的农田依赖雨水，而不是在较发达地区常见的灌溉。

en: It has consequences: South Africa's ongoing drought—the worst in three decades—will cost at least a quarter of its corn crop this year. (22 words)
cn: 这带来了后果：南非持续的干旱——三十年来最严重的一次——今年将损失至少四分之一的玉米收成。

en: Biologist Jill Farrant of the University of Cape Town in South Africa says that nature has plenty of answers for people who want to grow crops in places with unpredictable rainfall. (31 words)
cn: 南非开普敦大学的生物学家吉尔·法兰特表示，对于那些希望在降雨不可预测的地方种植作物的人来说，大自然有很多答案。

en: She is hard at work finding a way to take traits from rare wild plants that adapt to extreme dry weather and use them in food crops. (27 words)
cn: 她正在努力寻找一种方法，从适应极端干旱天气的稀有野生植物中提取特性，并将其用于粮食作物。

en: As the earth's climate changes and rainfall becomes even less predictable in some places, those answers will grow even more valuable. (21 words)
cn: 随着地球气候变化以及某些地区降雨变得更加不可预测，这些答案将变得更有价值。

en: 'The type of farming I'm aiming for is literally so that people can survive as it's going to get more and more dry,' Farrant says. (25 words)
cn: 法兰特说：‘我追求的那种农业模式，实际上是为了让人们在日益干旱的环境中生存下来。’

en: Extreme conditions produce extremely tough plants. (6 words)
cn: 极端条件造就了极端坚韧的植物。

en: In the rusty red deserts of South Africa, steep-sided rocky hills called inselbergs rear up from the plains like the bones of the earth. (24 words)
cn: 在南非铁锈红色的沙漠中，被称为“岛山”的陡峭岩石山从平原拔地而起，就像地球的骨骼。

en: The hills are remnants of an earlier geological era, scraped bare of most soil and exposed to the elements. (19 words)
cn: 这些山丘是早期地质时代的遗迹，大部分土壤被冲刷殆尽，暴露在自然环境中。

en: Yet on these and similar formations in deserts around the world, a few fierce plants have adapted to endure under ever-changing conditions. (22 words)
cn: 然而，在世界各地沙漠的这些和类似的地貌上，一些顽强的植物已经适应了在不断变化的条件下的生存。

en: Farrant calls them resurrection plants. (5 words)
cn: 法兰特称它们为“复活植物”。

en: During months without water under a harsh sun, they wither, shrink and contract until they look like a pile of dead gray leaves. (23 words)
cn: 在烈日下数月无水的期间，它们枯萎、收缩、蜷缩，直到看起来像一堆枯死的灰色叶子。

en: But rainfall can revive them in a matter of hours. (10 words)
cn: 但降雨可以在几小时内使它们复活。

en: Her time-lapse videos of the revivals look like someone playing a tape of the plant's death in reverse. (18 words)
cn: 她拍摄的复活过程的延时视频，看起来就像是有人倒放植物死亡的录像带。

en: The big difference between 'drought-tolerant' plants and these tough plants: metabolism. (11 words)
cn: “耐旱”植物和这些坚韧植物之间的最大区别在于：新陈代谢。

en: Many different kinds of plants have developed tactics to weather dry spells. (12 words)
cn: 许多不同种类的植物都发展出了度过干旱期的策略。

en: Some plants store reserves of water to see them through a drought; others send roots deep down to subsurface water supplies. (21 words)
cn: 有些植物储存水分储备以度过干旱；另一些植物则将根深入地下水源。

en: But once these plants use up their stored reserve or tap out the underground supply, they cease growing and start to die. (22 words)
cn: 但是一旦这些植物用完了储存的水分或耗尽了地下水源，它们就会停止生长并开始死亡。

en: They may be able to handle a drought of some length, and many people use the term 'drought tolerant' to describe such plants, but they never actually stop needing to consume water, so Farrant prefers to call them drought resistant. (40 words)
cn: 它们或许能应对一定程度的干旱，许多人用“耐旱”一词来描述这类植物，但它们从未真正停止过对水分的需求，所以法兰特更倾向于称它们为“抗旱植物”。

en: Resurrection plants, defined as those capable of recovering from holding less than 0.1 grams of water per gram of dry mass, are different. (23 words)
cn: 复活植物被定义为那些能够在每克干物质含水量低于0.1克时恢复的植物，它们有所不同。

en: They lack water-storing structures, and their existence on rock faces prevents them from tapping groundwater, so they have instead developed the ability to change their metabolism. (26 words)
cn: 它们缺乏储水结构，而且生长在岩石表面使它们无法利用地下水，因此它们反而发展出了改变新陈代谢的能力。

en: When they detect an extended dry period, they divert their metabolisms, producing sugars and certain stress-associated proteins and other materials in their tissues. (23 words)
cn: 当它们察觉到持续的干旱期时，它们会改变新陈代谢方向，在组织中产生糖分、某些与应激相关的蛋白质和其他物质。

en: As the plant dries, these resources take on first the properties of honey, then rubber, and finally enter a glass-like state that is 'the most stable state that the plant can maintain,' Farrant says. (34 words)
cn: 法兰特说，随着植物变干，这些物质首先呈现出蜂蜜的特性，然后是橡胶，最后进入一种玻璃状状态，这是‘植物所能维持的最稳定状态’。

en: That slows the plant's metabolism and protects its dried-out tissues. (10 words)
cn: 这减缓了植物的新陈代谢并保护了它干燥的组织。

en: The plants also change shape, shrinking to minimize the surface area through which their remaining water might evaporate. (18 words)
cn: 这些植物还会改变形状，收缩以尽量减少剩余水分可能蒸发的表面积。

en: They can recover from months and years without water, depending on the species. (13 words)
cn: 根据物种的不同，它们可以在数月甚至数年无水后恢复过来。

en: What else can do this dry-out-and-revive trick? (7 words)
cn: 还有什么能做到这种“干枯再复活”的把戏？

en: Seeds—almost all of them. (4 words)
cn: 种子——几乎所有的种子。

en: At the start of her career, Farrant studied 'recalcitrant seeds,' such as avocados, coffee and lychee. (16 words)
cn: 在职业生涯之初，法兰特研究了“顽拗性种子”，如牛油果、咖啡和荔枝的种子。

en: While tasty, such seeds are delicate—they cannot bud and grow if they dry out (as you may know if you've ever tried to grow a tree from an avocado pit). (30 words)
cn: 虽然味道鲜美，但这类种子很娇弱——如果干燥就不能发芽生长（如果你曾试图用牛油果核种树，你可能会知道这一点）。

en: In the seed world, that makes them rare, because most seeds from flowering plants are quite robust. (17 words)
cn: 在种子世界里，这使得它们很稀有，因为大多数开花植物的种子都相当强健。

en: Most seeds can wait out the dry, unwelcoming seasons until conditions are right and they sprout. (16 words)
cn: 大多数种子可以熬过干燥、不适宜的季节，直到条件适宜时才发芽。

en: Yet once they start growing, such plants seem not to retain the ability to hit the pause button on metabolism in their stems or leaves. (25 words)
cn: 然而一旦开始生长，这类植物的茎或叶似乎就不再保留暂停新陈代谢的能力。

en: After completing her Ph.D. on seeds, Farrant began investigating whether it might be possible to isolate the properties that make most seeds so resilient and transfer them to other plant tissues. (31 words)
cn: 在完成关于种子的博士学位后，法兰特开始研究是否可能分离出使大多数种子具有如此强恢复力的特性，并将其转移到其他植物组织中。

en: What Farrant and others have found over the past two decades is that there are many genes involved in resurrection plants' response to dryness. (24 words)
cn: 法兰特和其他人在过去二十年中发现，有许多基因参与了复活植物对干旱的反应。

en: Many of them are the same that regulate how seeds become dryness-tolerant while still attached to their parent plants. (19 words)
cn: 其中许多与调控种子在仍附着于母株时如何变得耐旱的基因相同。

en: Now they are trying to figure out what molecular signaling processes activate those seed-building genes in resurrection plants—and how to reproduce them in crops. (24 words)
cn: 现在他们正试图弄清是什么分子信号过程在复活植物中激活了那些构建种子的基因——以及如何在农作物中再现它们。

en: 'Most genes are regulated by a master set of genes,' Farrant says. (12 words)
cn: 法兰特说：‘大多数基因由一组主控基因调控。’

en: 'We're looking at gene promoters and what would be their master switch.' (12 words)
cn: ‘我们正在研究基因启动子以及它们的主控开关是什么。’

en: Once Farrant and her colleagues feel they have a better sense of which switches to throw, they will have to find the best way to do so in useful crops. (30 words)
cn: 一旦法兰特和她的同事们对应该拨动哪些开关有了更好的了解，他们将不得不在有用的作物中找到最佳的方法。

en: 'I'm trying three methods of breeding,' Farrant says: conventional, genetic modification and gene editing. (14 words)
cn: 法兰特说：‘我正在尝试三种育种方法：传统育种、基因改造和基因编辑。’

en: She says she is aware that plenty of people do not want to eat genetically modified crops, but she is pushing ahead with every available tool until one works. (29 words)
cn: 她说她知道很多人不想吃转基因作物，但她正在推进所有可用的工具，直到其中一种奏效。

en: Farmers and consumers alike can choose whether or not to use whichever version prevails: 'I'm giving people an option.' (19 words)
cn: 农民和消费者都可以选择是否使用最终胜出的任何一种版本：‘我是在给人们一个选择。’

en: Farrant and others in the resurrection business got together last year to discuss the best species of resurrection plant to use as a lab model. (25 words)
cn: 法兰特和其他从事复活植物研究的人去年聚在一起，讨论最适合用作实验室模型的复活植物物种。

en: Just like medical researchers use rats to test ideas for human medical treatments, botanists use plants that are relatively easy to grow in a lab or greenhouse setting to test their ideas for related species. (35 words)
cn: 就像医学研究人员用大鼠来测试人类医疗方案的想法一样，植物学家使用在实验室或温室环境中相对容易种植的植物来测试他们对相关物种的想法。

en: The Queensland rock violet is one of the best studied resurrection plants so far, with a draft genome published last year by a Chinese team. (25 words)
cn: 昆士兰岩紫罗兰是迄今为止研究得最深入的复活植物之一，去年一个中国团队公布了其基因组草图。

en: Also last year, Farrant and colleagues published a detailed molecular study of another candidate, Xerophyta viscosa, a tough-as-nail South African plant with lily-like flowers, and she says that a genome is on the way. (34 words)
cn: 同样在去年，法兰特和同事们发表了另一种候选植物——一种坚韧如钉、开百合状花朵的南非植物Xerophyta viscosa的详细分子研究，她说其基因组图谱正在研究中。

en: One or both of these models will help researchers test their ideas—so far mostly done in the lab—on test plots. (20 words)
cn: 这两种模型中的一种或两种将帮助研究人员在试验田里测试他们的想法——迄今为止这些工作大多在实验室进行。

en: Understanding the basic science first is key. (7 words)
cn: 首先理解基础科学是关键。

en: There are good reasons why crop plants do not use dryness defenses already. (13 words)
cn: 农作物尚未使用抗旱防御是有充分理由的。

en: For instance, there's a high energy cost in switching from a regular metabolism to an almost-no-water metabolism. (17 words)
cn: 例如，从常规新陈代谢切换到几乎无水新陈代谢的能量代价很高。

en: It will also be necessary to understand what sort of yield farmers might expect and to establish the plant's safety. (20 words)
cn: 还需要了解农民可能期望什么样的产量，并确认植物的安全性。

en: 'The yield is never going to be high,' Farrant says, so these plants will be targeted not at Iowa farmers trying to squeeze more cash out of high-yield fields, but subsistence farmers who need help to survive a drought like the present one in South Africa. (46 words)
cn: 法兰特说：‘产量永远不会很高，’所以这些植物的目标不是爱荷华州那些试图从高产农田中榨取更多收益的农民，而是那些需要帮助以度过像南非目前这样的干旱的自给自足的农民。

en: 'My vision is for the subsistence farmer,' Farrant says. (9 words)
cn: 法兰特说：‘我的愿景是为自给自足的农民服务的。’

en: 'I'm targeting crops that are of African value.' (8 words)
cn: ‘我的目标是那些对非洲有价值的作物。’

en: Human memory is notoriously unreliable. (5 words)
cn: 人类记忆力是出了名的不可靠。

en: Even people with the sharpest facial-recognition skills can only remember so much. (12 words)
cn: 即使是面部识别能力最强的人也只能记住这么多。

en: It's tough to quantify how good a person is at remembering. (11 words)
cn: 很难量化一个人的记忆力有多好。

en: No one really knows how many different faces someone can recall, for example, but various estimates tend to hover in the thousands—based on the number of acquaintances a person might have. (31 words)
cn: 例如，没有人真正知道一个人能回忆起多少张不同的面孔，但各种估计往往在数千张左右——基于一个人可能拥有的熟人数量。

en: Machines aren't limited this way. (5 words)
cn: 机器不受这种限制。

en: Give the right computer a massive database of faces, and it can process what it sees—then recognize a face it's told to find—with remarkable speed and precision. (27 words)
cn: 给合适的计算机一个庞大的面部数据库，它就能以惊人的速度和精度处理所看到的内容——然后识别出它被要求找到的面孔。

en: This skill is what supports the enormous promise of facial-recognition software in the 21st century. (15 words)
cn: 这种技能支撑着面部识别软件在21世纪的巨大前景。

en: It's also what makes contemporary surveillance systems so scary. (9 words)
cn: 这也使得当代监控系统如此可怕。

en: The thing is, machines still have limitations when it comes to facial recognition. (13 words)
cn: 问题是，机器在面部识别方面仍有局限性。

en: And scientists are only just beginning to understand what those constraints are. (12 words)
cn: 而科学家们才刚刚开始了解这些限制是什么。

en: To begin to figure out how computers are struggling, researchers at the University of Washington created a massive database of faces—they call it MegaFace—and tested a variety of facial-recognition algorithms as they scaled up in complexity. (36 words)
cn: 为了开始弄清计算机面临的困难，华盛顿大学的研究人员创建了一个庞大的面部数据库——他们称之为MegaFace——并在算法复杂度不断增加的情况下测试了各种面部识别算法。

en: The idea was to test the machines on a database that included up to 1 million different images of nearly 700,000 different people—and not just a large database featuring a relatively small number of different faces, more consistent with what's been used in other research. (45 words)
cn: 其想法是让机器在一个包含近70万不同人群的多达100万张不同图像的数据库上进行测试——而不仅仅是其他研究中常用的那种只包含相对少量不同面孔的大型数据库。

en: As the databases grew, machine accuracy dipped across the board. (10 words)
cn: 随着数据库的增长，机器的准确性全面下降。

en: Algorithms that were right 95% of the time when they were dealing with a 13,000-image database, for example, were accurate about 70% of the time when confronted with 1 million images. (31 words)
cn: 例如，在处理13,000张图像数据库时准确率达95%的算法，在面对100万张图像时准确率约为70%。

en: That's still pretty good, says one of the researchers, Ira Kemelmacher-Shlizerman. (11 words)
cn: 其中一位研究员艾拉·凯梅尔马赫-什利泽曼说，这仍然相当不错。

en: 'Much better than we expected,' she said. (7 words)
cn: 她说：‘比我们预想的要好得多。’

en: Machines also had difficulty adjusting for people who look a lot alike—either doppelgangers, whom the machine would have trouble identifying as two separate people, or the same person who appeared in different photos at different ages or in different lighting, whom the machine would incorrectly view as separate people. (49 words)
cn: 机器也难以处理看起来非常相似的人——要么是长相极相似的人，机器难以将它们识别为两个不同的人；要么是同一个人的不同照片，年龄不同或光线不同，机器会错误地将它们视为不同的人。

en: 'Once we scale up, algorithms must be sensitive to tiny changes in identities and at the same time invariant to lighting, pose, age,' Kemelmacher-Shlizerman said. (25 words)
cn: 凯梅尔马赫-什利泽曼说：‘一旦我们扩大规模，算法必须对身份的微小变化敏感，同时对光照、姿势、年龄保持不变。’

en: The trouble is, for many of the researchers who'd like to design systems to address these challenges, massive datasets for experimentation just don't exist—at least, not in formats that are accessible to academic researchers. (34 words)
cn: 问题是，对于许多想要设计系统来应对这些挑战的研究人员来说，用于实验的大量数据集根本不存在——至少，没有以学术研究人员可以访问的格式存在。

en: Training sets like the ones Google and Facebook have are private. (11 words)
cn: 像谷歌和Facebook拥有的那些训练集是私有的。

en: There are no public databases that contain millions of faces. (10 words)
cn: 没有包含数百万张面孔的公共数据库。

en: MegaFace's creators say it's the largest publicly available facial-recognition dataset out there. (12 words)
cn: MegaFace的创建者表示，这是目前最大的公开可用面部识别数据集。

en: 'An ultimate face recognition algorithm should perform with billions of people in a dataset,' the researchers wrote. (17 words)
cn: 研究人员写道：‘终极面部识别算法应该在包含数十亿人的数据集上进行测试。’

en: There're currently 21.5 million students in America, and many will be funding their college on borrowed money. (17 words)
cn: 美国目前有2150万名学生，其中许多人将通过借贷来支付大学费用。

en: Given that there's now over $1.3 trillion in student loans on the books, it's pretty clear that many students are far from sensible. (23 words)
cn: 考虑到目前账面上有超过1.3万亿美元的学生贷款，很明显许多学生远非明智。

en: The average student's debt upon graduation now approaches $40,000, and as college becomes ever more expensive, calls to make it 'free' are multiplying. (23 words)
cn: 现在学生毕业时的平均债务接近4万美元，随着大学变得越来越昂贵，要求“免费”的呼声越来越多。

en: Even Hillary Clinton says that when it comes to college, 'Costs won't be a barrier.' (15 words)
cn: 甚至连希拉里·克林顿也说，谈到大学，‘费用不会成为障碍。’

en: But the only way college could be free is if the faculty and staff donated their time, the buildings required no maintenance, and campuses required no utilities. (27 words)
cn: 但大学免费的唯一途径是教职员工无偿奉献时间、建筑无需维护、校园无需水电。

en: As long as it's impossible to produce something from nothing, costs are absolutely a barrier. (15 words)
cn: 只要不能无中生有，成本就绝对是一个障碍。

en: The actual question we debate is who should pay for people to go to college. (15 words)
cn: 我们实际辩论的问题是应该由谁来为人们上大学买单。

en: If taxpayers are to bear the cost of forgiving student loans, shouldn't they have a say in how their money is used? (22 words)
cn: 如果纳税人要承担免除学生贷款的费用，他们难道不应该对钱如何使用有发言权吗？

en: At least taxpayers should be able to decide what students will study on the public dime. (16 words)
cn: 至少纳税人应该能够决定学生用公共资金学习什么。

en: If we're going to force taxpayers to foot the bill for college degrees, students should only study those subjects that're of greatest benefit to taxpayers. (25 words)
cn: 如果我们要强迫纳税人为大学学位买单，学生就应该只学习那些对纳税人最有益的专业。

en: After all, students making their own choices in this respect is what caused the problem in the first place. (19 words)
cn: 毕竟，学生在这方面自己做选择正是问题的根源所在。

en: We simply don't need more poetry, gender studies, or sociology majors. (11 words)
cn: 我们根本不需要更多的诗歌、性别研究或社会学专业的学生。

en: How do we know which subjects benefit society? (8 words)
cn: 我们如何知道哪些学科对社会有益？

en: Easy. (1 words)
cn: 很简单。

en: Average starting salaries give a clear indication of what type of training society needs its new workers to have. (19 words)
cn: 平均起薪清晰地表明社会需要新员工接受什么类型的培训。

en: Certainly, there're benefits to a college major beyond the job a student can perform. (14 words)
cn: 当然，大学专业的价值不仅仅在于学生能从事的工作。

en: But if we're talking about the benefits to society, the only thing that matters is what the major enables the student to produce for society. (25 words)
cn: 但如果我们谈论的是对社会的益处，唯一重要的是该专业使学生能为社会创造什么。

en: And the value of what the student can produce is reflected in the wage employers are willing to pay the student to produce it. (24 words)
cn: 而学生所能创造的价值反映在雇主愿意支付给学生的工资上。

en: A low wage for elementary school teachers, however, doesn't mean elementary education isn't important. (14 words)
cn: 然而，小学教师的低工资并不意味着小学教育不重要。

en: It simply means there're too many elementary school teachers already. (10 words)
cn: 这仅仅意味着小学教师已经太多了。

en: Meanwhile, there're few who're willing and able to perform jobs requiring a petroleum engineering major, so the value of one more of those people is very high. (27 words)
cn: 同时，愿意并且能够从事石油工程专业相关工作的人很少，所以再增加一个这样的专业人员的价值非常高。

en: So we can have taxpayers pick up students' tuition in exchange for dictating what those students will study. (18 words)
cn: 所以我们可以让纳税人为学生支付学费，作为交换，由他们来决定这些学生学什么。

en: Or we can allow students both to choose their majors and pay for their education themselves. (16 words)
cn: 或者我们可以允许学生既选择自己的专业，又自己支付教育费用。

en: But in the end, one of two things is true: (10 words)
cn: 但最终，两种情况必居其一：

en: Either a college major is worth its cost or it isn't. (11 words)
cn: 要么一个大学专业物有所值，要么不是。

en: If yes, taxpayer financing isn't needed. (6 words)
cn: 如果是，就不需要纳税人资助。

en: If not, taxpayer financing isn't desirable. (6 words)
cn: 如果不是，纳税人资助也不可取。

en: Either way, taxpayers have no business paying for students' college education. (11 words)
cn: 无论哪种情况，纳税人都不应该为学生的大学教育买单。

en: When Elon Musk says that his new priority is using artificial intelligence to build domestic robots, we should look forward to the day in admiration. (25 words)
cn: 当埃隆·马斯克说他新的优先事项是使用人工智能来制造家用机器人时，我们应该怀着钦佩之情期待那一天的到来。

en: Mr. Musk is a guy who gets things done. (9 words)
cn: 马斯克先生是一个能把事情做成的人。

en: The founder of two tech companies, Tesla Motors and SpaceX, is bringing electric vehicles to mass market and enabling humans to live on other planets. (25 words)
cn: 作为两家科技公司——特斯拉汽车和SpaceX——的创始人，他正在将电动汽车推向大众市场，并使人类能够在其他星球上生活。

en: This sounds like so much hot air, but the near $13 billion fortune this entrepreneur has amassed comes from practical achievements rather than hypothetical ones. (25 words)
cn: 这听起来像是在说大话，但这位企业家积累的近130亿美元财富来自实际成就，而非假设。

en: A lot of clever people are terrified about artificial intelligence, fearing that robots will one day become so smart that they'll murder all of us. (25 words)
cn: 许多聪明人对人工智能感到恐惧，担心有一天机器人会变得如此聪明，以至于杀死我们所有人。

en: These fears are mostly exaggerated: as with hysteria about genetic modification, we humans are generally wise enough to manage these problems with speed and care. (25 words)
cn: 这些担忧大多被夸大了：就像对基因改造的歇斯底里一样，我们人类通常足够明智，能够迅速而谨慎地处理这些问题。

en: And just think of how wonderful it would be if you had a live-in robot. (15 words)
cn: 想想看，如果你有一个住家机器人，那该多好啊。

en: It could, eventually, be like having a babysitter and a nurse rolled into one—or, if that required emotional intelligence beyond the power of Mr. Musk's imagined machine, at least someone to chop the carrots, wash the car and mow the lawn. (41 words)
cn: 它最终可能就像一个保姆和护士合二为一——或者，如果那需要超出马斯克先生所设想的机器能力的情商，至少可以有人来切胡萝卜、洗车和修剪草坪。

en: Once purchased and trained, this would allow the casual user to save money and time, freeing up precious space in our busy lives to read a good book. (28 words)
cn: 一旦购买和训练完成，这将让普通用户节省金钱和时间，在我们忙碌的生活中腾出宝贵的空间来阅读一本好书。

en: That is why we welcome Mr. Musk's latest venture, and wish him well. (13 words)
cn: 这就是为什么我们欢迎马斯克先生的最新事业，并祝愿他一切顺利。

en: As long as robots add to the sum of human happiness, reduce suffering, and create time to read world-class journalism, we should be their fans. (25 words)
cn: 只要机器人能增加人类的幸福总量、减少痛苦，并创造时间让我们阅读世界级的新闻报道，我们就应该是它们的粉丝。

en: Especially since journalism is one job robots will never do. (10 words)
cn: 尤其是因为新闻工作是机器人永远无法从事的工作之一。

en: As a high school junior, everything in my life revolved around getting into the right college. (16 words)
cn: 作为一名高二学生，我生活中的一切都围绕着进入一所理想的大学。

en: I diligently attended my SAT, ACT, and Advanced Placement test preparation courses. (12 words)
cn: 我勤奋地参加了SAT、ACT和大学先修课程的备考班。

en: I juggled cross-country and track schedules, newspaper staff, and my church's youth group and drama team. (16 words)
cn: 我同时应付越野跑和田径训练安排、校报工作、以及教会的青年团和戏剧小组。

en: I didn't drink, party, or even do much dating. (9 words)
cn: 我不喝酒、不参加派对，甚至很少约会。

en: The right college, I thought, was one with prestige, one with a name. (13 words)
cn: 我认为，理想的大学是一所有声望、有名气的大学。

en: It didn't have to be the Ivy League, but it needed to be a 'top school.' (16 words)
cn: 它不一定是常春藤盟校，但必须是一所‘顶尖学校’。

en: Looking back now, nine years later, I can't remember exactly what it was about these universities that made them seem so much better. (23 words)
cn: 现在九年后再回头看，我记不清到底是什么让这些大学看起来好那么多。

en: Was it a curriculum that appeared more rigorous, perhaps? (9 words)
cn: 也许是看起来更严格的课程？

en: Or an alumni network that I hoped would open doors down the line? (13 words)
cn: 或者是我希望能在未来打开机会之门的校友网络？

en: Maybe. (1 words)
cn: 也许吧。

en: 'I do think there are advantages to schools with more recognition,' notes Marybeth Gasman, a professor of higher education at the University of Pennsylvania. (24 words)
cn: 宾夕法尼亚大学高等教育学教授玛丽贝丝·加斯曼指出：‘我确实认为知名度更高的学校有其优势。’

en: 'I don't necessarily think that's a reason to go to one.' (11 words)
cn: ‘我不一定认为那是去读的理由。’

en: In reflection, my firm belief in the power of the brand was naive, not to mention a bit snobby. (19 words)
cn: 回想起来，我对品牌力量的坚定信念是幼稚的，更不用说有点势利了。

en: I quickly passed over state schools and southern schools, believing their curriculums to be automatically inferior to northeastern or western counterparts. (21 words)
cn: 我很快就排除了州立大学和南方大学，认为它们的课程自然不如东北部或西部同类学校。

en: Instead, I dreamed of living in New York City and my parents obliged me with a visit to New York University's campus. (22 words)
cn: 相反，我梦想住在纽约市，父母便带我参观了纽约大学的校园。

en: During the tour, tuition fees were discussed. (7 words)
cn: 参观期间讨论了学费问题。

en: NYU is consistently ranked one of the country's most expensive schools, with room and board costs totaling upwards of $64,000 a year. (22 words)
cn: 纽约大学一直被评为全美最昂贵的学校之一，每年食宿费用总计超过64,000美元。

en: Up until then, I hadn't truly realized just how expensive an education can be. (14 words)
cn: 在那之前，我还没有真正意识到教育可以有多昂贵。

en: Over the next few months, I realized not only could I not afford my dream school, I couldn't even afford the ones where I'd been accepted. (26 words)
cn: 在接下来的几个月里，我意识到不仅我的梦想学校我上不起，就连我被录取的学校我也负担不起。

en: City University of New York (CUNY), Rutgers University, and Indiana University were out of reach as were Mississippi State and the University of Alabama, where I would have to pay out-of-state fees. (32 words)
cn: 纽约市立大学、罗格斯大学和印第安纳大学都遥不可及，密西西比州立大学和阿拉巴马大学也是如此，因为我要支付外州学费。

en: Further complicating my college search was a flourishing track career—I wanted to keep running but my times weren't quite fast enough to secure a scholarship. (25 words)
cn: 使我的大学选择更加复杂的是我蓬勃发展的田径生涯——我想继续跑步，但我的成绩还不足以获得奖学金。

en: And so, at 11 pm on the night of Georgia State University's (GSU) midnight deadline, I applied online. (18 words)
cn: 于是，在佐治亚州立大学午夜截止日期的晚上11点，我在线提交了申请。

en: Rated No. 466 overall on Forbes' Lists Top Colleges, No. 183 in Research Universities, and No. 108 in the South, I can't say it was my top choice. (28 words)
cn: 在福布斯顶尖大学榜单中总体排名第466位，研究型大学中排名第183位，南方地区排名第108位，我不能说它是我的首选。

en: Still, the track coach had offered me a walk-on spot, and I actually found the urban Atlanta campus a decent consolation prize after New York City. (26 words)
cn: 不过，田径教练给了我一个试训名额，而且我实际上发现亚特兰大市区的校园在纽约市之后算是一个不错的安慰奖。

en: While it may have been practical, it wasn't prestigious. (9 words)
cn: 虽然它可能很实际，但它并不有名望。

en: But here's the thing: I loved my 'lower-tier' university. (9 words)
cn: 但事实是：我爱我的‘低层次’大学。

en: I use the term 'low-tier' cautiously, because GSU is a well-regarded research institution that attracts high quality professors and faculty from all over the country. (25 words)
cn: 我谨慎地使用‘低层次’这个词，因为佐治亚州立大学是一所受人尊敬的研究机构，吸引了来自全国各地的高质量教授和教师。

en: We are taught to believe that only by going to the best schools and getting the best grades can we escape the rat race and build a better future. (29 words)
cn: 我们被教导相信，只有进入最好的学校、取得最好的成绩，我们才能逃离激烈的竞争，创造更美好的未来。

en: But what if lower-tier colleges and universities were the ticket to escaping the rat race? (15 words)
cn: 但如果低层次的学院和大学才是逃离激烈竞争的门票呢？

en: After all, where else can you leave school with a decent degree—but without a lifetime of debt? (17 words)
cn: 毕竟，还有哪里能让你带着一个体面的学位毕业——却没有背负一生的债务呢？

en: My school didn't come prepackaged like the more popular options, so we were left to take care of ourselves, figuring out city life and trying to complete degree programs that no one was championing for us to succeed in. (39 words)
cn: 我的学校不像更受欢迎的选择那样是预先包装好的，所以我们只能自己照顾自己，摸索城市生活，努力完成那些没有人支持我们成功的学位课程。

en: What I'm saying is, I loved my university because it taught us all to be resourceful and we could make what we wanted out of it. (26 words)
cn: 我想说的是，我爱我的大学，因为它教会了我们所有人随机应变，我们可以从中创造出我们想要的东西。

en: I was lucky enough to have my tuition covered by a lottery-funded scholarship called HOPE (Helping Outstanding Pupils Educationally). (19 words)
cn: 我很幸运，我的学费由一项名为HOPE（帮助优秀学生教育）的彩票资助奖学金支付。

en: When I started college, the HOPE scholarship was funded by the state of Georgia and offered to graduating high school seniors with a GPA of 3.0 or higher. (28 words)
cn: 当我开始上大学时，HOPE奖学金由佐治亚州资助，提供给GPA为3.0或更高的高中毕业班学生。

en: Living costs and books I paid for with money earned during high school, supplemented by a small college fund my deceased grandfather left for me and a modest savings account my parents created when I was born. (37 words)
cn: 生活费和书本费我用高中期间赚的钱支付，再加上我去世的祖父留给我的一小笔大学基金和我出生时父母为我建立的一个小额储蓄账户作为补充。

en: So what about all that name recognition? (7 words)
cn: 那么，所有这些名校声誉呢？

en: Sure, many of my colleagues and competitors have more glamorous alma maters than I do. (15 words)
cn: 当然，我的许多同事和竞争对手的母校都比我光鲜。

en: As a journalist, I have competed against NYU, Columbia, and Northeastern graduates for jobs. (14 words)
cn: 作为一名记者，我曾与纽约大学、哥伦比亚大学和东北大学的毕业生竞争工作。

en: And yet, not a single interviewer has ever asked me about my educational background. (14 words)
cn: 然而，没有一个面试官问过我的教育背景。

en: In fact, almost every interview I've ever had was due to a connection—one that I've gained through pure determination, not a school brand. (23 words)
cn: 事实上，我几乎每一次面试都是因为人脉关系——我通过纯粹的决心获得的人脉，而不是学校的品牌。

en: According to The Boston Globe, students who earned their bachelor's in 2012 have an average monthly loan payment of $312, which is one-third more than those who graduated in 2004. (30 words)
cn: 据《波士顿环球报》报道，2012年获得学士学位的学生平均每月贷款还款额为312美元，比2004年毕业生高出三分之一。

en: Ultimately, that's the thing universities don't want to admit. (9 words)
cn: 归根结底，这就是大学不愿承认的事情。

en: Private universities are money-making institutions. (5 words)
cn: 私立大学是营利机构。

en: If you can afford to buy prestige, that's your choice. (10 words)
cn: 如果你能负担得起购买声望，那是你的选择。

en: For the rest of us, however, our hearty lower-tiered universities are just fine, thank you. (15 words)
cn: 然而，对于我们其他人来说，我们心爱的低层次大学就很好，谢谢。

en: Wealthy universities talk up the benefits their name will give graduates: namely, strong alumni networks, star faculty, and a résumé boost. (21 words)
cn: 富有的大学大肆宣扬他们的名声将给毕业生带来的好处：即强大的校友网络、明星教授和简历加分。

en: But you needn't attend an Ivy League school to reap those rewards. (12 words)
cn: 但你不需要上常春藤盟校才能获得这些好处。

en: Ludacris and the former CEO of Bank of America Ken Lewis are alumni of my college, as well as VICE's first female editor-in-chief, Ellis Jones. (25 words)
cn: 卢达克里斯和美国银行前首席执行官肯·刘易斯都是我校校友，还有VICE的首位女性主编埃利斯·琼斯。

en: Successful people tend to be successful no matter where they go to school, and lower-tier schools can have alumni networks just as strong as their big name counterparts. (28 words)
cn: 无论上哪所学校，成功的人往往都会成功，低层次学校的校友网络可以和名牌学校一样强大。

en: In fact, lower-tier school alumni networks are arguably stronger, because fellow alumni recognize that you didn't necessarily have an easy path to follow. (23 words)
cn: 事实上，低层次学校的校友网络可以说更强大，因为校友们认识到你走的道路不一定容易。

en: They might be more willing to offer career help, because your less famous school denotes that, like them, you are also full of energy and perseverance. (26 words)
cn: 他们可能更愿意提供职业帮助，因为你不那么出名的学校意味着，像他们一样，你也充满了活力和毅力。

en: The Washington Post reported on a recent study by Princeton economists, in which college graduates who applied to the most selective schools in the 12th grade were compared to those who applied to slightly less selective schools. (37 words)
cn: 《华盛顿邮报》报道了普林斯顿大学经济学家最近的一项研究，该研究将申请了12年级最具选择性学校的大学生与申请了略低选择性学校的大学生进行了比较。

en: They found that students with more potential earned more as adults, and the reverse held true as well, no matter where they went to school. (25 words)
cn: 他们发现，无论上哪所学校，潜力更大的学生在成年后收入更高，反之亦然。

en: Likewise, star faculty are not always found where you'd expect. (10 words)
cn: 同样，明星教授并不总是在你期望的地方。

en: Big name schools are not necessarily the best places for professors; plus, many professors split teaching time between multiple colleges and/or universities. (22 words)
cn: 名牌大学不一定是教授们的最佳去处；此外，许多教授在多所学院或大学之间分配教学时间。

en: This means, for instance, a CUNY student could reasonably expect to receive the same quality of instruction from a prestigious professor as they would if they were enrolled in the same class at NYU. (34 words)
cn: 例如，这意味着纽约市立大学的学生可以有理由期望从一位著名教授那里获得与在纽约大学注册同一课程相同质量的教学。

en: It's possible that some hiring managers may be drawn to candidates with a particular educational résumé, but it's no guarantee. (20 words)
cn: 有可能一些招聘经理会被具有特定教育背景简历的求职者所吸引，但这并不能保证什么。

en: According to a 2012 survey described in The Atlantic, college reputation ranked lowest in relative importance of attributes in evaluating graduates for hire, beaten out by top factors like internships, employment during college, college major, volunteer experience, and extracurriculars. (39 words)
cn: 根据《大西洋月刊》报道的2012年一项调查，在评估毕业生招聘时的各项属性相对重要性中，大学声誉排名最低，被实习经历、大学期间工作经历、专业、志愿者经历和课外活动等顶级因素击败。

en: Maybe students who choose less prestigious universities are bound to succeed because they are determined to. (16 words)
cn: 也许选择知名度较低的大学的学生注定会成功，因为他们有决心。

en: I tend to think so. (5 words)
cn: 我倾向于这么认为。

en: In any case, if I could do it again, I'd still make the same choice. (15 words)
cn: 无论如何，如果我能重来一次，我仍然会做出同样的选择。

en: Today I'm debt-free, resourceful—and I understand that even the shiniest packaging can't predict what you'll find on the inside. (19 words)
cn: 今天我没有债务，足智多谋——而且我明白，即使是最光鲜的包装也无法预测你会在里面发现什么。

en: Economically speaking, are we better off than we were ten years ago? (12 words)
cn: 从经济角度看，我们比十年前过得更好吗？

en: Twenty years ago? (3 words)
cn: 二十年前呢？

en: In their thirst for evidence on this issue, commentators seized on the recent report by the Census Bureau, which found that average household income rose by 5.2% in 2015. (29 words)
cn: 在对此问题渴求证据的过程中，评论员们抓住了人口普查局最近的报告，该报告发现2015年平均家庭收入增长了5.2%。

en: Unfortunately, that conclusion puts too much weight on a useful, but flawed and incomplete, statistic. (15 words)
cn: 不幸的是，这个结论过分依赖于一个有用但有缺陷且不完整的统计数据。

en: Among the more significant problems with the Census's measure are that: 1) it excludes taxes, transfers, and compensation like employer-provided health insurance; and 2) it is based on surveys rather than data. (32 words)
cn: 人口普查局衡量标准中较显著的问题包括：1）它排除了税收、转移支付和雇主提供的健康保险等补偿；2）它基于调查而非数据。

en: Even if precisely measured, income data exclude important determinants of economic well-being, such as the hours of work needed to earn that income. (23 words)
cn: 即使被精确测量，收入数据也排除了经济福祉的重要决定因素，如赚取该收入所需的工作时间。

en: While thinking about the question, we came across a recently published article by Charles Jones and Peter Klenow, which proposes an interesting new measure of economic welfare. (27 words)
cn: 在思考这个问题时，我们偶然发现了查尔斯·琼斯和彼得·克勒诺最近发表的一篇文章，其中提出了一种有趣的经济福利新衡量标准。

en: While by no means perfect, it is considerably more comprehensive than average income, taking into account not only growth in consumption per person but also changes in working time, life expectancy, and inequality. (33 words)
cn: 虽然绝非完美，但它比平均收入要全面得多，不仅考虑了人均消费增长，还考虑了工作时间、预期寿命和不平等的变化。

en: Moreover, it can be used to assess economic performance both across countries and over time. (15 words)
cn: 此外，它可以用来评估跨国家和跨时间的经济表现。

en: The Jones-Klenow method can be illustrated by a cross-country example. (10 words)
cn: 琼斯-克勒诺方法可以通过一个跨国例子来说明。

en: Suppose we want to compare the economic welfare of citizens of the U.S. and France in 2005. (17 words)
cn: 假设我们想比较2005年美国公民和法国公民的经济福利。

en: In 2005, as the authors observe: real consumption per person in France was only 60% as high as the U.S., making it appear that Americans were economically much better off than the French on average. (35 words)
cn: 正如作者所观察到的，2005年：法国人均实际消费仅为美国的60%，这使得美国人平均而言在经济上比法国人富裕得多。

en: However, that comparison omits other relevant factors: leisure time, life expectancy, and economic inequality. (14 words)
cn: 然而，这种比较忽略了其他相关因素：休闲时间、预期寿命和经济不平等。

en: The French take longer vacations and retire earlier, so typically work fewer hours; they enjoy a higher life expectancy, presumably reflecting advantages with respect to health care, diet, lifestyle, and the like; and income and consumption are somewhat more equally distributed there than in the U.S. (46 words)
cn: 法国人假期更长、退休更早，因此工作时间通常更少；他们的预期寿命更高，可能反映了在医疗保健、饮食、生活方式等方面的优势；而且法国的收入和消费分配比美国更平等。

en: Because of these differences, comparing France's consumption with the U.S.'s overstates the gap in economic welfare. (16 words)
cn: 由于这些差异，比较法国和美国的消费高估了经济福利的差距。

en: Similar calculations can be used to compare the U.S. and other countries. (12 words)
cn: 类似的计算可用于比较美国和其他国家。

en: For example, this calculation puts economic welfare in the United Kingdom at 97% of U.S. levels, but estimates Mexican well-being at 22%. (22 words)
cn: 例如，该计算将英国的经济福利定为美国水平的97%，但估计墨西哥的福利为22%。

en: The Jones-Klenow measure can also assess an economy's performance over time. (11 words)
cn: 琼斯-克勒诺衡量标准也可以评估一个经济体随时间推移的表现。

en: According to this measure, as of the early-to-mid-2000s, the U.S. had the highest economic welfare of any large country. (19 words)
cn: 根据这一衡量标准，到21世纪初至中期，美国在所有大国中拥有最高的经济福利。

en: Since 2007, economic welfare in the U.S. has continued to improve. (11 words)
cn: 自2007年以来，美国的经济福利持续改善。

en: However, the pace of improvement has slowed markedly. (8 words)
cn: 然而，改善的步伐已显著放缓。

en: Methodologically, the lesson from the Jones-Klenow research is that economic welfare is multi-dimensional. (13 words)
cn: 从方法论上讲，琼斯-克勒诺研究的启示是经济福利是多维度的。

en: Their approach is flexible enough that in principle other important quality-of-life changes could be incorporated—for example, decreases in total emissions of pollutants and declines in crime rates. (27 words)
cn: 他们的方法足够灵活，原则上可以纳入其他重要的生活质量变化——例如，污染物排放总量的减少和犯罪率的下降。

en: If you've ever started a sentence with, 'If I were you...' or found yourself scratching your head at a colleague's agony over a decision when the answer is crystal-clear, there's a scientific reason behind it. (35 words)
cn: 如果你曾经以‘如果我是你……’开头说过话，或者发现自己在同事为一个答案显而易见的问题痛苦抉择时感到困惑，这背后是有科学原因的。

en: Our own decision-making abilities can become depleted over the course of the day causing indecision or poor choices, but choosing on behalf of someone else is an enjoyable task that doesn't suffer the same pitfalls. (35 words)
cn: 我们自己的决策能力会在一天中逐渐耗竭，导致优柔寡断或糟糕的选择，但代表他人做选择是一项愉快的任务，不会遭遇同样的陷阱。

en: The problem is 'decision fatigue,' a psychological phenomenon that takes a toll on the quality of your choices after a long day of decision making, says Evan Polman, a leading psychologist. (31 words)
cn: 主要心理学家埃文·波尔曼说，这个问题就是‘决策疲劳’，一种在长时间做决策后影响你选择质量的心理现象。

en: Physicians who have been on the job for several hours, for example, are more likely to prescribe antibiotics to patients when it's unwise to do so. (26 words)
cn: 例如，连续工作数小时的医生更可能在不宜使用抗生素时给病人开抗生素。

en: 'Presumably it's because it's simple and easy to write a prescription and consider a patient case closed rather than investigate further,' Polman says. (23 words)
cn: 波尔曼说：‘大概是因为开处方简单容易，可以把一个病例视为已处理而不必进一步调查。’

en: But decision fatigue goes away when you are making the decision for someone else. (14 words)
cn: 但当你为他人做决策时，决策疲劳就消失了。

en: When people imagine themselves as advisers and imagine their own choices as belonging to someone else, they feel less tired and rely less on decision shortcuts to make those choices. (30 words)
cn: 当人们想象自己是顾问，并想象自己的选择属于他人时，他们感觉不那么疲惫，并且在做这些选择时更少依赖决策捷径。

en: 'By taking upon the role of adviser rather than decision maker, one does not suffer the consequences of decision fatigue,' he says. (22 words)
cn: 他说：‘通过扮演顾问而非决策者的角色，人们不会承受决策疲劳的后果。’

en: 'It's as if there's something fun and liberating about making someone else's choice.' (13 words)
cn: ‘好像为别人做选择有一种有趣和解放的感觉。’

en: Getting input from others not only offers a fresh perspective and thought process; it often also includes riskier choices. (19 words)
cn: 从他人那里获取意见不仅提供了新的视角和思考过程；它还往往包含更大胆的选择。

en: While this sounds undesirable, it can be quite good, says Polman. (11 words)
cn: 波尔曼说，虽然这听起来不可取，但它可能相当好。

en: 'When people experience decision fatigue—when they are tired of making choices—they have a tendency to choose to go with the status quo,' he says. (24 words)
cn: 他说：‘当人们经历决策疲劳时——当他们厌倦了做选择时——他们倾向于选择维持现状。’

en: 'But the status quo can be problematic, since a change in the course of action can sometimes be important and lead to a positive outcome.' (25 words)
cn: ‘但现状可能是有问题的，因为改变行动方向有时可能很重要，并带来积极的结果。’

en: In order to achieve a successful outcome or reward, some level of risk is almost always essential. (17 words)
cn: 为了达到成功的结果或获得回报，某种程度的风险几乎总是必不可少的。

en: 'People who are susceptible to decision fatigue will likely choose to do nothing over something,' he says, 'That's not to say that risk is always good, but it is related to taking action whereas decision fatigue assuredly leads to inaction and the possible chagrin of a decision maker who might otherwise prefer a new course but is unfortunately hindered.' (59 words)
cn: 他说：‘容易受决策疲劳影响的人很可能选择什么都不做而不选择做点什么。’‘这并不是说冒险总是好的，但它与采取行动有关，而决策疲劳肯定会导致不作为，以及决策者可能产生的懊恼——他们本来可能更倾向于新的方向，但不幸受阻。’

en: Just because you can make good choices for others doesn't mean you'll do the same for yourself, Polman cautions. (19 words)
cn: 波尔曼警告说，仅仅因为你能为他人做出好的选择，并不意味着你会为自己做同样的事。

en: 'Research has found that women negotiate higher salaries for others than they do for themselves,' he says, adding that people slip in and out of decision roles. (27 words)
cn: 他说：‘研究发现，女性为他人谈判的薪水比为自己谈判的更高。’他补充说，人们在决策角色之间切换。

en: Just off the coast of Southern California sits Santa Cruz Island, where a magical creature called the island fox dwells. (20 words)
cn: 在南加州海岸附近，坐落着圣克鲁斯岛，那里生活着一种神奇的生物——岛屿灰狐。

en: A decade ago, this island's ecosystem was in crisis. (9 words)
cn: 十年前，这个岛屿的生态系统陷入了危机。

en: Wild pigs attracted golden eagles from the mainland, and those flying predators crashed the fox population. (16 words)
cn: 野猪吸引了来自大陆的金雕，而这些飞行的捕食者使灰狐种群数量锐减。

en: So the Nature Conservancy launched a vicious war against the pigs, complete with helicopters and sharp shooters. (17 words)
cn: 因此，大自然保护协会对野猪发起了一场猛烈的清剿行动，动用了直升机和神枪手。

en: And it worked. (3 words)
cn: 这奏效了。

en: Today, federal agencies are pulling the island fox from the Endangered Species List. (13 words)
cn: 如今，联邦机构正将岛屿灰狐从濒危物种名单中移除。

en: It's the fastest-ever recovery of a mammal, joining peers like the Louisiana black bear as glowing successes in the history of the Endangered Species Act. (25 words)
cn: 这是有史以来哺乳动物恢复速度最快的案例，与路易斯安那黑熊等物种一起，成为《濒危物种法》历史上的光辉成功典范。

en: But the recovery of Santa Cruz Island isn't just about the fox. (12 words)
cn: 但圣克鲁斯岛的恢复不仅仅是关于狐狸的。

en: The Nature Conservancy has declared war on a multitude of invasive species here, from sheep to plants to the tiny Argentine ant. (22 words)
cn: 大自然保护协会已经向这里的众多入侵物种宣战，从绵羊到植物，再到微小的阿根廷蚂蚁。

en: 'Our philosophy with the island has always been, 'OK, lapse the threats and let the island go back to what it was,'' says ecologist Christina Boser. (26 words)
cn: 生态学家克里斯蒂娜·博瑟说：‘我们对这个岛屿的理念一直是：‘好吧，消除这些威胁，让岛屿恢复到原来的状态。’

en: And it appears to be working. (6 words)
cn: 而且这似乎正在起作用。

en: Native plants are coming back, and the fox once again bounds about carefree. (13 words)
cn: 本土植物正在回归，灰狐再次无忧无虑地四处跳跃。

en: But keeping those foxes from harm will occupy Boser and her colleagues for years to come. (16 words)
cn: 但保护这些灰狐免受伤害将是博瑟和她的同事们未来多年要持续关注的工作。

en: You see, humans are still allowed on Santa Cruz Island, and they bring dogs. (14 words)
cn: 要知道，人类仍然被允许进入圣克鲁斯岛，而且他们会带狗。

en: So Boser has to vaccinate her foxes against various diseases. (10 words)
cn: 因此，博瑟必须为她的灰狐接种各种疾病的疫苗。

en: 'We're obligated to keep a pulse on the population for at least five years after the foxes are delisted,' says Boser. (21 words)
cn: 博瑟说：‘我们有义务在灰狐被除名后至少五年内持续监测其种群状况。’

en: That includes tagging the foxes and monitoring their numbers to ensure nothing goes wrong. (14 words)
cn: 这包括给灰狐做标记并监测其数量，以确保不出任何问题。

en: This is the story of the little fox that has come back, and the people who have dedicated their lives to protecting it. (23 words)
cn: 这是关于这只小狐狸回归的故事，以及那些毕生致力于保护它的人们的故事。

en: This is the story of wildlife conservation in the age of mass extinction. (13 words)
cn: 这是大规模灭绝时代野生动物保护的故事。

en: When Katlyn Burbidge's son was 6 years old, he was performing some ridiculous song and dance typical of a first-grader. (20 words)
cn: 当凯特琳·伯比奇的儿子6岁时，他正在表演一些典型的一年级学生的可笑歌舞。

en: But after she snapped a photo and started using her phone, he asked her a serious question: 'Are you going to post that online?' (24 words)
cn: 但当她拍了一张照片并开始使用手机时，他问了她一个严肃的问题：‘你要把它发到网上吗？’

en: She laughed and answered, 'Yes, I think I will.' (9 words)
cn: 她笑着回答：‘是的，我想我会的。’

en: What he said next stopped her. (6 words)
cn: 他接下来说的话让她停了下来。

en: 'Can you not?' (3 words)
cn: ‘你能不能不发？’

en: That's when it dawned on her: She had been posting photos of him online without asking his permission. (18 words)
cn: 那一刻她恍然大悟：她一直在未经他允许的情况下把他的照片发到网上。

en: 'We're big advocates of bodily autonomy and not forcing him to hug or kiss people unless he wants to, but it never occurred to me that I should ask his permission to post photos of him online,' says Burbidge, a mom of two in Wakefield, Massachusetts. (46 words)
cn: 伯比奇说：‘我们非常倡导身体自主权，不会强迫他拥抱或亲吻别人，除非他愿意，但我从未想过我应该征求他的同意才把他的照片发到网上。’她是马萨诸塞州韦克菲尔德的一位两个孩子的母亲。

en: 'Now when I post a photo of him online, I show him the photo and get his okay.' (18 words)
cn: ‘现在当我要在网上发他的照片时，我会把照片给他看，并征得他的同意。’

en: When her 8-month-old is 3 or 4 years old, she plans to start asking him in an age-appropriate way, 'Do you want other people to see this?' (27 words)
cn: 当她8个月大的孩子长到3、4岁时，她计划开始用适合他年龄的方式问他：‘你想让别人看到这个吗？’

en: That's precisely the approach that two researchers advocated before a room of pediatricians last week at the American Academy of Pediatrics meeting, when they discussed the 21st century challenge of 'sharenting,' a new term for parents' online sharing about their children. (41 words)
cn: 这正是两位研究人员上周在美国儿科学会会议上向儿科医生们倡导的方法，当时他们讨论了21世纪‘晒娃’的挑战——‘sharenting’是一个新词，指父母在网上分享关于孩子的信息。

en: 'As advocates of children's rights, we believe that children should have a voice about what information is shared about them if possible,' says Stacey Steinberg, a legal skills professor at the University of Florida Levin College of Law in Gainesville. (40 words)
cn: 盖恩斯维尔佛罗里达大学莱文法学院的法律技能教授斯泰西·斯坦伯格说：‘作为儿童权利的倡导者，我们认为，如果可能的话，孩子们应该对关于他们自己的哪些信息被分享有发言权。’

en: Whether it's ensuring that your child isn't bullied over something you post, that their identity isn't digitally 'kidnapped', or that their photos don't end up on a half dozen child pornography sites, as one Australian mom discovered, parents and pediatricians are increasingly aware of the importance of protecting children's digital presence. (51 words)
cn: 无论是确保你的孩子不会因为你发布的内容而被欺负，还是确保他们的身份不被数字‘绑架’，或者确保他们的照片不会出现在多个儿童色情网站上——正如一位澳大利亚妈妈所发现的那样——父母和儿科医生越来越意识到保护儿童数字形象的重要性。

en: Steinberg and Bahareh Keith, an assistant professor of pediatrics at the University of Florida College of Medicine, say most children will likely never experience problems related to what their parents share, but a tension still exists between parents' rights to share their experiences and their children's rights to privacy. (49 words)
cn: 斯坦伯格和佛罗里达大学医学院儿科助理教授巴赫雷·基思表示，大多数孩子可能永远不会因父母分享的内容而遇到问题，但父母分享经历的权利与孩子隐私权之间仍然存在紧张关系。

en: 'We're in no way trying to silence parents' voices,' Steinberg says. (11 words)
cn: 斯坦伯格说：‘我们绝不是在试图压制父母的声音。’

en: 'At the same time, we recognize that children might have an interest in entering adulthood free to create their own digital footprint.' (22 words)
cn: ‘同时，我们认识到孩子们可能希望在进入成年后能自由地创建自己的数字足迹。’

en: They cited a study presented earlier this year of 249 pairs of parents and their children in which twice as many children as parents wanted rules on what parents could share. (31 words)
cn: 他们引用了今年早些时候发表的一项研究，该研究调查了249对父母和子女，其中希望制定父母分享规则的孩子数量是父母的两倍。

en: 'The parents said, 'We don't need rules—we're fine,' and the children said, 'Our parents need rules,'' Keith says. (18 words)
cn: 基思说：‘父母说：‘我们不需要规则——我们很好’，而孩子们说：‘我们的父母需要规则’。’

en: 'The children wanted autonomy about this issue and were worried about their parents sharing information about them.' (17 words)
cn: ‘孩子们希望在这个问题上拥有自主权，并担心父母分享关于他们的信息。’
