en: Although the American Academy of Pediatrics offers guidelines recommending that parents model appropriate social media use for their children, it does not explicitly discuss oversharing by parents. (27 words)
cn: 虽然美国儿科学会提供了指导方针，建议父母为孩子树立适当使用社交媒体的榜样，但并没有明确讨论父母的过度分享问题。

en: 'I think this is a very legitimate concern, and I appreciate their drawing our attention to it,' David Hill, a father of five, says. (24 words)
cn: 五个孩子的父亲戴维·希尔说：‘我认为这是一个非常合理的担忧，我很感激他们引起我们对这个问题的关注。’

en: He sees a role for pediatricians to talk with parents about this, but believes the messaging must extend far beyond pediatricians' offices. (22 words)
cn: 他认为儿科医生可以与父母讨论这个问题，但他认为相关信息传播必须远不止于儿科医生的办公室。

en: 'I look forward to seeing researchers expand our understanding of the issue so we can translate it into effective education and policy,' he says. (24 words)
cn: 他说：‘我期待研究人员加深我们对这个问题的理解，以便我们将其转化为有效的教育和政策。’

en: There's been little research on the topic, Steinberg wrote in a law article about this issue. (16 words)
cn: 斯坦伯格在一篇关于这个问题的法律文章中写道，关于这个话题的研究很少。

en: While states could pass laws related to sharing information about children online, Steinberg feels parents themselves are generally best suited to make these decisions for their families. (27 words)
cn: 虽然各州可以通过与网上分享儿童信息相关的法律，但斯坦伯格认为，父母本身通常最适合为他们的家庭做出这些决定。

en: 'While we didn't want to create any unnecessary panic, we did find some concerns that were troublesome, and we thought that parents or at least physicians should be aware of those potential risks,' Steinberg says. (35 words)
cn: 斯坦伯格说：‘虽然我们不想制造任何不必要的恐慌，但我们确实发现了一些令人担忧的问题，我们认为父母或至少医生应该意识到这些潜在风险。’

en: They include photos repurposed for inappropriate or illegal means, identity theft, embarrassment, bullying by peers or digital kidnapping. (18 words)
cn: 这些风险包括照片被用于不当或非法目的、身份盗窃、尴尬、同伴欺凌或数字绑架。

en: But that's the negative side, with risks that must be balanced against the benefits of sharing. (16 words)
cn: 但那是消极的一面，这些风险必须与分享的好处相权衡。

en: Steinberg pointed out that parental sharing on social media helps build communities, connect spread-out families, provide support and raise awareness around important social issues for which parents might be their children's only voice. (33 words)
cn: 斯坦伯格指出，父母在社交媒体上的分享有助于建立社区、联系分散的家人、提供支持，并提高人们对重要社会问题的认识，而在这些问题上，父母可能是孩子唯一的代言人。

en: A C.S. Mott survey found among the 56 percent of mothers and 34 percent of fathers who discussed parenting on social media, 72 percent of them said sharing made them feel less alone, and nearly as many said sharing helped them worry less and gave them advice from other parents. (50 words)
cn: 一项C.S.莫特调查发现，在56%的母亲和34%的父亲在社交媒体上讨论育儿话题中，72%的人表示分享让他们感觉不那么孤独，差不多同样多的人表示分享有助于减少他们的担忧，并从其他父母那里获得建议。

en: The most common topics they discussed included kids' sleep, nutrition, discipline, behavior problems and day care and preschool. (18 words)
cn: 他们讨论的最常见话题包括孩子的睡眠、营养、纪律、行为问题以及日托和学前班。

en: 'There's this peer-to-peer nature of health care these days with a profound opportunity for parents to learn helpful tips, safety and prevention efforts, pro-vaccine messages and all kinds of other messages from other parents in their social communities,' says Wendy Sue Swanson, a pediatrician and executive director of digital health at Seattle Children's Hospital, where she blogs about her own parenting journey to help other parents. (66 words)
cn: 西雅图儿童医院的儿科医生兼数字健康执行主任温迪·苏·斯旺森说：‘如今，医疗保健具有这种点对点的性质，父母有很好的机会从他们社交社区中的其他父母那里学习有用的技巧、安全和预防措施、支持疫苗的信息以及各种其他信息。’她通过博客分享自己的育儿经历来帮助其他父母。

en: 'They're getting nurtured by people they've already selected that they trust,' she says. (13 words)
cn: 她说：‘他们正在接受他们已经选择并信任的人的滋养。’

en: 'How do we weigh the risks, how do we think about the benefits, and how do we alleviate the risks?' she says. (22 words)
cn: 她说：‘我们如何权衡风险？我们如何考虑收益？我们如何减轻风险？’

en: 'Those are the questions we need to ask ourselves, and everyone can have a different answer.' (16 words)
cn: ‘这些是我们需要问自己的问题，每个人都可以有不同的答案。’

en: Some parents find the best route for them is not to share at all. (14 words)
cn: 一些父母发现对他们来说最好的方式是完全不分享。

en: Bridget O'Hanlon and her husband, who live in Cleveland, decided before their daughter was born that they would not post her photos online. (23 words)
cn: 住在克利夫兰的布里奇特·奥汉伦和她的丈夫在女儿出生前就决定不把她的照片发到网上。

en: When a few family members did post pictures, O'Hanlon and her husband made their wishes clear. (16 words)
cn: 当几位家人确实发了照片时，奥汉伦和她的丈夫明确表达了他们的意愿。

en: 'It's been hard not to share pictures of her because people always want to know how babies and toddlers are doing and to see pictures, but we made the decision to have social media while she did not,' O'Hanlon said. (40 words)
cn: 奥汉伦说：‘不分享她的照片很难，因为人们总是想知道婴儿和幼儿的情况并看照片，但我们决定她本人没有社交媒体，而我们自己可以拥有社交媒体。’

en: Similarly, Alison Jamison of New York decided with her husband that their child had a right to their own online identity. (21 words)
cn: 同样，纽约的艾莉森·贾米森和她的丈夫决定他们的孩子有权拥有自己的在线身份。

en: They did use an invitation-only photo sharing platform so that friends and family, including those far away, could see the photos, but they stood firm, simply refusing to put their child's photos on other social media platforms. (37 words)
cn: 他们确实使用了一个仅限邀请的照片分享平台，以便朋友和家人（包括远方的）能看到照片，但他们立场坚定，坚决不把孩子的照片放在其他社交媒体平台上。

en: 'For most families, it's a journey. (6 words)
cn: 斯旺森说：‘对大多数家庭来说，这是一个过程。’

en: Sometimes it goes wrong, but most of the time it doesn't,' says Swanson, who recommends starting to ask children permission to post narratives or photos around ages 6 to 8. (30 words)
cn: ‘有时会出错，但大多数时候不会。’她建议在孩子6到8岁左右开始征求他们的许可再发布文字或照片。

en: 'We'll learn more and more what our tolerance is. (9 words)
cn: ‘我们会越来越了解我们的容忍度。’

en: We can ask our kids to help us learn as a society what's okay and what's not.' (17 words)
cn: ‘我们可以让我们的孩子帮助我们作为一个社会去了解什么是可以接受的，什么是不可以接受的。’

en: Indeed, that learning process goes both ways. (7 words)
cn: 确实，这种学习过程是双向的。

en: Bria Dunham, a mother in Somerville, Massachusetts, was so excited to watch a moment of brotherly bonding while her first-grader and baby took a bath together that she snapped a few photos. (32 words)
cn: 马萨诸塞州萨默维尔的一位母亲布里亚·邓纳姆非常激动地看着她的一年级儿子和婴儿一起洗澡时的兄弟情深时刻，于是她拍了几张照片。

en: But when she considered posting them online, she took the perspective of her son: How would he feel if his classmates' parents saw photos of him chest-up in the bathtub? (30 words)
cn: 但当她考虑把它们发到网上时，她站在了儿子的角度：如果他的同学家长看到他在浴缸里赤膊的照片，他会怎么想？

en: 'It made me think about how I'm teaching him to have ownership of his own body and how what is shared today endures into the future,' Dunham says. (28 words)
cn: 邓纳姆说：‘这让我思考我是如何教他拥有自己身体的所有权，以及今天分享的东西会延续到未来。’

en: 'So I kept the pictures to myself and accepted this as one more step in supporting his increasing autonomy.' (19 words)
cn: ‘所以我把照片留给自己，并把这看作是支持他日益增长的自主权的又一步。’

en: Perhaps it is time for farmers to put their feet up now that robots are used to inspect crops, dig up weeds, and even have become shepherds, too. (28 words)
cn: 也许现在农民们可以歇歇脚了，因为机器人被用来检查作物、除草，甚至当起了牧羊人。

en: Commercial growing fields are astronomically huge and take thousands of man-hours to operate. (13 words)
cn: 商业种植田面积大得惊人，需要数千个工时来经营。

en: One prime example is one of Australia's most isolated cattle stations, Suplejack Downs in the Northern Territory, extending across 4,000 square kilometers, taking over 13 hours to reach by car from the nearest major town—Alice Springs. (36 words)
cn: 一个典型的例子是澳大利亚最偏远的牧场之一——位于北领地的苏普尔杰克牧场，占地4000平方公里，从最近的主要城镇爱丽丝泉开车过去需要13个多小时。

en: The extreme isolation of these massive farms leaves them often unattended, and monitored only once or twice a year, which means if the livestock falls ill or requires assistance, it can be a long time for farmers to discover. (39 words)
cn: 这些大型农场的极度偏远使得它们经常无人看管，每年只监测一两次，这意味着如果牲畜生病或需要帮助，农民可能需要很长时间才能发现。

en: However, robots are coming to the rescue. (7 words)
cn: 然而，机器人正前来救援。

en: Robots are currently under a two-year trial in Wales which will train 'farmbots' to herd, monitor the health of livestock, and make sure there is enough pasture for them to graze on. (32 words)
cn: 目前，机器人正在威尔士进行为期两年的试验，该试验将训练‘农场机器人’放牧、监测牲畜健康状况，并确保有足够的牧场供它们放牧。

en: The robots are equipped with many sensors to identify conditions of the environment, cattle and food, using thermal and vision sensors that detect changes in body temperature. (27 words)
cn: 这些机器人配备了多种传感器，用于识别环境、牛群和食物的状况，使用热传感器和视觉传感器来检测体温变化。

en: 'You've also got color, texture and shape sensors looking down at the ground to check pasture quality,' says Salah Sukkarieh of the University of Sydney, who will carry out trials on several farms in central New South Wales. (38 words)
cn: 悉尼大学的萨拉赫·苏卡里耶说：‘你还有颜色、纹理和形状传感器向下扫描地面，以检查牧草质量。’他将在新南威尔士州中部的几个农场进行试验。

en: During the trials, the robot algorithms and mechanics will be fine-tuned to make it better suited to ailing livestock and ensure it safely navigates around potential hazards including trees, mud, swamps, and hills. (33 words)
cn: 在试验期间，机器人的算法和机械装置将被微调，以使其更好地适应生病的牲畜，并确保它能安全地绕过树木、泥地、沼泽和山丘等潜在危险。

en: 'We want to improve the quality of animal health and make it easier for farmers to maintain large landscapes where animals roam free,' says Sukkarieh. (25 words)
cn: 苏卡里耶说：‘我们希望提高动物健康质量，并让农民更容易维护动物自由活动的广阔土地。’

en: The robots are not limited to herding and monitoring livestock. (10 words)
cn: 机器人不仅限于放牧和监测牲畜。

en: They have been created to count individual fruit, inspect crops, and even pull weeds. (14 words)
cn: 它们还被设计用来清点单个水果、检查作物，甚至拔草。

en: Many robots are equipped with high-tech sensors and complex learning algorithms to avoid injuring humans as they work side by side. (21 words)
cn: 许多机器人配备了高科技传感器和复杂的学习算法，以避免在与人类并肩工作时伤害到人。

en: The robots also learn the most efficient and safest passages, and allow engineers and farmers to analyze and better optimize the attributes and tasks of the robot, as well as provide a live stream giving real-time feedback on exactly what is happening on the farms. (45 words)
cn: 机器人还能学习最高效、最安全的路径，让工程师和农民分析和优化机器人的属性和任务，并提供实时反馈，让他们准确了解农场正在发生的情况。

en: Of course, some worry lies in replacing agricultural workers. (9 words)
cn: 当然，也有人担心这会取代农业工人。

en: However, it is farmers that are pushing for the advancements due to ever-increasing labor vacancies, making it difficult to maintain large-scale operations. (22 words)
cn: 然而，正是因为劳动力空缺日益增加，使得维持大规模运营变得困难，农民们正在推动这些技术进步。

en: The robots have provided major benefits to farmers in various ways, from hunting and pulling weeds to monitoring the condition of every single fruit. (24 words)
cn: 机器人在各个方面为农民提供了巨大的好处，从除虫拔草到监测每个水果的状况。

en: Future farms will likely experience a greater deal of autonomy as robots take up more and more farm work efficiently. (20 words)
cn: 随着机器人高效地承担越来越多的农活，未来的农场可能会实现更大程度的自动化。

en: The public must be able to understand the basics of science to make informed decisions. (15 words)
cn: 公众必须能够理解科学基础知识，才能做出明智的决定。

en: Perhaps the most dramatic example of the negative consequences of poor communication between scientists and the public is the issue of climate change, where a variety of factors, not the least of which is a breakdown in the transmission of fundamental climate data to the general public, has contributed to widespread mistrust and misunderstanding of scientists and their research. (59 words)
cn: 也许科学家与公众之间沟通不畅造成负面后果的最显著例子就是气候变化问题，其中多种因素——尤其是基本气候数据向公众传播的中断——导致了人们对科学家及其研究的普遍不信任和误解。

en: The issue of climate change also illustrates how the public acceptance and understanding of science (or the lack of it) can influence governmental decision-making with regard to regulation, science policy and research funding. (33 words)
cn: 气候变化问题也说明了公众对科学的接受和理解（或缺乏理解）如何影响政府在监管、科学政策和研究经费方面的决策。

en: However, the importance of effective communication with a general audience is not limited to hot issues like climate change. (19 words)
cn: 然而，与普通受众有效沟通的重要性并不仅限于气候变化等热点问题。

en: It is also critical for socially charged neuroscience issues such as the genetic basis for a particular behavior, the therapeutic potential of stem cell therapy for neurodegenerative diseases, or the use of animal models, areas where the public understanding of science can also influence policy and funding decisions. (48 words)
cn: 这对具有社会争议的神经科学问题也至关重要，例如特定行为的遗传基础、干细胞疗法对神经退行性疾病的治疗潜力，或动物模型的使用——在这些领域中，公众对科学的理解同样可以影响政策和资金决策。

en: Furthermore, with continuing advances in individual genome sequencing and the advent of personalized medicine, more non-scientists will need to be comfortable analyzing complex scientific information to make decisions that directly affect their quality of life. (35 words)
cn: 此外，随着个体基因组测序的不断进步和个性化医疗的出现，更多的非科学家将需要能够自如地分析复杂的科学信息，以做出直接影响他们生活质量的决定。

en: Science journalism is the main channel for the popularization of scientific information among the public. (15 words)
cn: 科学新闻是向公众普及科学信息的主要渠道。

en: Much has been written about how the relationship between scientists and the media can shape the efficient transmission of scientific advances to the public. (24 words)
cn: 关于科学家与媒体之间的关系如何影响科学进步向公众的高效传播，已有大量论述。

en: Good science journalists are specialists in making complex topics accessible to a general audience, while adhering to scientific accuracy. (19 words)
cn: 优秀的科学记者是使复杂话题易于普通受众理解的同时保持科学准确性的专家。

en: Unfortunately, pieces of science journalism can also oversimplify and generalize their subject material to the point that the basic information conveyed is obscured or at worst, obviously wrong. (28 words)
cn: 不幸的是，一些科学新闻也可能过度简化和泛化其主题材料，以至于所传达的基本信息变得模糊不清，甚至在最糟糕的情况下明显错误。

en: The impact of a basic discovery on human health can be exaggerated so that the public thinks a miraculous cure is a few months to years away when in reality the significance of the study is far more limited. (39 words)
cn: 一项基础发现对人类健康的影响可能被夸大，以至于公众认为奇迹般的治疗方法再过几个月或几年就能实现，而实际上该研究的意义要有限得多。

en: Even though scientists play a part in transmitting information to journalists and ultimately the public, too often the blame for ineffective communication is placed on the side of the journalists. (30 words)
cn: 尽管科学家在向记者以及最终向公众传递信息方面发挥着作用，但沟通无效的责任往往被归咎于记者。

en: We believe that at least part of the problem lies in places other than the interaction between scientists and members of the media, and exists because for one thing we underestimate how difficult it is for scientists to communicate effectively with a diversity of audiences, and for another most scientists do not receive formal training in science communication. (58 words)
cn: 我们认为，至少部分问题存在于科学家与媒体成员互动之外的地方，其存在的原因一方面是，我们低估了科学家与不同受众有效沟通的难度；另一方面，大多数科学家没有接受过科学传播方面的正式培训。

en: Surfing the Internet during class doesn't just steal focus from the educator; it also hurts students who're already struggling to grasp the material. (23 words)
cn: 在课堂上上网不仅会分散学生对教师的注意力；还会伤害那些已经在努力掌握课程内容的学生。

en: A new study from Michigan State University, though, argues that all students—including high achievers—see a decline in performance when they browse the Internet during class for non-academic purposes. (28 words)
cn: 然而，密歇根州立大学的一项新研究认为，所有学生——包括成绩优异者——在课堂上出于非学术目的浏览互联网时，成绩都会下降。

en: To measure the effects of Internet-based distractions during class, researchers enrolled 500 students taking an introductory psychology class at Michigan State University. (22 words)
cn: 为了衡量课堂上基于互联网的干扰的影响，研究人员招募了密歇根州立大学500名选修心理学入门课程的学生。

en: Researchers used ACT scores as a measure of intellectual aptitude. (10 words)
cn: 研究人员使用ACT分数作为智力能力的衡量标准。

en: Because previous research has shown that people with high intellectual abilities are better at filtering out distractions, researchers believed students with high ACT scores would not show a significant decrease in performance due to their use of digital devices. (39 words)
cn: 由于先前的研究表明，智力能力高的人更擅长过滤干扰，研究人员认为ACT分数高的学生不会因为使用数字设备而表现出成绩显著下降。

en: But students who surfed the web during class did worse on their exams regardless of their ACT scores, suggesting that even the academically smartest students are harmed when they're distracted in class. (32 words)
cn: 但那些在课堂上上网的学生，无论ACT分数如何，考试成绩都更差，这表明即使是学业上最聪明的学生，在课堂上分心也会受到损害。

en: College professors are increasingly sounding alarm bells about the effects smartphones, laptops, and tablets have on academic performance. (18 words)
cn: 大学教授们越来越多地就智能手机、笔记本电脑和平板电脑对学业成绩的影响敲响警钟。

en: One 2013 study of college students found that 80% of students use their phones or laptops during class, with the average student checking their digital device 11 times in a typical class. (32 words)
cn: 2013年一项针对大学生的研究发现，80%的学生在课堂上使用手机或笔记本电脑，普通学生在一次典型课上查看数字设备11次。

en: A quarter of students report that their use of digital devices during class causes their grades to suffer. (18 words)
cn: 四分之一的学生报告说，他们在课堂上使用数字设备导致成绩下降。

en: Professors sometimes implement policies designed to curb students' use of digital devices, and some instructors even confiscate tablets and phones. (20 words)
cn: 教授们有时会实施旨在限制学生使用数字设备的政策，有些教师甚至会没收平板电脑和手机。

en: In a world where people are increasingly dependent on their phones, though, such strategies often fail. (16 words)
cn: 然而，在一个人们越来越依赖手机的世界里，这种策略往往失败。

en: One international study found that 84% of people say they couldn't go a day without their smartphones. (17 words)
cn: 一项国际研究发现，84%的人表示他们一天都离不开智能手机。

en: Until students are able to resist the pull of social networking, texting, and endlessly surfing the web, they may continue to struggle in their classes. (25 words)
cn: 除非学生能够抵制社交网络、短信和无休止上网的诱惑，否则他们可能会继续在课堂上苦苦挣扎。

en: Maria Sibylla Merian, like many European women of the 17th century, stayed busy managing a household and rearing children. (19 words)
cn: 玛丽亚·西比拉·梅里安像许多17世纪的欧洲女性一样，忙于管理家务和抚养孩子。

en: But on top of that, Merian, a German-born woman who lived in the Netherlands, also managed a successful career as an artist, botanist, naturalist and entomologist. (26 words)
cn: 但除此之外，梅里安——一位出生于德国、生活在荷兰的女性——还成功地从事着艺术家、植物学家、博物学家和昆虫学家的职业。

en: 'She was a scientist on the level with a lot of people we spend a lot of time talking about,' said Kay Etheridge, a biologist at Gettysburg College in Pennsylvania who has been studying the scientific history of Merian's work. (40 words)
cn: 宾夕法尼亚州葛底斯堡学院的生物学家凯·埃瑟里奇一直在研究梅里安工作的科学史，她说：‘她是一位与我们花费大量时间谈论的许多人处于同一水平的科学家。’

en: 'She didn't do as much to change biology as Charles Darwin, but she was significant.' (15 words)
cn: ‘她没有像查尔斯·达尔文那样对生物学做出那么多改变，但她很重要。’

en: At a time when natural history was a valuable tool for discovery, Merian discovered facts about plants and insects that were not previously known. (24 words)
cn: 在自然史是发现的有价值工具的时代，梅里安发现了关于植物和昆虫的此前不为人知的事实。

en: Her observations helped dismiss the popular belief that insects spontaneously emerged from mud. (13 words)
cn: 她的观察帮助驳斥了昆虫从泥浆中自然产生的普遍观点。

en: The knowledge she collected over decades didn't just satisfy those curious about nature, but also provided valuable insights into medicine and science. (22 words)
cn: 她几十年来收集的知识不仅满足了那些对自然好奇的人，还为医学和科学提供了宝贵的见解。

en: She was the first to bring together insects and their habitats, including food they ate, into a single ecological composition. (20 words)
cn: 她是第一个将昆虫及其栖息地（包括它们吃的食物）整合到一个生态组合中的人。

en: After years of pleasing a fascinated audience across Europe with books of detailed descriptions and life-size paintings of familiar insects, in 1699 she sailed with her daughter nearly 5,000 miles from the Netherlands to South America to study insects in the jungles of what is now known as Suriname. (49 words)
cn: 在多年来用详细描述和实物大小绘画的书籍取悦了整个欧洲着迷的观众之后，1699年，她带着女儿从荷兰航行近5000英里到南美洲，研究现在被称为苏里南的丛林中的昆虫。

en: She was 52 years old. (5 words)
cn: 她当时52岁。

en: The result was her masterpiece, Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium. (8 words)
cn: 其成果就是她的杰作《苏里南昆虫变态》。

en: In her work, she revealed a side of nature so exotic, dramatic and valuable to Europeans of the time that she received much acclaim. (24 words)
cn: 在她的作品中，她展现了大自然如此奇异、戏剧性且对当时的欧洲人如此有价值的一面，以至于她获得了许多赞誉。

en: But a century later, her findings came under scientific criticism. (10 words)
cn: 但一个世纪后，她的发现受到了科学批评。

en: Shoddy reproductions of her work along with setbacks to women's roles in 18th- and 19th-century Europe resulted in her efforts being largely forgotten. (23 words)
cn: 她作品的粗糙复制品以及18和19世纪欧洲女性地位的倒退导致她的努力在很大程度上被遗忘。

en: 'It was kind of stunning when she sort of dropped off into oblivion,' said Dr. Etheridge. (16 words)
cn: 埃瑟里奇博士说：‘当她逐渐被遗忘时，这有点令人震惊。’

en: 'Victorians started putting women in a box, and they're still trying to crawl out of it.' (16 words)
cn: ‘维多利亚时代的人开始把女性关进盒子里，而她们至今仍在努力爬出来。’

en: Today, the pioneering woman of the sciences has re-emerged. (9 words)
cn: 如今，这位科学界的先驱女性重新出现了。

en: In recent years, feminists, historians and artists have all praised Merian's tenacity, talent and inspirational artistic compositions. (17 words)
cn: 近年来，女权主义者、历史学家和艺术家都称赞了梅里安的坚韧、才华和鼓舞人心的艺术作品。

en: And now biologists like Dr. Etheridge are digging into the scientific texts that accompanied her art. (16 words)
cn: 现在，像埃瑟里奇博士这样的生物学家正在深入研究伴随她艺术的科学文本。

en: Three hundred years after her death, Merian will be celebrated at an international symposium in Amsterdam this June. (18 words)
cn: 在她去世三百年后，梅里安将于今年6月在阿姆斯特丹的一个国际研讨会上受到纪念。

en: And last month, Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium was republished. (8 words)
cn: 上个月，《苏里南昆虫变态》再版了。

en: It contains 60 plates and original descriptions, along with stories about Merian's life and updated scientific descriptions. (17 words)
cn: 它包含60幅插图和原始描述，以及关于梅里安生平的故事和更新的科学描述。

en: Before writing Metamorphosis, Merian spent decades documenting European plants and insects that she published in a series of books. (19 words)
cn: 在写《变态》之前，梅里安花了几十年时间记录欧洲植物和昆虫，并以一系列书籍出版。

en: She began in her 20s, making textless, decorative paintings of flowers with insects. (13 words)
cn: 她从20多岁开始，创作了没有文字的花卉与昆虫装饰画。

en: 'Then she got really serious,' Dr. Etheridge said. (8 words)
cn: 埃瑟里奇博士说：‘然后她变得非常认真。’

en: Merian started raising insects at home, mostly butterflies and caterpillars. (10 words)
cn: 梅里安开始在家里饲养昆虫，主要是蝴蝶和毛虫。

en: 'She would sit up all night until they came out of the pupa so she could draw them,' she said. (20 words)
cn: 她说：‘她会整夜不睡，直到它们破蛹而出，这样她就可以画它们了。’

en: The results of her decades' worth of careful observations were detailed paintings and descriptions of European insects, followed by unconventional visuals and stories of insects and animals from a land that most at the time could only imagine. (38 words)
cn: 她数十年细致观察的成果是详细的欧洲昆虫绘画和描述，以及来自当时大多数人只能想象的土地上的非传统视觉图像和昆虫与动物的故事。

en: It's possible Merian used a magnifying glass to capture the detail of the split tongues of sphinx moths depicted in the painting. (22 words)
cn: 梅里安可能使用了放大镜来捕捉画中所描绘的斯芬克斯飞蛾分叉舌头的细节。

en: She wrote that the two tongues combine to form one tube for drinking nectar. (14 words)
cn: 她写道，两个舌头合并成一个管子用于吸食花蜜。

en: Some criticized this detail later, saying there was just one tongue, but Merian wasn't wrong. (15 words)
cn: 后来有些人批评这个细节，说只有一个舌头，但梅里安并没有错。

en: She may have observed the adult moth just as it emerged from its pupa. (14 words)
cn: 她可能是在成虫蛾刚破蛹时就观察到了它。

en: For a brief moment during that stage of its life cycle, the tongue consists of two tiny half-tubes before merging into one. (22 words)
cn: 在其生命周期的那一阶段的短暂时刻，舌头由两个微小的半管组成，然后合并成一个。

en: It may not have been ladylike to depict a giant spider devouring a hummingbird, but when Merian did it at the turn of the 18th century, surprisingly, nobody objected. (29 words)
cn: 描绘一只巨大的蜘蛛吞噬蜂鸟可能不符合淑女风范，但当梅里安在18世纪之交这样做时，令人惊讶的是，没有人反对。

en: Dr. Etheridge called it revolutionary. (5 words)
cn: 埃瑟里奇博士称之为革命性的。

en: The image, which also contained novel descriptions of ants, fascinated a European audience that was more concerned with the exotic story unfolding before them than the gender of the person who painted it. (33 words)
cn: 这幅画还包含了对蚂蚁的新颖描述，吸引了欧洲观众，他们更关注展现在他们面前的异国故事，而不是画家的性别。

en: 'All of these things shook up their nice, neat little view,' Dr. Etheridge said. (14 words)
cn: 埃瑟里奇博士说：‘所有这些都动摇了他们美好、整洁的小观点。’

en: But later, people of the Victorian era thought differently. (9 words)
cn: 但后来，维多利亚时代的人想法不同。

en: Her work had been reproduced, sometimes incorrectly. (7 words)
cn: 她的作品被复制，有时是不正确的。

en: A few observations were deemed impossible. (6 words)
cn: 一些观察被认为是不可能的。

en: 'She'd been called a silly woman for saying that a spider could eat a bird,' Dr. Etheridge said. (18 words)
cn: 埃瑟里奇博士说：‘她因为说蜘蛛能吃鸟而被叫作傻女人。’

en: But Henry Walter Bates, a friend of Charles Darwin, observed it and put it in a book in 1863, proving Merian was correct. (23 words)
cn: 但查尔斯·达尔文的朋友亨利·沃尔特·贝茨观察到了这一点，并于1863年将其写进书中，证明了梅里安是正确的。

en: In the same plate, Merian depicted and described leaf-cutter ants for the first time. (14 words)
cn: 在同一幅画中，梅里安首次描绘和描述了切叶蚁。

en: 'In America there are large ants which can eat whole trees bare as a broom handle in a single night,' she wrote in the description. (25 words)
cn: 她在描述中写道：‘在美洲，有一种大蚂蚁能在一夜之间把整棵树吃得光秃秃的，像扫帚柄一样。’

en: Merian noted how the ants took the leaves below ground to their young. (13 words)
cn: 梅里安注意到蚂蚁如何把叶子带到地下的幼虫那里。

en: And she wouldn't have known this at the time, but the ants use the leaves to farm fungi underground to feed their developing babies. (24 words)
cn: 她当时不会知道这一点，但蚂蚁用这些叶子在地下培育真菌来喂养它们的幼虫。

en: Merian was correct about the giant bird-eating spiders, ants building bridges with their bodies and other details. (17 words)
cn: 梅里安关于巨型食鸟蜘蛛、蚂蚁用身体搭桥以及其他细节是正确的。

en: But in the same drawing, she incorrectly lumped together army and leaf-cutter ants. (13 words)
cn: 但在同一幅画中，她错误地将行军蚁和切叶蚁混为一谈。

en: And instead of showing just the typical pair of eggs in a hummingbird nest, she painted four. (17 words)
cn: 她没有画出蜂鸟巢中典型的一对蛋，而是画了四个。

en: She made other mistakes in Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium as well: not every caterpillar and butterfly matched. (16 words)
cn: 她在《苏里南昆虫变态》中也犯了其他错误：不是每只毛虫和蝴蝶都匹配。

en: Perhaps one explanation for her mistakes is that she cut short her Suriname trip after getting sick, and completed the book at home in Amsterdam. (25 words)
cn: 也许对她错误的一个解释是，她在生病后缩短了苏里南之行，并在阿姆斯特丹的家中完成了这本书。

en: And errors are common among some of history's most-celebrated scientific minds, too. (12 words)
cn: 错误在一些历史上最著名的科学头脑中也很常见。

en: 'These errors no more invalidate Ms. Merian's work than do well-known misconceptions published by Charles Darwin or Isaac Newton,' Dr. Etheridge wrote in a paper that argued that too many have wrongly focused on the mistakes of her work. (39 words)
cn: 埃瑟里奇博士在一篇论文中写道：‘这些错误并不比查尔斯·达尔文或艾萨克·牛顿发表的著名错误观念更能使梅里安女士的工作无效。’该论文认为太多人错误地关注了她工作中的错误。

en: Merian's paintings inspired artists and ecologists. (6 words)
cn: 梅里安的画作启发了艺术家和生态学家。

en: In an 1801 drawing from his book, General Zoology Amphibia, George Shaw, an English botanist and zoologist, credited Merian for describing a frog in the account of her South American expedition, and named the young tree frog after her in his portrayal of it. (44 words)
cn: 在1801年他的《普通动物学·两栖类》一书中，英国植物学家和动物学家乔治·肖在描述她南美探险的记述中称赞梅里安描述了一种青蛙，并在他的描绘中以她的名字命名了这种幼年树蛙。

en: It wouldn't be fair to give Merian all the credit. (10 words)
cn: 把所有的功劳都归于梅里安是不公平的。

en: She received assistance naming plants, making sketches and referencing the work of others. (13 words)
cn: 她在命名植物、制作草图和引用他人作品方面得到了帮助。

en: Her daughters helped her color her drawings. (7 words)
cn: 她的女儿们帮她给画作上色。

en: Merian also made note of the help she received from the natives of Suriname, as well as slaves or servants that assisted her. (23 words)
cn: 梅里安也记录了她从苏里南土著以及帮助她的奴隶或仆人那里得到的帮助。

en: In some instances she wrote moving passages that included her helpers in descriptions. (13 words)
cn: 在一些情况下，她写了感人的段落，在描述中包括了她的助手。

en: As she wrote in her description of the peacock flower, 'The Indians, who are not treated well by their Dutch masters, use the seeds to abort their children, so that they will not become slaves like themselves. (37 words)
cn: 正如她在描述孔雀花时所写的：‘那些不被荷兰主人善待的印第安人用种子来堕胎，这样他们的孩子就不会成为像他们一样的奴隶。’

en: The black slaves from Guinea and Angola have demanded to be well treated, threatening to refuse to have children. (19 words)
cn: ‘来自几内亚和安哥拉的黑奴要求得到善待，威胁拒绝生育。’

en: In fact, they sometimes take their own lives because they are treated so badly, and because they believe they will be born again, free and living in their own land. (30 words)
cn: ‘事实上，他们有时会自杀，因为他们受到的待遇太差，而且因为他们相信他们会重生，自由地生活在自己土地上。’

en: They told me this themselves.' (5 words)
cn: ‘这是他们亲口告诉我的。’

en: Londa Schiebinger, a professor of the history of science at Stanford University, called this passage rather astonishing. (17 words)
cn: 斯坦福大学科学史教授隆达·席宾格称这段文字相当惊人。

en: It's particularly striking centuries later when these issues are still prominent in public discussions about social justice and women's rights. (20 words)
cn: 几个世纪后，当这些问题在关于社会正义和妇女权利的公共讨论中仍然突出时，这一点尤其引人注目。

en: 'She was ahead of her time,' Dr. Etheridge said. (9 words)
cn: 埃瑟里奇博士说：‘她走在了她的时代前面。’

en: While human achievements in mathematics continue to reach new levels of complexity, many of us who aren't mathematicians at heart (or engineers by trade) may struggle to remember the last time we used calculus. (34 words)
cn: 虽然人类在数学方面的成就不断达到新的复杂水平，但我们这些内心不是数学家（或职业不是工程师）的人可能很难记住上次使用微积分是什么时候。

en: It's a fact not lost on American educators, who amid rising math failure rates are debating how math can better meet the real-life needs of students. (26 words)
cn: 这一事实并未被美国教育者忽视，他们在数学不及格率不断上升的情况下正在讨论数学如何更好地满足学生的现实生活需求。

en: Should we change the way math is taught in schools, or eliminate some courses entirely? (15 words)
cn: 我们应该改变学校数学的教学方式，还是完全取消一些课程？

en: Andrew Hacker, Queens College political science professor, thinks that advanced algebra and other higher-level math should be cut from curricula in favor of courses with more routine usefulness, like statistics. (30 words)
cn: 皇后学院政治学教授安德鲁·哈克认为，高级代数和其他高等数学应该从课程中删除，转而开设像统计学这样更实用的课程。

en: 'We hear on all sides that we're not teaching enough mathematics, and the Chinese are running rings around us,' Hacker says. (21 words)
cn: 哈克说：‘我们听到各方都在说我们没有教足够的数学，而中国人在远远超过我们。’

en: 'I'm suggesting we're teaching too much mathematics to too many people...not everybody has to know calculus. (16 words)
cn: ‘我建议我们教太多人太多的数学了……不是每个人都必须懂微积分。’

en: If you're going to become an aeronautical engineer, fine. (9 words)
cn: ‘如果你要成为一名航空工程师，那没问题。’

en: But most of us aren't.' (5 words)
cn: ‘但我们大多数人不是。’

en: Instead, Hacker is pushing for more courses like the one he teaches at Queens College: Numeracy 101. (17 words)
cn: 相反，哈克正在推动更多像他在皇后学院教授的那样的课程：计算能力101。

en: There, his students of 'citizen statistics' learn to analyze public information like the federal budget and corporate reports. (18 words)
cn: 在那里，他的‘公民统计’学生学习分析联邦预算和公司报告等公共信息。

en: Such courses, Hacker argues, are a remedy for the numerical illiteracy of adults who have completed high-level math like algebra but are unable to calculate the price of, say, a carpet by area. (33 words)
cn: 哈克认为，这样的课程是对那些已完成代数等高等数学但无法按面积计算地毯价格等成人数值文盲的补救措施。

en: Hacker's argument has met with opposition from other math educators who say what's needed is to help students develop a better relationship with math earlier, rather than teaching them less math altogether. (32 words)
cn: 哈克的论点遭到了其他数学教育工作者的反对，他们认为需要的是帮助学生更早地与数学建立更好的关系，而不是完全减少数学教学。

en: Maria Droujkova is a founder of Natural Math, and has taught basic calculus concepts to 5-year-olds. (16 words)
cn: 玛丽亚·德鲁日科娃是Natural Math的创始人，曾教过5岁孩子基本的微积分概念。

en: For Droujkova, high-level math is important, and what it could use in American classrooms is an injection of childlike wonder. (20 words)
cn: 对德鲁日科娃来说，高等数学是重要的，而美国课堂可以利用的是注入孩子般的好奇心。

en: 'Make mathematics more available,' Droujkova says. (6 words)
cn: 德鲁日科娃说：‘让数学更容易接触。’

en: 'Redesign it so it's more accessible to more kinds of people: young children, adults who worry about it, adults who may have had bad experiences.' (25 words)
cn: ‘重新设计它，让更多类型的人更容易接触它：幼儿、担心它的人、可能有不好经历的人。’

en: Pamela Harris, a lecturer at the University of Texas at Austin, has a similar perspective. (15 words)
cn: 德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校讲师帕梅拉·哈里斯有类似的观点。

en: Harris says that American education is suffering from an epidemic of 'fake math'—an emphasis on rote memorization of formulas and steps, rather than an understanding of how math can influence the ways we see the world. (36 words)
cn: 哈里斯说，美国教育正遭受‘虚假数学’的困扰——强调对公式和步骤的死记硬背，而不是理解数学如何影响我们看待世界的方式。

en: Andrew Hacker, for the record, remains skeptical. (7 words)
cn: 安德鲁·哈克，郑重声明，仍然持怀疑态度。

en: 'I'm going to leave it to those who are in mathematics to work out the ways to make their subject interesting and exciting so students want to take it,' Hacker says. (31 words)
cn: 哈克说：‘我打算让那些从事数学工作的人去想办法让他们的学科变得有趣和令人兴奋，让学生们愿意学习它。’

en: 'All that I ask is that alternatives be offered instead of putting all of us on the road to calculus.' (20 words)
cn: ‘我只要求提供替代方案，而不是让我们所有人都走上微积分之路。’

en: For years, the U.S. has experienced a shortage of registered nurses. (11 words)
cn: 多年来，美国一直面临注册护士短缺的问题。

en: The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects that while the number of nurses will increase by 19 percent by 2022, demand will grow faster than supply, and that there will be over one million unfilled nursing jobs by then. (38 words)
cn: 劳工统计局预测，虽然护士数量到2022年将增长19%，但需求增长速度将超过供应，届时将有超过一百万个护理职位空缺。

en: So what's the solution? (4 words)
cn: 那么解决方案是什么呢？

en: Robots. (1 words)
cn: 机器人。

en: Japan is ahead of the curve when it comes to this trend. (12 words)
cn: 在这一趋势方面，日本走在了前列。

en: Toyohashi University of Technology has developed Terapio, a robotic medical cart that can make hospital rounds, deliver medications and other items, and retrieve records. (24 words)
cn: 丰桥技术大学开发了Terapio，一种机器人医疗车，可以进行医院巡诊、运送药物和其他物品以及检索记录。

en: It follows a specific individual, such as a doctor or nurse, who can use it to record and access patient data. (21 words)
cn: 它跟随特定的人，如医生或护士，后者可以使用它来记录和访问患者数据。

en: This type of robot will likely be one of the first to be implemented in hospitals because it has fairly minimal patient contact. (23 words)
cn: 这种类型的机器人很可能是最早在医院投入使用的机器人之一，因为它与患者的接触相当少。

en: Robots capable of social engagement help with loneliness as well as cognitive functioning, but the robot itself doesn't have to engage directly—it can serve as an intermediary for human communication. (30 words)
cn: 能够进行社交互动的机器人有助于缓解孤独感和改善认知功能，但机器人本身不必直接参与——它可以作为人类交流的中介。

en: Telepresence robots such as MantaroBot, Vgo, and Giraff can be controlled through a computer, smartphone, or tablet, allowing family members or doctors to remotely monitor patients or Skype them, often via a screen where the robot's 'face' would be. (39 words)
cn: 像MantaroBot、Vgo和Giraff这样的远程临场机器人可以通过电脑、智能手机或平板电脑控制，让家人或医生远程监控患者或与他们进行Skype通话，通常通过机器人‘脸部’位置的屏幕进行。

en: If you can't get to the nursing home to visit grandma, you can use a telepresence robot to hang out with her. (22 words)
cn: 如果你不能去养老院看望奶奶，你可以使用远程临场机器人与她待在一起。

en: A 2016 study found that users had a 'consistently positive attitude' about the Giraff robot's ability to enhance communication and decrease feelings of loneliness. (24 words)
cn: 2016年的一项研究发现，用户对Giraff机器人增强沟通和减少孤独感的能力持‘持续积极态度’。

en: A robot's appearance affects its ability to successfully interact with humans, which is why the RIKEN-TRI Collaboration Center for Human-Interactive Robot Research decided to develop a robotic nurse that looks like a huge teddy bear. (35 words)
cn: 机器人的外观影响其成功与人类互动的能力，这就是为什么RIKEN-TRI人机交互机器人研究中心决定开发一种看起来像大泰迪熊的机器人护士。

en: RIBA (Robot for Interactive Body Assistance), also known as 'Robear,' can help patients into and out of wheelchairs and beds with its strong arms. (24 words)
cn: RIBA（互动身体辅助机器人），也被称为‘Robear’，可以用它强壮的臂膀帮助患者进出轮椅和床。

en: On the less cute and more scary side there is Actroid F, which is so human-like that some patients may not know the difference. (24 words)
cn: 在不太可爱而更可怕的一面，有Actroid F，它如此像人类，以至于一些患者可能分辨不出区别。

en: This conversational robot companion has cameras in its eyes, which allow it to track patients and use appropriate facial expressions and body language in its interactions. (26 words)
cn: 这个会说话的机器人伴侣眼睛里有摄像头，使其能够追踪患者，并在互动中使用适当的面部表情和肢体语言。

en: During a month-long hospital trial, researchers asked 70 patients how they felt being around the robot and 'only three or four said they didn't like having it around.' (28 words)
cn: 在为期一个月的医院试验中，研究人员询问了70名患者他们在机器人周围的感觉，‘只有三四人表示不喜欢它在身边’。

en: It's important to note that robotic nurses don't decide courses of treatment or make diagnoses (though robot doctors and surgeons may not be far off). (25 words)
cn: 重要的是要注意，机器人护士不会决定治疗方案或做出诊断（尽管机器人医生和外科医生可能不远了）。

en: Instead, they perform routine and laborious tasks, freeing nurses up to attend to patients with immediate needs. (17 words)
cn: 相反，它们执行日常和繁重的任务，把护士解放出来照顾有紧急需求的患者。

en: This is one industry where it seems the integration of robots will lead to collaboration, not replacement. (17 words)
cn: 这是一个似乎机器人的整合将导致协作而非取代的行业。

en: In what's probably the craziest headline I've ever written, I've reported that advances in livestock protection are happening with scientists painting eyes on the butts of cows. (27 words)
cn: 在我可能写过的最疯狂的头条新闻中，我报道了科学家在牛屁股上画眼睛这一牲畜保护方面的进展。

en: The experiment is based upon the idea that farmers who're protecting their herd from lions would shoot and kill lions in an effort to protect their livestock. (27 words)
cn: 该实验基于这样一种想法：为了保护牛群免受狮子侵害的农民会射杀狮子以保护他们的牲畜。

en: While this makes a lot of sense, it results in many lion deaths that otherwise would have been unnecessary. (19 words)
cn: 虽然这很有道理，但它导致了许多原本不必要的狮子死亡。

en: Researchers in Australia have been developing and testing a method of trickery to make lions think they are being watched by the painted eyes on cow butts. (27 words)
cn: 澳大利亚的研究人员一直在开发和测试一种欺骗方法，让狮子以为它们正被牛屁股上画的眼睛监视着。

en: This idea is based on the principle that lions and other predators are far less likely to attack when they feel they are being watched. (25 words)
cn: 这一想法基于这样一个原理：狮子和其他捕食者在感觉被监视时攻击的可能性大大降低。

en: As conservation areas become smaller, lions are increasingly coming into contact with human populations, which are expanding to the boundaries of these protected areas. (24 words)
cn: 随着保护区变得越来越小，狮子越来越多地与人类接触，而人类正在向这些保护区的边界扩张。

en: Efforts like painting eyes on cow butts may seem crazy at first, but they could make actual headway in the fight for conservation. (23 words)
cn: 在牛屁股上画眼睛这样的努力起初可能看起来很疯狂，但它们可能会在保护斗争中取得实际进展。

en: If the method works, it could provide farmers in Botswana—and elsewhere—with a low-cost, sustainable tool to protect their livestock, and a way to keep lions safe from being killed. (29 words)
cn: 如果这种方法有效，它可以为博茨瓦纳和其他地方的农民提供一种低成本、可持续的工具来保护他们的牲畜，并让狮子免于被杀害。

en: Lions are ambush hunters, so when they feel their prey has spotted them, they usually give up on the hunt. (20 words)
cn: 狮子是伏击型捕食者，所以当它们感觉猎物发现了它们时，通常会放弃捕猎。

en: Researchers are currently testing their idea on a select herd of cattle. (12 words)
cn: 研究人员目前正在一组精选的牛群上测试他们的想法。

en: They have painted half of the cows with eyes and left the other half as normal. (16 words)
cn: 他们在半数牛身上画了眼睛，另一半保持原样。

en: Through satellite tracking of both the herd and the lions in the area, they will be able to determine if their psychological trickery will work to help keep farmers from shooting lions. (32 words)
cn: 通过对牛群和该地区狮子的卫星跟踪，他们将能够确定他们的心理诡计是否有效，以帮助阻止农民射杀狮子。

en: As constant travelers and parents of a 2-year-old, we sometimes fantasize about how much work we can do when one of us gets on a plane, undistracted by phones, friends, or movies. (32 words)
cn: 作为经常旅行的人和两岁孩子的父母，我们有时会幻想当其中一人登上飞机，不受手机、朋友或电影的干扰时，我们能完成多少工作。

en: We race to get all our ground work done: packing, going through security, doing a last-minute work call, calling each other, then boarding the plane. (25 words)
cn: 我们匆忙完成所有地面工作：打包、过安检、打最后一通工作电话、互相通话，然后登机。

en: Then, when we try to have that amazing work session in flight, we get nothing done. (16 words)
cn: 然后，当我们试图在飞行中进行高效的工作时，却一事无成。

en: Even worse, after refreshing our email or reading the same studies over and over, we are too exhausted when we land to soldier on with the emails that have inevitably still piled up. (33 words)
cn: 更糟糕的是，在刷新电子邮件或一遍又一遍地阅读同样的研究之后，我们着陆时已筋疲力尽，无法继续处理那些不可避免地堆积起来的邮件。

en: Why should flying deplete us? (5 words)
cn: 为什么飞行会让我们疲惫不堪？

en: We're just sitting there doing nothing. (6 words)
cn: 我们只是坐在那里什么都不做。

en: Why can't we be tougher, more resilient and determined in our work so we can accomplish all of the goals we set for ourselves? (24 words)
cn: 为什么我们不能在工作中更坚强、更有韧性、更坚定，这样我们就能完成我们为自己设定的所有目标？

en: Based on our current research, we have come to realize that the problem is not our hectic schedule or the plane travel itself; the problem comes from a misconception of what it means to be resilient, and the resulting impact of overworking. (42 words)
cn: 基于我们目前的研究，我们意识到问题不在于我们繁忙的日程或飞机旅行本身；问题源于对‘韧性’含义的误解，以及由此产生的过度工作影响。

en: We often take a militaristic, 'tough' approach to resilience and determination like a Marine pulling himself through the mud, a boxer going one more round, or a football player picking himself up off the ground for one more play. (39 words)
cn: 我们经常对韧性和决心采取一种军事化的‘强硬’方式，就像海军陆战队员在泥泞中挣扎前行，拳击手再打一轮，或足球运动员从地上爬起来再打一场。

en: We believe that the longer we tough it out, the tougher we are, and therefore the more successful we will be. (21 words)
cn: 我们相信，我们坚持得越久，我们就越坚强，因此我们就越成功。

en: However, this entire conception is scientifically inaccurate. (7 words)
cn: 然而，这整个概念在科学上是不准确的。

en: The very lack of a recovery period is dramatically holding back our collective ability to be resilient and successful. (19 words)
cn: 正是缺乏恢复期极大地阻碍了我们集体的韧性和成功能力。

en: Research has found that there is a direct correlation between lack of recovery and increased incidence of health and safety problems. (21 words)
cn: 研究发现，缺乏恢复与健康和安全问题发生率增加之间存在直接关联。

en: And lack of recovery—whether by disrupting sleep with thoughts of work or having continuous cognitive arousal by watching our phones—is costing our companies $62 billion a year in lost productivity. (30 words)
cn: 缺乏恢复——无论是因工作思绪而扰乱睡眠，还是因看手机而持续认知唤醒——每年给我们的公司造成620亿美元的生产力损失。

en: And just because work stops, it doesn't mean we are recovering. (11 words)
cn: 仅仅因为工作停止了，并不意味着我们正在恢复。

en: We 'stop' work sometimes at 5 pm, but then we spend the night wrestling with solutions to work problems, talking about our work over dinner, and falling asleep thinking about how much work we'll do tomorrow. (36 words)
cn: 我们有时下午5点‘停止’工作，但随后我们整晚都在思考工作问题的解决方案，晚餐时谈论工作，并在思考明天要做多少工作中入睡。

en: In a study just released, researchers from Norway found that 7.8% of Norwegians have become workaholics. (16 words)
cn: 在刚刚发布的一项研究中，挪威的研究人员发现，7.8%的挪威人已经成为工作狂。

en: The scientists cite a definition of 'workaholism' as 'being overly concerned about work, driven by an uncontrollable work motivation, and investing so much time and effort in work that it impairs other important life areas.' (35 words)
cn: 科学家引用‘工作狂’的定义为‘过度关注工作，被无法控制的工作动机所驱使，并在工作中投入太多时间和精力，以至于损害了其他重要的生活领域’。

en: We believe that the number of people who fit that definition includes the majority of American workers, which prompted us to begin a study of workaholism in the U.S. (29 words)
cn: 我们认为符合这一定义的人数包括大多数美国工人，这促使我们开始在美国进行研究工作狂现象。

en: Our study will use a large corporate dataset from a major medical company to examine how technology extends our working hours and thus interferes with necessary cognitive recovery, resulting in huge health care costs and turnover costs for employers. (39 words)
cn: 我们的研究将使用一家大型医疗公司的大量企业数据集，来研究技术如何延长我们的工作时间，从而干扰必要的认知恢复，给雇主带来巨大的医疗成本和人员流动成本。

en: The misconception of resilience is often bred from an early age. (11 words)
cn: 对韧性的误解往往从小就产生了。

en: Parents trying to teach their children resilience might celebrate a high school student staying up until 3 am to finish a science fair project. (24 words)
cn: 试图教孩子韧性的父母可能会称赞一个高中生熬夜到凌晨3点完成科学展览项目。

en: What a distortion of resilience! (5 words)
cn: 这是对韧性多么大的扭曲啊！

en: A resilient child is a well-rested one. (7 words)
cn: 一个坚韧的孩子是一个休息良好的孩子。

en: When an exhausted student goes to school, he risks hurting everyone on the road with his impaired driving; he doesn't have the cognitive resources to do well on his English test; he has lower self-control with his friends; and at home, he is moody with his parents. (47 words)
cn: 当一个精疲力尽的学生去上学时，他可能会因驾驶能力受损而伤害路上的每个人；他没有足够的认知资源在英语考试中取得好成绩；他对朋友的自控力更低；在家里，他对父母脾气暴躁。

en: Overwork and exhaustion are the opposite of resilience and the bad habits we acquire when we're young only magnify when we hit the workforce. (24 words)
cn: 过度工作和疲惫是韧性的反面，而我们年轻时养成的坏习惯在进入职场后只会更加严重。

en: As Jim Loehr and Tony Schwartz have written, if you have too much time in the performance zone, you need more time in the recovery zone, otherwise you risk burnout. (30 words)
cn: 正如吉姆·洛尔和托尼·施瓦茨所写，如果你在表现区花费太多时间，就需要在恢复区花更多时间，否则你就有倦怠的风险。

en: Gathering your resources to 'try hard' requires burning energy in order to overcome your currently low arousal level. (18 words)
cn: 集中资源去‘努力’需要消耗能量来克服你目前低唤醒水平的状态。

en: It also worsens exhaustion. (4 words)
cn: 这也会加重疲惫。

en: Thus the more imbalanced we become due to overworking, the more value there is in activities that allow us to return to a state of balance. (26 words)
cn: 因此，由于过度工作而变得越不平衡，能让我们恢复平衡状态的活动就越有价值。

en: The value of a recovery period rises in proportion to the amount of work required of us. (17 words)
cn: 恢复期的价值与我们被要求的工作量成正比。

en: So how do we recover and build resilience? (8 words)
cn: 那么我们如何恢复和建立韧性呢？

en: Most people assume that if you stop doing a task like answering emails or writing a paper, your brain will naturally recover, so that when you start again later in the day or the next morning, you'll have your energy back. (41 words)
cn: 大多数人认为，如果你停止做一项任务，比如回复邮件或写论文，你的大脑会自然恢复，这样当你当天晚些时候或第二天早上重新开始时，你会恢复精力。

en: But surely everyone reading this has had times when you lie in bed for hours, unable to fall asleep because your brain is thinking about work. (26 words)
cn: 但毫无疑问，每个读到这篇文章的人都有过躺在床上几个小时无法入睡的经历，因为你的大脑在想工作。

en: If you lie in bed for eight hours, you may have rested, but you can still feel exhausted the next day. (21 words)
cn: 如果你在床上躺八个小时，你可能休息了，但第二天你仍然会感到筋疲力尽。

en: That's because rest and recovery are not the same thing. (10 words)
cn: 那是因为休息和恢复不是一回事。

en: If you're trying to build resilience at work, you need adequate internal and external recovery periods. (16 words)
cn: 如果你想在工作中建立韧性，你需要充分的内部和外部恢复期。

en: As researchers Zijlstra, Cropley and Rydstedt write in their 2014 paper: 'Internal recovery refers to the shorter periods of relaxation that take place within the frames of the work day or the work setting in the form of short scheduled or unscheduled breaks, by shifting attention or changing to other work tasks when the mental or physical resources required for the initial task are temporarily depleted or exhausted. (68 words)
cn: 正如研究人员齐尔斯特拉、克罗普利和里德斯泰特在他们2014年的论文中所写：‘内部恢复指的是在工作日或工作环境框架内发生的较短的放松期，以计划内或计划外的短暂休息形式出现，通过转移注意力或在初始任务所需的心理或身体资源暂时耗尽时切换到其他工作任务来实现。’

en: External recovery refers to actions that take place outside of work—e.g. in the free time between the work days, and during weekends, holidays or vacations.' (25 words)
cn: ‘外部恢复指在工作之外发生的活动——例如工作日之间的空闲时间、周末、假日或假期期间。’

en: If after work you lie around on your bed and get irritated by political commentary on your phone or get stressed thinking about decisions about how to renovate your home, your brain has not received a break from high mental arousal states. (42 words)
cn: 如果下班后你躺在床上，因手机上的政治评论而恼怒，或因思考如何装修房子的决定而感到压力，那么你的大脑并没有从高度精神唤醒状态中得到休息。

en: Our brains need a rest as much as our bodies do. (11 words)
cn: 我们的大脑和身体一样需要休息。

en: If you really want to build resilience, you can start by strategically stopping. (13 words)
cn: 如果你真的想建立韧性，你可以从有策略地停止开始。

en: Give yourself the resources to be tough by creating internal and external recovery periods. (14 words)
cn: 通过创造内部和外部恢复期，给自己变得坚强的资源。

en: Amy Blankson describes how to strategically stop during the day by using technology to control overworking. (16 words)
cn: 艾米·布兰克森描述了如何通过使用技术来控制过度工作，从而在白天有策略地停下来。

en: She suggests downloading the Instant or Moment apps to see how many times you turn on your phone each day. (20 words)
cn: 她建议下载Instant或Moment应用程序，查看你每天打开手机多少次。

en: You can also use apps like Offtime or Unplugged to create tech free zones by strategically scheduling automatic airplane modes. (20 words)
cn: 你也可以使用Offtime或Unplugged等应用程序，通过有策略地安排自动飞行模式来创建无技术区。

en: The average person turns on their phone 150 times every day. (11 words)
cn: 普通人每天打开手机150次。

en: If every distraction took only 1 minute, that would account for 2.5 hours a day. (15 words)
cn: 如果每次分心只花1分钟，那每天就占了2.5小时。

en: In addition, you can take a cognitive break every 90 minutes to charge your batteries. (15 words)
cn: 此外，你可以每90分钟进行一次认知休息来充电。

en: Try to not have lunch at your desk, but instead spend time outside or with your friends—not talking about work. (20 words)
cn: 尽量不要在办公桌前吃午餐，而是到户外或与朋友一起度过——不要谈论工作。

en: Take all of your paid time off, which not only gives you recovery periods, but raises your productivity and likelihood of promotion. (22 words)
cn: 休完所有带薪假期，这不仅给你恢复期，还能提高你的生产力和晋升的可能性。

en: As for us, we've started using our plane time as a work-free zone, and thus time to dip into the recovery phase. (22 words)
cn: 至于我们，我们已经开始把乘飞机的时间作为无工作区，从而进入恢复阶段。

en: The results have been fantastic. (5 words)
cn: 效果非常棒。

en: We are usually tired already by the time we get on a plane, and the crowded space and unstable internet connection make work more challenging. (25 words)
cn: 我们通常在登机时已经累了，拥挤的空间和不稳定的网络连接使工作更具挑战性。

en: Now, instead of swimming upstream, we relax, sleep, watch movies, or listen to music. (14 words)
cn: 现在，我们不再逆流而上，而是放松、睡觉、看电影或听音乐。

en: And when we get off the plane, instead of being depleted, we feel recovered and ready to return to the performance zone. (22 words)
cn: 当我们下飞机时，不再感到精疲力尽，而是感觉恢复好了，准备好回到表现区。

en: Children with attention problems in early childhood were 40% less likely to graduate from high school, says a new study from Duke University. (23 words)
cn: 杜克大学的一项新研究表明，儿童早期有注意力问题的孩子高中毕业的可能性要低40%。

en: The study included 386 kindergarteners from schools in the Fast Track Project, a multi-site clinical trial in the U.S. that in 1991 began tracking how children developed across their lives. (30 words)
cn: 该研究包括了来自Fast Track Project学校的386名幼儿园儿童，这是一个美国多地点临床试验项目，于1991年开始追踪儿童一生的成长。

en: With this study, researchers examined early academic attention and socio-emotional skills and how each contributed to academic success into young adulthood. (21 words)
cn: 在这项研究中，研究人员考察了早期的学业注意力和社会情感技能，以及它们各自如何对进入成年早期的学业成功做出贡献。

en: They found that early attention skills were the most consistent predictor of academic success, and that likability by peers also had a modest effect on academic performance. (27 words)
cn: 他们发现，早期的注意力技能是学业成功最一致的预测指标，而同伴的喜爱程度对学业成绩也有适度的积极影响。

en: By fifth grade, children with early attention difficulties had lower grades and reading achievement scores than their peers. (18 words)
cn: 到五年级时，早期有注意力困难的孩子成绩和阅读成就分数都低于同龄人。

en: As fifth-graders, children with early attention problems obtained average reading scores at least 3% lower than their contemporaries' and grades at least 8% lower than those of their peers. (29 words)
cn: 作为五年级学生，早期有注意力问题的孩子的平均阅读分数至少比同龄人低3%，成绩至少比同龄人低8%。

en: This was after controlling for IQ, socio-economic status and academic skills at school entry. (14 words)
cn: 这是在控制了智商、社会经济地位和入学时的学业技能之后得出的结论。

en: Although these may not seem like large effects, the impact of early attention problems continued throughout the children's academic careers. (20 words)
cn: 虽然这些看起来可能不是很大的影响，但早期注意力问题的影响贯穿了孩子们的整个学业生涯。

en: Lower reading achievement scores and grades in fifth grade contributed to reduced grades in middle school and thereby contributed to a 40% lower high school graduation rate. (27 words)
cn: 五年级较低的阅读成就分数和成绩导致了中学成绩下降，从而使高中毕业率降低了40%。

en: The children we identified as having attention difficulties were not diagnosed with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), although some may have had the disorder. (24 words)
cn: 我们确定为有注意力困难的孩子并没有被诊断为注意力缺陷多动障碍（ADHD），尽管有些可能患有这种障碍。

en: Our findings suggest that even more modest attention difficulties may increase the risk of negative academic outcomes. (17 words)
cn: 我们的发现表明，即使是更轻微的注意力困难也可能增加学业不良的风险。

en: Social acceptance by peers in early childhood also predicted grades in fifth grade. (13 words)
cn: 儿童早期被同伴接纳也预示着五年级的成绩。

en: Children not as liked by their first-grade peers had slightly lower grades in fifth grade, while those with higher social acceptance had higher grades. (24 words)
cn: 一年级时不太被同伴喜欢的孩子在五年级时成绩略低，而那些社会接纳度更高的孩子成绩更高。

en: This study shows the importance of so-called 'non-cognitive' or soft skills in contributing to children's positive peer relationships, which, in turn, contribute to their academic success, said Kenneth Dodge, director of the Duke Center for Child and Family Policy. (39 words)
cn: 杜克大学儿童与家庭政策中心主任肯尼斯·道奇说：‘这项研究显示了所谓的“非认知”或软技能在促进儿童积极同伴关系方面的重要性，而这反过来又有助于他们的学业成功。’

en: The results highlight the need to develop effective early interventions to help those with attention problems stay on track academically and for educators to encourage positive peer relationships, the researchers said. (31 words)
cn: 研究人员表示，研究结果强调了开发有效早期干预措施的必要性，以帮助有注意力问题的孩子保持在学业轨道上，同时教育工作者应鼓励积极的同伴关系。

en: We're learning that student success requires a more comprehensive approach, one that incorporates not only academic skills but also social, self-regulatory and attention skills, Dodge said. (26 words)
cn: 道奇说：‘我们正在认识到学生的成功需要一种更全面的方法，它不仅包括学业技能，还包括社交、自我调节和注意力技能。’

en: If we neglect any of these areas, the child's development lags. (11 words)
cn: ‘如果我们忽视其中任何一个领域，孩子的发展就会滞后。’

en: If we attend to these areas, a child's success may reinforce itself with positive feedback loops. (16 words)
cn: ‘如果我们关注这些领域，孩子的成功可能会通过积极反馈循环而自我强化。’

en: On Jan. 9, 2007, Steve Jobs formally announced Apple's 'revolutionary mobile phone' — a device that combined the functionality of an iPod, phone and Internet communication into a single unit, navigated by touch. (33 words)
cn: 2007年1月9日，史蒂夫·乔布斯正式发布了苹果的‘革命性手机’——一款将iPod、手机和互联网通信功能整合为一体、通过触摸操作的设备。

en: It was a huge milestone in the development of smartphones, which are now owned by a majority of American adults and are increasingly common across the globe. (27 words)
cn: 这是智能手机发展的一个巨大里程碑，如今大多数美国成年人都拥有智能手机，而且智能手机在全球越来越普遍。

en: As smartphones have multiplied, so have questions about their impact on how we live and how we work. (18 words)
cn: 随着智能手机的激增，关于它们如何影响我们生活和工作方式的问题也随之增多。

en: Often the advantages of convenient, mobile technology are both obvious and taken for granted, leaving more subtle topics for concerned discussion: Are smartphones disturbing children's sleep? (26 words)
cn: 便利的移动技术的优势往往既明显又被认为是理所当然的，从而留下更微妙的话题供讨论：智能手机是否在干扰儿童的睡眠？

en: Is an inability to get away from work having a negative impact on health? (14 words)
cn: 无法摆脱工作是否对健康产生负面影响？

en: And what are the implications for privacy? (7 words)
cn: 对隐私有什么影响？

en: But today, on the 10th anniversary of the iPhone, let's take a moment to consider a less obvious advantage: the potential for smartphone technology to revolutionize behavioral science. (28 words)
cn: 但在今天，iPhone发布十周年之际，让我们花点时间思考一个不那么明显的优势：智能手机技术彻底改变行为科学的潜力。

en: That's because, for the first time in human history, a large proportion of the species is in continuous contact with technology that can record key features of an individual's behavior and environment. (32 words)
cn: 这是因为，在人类历史上第一次，很大一部分人类在持续接触能够记录个体行为和环境关键特征的技术。

en: Researchers have already begun to use smartphones in social scientific research, either to query people regularly as they engage in their normal lives or to record activity using the device's built-in sensors. (32 words)
cn: 研究人员已经开始在社会科学研究中使用智能手机，要么在人们正常生活中定期询问他们，要么使用设备内置传感器记录活动。

en: These studies are confirming, challenging and extending what's been found using more traditional approaches, in which people report how they behaved in real life or participate in relatively short and artificial laboratory-based tasks. (33 words)
cn: 这些研究正在证实、挑战和扩展使用更传统方法所发现的结论——传统方法中人们报告他们在现实生活中的行为方式，或参与相对简短、人为的实验室任务。

en: Such studies are just first steps. (6 words)
cn: 这类研究只是第一步。

en: As more data are collected and methods for analysis improve, researchers will be in a better position to identify how different experiences, behaviors and environments relate to each other and evolve over time, with the potential to improve people's productivity and wellbeing in a variety of domains. (47 words)
cn: 随着更多数据的收集和分析方法的改进，研究人员将能够更好地识别不同经历、行为和环境如何相互关联并随时间演变，从而有可能提高人们在各个领域的生产力和幸福感。

en: Beyond revealing population-wide patterns, the right combination of data and analysis can also help individuals identify unique characteristics of their own behavior, including conditions that could indicate the need for some form of intervention—such as an unusual increase in behaviors that signal a period of depression. (46 words)
cn: 除了揭示整个人群的模式外，数据和分析的正确组合还可以帮助个体识别自身行为的独特特征，包括可能表明需要某种形式干预的状况——例如预示抑郁期的不寻常行为增加。

en: Smartphone-based data collection comes at an appropriate time in the evolution of psychological science. (14 words)
cn: 基于智能手机的数据收集恰逢心理科学演进的适当时机。

en: Today, the field is in transition, moving away from a focus on laboratory studies with undergraduate participants towards more complex, real-world situations studied with more diverse groups of people. (29 words)
cn: 如今，该领域正处于转型期，从关注以大学生为参与者的实验室研究，转向以更多样化的人群为对象研究更复杂的现实世界情境。

en: Smartphones offer new tools for achieving these ambitions, providing rich data about everyday behaviors in a variety of contexts. (19 words)
cn: 智能手机为实现这些雄心壮志提供了新工具，提供了关于各种情境下日常行为的丰富数据。

en: So here's another way in which smartphones might transform the way we live and work: by offering insights into human psychology and behavior and, thus, supporting smarter social science. (29 words)
cn: 所以这是智能手机可能改变我们生活和工作方式的另一种途径：通过提供对人类心理和行为的洞察，从而支持更智慧的社会科学。

en: Pasta is no longer off the menu, after a new review of studies suggested that the carbohydrate can form part of a healthy diet, and even help people lose weight. (30 words)
cn: 在一项新的研究综述表明碳水化合物可以成为健康饮食的一部分，甚至可以帮助人们减肥之后，意大利面不再被排除在菜单之外。

en: For years, nutritionists have recommended that pasta be kept to a minimum, to cut calories, prevent fat build-up and stop blood sugar shooting up. (24 words)
cn: 多年来，营养学家一直建议将意大利面的摄入量控制在最低限度，以减少热量摄入，防止脂肪堆积并阻止血糖飙升。

en: The low-carbohydrate food movement gave birth to such diets as the Atkins, Paleo and Keto, which advised swapping foods like bread, pasta and potatoes for vegetables, fish and meat. (29 words)
cn: 低碳水化合物食品运动催生了像阿特金斯饮食法、旧石器饮食法和生酮饮食法这样的饮食方式，这些饮食建议将面包、意大利面和土豆等食物换成蔬菜、鱼肉和肉类。

en: More recently the trend of swapping spaghetti for vegetables has been championed by clean-eating experts. (15 words)
cn: 最近，用蔬菜代替意大利面的趋势受到了健康饮食专家的推崇。

en: But now a systematic review and analysis of 30 studies by Canadian researchers found that not only does pasta not cause weight gain, but three meals a week can help people drop more than half a kilogram over four months. (40 words)
cn: 但现在，加拿大研究人员对30项研究进行的系统性回顾和分析发现，意大利面不仅不会导致体重增加，而且每周吃三餐意大利面可以帮助人们在四个月内减重超过半公斤。

en: The reviewers found that pasta had been unfairly demonized because it had been lumped in with other, more fat-promoting carbohydrates. (20 words)
cn: 评审人员发现，意大利面被不公正地妖魔化了，因为它被和其他更易致胖的碳水化合物混为一谈。

en: The study found that pasta didn't contribute to weight gain or increase in body fat, said lead author Dr. John Sievenpiper. (21 words)
cn: 该研究的主要作者约翰·西文派珀博士说：‘研究发现，意大利面不会导致体重增加或体脂增加。’

en: In weighing the evidence, we can now say with some confidence that pasta does not have an adverse effect on body weight outcomes when it is consumed as part of a healthy dietary pattern. (34 words)
cn: ‘在权衡证据后，我们现在可以有把握地说，当意大利面作为健康饮食模式的一部分食用时，不会对体重结果产生不利影响。’

en: In fact, analysis actually showed a small weight loss contrary to concerns. (12 words)
cn: 事实上，分析实际上显示出了小幅的体重下降，与人们的担忧相反。

en: Perhaps pasta can be part of a healthy diet. (9 words)
cn: 也许意大利面可以成为健康饮食的一部分。

en: Those involved in the clinical trials on average ate 3.3 servings of pasta a week instead of other carbohydrates, one serving equaling around half a cup. (26 words)
cn: 参与临床试验的人平均每周吃3.3份意大利面来代替其他碳水化合物，一份大约相当于半杯。

en: They lost around half a kilogram over an average follow-up of 12 weeks. (13 words)
cn: 在平均为期12周的跟踪期间，他们减掉了大约半公斤。

en: Retail profits are falling sharply. (5 words)
cn: 零售利润正在急剧下降。

en: Stores are closing. (3 words)
cn: 商店正在关闭。

en: Malls are emptying. (3 words)
cn: 购物中心正在变得空荡荡。

en: The depressing stories just keep coming. (6 words)
cn: 令人沮丧的消息接连不断。

en: Reading the earnings announcements of large retail stores like Macy's, Nordstrom, and Target is about as uplifting as a tour of an intensive care unit. (25 words)
cn: 阅读像梅西百货、诺德斯特龙和塔吉特这样的大型零售商店的收益公告，其振奋程度就像参观重症监护病房一样。

en: The internet is apparently taking down yet another industry. (9 words)
cn: 互联网显然正在摧毁又一个行业。

en: Brick and mortar stores seem to be going the way of the yellow pages. (14 words)
cn: 实体店似乎正在走向像黄页一样的命运。

en: Sure enough, the Census Bureau just released data showing that online retail sales surged 15.2 percent between the first quarter of 2015 and the first quarter of 2016. (28 words)
cn: 果然，人口普查局刚刚发布的数据显示，2015年第一季度至2016年第一季度，在线零售额飙升了15.2%。

en: But before you dump all of your retail stocks, there are more facts you should consider. (16 words)
cn: 但在你抛售所有零售股票之前，还有更多事实你应该考虑。

en: Looking only at that 15.2 percent 'surge' would be misleading. (10 words)
cn: 只看那15.2%的‘飙升’会产生误导。

en: It was an increase that was on a small base of 6.9 percent. (13 words)
cn: 这是在6.9%的较小基数上的增长。

en: Even when a tiny number grows by a large percentage terms, it is often still tiny. (16 words)
cn: 即使一个很小的数字增长比例很大，它往往仍然很小。

en: More than 20 years after the internet was opened to commerce, the Census Bureau tells us that brick and mortar sales accounted for 92.3 percent of retail sales in the first quarter of 2016. (34 words)
cn: 在互联网向商业开放20多年后，人口普查局告诉我们，2016年第一季度实体店销售额占零售总额的92.3%。

en: Their data show that only 0.8 percent of retail sales shifted from offline to online between the beginning of 2015 and 2016. (22 words)
cn: 他们的数据显示，从2015年初到2016年，只有0.8%的零售额从线下转移到了线上。

en: So, despite all the talk about drone deliveries to your doorstep, all the retail executives expressing anxiety over consumers going online, and even a Presidential candidate exclaiming that Amazon has a 'huge antitrust problem,' the Census data suggest that physical retail is thriving. (43 words)
cn: 因此，尽管有各种关于无人机送货到你家门口的讨论，所有零售业高管对消费者转向线上购物表示焦虑，甚至有一位总统候选人宣称亚马逊存在‘巨大的反垄断问题’，但人口普查数据表明，实体零售业仍在蓬勃发展。

en: Of course, the closed stores, depressed executives, and sinking stocks suggest otherwise. (12 words)
cn: 当然，关闭的商店、沮丧的高管和下跌的股票则表明了相反的情况。

en: What's the real story? (4 words)
cn: 真实情况是怎样的呢？

en: Many firms operating brick and mortar stores are in trouble. (10 words)
cn: 许多经营实体店的公司在陷入困境。

en: The retail industry is getting reinvented, as we describe in our new book Matchmakers. (14 words)
cn: 正如我们在新书《媒人》中所描述的，零售业正在被重塑。

en: It's standing in the path of what Schumpeter called a gale of creative destruction. (14 words)
cn: 它正站在熊彼特所称的创造性破坏风暴的道路上。

en: That storm has been brewing for some time, and as it has reached gale force, most large retailers are searching for a response. (23 words)
cn: 这场风暴已经酝酿了一段时间，当它达到狂风级别时，大多数大型零售商都在寻找应对之策。

en: As the CFO of Macy's put it recently, 'We're frankly scratching our heads.' (13 words)
cn: 正如梅西百货的首席财务官最近所说：‘坦率地说，我们正在挠头。’

en: But it's not happening as experts predicted. (7 words)
cn: 但事情并没有像专家预测的那样发生。

en: In the peak of the dot.com bubble, brick and mortar retail was one of those industries the internet was going to kill—and quickly. (23 words)
cn: 在互联网泡沫的顶峰时期，实体零售业是互联网将要快速摧毁的行业之一。

en: The dot.com bust discredited most predictions of that sort and in the years that followed, conventional retailers' confidence in the future increased as Census continued to report weak online sales. (30 words)
cn: 互联网泡沫的破灭使大多数此类预测失去了可信度，在随后的几年里，由于人口普查局持续报告在线销售疲软，传统零售商对未来信心增强。

en: And then the gale hit. (5 words)
cn: 然后风暴来袭了。

en: It is becoming increasingly clear that retail reinvention isn't a simple battle to the death between bricks and clicks. (19 words)
cn: 越来越清楚的是，零售业的转型不是实体店和网店之间简单的生死之战。

en: It is about devising retail models that work for people who are making increasing use of a growing array of internet-connected tools to change how they search, shop, and buy. (30 words)
cn: 而是要设计出适合那些越来越多地使用各种互联网连接工具来改变他们搜索、购物和购买方式的人们的零售模式。

en: Creative retailers are using the new technologies to innovate just about everything stores do from managing inventory, to marketing, to getting paid. (22 words)
cn: 有创意的零售商正在利用新技术来创新商店所做的几乎所有事情——从库存管理到营销，再到收款。

en: More than drones dropping a new supply of underwear on your doorstep, Apple's massively successful brick-and-mortar-and-glass retail stores and Amazon's small steps in the same direction are what should keep old-fashioned retailers awake at night. (35 words)
cn: 比起无人机将新一批内衣送到你家门口，苹果公司极其成功的实体玻璃零售店以及亚马逊在同方向上的小步前进，才是让传统零售商夜不能寐的原因。

en: Not to mention the large number of creative new retailers, like Bonobos, that are blending online and offline experiences in creative ways. (22 words)
cn: 更不用说大量像Bonobos这样有创意的新型零售商，它们正以创造性的方式融合线上和线下体验。

en: Retail reinvention is not a simple process, and it's also not happening on what used to be called 'Internet Time.' (20 words)
cn: 零售业的转型不是一个简单的过程，它也没有以所谓的‘互联网速度’发生。

en: Some internet-driven changes have happened quickly, of course. (8 words)
cn: 当然，一些互联网驱动的变化确实发生得很快。

en: Craigslist quickly overtook newspaper classified ads and turned newspaper economics upside down. (12 words)
cn: Craigslist迅速取代了报纸分类广告，颠覆了报纸的经济模式。

en: But many widely anticipated changes weren't quick, and some haven't really started. (12 words)
cn: 但许多被广泛预期的变化并不快，有些甚至尚未真正开始。

en: With the benefit of hindsight, it looks like the internet will transform the economy at something like the pace of other great inventions like electricity. (25 words)
cn: 事后看来，互联网将以类似于电力等其他伟大发明的速度来改变经济。

en: B2B commerce, for example, didn't move mainly online by 2005 as many had predicted in 2000, nor even by 2016, but that doesn't mean it won't do so over the next few decades. (33 words)
cn: 例如，B2B商务并没有像许多人在2000年预测的那样在2005年之前主要转移到线上，甚至到2016年也没有，但这并不意味着未来几十年不会如此。

en: But the gale is still blowing. (6 words)
cn: 但风暴仍在刮。

en: The sudden decline in foot traffic in recent years, even though it hasn't been accompanied by a massive decline in physical sales, is a critical warning. (26 words)
cn: 近年来客流量的突然下降，即使没有伴随着实体销售的大幅下降，也是一个关键的警告。

en: People can shop more efficiently online and therefore don't need to go to as many stores to find what they want. (21 words)
cn: 人们可以在网上更高效地购物，因此不需要去那么多商店就能找到他们想要的东西。

en: There's a surplus of physical shopping space for the crowds, which is one reason why stores are downsizing and closing. (20 words)
cn: 对于购物人群来说，实体购物空间过剩，这是商店缩减规模和关闭的原因之一。

en: The rise of the mobile phone has recently added a new level of complexity to the process of retail reinvention. (20 words)
cn: 手机的兴起最近为零售业转型的过程增添了新的复杂性。

en: Even five years ago most people faced a choice. (9 words)
cn: 即使在五年前，大多数人也面临着一个选择。

en: Sit at your computer, probably at home or at the office, search and browse, and buy. (16 words)
cn: 坐在电脑前——可能在家或办公室——搜索、浏览并购买。

en: Or head out to the mall, or Main Street, look and shop, and buy. (14 words)
cn: 或者去购物中心或商业街，逛逛商店并购买。

en: Now, just about everyone has a smartphone, connected to the internet almost everywhere almost all the time. (17 words)
cn: 现在，几乎每个人都有一部智能手机，几乎随时随地都能连接互联网。

en: Even when a retailer gets a customer to walk in the store, she can easily see if there's a better deal online or at another store nearby. (27 words)
cn: 即使零售商让顾客走进店内，她也能轻松查看网上或附近其他商店是否有更好的交易。

en: So far, the main thing many large retailers have done in response to all this is to open online stores, so people will come to them directly rather than to Amazon and its smaller online rivals. (36 words)
cn: 到目前为止，许多大型零售商对此所做的主要应对措施是开设在线商店，这样人们就会直接找到他们，而不是去亚马逊及其规模较小的在线竞争对手。

en: Many are having the same problem that newspapers have. (9 words)
cn: 许多零售商面临着与报纸同样的问题。

en: Even if they get online traffic, they struggle to make enough money online to compensate for what they are losing offline. (21 words)
cn: 即使它们获得了线上流量，也很难在线赚到足够的钱来弥补线下损失。

en: A few seem to be making this work. (8 words)
cn: 少数几家似乎正在做到这一点。

en: Among large traditional retailers, Walmart recently reported the best results, leading its stock price to surge, while Macy's, Target, and Nordstrom's dropped. (22 words)
cn: 在大型传统零售商中，沃尔玛最近报告了最佳业绩，导致其股价飙升，而梅西百货、塔吉特和诺德斯特龙的股价则下跌。

en: Yet Walmart's year-over-year online sales only grew 7 percent, leading its CEO to lament, 'Growth here is too slow.' (19 words)
cn: 然而，沃尔玛的在线销售额同比仅增长了7%，导致其首席执行官感叹：‘这里的增长太慢了。’

en: Part of the problem is that almost two decades after Amazon filed the one-click patent, the online retail shopping and buying experience is filled with frictions. (26 words)
cn: 部分问题在于，在亚马逊提交一键式专利近20年后，在线零售购物和购买体验仍然充满摩擦。

en: A recent study graded more than 600 internet retailers on how easy it was for consumers to shop, buy, and pay. (21 words)
cn: 最近的一项研究对600多家互联网零售商进行了评级，评估消费者购物、购买和支付的便捷程度。

en: Almost half of the sites didn't get a passing grade and only 18 percent got an A or B. (19 words)
cn: 近一半的网站没有获得及格分数，只有18%获得了A或B。

en: The turmoil on the ground in physical retail is hard to square with the Census data. (16 words)
cn: 实体零售领域的动荡很难与人口普查数据相吻合。

en: Unfortunately, part of the explanation is that the Census retail data are unreliable. (13 words)
cn: 不幸的是，部分解释是人口普查的零售数据不可靠。

en: Our deep look into those data and their preparation revealed serious problems. (12 words)
cn: 我们对这些数据及其准备过程的深入调查揭示了严重的问题。

en: It seems likely that Census simply misclassifies a large chunk of online sales. (13 words)
cn: 人口普查很可能只是将大量在线销售错误分类。

en: It is certain that the Census procedures, which lump the online sales of major traditional retailers like Walmart with 'non-store retailers' like food trucks, can mask major changes in individual retail categories. (32 words)
cn: 可以肯定的是，人口普查程序将沃尔玛等主要传统零售商的在线销售与食品卡车等‘非店铺零售商’混为一谈，这可能掩盖了各个零售类别的重大变化。

en: The bureau could easily present their data in more useful ways. (11 words)
cn: 该机构本可以很容易地以更有用的方式呈现他们的数据。

en: But they have chosen not to. (6 words)
cn: 但他们选择了不这样做。

en: Despite the turmoil, brick and mortar won't disappear any time soon. (11 words)
cn: 尽管动荡不安，实体店不会很快消失。

en: The big questions are which, if any, of the large traditional retailers will still be on the scene in a decade or two because they have successfully reinvented themselves, which new players will operate busy stores on Main Streets and maybe even in shopping malls, and how the shopping and buying experience will have changed in each retail category. (59 words)
cn: 大问题是：在一二十年里，哪些大型传统零售商（如果有的话）会因为它们成功地实现了自我转型而继续存在；哪些新玩家将在商业街甚至购物中心经营繁忙的商店；以及每个零售类别的购物和购买体验将发生怎样的变化。

en: Investors shouldn't write off brick and mortar. (7 words)
cn: 投资者不应该完全放弃实体店。

en: Whether they should bet on the traditional players who run those stores now is another matter. (16 words)
cn: 他们是否应该押注于现在经营这些商店的传统企业则是另一回事。

en: Professor Stephen Hawking has warned that the creation of powerful artificial intelligence (AI) will be 'either the best, or the worst thing, ever to happen to humanity', and praised the creation of an academic institute dedicated to researching the future of intelligence as 'crucial to the future of our civilisation and our species'. (53 words)
cn: 斯蒂芬·霍金教授警告说，强大的人工智能的创造将是‘人类有史以来可能发生的最好或最坏的事情’，并称赞建立一个致力于研究智能未来的学术机构‘对我们文明和我们物种的未来至关重要’。

en: Hawking was speaking at the opening of the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence (LCFI) at Cambridge University, a multi-disciplinary institute that will attempt to tackle some of the open-ended questions raised by the rapid pace of development in AI research. (42 words)
cn: 霍金是在剑桥大学莱弗休姆智能未来中心（LCFI）的开幕式上发表上述讲话的，该中心是一个多学科研究机构，将尝试解决人工智能研究快速发展带来的一些开放性问题。

en: We spend a great deal of time studying history, Hawking said, 'which, let's face it, is mostly the history of stupidity. (21 words)
cn: 霍金说：‘我们花大量时间研究历史，’‘说实在的，那基本上是愚蠢的历史。’

en: So it's a welcome change that people are studying instead the future of intelligence.' (14 words)
cn: ‘所以，人们转而研究智能的未来，这是一个受欢迎的转变。’

en: While the world-renowned physicist has often been cautious about AI, raising concerns that humanity could be the architect of its own destruction if it creates a super-intelligence with a will of its own, he was also quick to highlight the positives that AI research can bring. (46 words)
cn: 虽然这位世界著名的物理学家经常对人工智能持谨慎态度，担心如果人类创造出拥有自己意志的超级智能，可能会成为自我毁灭的始作俑者，但他也很快强调了人工智能研究可以带来的积极方面。

en: The potential benefits of creating intelligence are huge, he said. (10 words)
cn: 他说：‘创造智能的潜在好处是巨大的。’

en: We cannot predict what we might achieve when our own minds are amplified by AI. (15 words)
cn: ‘当我们的思想被人工智能增强时，我们无法预测可能实现什么。’

en: Perhaps with the tools of this new technological revolution, we will be able to undo some of the damage done to the natural world by the last one—industrialisation. (28 words)
cn: ‘也许借助这场新技术革命的工具，我们将能够消除上一次革命——工业化——对自然界造成的一些损害。’

en: And surely we will aim to finally eradicate disease and poverty. (11 words)
cn: ‘而且我们一定会致力于最终根除疾病和贫困。’

en: And every aspect of our lives will be transformed. (9 words)
cn: ‘我们生活的方方面面都将被改变。’

en: In short, success in creating AI could be the biggest event in the history of our civilisation. (17 words)
cn: ‘简而言之，成功创造人工智能可能是我们文明史上最大的事件。’

en: Huw Price, the centre's academic director and the Bertrand Russell professor of philosophy at Cambridge University, where Hawking is also an academic, said that the centre came about partially as a result of the university's Centre for Existential Risk. (39 words)
cn: 该中心的学术主任、剑桥大学伯特兰·罗素哲学教授休·普莱斯——霍金也是该校的学者——表示，该中心的成立部分归功于剑桥大学的存在风险中心。

en: That institute examined a wider range of potential problems for humanity, while the LCFI has a narrower focus. (18 words)
cn: 那个研究所研究了人类面临的更广泛的潜在问题，而LCFI的关注范围更窄。

en: AI pioneer Margaret Boden, professor of cognitive science at the University of Sussex, praised the progress of such discussions. (19 words)
cn: 人工智能先驱、苏塞克斯大学认知科学教授玛格丽特·博登赞扬了此类讨论的进展。

en: As recently as 2009, she said, the topic wasn't taken seriously, even among AI researchers. (15 words)
cn: 她说，就在2009年，即使在人工智能研究人员中，这个话题也没有被认真对待。

en: AI is hugely exciting, she said, 'but it has limitations, which present grave dangers given uncritical use.' (17 words)
cn: 她说：‘人工智能非常令人兴奋，’‘但它也有局限性，如果被不加批判地使用，会带来严重危险。’

en: The academic community is not alone in warning about the potential dangers of AI as well as the potential benefits. (20 words)
cn: 学术界并非唯一就人工智能的潜在危险和潜在好处发出警告的群体。

en: A number of pioneers from the technology industry, most famously the entrepreneur Elon Musk, have also expressed their concerns about the damage that a super-intelligent AI could do to humanity. (30 words)
cn: 许多来自科技行业的先驱，其中最著名的是企业家埃隆·马斯克，也表达了他们对超级智能人工智能可能对人类造成的损害的担忧。

en: The market for products designed specifically for older adults could reach $30 billion by next year, and startups want in on the action. (23 words)
cn: 专为老年人设计的产品市场到明年可能达到300亿美元，初创公司也想参与其中。

en: What they sometimes lack is feedback from the people who they hope will use their products. (16 words)
cn: 他们有时缺乏的是来自他们希望使用其产品的人的反馈。

en: So Brookdale, the country's largest owner of retirement communities, has been inviting a few select entrepreneurs just to move in for a few days, show off their products and hear what the residents have to say. (36 words)
cn: 因此，该国最大的退休社区所有者Brookdale一直在邀请一些精选的企业家入住几天，展示他们的产品，并听取居民的意见。

en: That's what brought Dayle Rodriguez, 28, all the way from England to the dining room of Brookdale South Bay in Torrance, California. (22 words)
cn: 这就是把28岁的戴尔·罗德里格斯从英格兰一路带到加利福尼亚州托兰斯的Brookdale South Bay餐厅的原因。

en: Rodriguez is the community and marketing manager for a company called Sentab. (12 words)
cn: 罗德里格斯是一家名为Sentab的公司的社区和营销经理。

en: The startup's product, SentabTV, enables older adults who may not be comfortable with computers to access email, video chat and social media using just their televisions and a remote control. (30 words)
cn: 这家初创公司的产品SentabTV让可能不习惯使用电脑的老年人只需使用电视和遥控器就能访问电子邮件、视频聊天和社交媒体。

en: It's nothing new, it's nothing too complicated and it's natural because lots of people have TV remotes, says Rodriguez. (19 words)
cn: 罗德里格斯说：‘这不是什么新鲜事，也不是太复杂，而且很自然，因为很多人都有电视遥控器。’

en: But none of that is the topic of conversation in the Brookdale dining room. (14 words)
cn: 但这些都不是Brookdale餐厅里的话题。

en: Instead, Rodriguez solicits residents' advice on what he should get on his cheeseburger and how he should spend the afternoon. (20 words)
cn: 相反，罗德里格斯向居民征求意见，询问他的芝士汉堡应该加什么，以及他应该如何度过下午。

en: Playing cards was on the agenda, as well as learning to play mahjong. (13 words)
cn: 打牌和学习打麻将都在议程上。

en: Rodriguez says it's important that residents here don't feel like he's selling them something. (14 words)
cn: 罗德里格斯说，这里的居民不要觉得他在向他们推销产品，这一点很重要。

en: I've had more feedback in a passive approach, he says. (10 words)
cn: 他说：‘我通过被动的方式获得了更多的反馈。’

en: Playing pool, playing cards, having dinner, having lunch, all work better 'than going through a survey of questions. (18 words)
cn: ‘打台球、打牌、吃晚饭、吃午饭，都比做问卷调查效果好。’

en: When they get to know me and to trust me, knowing for sure I'm not selling them something—there'll be more honest feedback from them.' (24 words)
cn: ‘当他们了解我并信任我，确信我不是在向他们推销东西时，他们会给出更诚实的反馈。’

en: Rodriguez is just the seventh entrepreneur to move into one of Brookdale's 1,100 senior living communities. (16 words)
cn: 罗德里格斯只是入住Brookdale的1,100个老年生活社区之一的第七位企业家。

en: Other new products in the program have included a kind of full-body blow dryer and specially designed clothing that allows people with disabilities to dress and undress themselves. (28 words)
cn: 该项目中的其他新产品包括一种全身吹风机和专为残疾人设计的、让他们能够自己穿脱衣服的服装。

en: Mary Lou Busch, 93, agreed to try the Sentab system. (10 words)
cn: 93岁的玛丽·卢·布希同意试用Sentab系统。

en: She tells Rodriguez that it might be good for someone, but not for her. (14 words)
cn: 她告诉罗德里格斯，这对某些人可能有用，但对她来说不适合。

en: I have the computer and FaceTime, which I talk with my family on, she explains. (15 words)
cn: 她解释道：‘我有电脑和FaceTime，用来和家人通话。’

en: She also has an iPad and a smartphone. (8 words)
cn: 她还有一台iPad和一部智能手机。

en: So I do pretty much everything I need to do. (10 words)
cn: ‘所以我能做几乎所有我需要做的事情。’

en: To be fair, if Rodriguez had wanted feedback from some more technophobic seniors, he might have ended up in the wrong Brookdale community. (23 words)
cn: 公平地说，如果罗德里格斯想要从一些更害怕技术的老年人那里获得反馈，他可能选错了Brookdale社区。

en: This one is located in the heart of Southern California's aerospace corridor. (12 words)
cn: 这个社区位于南加州航空航天走廊的中心地带。

en: Many residents have backgrounds in engineering, business and academic circles. (10 words)
cn: 许多居民有工程、商业和学术界的背景。

en: But Rodriguez says he's still learning something important by moving into this Brookdale community: 'People are more tech-proficient than we thought.' (21 words)
cn: 但罗德里格斯说，他通过搬进Brookdale社区仍然学到了一些重要的东西：‘人们比我们想象中更精通技术。’

en: And besides, where else would he learn to play mahjong? (10 words)
cn: 此外，他还能在哪儿学打麻将呢？

en: The dream of personalised flight is still vivid in the minds of many inventors, some developing cycle-powered craft, others pouring money into jetpacks. (23 words)
cn: 个性化飞行的梦想在许多发明家的脑海中仍然生动，有些人在开发自行车动力飞行器，另一些人则将资金投入喷气背包。

en: However, the flying car has always remained the ultimate symbol of personal transport freedom. (14 words)
cn: 然而，飞行汽车始终是个人交通自由的终极象征。

en: Several companies around the world have produced prototypes that can drive on roads and fly. (15 words)
cn: 世界各地有几家公司已经生产出可以在道路上行驶和飞行的原型车。

en: Airbus has a futuristic modular concept involving a passenger capsule that can be detached from the road-going chassis and picked up by a helicopter-type machine. (25 words)
cn: 空客有一个未来派的模块化概念，涉及一个乘客舱，该乘客舱可以从公路底盘上分离，并由直升机式机器接走。

en: But all these concepts are massively expensive, require safety certification standards for road and air, need autonomous controls, involve complex folding wings and propellers, and have to be flown from air-strips. (31 words)
cn: 但所有这些概念都极其昂贵，需要道路和空中安全认证标准，需要自主控制，涉及复杂的折叠机翼和螺旋桨，并且必须从机场跑道起飞。

en: So they are likely to remain rich people's playthings rather than practical transport solutions for the masses. (17 words)
cn: 因此，它们很可能仍然是富人的玩具，而不是大众的实用交通解决方案。

en: A car that takes off from some London street and lands in another random street is unlikely to happen, says Prof. Gray, a leading aeronautical engineer. (26 words)
cn: 领先的航空工程师格雷教授说：‘一辆从伦敦某条街道起飞并降落在另一条随机街道上的汽车不太可能实现。’

en: Sky taxis are much more likely. (6 words)
cn: ‘空中出租车更有可能实现。’

en: But that won't stop inventors from dreaming up new ways to fly and trying to persuade investors to back their sometimes outrageous schemes. (23 words)
cn: 但这不会阻止发明家们构想新的飞行方式，并试图说服投资者支持他们有时十分离谱的计划。
