en: Civilian aviation is being disrupted, not by the age-old desires for speed, romanticism and glamour, but by the pressing need to respond to a changing climate. (26 words)
cn: 民用航空正在被颠覆，不是被对速度、浪漫主义和魅力的古老渴望所颠覆，而是被应对气候变化的迫切需求所颠覆。

en: New electric engines coupled with artificial intelligence and dual systems will contribute to a more efficient, integrated transport system that is less polluting and less noisy. (26 words)
cn: 新电动机与人工智能和双重系统相结合，将有助于建立一个更高效、更集成、污染更少、噪音更小的交通系统。

en: That may sound simple, but as Prof. Gray says, 'When I travel somewhere I like this notion that when I finish my journey I feel better than when I started it.' (31 words)
cn: 这听起来可能很简单，但正如格雷教授所说：‘当我去某个地方旅行时，我喜欢这样的想法：当我结束旅程时，我感觉比出发时更好。’

en: That's completely at odds with how I feel today. (9 words)
cn: ‘这与我今天的感受完全相反。’

en: Now that would be progress. (5 words)
cn: 那才是进步。

en: As consumers, we are very wasteful. (6 words)
cn: 作为消费者，我们非常浪费。

en: Annually, the world generates 1.3 billion tons of solid waste. (10 words)
cn: 每年，世界产生13亿吨固体废物。

en: This is expected to go up to 2.2 billion by 2025. (11 words)
cn: 预计到2025年，这一数字将增至22亿吨。

en: The developed countries are responsible for 44% of waste, and in the U.S. alone, the average person throws away their body weight in rubbish every month. (26 words)
cn: 发达国家占废物的44%，仅在美国，平均每人每月就扔掉相当于自身体重的垃圾。

en: Conventional wisdom would seem to suggest that companies have no incentive to lengthen the life cycle of their products and reduce the revenue they would get from selling new goods. (30 words)
cn: 传统观点似乎表明，公司没有动力延长产品的生命周期，也没有动力减少销售新产品所带来的收入。

en: Yet, more and more businesses are thinking about how to reduce consumer waste. (13 words)
cn: 然而，越来越多的企业正在思考如何减少消费者浪费。

en: This is partly driven by the rising price of raw materials and metals. (13 words)
cn: 这部分是受原材料和金属价格上涨的推动。

en: It is also partly due to both consumers and companies becoming more aware of the need to protect our environment. (20 words)
cn: 也部分归因于消费者和公司都越来越意识到保护环境的必要性。

en: When choosing what products to buy and which brands to buy from, more and more consumers are looking into sustainability. (20 words)
cn: 在选择购买什么产品和购买哪些品牌时，越来越多的消费者正在关注可持续性。

en: This is opposed to just price and performance they were concerned about in the past. (15 words)
cn: 这与他们过去只关注价格和性能不同。

en: In a survey of 54 of the world's leading brands, almost all of them reported that consumers are showing increasing care about sustainable lifestyles. (24 words)
cn: 在对世界54家领先品牌进行的一项调查中，几乎所有品牌都报告说，消费者越来越关注可持续的生活方式。

en: At the same time, surveys on consumers in the U.S. and the U.K. show that they also care about minimizing energy use and reducing waste. (25 words)
cn: 与此同时，对美国消费者的调查发现，他们也关心尽量减少能源使用和减少浪费。

en: For the most part, consumers control what happens to a product. (11 words)
cn: 在大多数情况下，消费者控制着产品的最终去向。

en: But some companies are realizing that placing the burden of recycling entirely on the consumer is not an effective strategy, especially when tossing something away seems like the easiest and most convenient option. (33 words)
cn: 但一些公司正在意识到，将回收的全部负担放在消费者身上并不是一个有效的策略，尤其是在丢弃东西似乎是最简单、最方便的选择时。

en: Some retailers and manufacturers in the clothing, footwear, and electronics industries have launched environmental programs. (15 words)
cn: 服装、鞋类和电子行业的一些零售商和制造商已经启动了环保计划。

en: They want to make their customers interested in preserving their products and preventing things that still have value from going to the garbage dump. (24 words)
cn: 他们想让客户对保护他们的产品感兴趣，并防止仍有价值的东西被扔进垃圾堆。

en: By offering services to help expand the longevity of their products, they're promising quality and durability to consumers, and receiving the reputational gains for being environmentally friendly. (27 words)
cn: 通过提供有助于延长产品寿命的服务，他们向消费者承诺质量和耐用性，并获得环保带来的声誉收益。

en: For example, the Swedish jeans company Nudie Jeans offers free repair at twenty of their shops. (16 words)
cn: 例如，瑞典牛仔公司Nudie Jeans在其二十家门店提供免费维修服务。

en: Instead of discarding their old worn-out jeans, customers bring them in to be renewed. (14 words)
cn: 顾客不会丢弃旧的破旧牛仔裤，而是把它们带来进行翻新。

en: The company even provides mail-order repair kits and online videos, so that customers can learn how to fix a pair of jeans at home. (24 words)
cn: 该公司甚至提供邮购维修套件和在线视频，让顾客可以在家学习如何修复牛仔裤。

en: Their philosophy is that extending the life of a pair of jeans is not only great for the environment, but allows the consumer to get more value out of their product. (31 words)
cn: 他们的理念是，延长牛仔裤的使用寿命不仅对环境有益，而且还能让消费者从产品中获得更多价值。

en: When customers do want to toss their pair, they can give them back to the store, which will repurpose and resell them. (22 words)
cn: 当顾客确实想要丢弃他们的牛仔裤时，他们可以将其送回商店，商店会重新利用并转售。

en: Another clothing company, Patagonia, a high-end outdoor clothing store, follows the same principle. (13 words)
cn: 另一家服装公司Patagonia，一家高端户外服装店，也遵循同样的原则。

en: It has partnered with DIY website iFixit to teach consumers how to repair their clothing, such as waterproof outerwear, at home. (21 words)
cn: 它与DIY网站iFixit合作，教消费者如何在家修理他们的服装，例如防水外套。

en: The company also offers a repair program for their customers for a modest fee. (14 words)
cn: 该公司还为客户提供收费合理的维修服务。

en: Currently, Patagonia repairs about 40,000 garments a year in their Reno, Nevada, service center. (14 words)
cn: 目前，Patagonia每年在内华达州里诺的服务中心修复约4万件服装。

en: According to the company's CEO, Rose Marcario, this is about building a company that cares about the environment. (18 words)
cn: 据该公司首席执行官罗斯·马卡里奥称，这是关于建立一家关心环境的公司。

en: At the same time, offering repair supports the perceived quality of its products. (13 words)
cn: 同时，提供维修服务也支撑了其产品的感知质量。

en: In Brazil, the multinational corporation Adidas has been running a shoe-recycling program called 'Sustainable Footprint' since 2012. (17 words)
cn: 在巴西，跨国公司阿迪达斯自2012年以来一直在运营一项名为‘可持续足迹’的鞋子回收计划。

en: Customers can bring shoes of any brand into an Adidas store to be shredded and turned into alternative fuels for energy creation instead of being burned as trash. (28 words)
cn: 顾客可以将任何品牌的鞋子带到阿迪达斯门店，将其粉碎并转化为替代燃料用于能源生产，而不是作为垃圾焚烧。

en: They are used to fuel cement ovens. (7 words)
cn: 它们被用来为水泥窑提供燃料。

en: To motivate visitors to bring in more old shoes, Adidas Brazil promotes the program in stores by showing videos to educate customers, and it even offers a discount each time a customer brings in an old pair of shoes. (39 words)
cn: 为了激励顾客带来更多的旧鞋，阿迪达斯巴西在店内通过播放视频教育顾客来推广该计划，甚至每次顾客带来一双旧鞋时都会提供折扣。

en: This boosts the reputation and image of Adidas by making people more aware of the company's values. (17 words)
cn: 这通过让人们更加了解公司的价值观来提升阿迪达斯的声誉和形象。

en: Enormous opportunities also lie with e-waste. (6 words)
cn: 电子垃圾中也蕴藏着巨大的机会。

en: It is estimated that in 2014 the world produced some 42 million metric tons of e-waste (discarded electrical and electronic equipment and its parts) with North America and Europe accounting for 8 and 12 million metric tons respectively. (38 words)
cn: 据估计，2014年全球产生了约4200万吨电子垃圾（废弃的电气和电子设备及其部件），其中北美和欧洲分别占800万和1200万吨。

en: The materials from e-waste include iron, copper, gold, silver, and aluminum materials that could be reused, resold, salvaged, or recycled. (20 words)
cn: 电子垃圾中的材料包括铁、铜、金、银和铝，这些材料可以重复使用、转售、回收或再生。

en: Together, the value of these metals is estimated to be about $52 billion. (13 words)
cn: 这些金属的总价值估计约为520亿美元。

en: Electronics giants like Best Buy and Samsung have provided e-waste take-back programs over the past few years, which aim to refurbish old electronic components and parts into new products. (29 words)
cn: 像Best Buy和三星这样的电子巨头在过去几年中提供了电子垃圾回收计划，旨在将旧的电子元器件翻新为新产品的部件。

en: For other companies interested in reducing waste, helping the environment, and providing the sustainable lifestyles that consumers seek, here are some first steps for building a relationship with customers that focuses on recycling and restoring value to products. (38 words)
cn: 对于其他有意减少浪费、帮助环境和提供消费者所寻求的可持续生活方式的公司来说，以下是建立客户关系的首要步骤，重点在于回收和恢复产品的价值。

en: Find partners. (2 words)
cn: 寻找合作伙伴。

en: If you are a manufacturer who relies on outside distributors, then retailers are the ideal partner for collecting old products. (20 words)
cn: 如果你是一家依赖外部经销商的制造商，那么零售商是收集旧产品的理想合作伙伴。

en: Power tool maker DeWalt partners with companies, such as Lowes and Napa Auto Parts, to collect old tools at their stores for recycling. (23 words)
cn: 电动工具制造商DeWalt与Lowes和Napa Auto Parts等公司合作，在它们的商店收集旧工具进行回收。

en: The partnership benefits both sides by allowing unconventional partners (for example, two companies from two different industries) to work together on a specific aspect of the value chain, like, in this example, an engine firm with an accessory one. (39 words)
cn: 这种合作关系使双方受益，它允许非传统合作伙伴（例如来自两个不同行业的两家公司）在价值链的特定方面合作，例如在这个例子中，一家发动机公司与一家配件公司合作。

en: Create incentives. (2 words)
cn: 创造激励措施。

en: Environmental conscientiousness isn't always enough to make customers recycle old goods. (11 words)
cn: 环保意识并不总是足以让顾客回收旧物品。

en: For instance, DeWalt discovered that many contractors were holding on to their old tools, even if they no longer worked, because they were expensive purchases and it was hard to justify bringing them in to recycle. (36 words)
cn: 例如，DeWalt发现许多承包商即使旧工具已经无法使用也仍然留着它们，因为这些工具价格昂贵，很难有足够的理由把它们送去回收。

en: By offering instant discounts worth as much as $100, DeWalt launched a trade-in program to encourage people to bring back tools. (21 words)
cn: 通过提供高达100美元的即时折扣，DeWalt推出了以旧换新计划，鼓励人们带回旧工具。

en: As a result, DeWalt now reuses those materials to create new products. (12 words)
cn: 因此，DeWalt现在重复使用这些材料来制造新产品。

en: Start with a trial program, and expect to change the details as you go. (14 words)
cn: 从试验计划开始，并随着进展调整细节。

en: Any take-back program will likely change over time, depending on what works for your customers and company goals. (18 words)
cn: 任何回收计划都可能随着时间的推移而变化，这取决于对客户和公司目标有效的因素。

en: Maybe you see low customer participation at first, or conversely, so much success that the cost of recycling becomes too high. (21 words)
cn: 也许你一开始看到客户参与度很低，或者相反，取得如此大的成功以至于回收成本变得过高。

en: Best Buy, for instance, has been bearing the lion's share of e-waste volume since two of its largest competitors, Amazon and Wal-mart, do not have their own recycling programs. (29 words)
cn: 例如，Best Buy一直承担着电子垃圾处理的主要份额，因为其两个最大的竞争对手亚马逊和沃尔玛没有自己的回收计划。

en: Since the launch of its program, Best Buy changed its policy to add a $25 fee for recycling old televisions in order to keep the program going. (27 words)
cn: 自其计划启动以来，Best Buy改变了政策，为回收旧电视增加了25美元的费用，以维持该计划的运行。

en: Build a culture of collective values with customers. (8 words)
cn: 与客户建立共同价值观的文化。

en: A stronger relationship between the retailer/producer and the consumer isn't just about financial incentives. (14 words)
cn: 零售商/生产商与消费者之间更牢固的关系不仅仅是金钱激励。

en: By creating more awareness around your efforts to reduce waste, and by developing a culture of responsibility, repair, and reuse, you can build customer loyalty based on shared values and responsibilities. (31 words)
cn: 通过在减少废物的努力方面提高认知度，并培养责任、维修和再利用的文化，你可以在共同价值观和责任感的基础上建立客户忠诚度。

en: These examples are just the tip of the iceberg, but they demonstrate how helping customers get more use of their materials can transform value chains and operations. (27 words)
cn: 这些例子只是冰山一角，但它们展示了帮助客户更多地利用他们的材料如何能够改变价值链和运营。

en: Reducing waste by incorporating used materials into production can cut costs and decrease the price of procurement: less to be procured from the outside and more to be re-utilized from the inside. (32 words)
cn: 通过将使用过的材料纳入生产来减少浪费可以降低成本并降低采购价格：从外部采购的更少，从内部重复利用的更多。

en: Companies play a big role in creating a circular economy, in which value is generated less from extracting new resources and more from getting better use out of the resources we already have—but they must also get customers engaged in the process. (42 words)
cn: 公司在创造循环经济中扮演着重要角色，在循环经济中，价值更多地来自更好地利用我们已有的资源，而不是开采新资源——但公司还必须让客户参与其中。

en: Effective Friday, Screen Actors Guild-American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA) has declared a strike against 11 video game publishers over games that went into production after Feb. 17, 2015. (31 words)
cn: 自上周五起，美国演员工会-美国电视和广播艺人联合会（SAG-AFTRA）已宣布对11家视频游戏发行商发起罢工，涉及2015年2月17日之后投入生产的游戏。

en: The companies include some of the heavyweights of the industry, like Electronic Arts Productions, Insomniac Games, Activision and Disney. (19 words)
cn: 这些公司包括业内的一些巨头，如Electronic Arts Productions、Insomniac Games、Activision和Disney。

en: The strike comes in light of an unsuccessful 19 months of negotiations after the existing labor contract known as the Interactive Media Agreement expired in late 2014. (27 words)
cn: 此次罢工是由于2014年底到期的现有劳动合同（即互动媒体协议）之后长达19个月的谈判未果。

en: Overall, the strike is an effort to provide more secondary compensation along with other concerns, such as transparency upon hiring talent and on-set safety precautions. (25 words)
cn: 总体而言，此次罢工是为了争取更多的追加报酬，以及解决其他关切，如招聘人才时的透明度和制作现场的安全预防措施。

en: The video gaming industry has ballooned in recent years. (9 words)
cn: 近年来，电子游戏产业急剧扩张。

en: The Los Angeles Times reports that the industry is in the midst of an intense increase in cash flow. (19 words)
cn: 《洛杉矶时报》报道称，该行业正处于现金流急剧增长之中。

en: In 2015, gaming produced $23.5 billion in domestic revenue. (9 words)
cn: 2015年，游戏产业在国内创造了235亿美元的收入。

en: But SAG-AFTRA says voice actors don't receive residuals for their gaming work. (12 words)
cn: 但SAG-AFTRA表示，配音演员的配音工作没有追加报酬。

en: Instead, they receive a fixed rate, which is typically about $825 for a standard four-hour vocal session. (17 words)
cn: 相反，他们获得固定报酬，通常一次标准的四小时配音工作约为825美元。

en: So the voice actors are pushing for the idea of secondary compensation—a performance bonus every time a game sells 2 million copies or downloads, or reaches 2 million subscribers, with a cap at 8 million. (35 words)
cn: 因此，配音演员们正在推动追加报酬的想法——每当一款游戏售出或下载量达到200万，或订阅用户达到200万时，就获得一次绩效奖金，上限为800万。

en: It's a very small number of games that would trigger this secondary compensation issue, said voice actor Crispin Freeman, who's a member of the union's negotiating committee. (27 words)
cn: 工会谈判委员会成员、配音演员克里斯平·弗里曼说：‘会触发追加报酬问题的游戏数量很少。’

en: This is an important aspect of what it means to be a freelance performer, who isn't regularly employed every single day working on projects. (24 words)
cn: ‘这是作为自由职业表演者意义的一个重要方面——他们并非每天都有固定的项目工作。’

en: Another major complaint from the actors is the secrecy of the industry. (12 words)
cn: 演员们的另一个主要不满是行业的不透明性。

en: I can't imagine if there's any other acting job in the world where you don't know what show you're in, when you're hired, says voice actor Keythe Farley, who chairs the SAG-AFTRA negotiating committee. (34 words)
cn: SAG-AFTRA谈判委员会主席、配音演员基思·法利说：‘我无法想象世界上还有哪种表演工作，当你被雇佣时，你不知道自己参演的是什么节目。’

en: And yet that happens every day in the video game world, Farley told reporters during a press conference Friday. (19 words)
cn: 法利在周五的新闻发布会上告诉记者：‘然而这种情况在电子游戏界每天都在发生。’

en: I was a main character in Fallout 4, a character by the name of Kellogg, and I never knew that I was doing vocal recording for that game throughout the year and a half. (34 words)
cn: ‘我是《辐射4》中的一个主要角色，一个叫凯洛格的角色，而我在整整一年半的时间里都不知道自己在为那款游戏做配音。’

en: Scott Witlin, the lawyer representing the video game companies, says voice actors 'represent less than one tenth of 1 percent of the work that goes into making a video game.' (30 words)
cn: 代表视频游戏公司的律师斯科特·威特林表示，配音演员‘占游戏制作总工作量不到千分之一’。

en: So 'even though they're the top craftsmen in their field,' Witlin says, 'if we pay them under a vastly different system than the people who do the 99.9 percent of the work, that's going to create far more problems for the video game companies.' (44 words)
cn: 威特林说：‘因此，即使他们是各自领域顶尖的工匠，如果我们用一种与承担99.9%工作的人截然不同的薪酬体系来支付他们的报酬，这会给视频游戏公司带来更多的问题。’

en: Officials at the White House announced a new space policy focused on managing the increasing number of satellites that companies and governments are launching into space. (26 words)
cn: 白宫官员宣布了一项新的太空政策，重点管理公司和政府发射到太空的越来越多的卫星。

en: Space Policy Directive-3 lays out general guidelines for the United States to mitigate the effects of space debris and track and manage traffic in space. (25 words)
cn: 《太空政策指令-3》为美国制定了缓解太空碎片影响以及跟踪和管理太空交通的总体指导方针。

en: This policy sets the stage for the Department of Commerce to take over the management of traffic in space. (19 words)
cn: 这项政策为商务部接管太空交通管理奠定了基础。

en: The department will make sure that newly launched satellites don't use radio frequencies that would interfere with existing satellites, and schedule when such new satellites can be launched. (28 words)
cn: 该部门将确保新发射的卫星不使用会干扰现有卫星的无线电频率，并安排新卫星的发射时间。

en: This only applies to American space activities, but the hope is that it will help standardize a set of norms in the dawning commercial spaceflight industry throughout the world. (29 words)
cn: 这仅适用于美国的太空活动，但希望它能有助于在全球新兴的商业航天产业中标准化一套规范。

en: Space, especially the space directly around our planet, is getting more crowded as more governments and companies launch satellites. (19 words)
cn: 随着越来越多的政府和公司发射卫星，太空，尤其是地球周围的太空，正变得越来越拥挤。

en: One impetus for the policy is that companies are already starting to build massive constellations, comprising hundreds or thousands of satellites with many moving parts among them. (27 words)
cn: 这项政策的一个推动因素是，公司已经开始建造大规模的卫星星座，包含数百或数千颗卫星，其中有许多活动部件。

en: With so much stuff in space, and a limited area around our planet, the government wants to reduce the chances of a collision. (23 words)
cn: 太空中有这么多的物体，而地球周围的区域有限，政府希望降低碰撞的可能性。

en: Two or more satellites slamming into each other could create many more out-of-control bits that would pose even more hazards to the growing collection of satellites in space. (28 words)
cn: 两颗或多颗卫星相撞会产生更多失控碎片，对太空中日益增多的卫星群构成更多危害。

en: And it's not like this hasn't happened before. (8 words)
cn: 而且这并非没有发生过。

en: In 2009 an old Russian craft slammed into a communications satellite, creating a cloud of hundreds of pieces of debris and putting other hardware at risk. (26 words)
cn: 2009年，一艘俄罗斯旧航天器撞上了一颗通信卫星，产生了数百块碎片云，并使其他硬件面临风险。

en: Journalist Sarah Scoles reports that NASA currently tracks about 24,000 objects in space, and in 2016 the Air Force had to issue 3,995,874 warnings to satellite owners alerting them to a potential nearby threat from another satellite or bit of debris. (41 words)
cn: 记者莎拉·斯科尔斯报道说，NASA目前追踪太空中约24,000个物体，而在2016年，空军不得不向卫星所有者发出3,995,874次警告，提醒他们附近可能存在来自另一颗卫星或碎片的威胁。

en: That's why this new policy also includes directions to update the current U.S. Government Orbital Debris Mitigation Standard Practices, which already require any entity that launches a satellite or spacecraft to vigorously analyze the likelihood that any of their actions, from an unexpected failure or normal operations, will create more space debris. (52 words)
cn: 这就是为什么这项新政策还包括更新当前美国政府轨道碎片减缓标准实践的方向，该标准已经要求任何发射卫星或航天器的实体都要积极分析其任何行动——从意外故障到正常操作——产生更多太空碎片的可能性。

en: It includes accounting for any piece of debris they plan to release over 5mm that might stay in orbit for 25 years or more. (24 words)
cn: 它包括核算他们计划释放的超过5毫米、可能在轨道上停留25年或更长时间的任何碎片。

en: It might seem surprising to think about an item staying in space for that long, but the oldest satellite still in orbit—Vanguard 1—turned 60 in 2018. (26 words)
cn: 想到一个物体在太空中停留那么长时间可能会让人感到惊讶，但仍在轨道上的最古老卫星——先锋1号——在2018年已经60岁了。

en: Agencies and companies throughout the world are working on developing technology that would dispose of or capture space debris before it causes serious damage. (24 words)
cn: 世界各地的机构和公司正在致力于开发技术，以便在太空碎片造成严重损害之前对其进行处理或捕获。

en: But for now, the U.S. government is more focused on preventing new debris from forming than taking the trash out of orbit. (22 words)
cn: 但目前，美国政府更侧重于防止新碎片的形成，而不是将垃圾清除出轨道。

en: Steel is valued for its reliability, but not when it gets cold. (12 words)
cn: 钢材因其可靠性而受到重视，但在低温环境下则不然。

en: Most forms of steel abruptly become brittle at temperatures below about -25℃ unless they are mixed with other metals. (19 words)
cn: 大多数钢材在大约零下25摄氏度以下时会突然变脆，除非它们与其他金属混合。

en: Now, though, a novel type of steel has been developed that resists fractures at much lower temperatures, while retaining its strength and toughness—without the need for expensive additives. (28 words)
cn: 然而，现在一种新型钢材已被开发出来，它能在更低的温度下抵抗断裂，同时保持其强度和韧性——且无需昂贵的添加剂。

en: Steel's fragility at low temperatures first became a major concern during the Second World War. (15 words)
cn: 钢材在低温下的脆性在第二次世界大战期间首次成为一个主要问题。

en: After German U-boats torpedoed numerous British ships, a 2700-strong fleet of cheap-and-cheerful 'Liberty ships' was introduced to replace the lost vessels, providing a lifeline for the besieged British. (28 words)
cn: 在德国U型潜艇用鱼雷击沉了大量英国船只后，一支由2700艘廉价而实用的“自由轮”组成的船队被引入以取代损失的船只，为被围困的英国人提供了生命线。

en: But the steel shells of hundreds of the ships cracked in the icy north Atlantic, and 12 broke in half and sank. (22 words)
cn: 但数百艘船只的钢壳在冰冷的北大西洋中开裂，其中12艘断裂成两半并沉没。

en: Brittleness remains a problem when building steel structures in cold conditions, such as oil rigs in the Arctic. (18 words)
cn: 在寒冷条件下建造钢结构时，脆性仍然是一个问题，例如北极的石油钻井平台。

en: So scientists have strived to find a solution by mixing it with expensive metals such as nickel. (17 words)
cn: 因此，科学家们努力通过将其与镍等昂贵金属混合来寻找解决方案。

en: Yuuji Kimura and colleagues in Japan tried a more physical approach. (11 words)
cn: 日本的木村雄二及其同事尝试了一种更物理的方法。

en: Rather than adding other metals, they developed a complex mechanical process involving repeated heating and very severe mechanical deformation, known as temp forming. (23 words)
cn: 他们没有添加其他金属，而是开发了一种复杂的机械工艺，涉及反复加热和非常剧烈的机械变形，称为“形变热处理”。

en: The resulting steel appears to achieve a combination of strength and toughness that is comparable to that of modern steels that are very rich in alloy content and, therefore, very expensive. (31 words)
cn: 由此产生的钢材似乎实现了强度和韧性的结合，可与合金含量非常高、因此非常昂贵的现代钢材相媲美。

en: Kimura's team intends to use its tempformed steel to make ultra-high strength parts, such as bolts. (16 words)
cn: 木村团队打算使用其形变热处理钢材制造超高强度部件，如螺栓。

en: They hope to reduce both the number of components needed in a construction job and their weight—by replacing solid supports with hollow tubes, for example. (25 words)
cn: 他们希望通过用空心管代替实心支撑等方式，减少建筑工程所需部件的数量及其重量。

en: This could reduce the amount of steel needed to make everything from automobiles to buildings and bridges. (17 words)
cn: 这可以减少从汽车到建筑物和桥梁等各种制造所需的钢材用量。

en: Satellites used to be the exclusive playthings of rich governments and wealthy corporations. (13 words)
cn: 卫星曾经是富有的政府和富裕的企业的专属玩物。

en: But increasingly, as space becomes more democratized, they are coming within reach of ordinary people. (15 words)
cn: 但如今，随着太空日益民主化，它们正在进入普通人的视野。

en: Just like drones before them, miniature satellites are beginning to fundamentally transform our conceptions of who gets to do what up above our heads. (24 words)
cn: 就像之前的无人机一样，微型卫星正开始从根本上改变我们对谁能在我们头顶上空做什么的认知。

en: As a recent report from the National Academy of Sciences highlights, these satellites hold tremendous potential for making satellite-based science more accessible than ever before. (25 words)
cn: 正如美国国家科学院最近的一份报告所强调的，这些卫星在使基于卫星的科学变得比以往任何时候都更容易获取方面具有巨大潜力。

en: However, as the cost of getting your own satellite in orbit drops sharply, the risks of irresponsible use grow. (19 words)
cn: 然而，随着将自己卫星送入轨道的成本急剧下降，不负责任使用的风险也在增加。

en: The question here is no longer 'Can we?' but 'Should we?' (11 words)
cn: 这里的问题不再是‘我们能吗？’而是‘我们应该吗？’

en: What are the potential downsides of having a slice of space densely populated by equipment built by people not traditionally labeled as 'professionals'? (23 words)
cn: 让一片太空区域被那些传统上不被视为‘专业人士’的人制造的设备所密集占据，潜在的负面影响是什么？

en: And what would the responsible and beneficial development and use of this technology actually look like? (16 words)
cn: 而负责任、有益地开发和使用这项技术实际上会是什么样的呢？

en: Some of the answers may come from a nonprofit organization that has been building and launching amateur satellites for nearly 50 years. (22 words)
cn: 部分答案可能来自一个近50年来一直在建造和发射业余卫星的非营利组织。

en: Having your personal satellite launched into orbit might sound like an idea straight out of science fiction. (17 words)
cn: 将你的个人卫星送入轨道可能听起来像是科幻小说中的想法。

en: But over the past few decades a unique class of satellites has been created that fits the bill: CubeSats. (19 words)
cn: 但在过去的几十年里，一种符合要求的独特卫星类型被创造出来：立方体卫星。

en: The 'Cube' here simply refers to the satellite's shape. (9 words)
cn: 这里的‘立方体’仅仅指的是卫星的形状。

en: The most common CubeSat is a 10cm cube, so small that a single CubeSat could easily be mistaken for a paperweight on your desk. (24 words)
cn: 最常见的立方体卫星是一个10厘米的立方体，小到一个立方体卫星很容易被误认为是桌上的镇纸。

en: These mini-satellites can fit in a launch vehicle's formerly 'wasted space.' (11 words)
cn: 这些微型卫星可以装入运载火箭以前‘浪费的空间’中。

en: Multiples can be deployed in combination for more complex missions than could be achieved by one CubeSat alone. (18 words)
cn: 多个立方体卫星可以组合部署，以完成比单个立方体卫星更复杂的任务。

en: Within their compact bodies these minute satellites are able to house sensors and communications receivers/transmitters that enable operators to study Earth from space, as well as space around Earth. (29 words)
cn: 在它们紧凑的机身内，这些微小卫星能够容纳传感器和通信接收器/发射器，使操作者能够从太空研究地球以及地球周围的太空。

en: They're primarily designed for Low Earth Orbit (LEO)—an easily accessible region of space from around 200 to 800 miles above Earth, where human-tended missions like the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station (ISS) hang out. (37 words)
cn: 它们主要设计用于低地球轨道（LEO）——一个距离地球约200至800英里、易于到达的太空区域，哈勃太空望远镜和国际空间站等有人维护的任务就在那里。

en: But they can attain more distant orbits; NASA plans for most of its future Earth-escaping payloads (to the moon and Mars especially) to carry CubeSats. (25 words)
cn: 但它们可以到达更远的轨道；NASA计划其未来大多数逃离地球的载荷（特别是前往月球和火星的）都携带立方体卫星。

en: Because they're so small and light, it costs much less to get a CubeSat into Earth's orbit than a traditional communications or GPS satellite. (24 words)
cn: 因为它们非常小而且轻，将一颗立方体卫星送入地球轨道的成本远低于传统通信或GPS卫星。

en: For instance, a research group here at Arizona State University recently claimed their developmental small CubeSats could cost as little as $3,000 to put in orbit. (26 words)
cn: 例如，亚利桑那州立大学的一个研究小组最近声称，他们开发的小型立方体卫星送入轨道的成本可能低至3,000美元。

en: This decrease in cost allows researchers, hobbyists and even elementary school groups to put simple instruments into LEO or even having them deployed from the ISS. (26 words)
cn: 成本的降低使研究人员、爱好者甚至小学生团体能够将简单的仪器送入低地球轨道，甚至从国际空间站部署它们。

en: The first CubeSat was created in the early 2000s, as a way of enabling Stanford graduate students to design, build, test and operate a spacecraft with similar capabilities to the USSR's Sputnik. (32 words)
cn: 第一颗立方体卫星创建于21世纪初，目的是让斯坦福大学的研究生能够设计、建造、测试和操作一艘与前苏联人造卫星能力相当的航天器。

en: Since then, NASA, the National Reconnaissance Office and even Boeing have all launched and operated CubeSats. (16 words)
cn: 从那时起，NASA、国家侦察局甚至波音公司都发射和运营过立方体卫星。

en: There are more than 130 currently in operation. (8 words)
cn: 目前有130多颗在运行中。

en: The NASA Educational Launch of Nano Satellite program, which offers free launches for educational groups and science missions, is now open to U.S. nonprofit corporations as well. (27 words)
cn: NASA的纳米卫星教育发射计划为教育团体和科学任务提供免费发射服务，现在也向美国非营利企业开放。

en: Clearly, satellites are not just for rocket scientists anymore. (9 words)
cn: 显然，卫星不再只是火箭科学家的专属了。

en: The National Academy of Sciences report emphasizes CubeSats' importance in scientific discovery and the training of future space scientists and engineers. (21 words)
cn: 美国国家科学院的报告强调了立方体卫星在科学发现和培训未来太空科学家及工程师方面的重要性。

en: Yet it also acknowledges that widespread deployment of LEO CubeSats isn't risk-free. (12 words)
cn: 但它也承认，低地球轨道立方体卫星的广泛部署并非没有风险。

en: The greatest concern the authors raise is space debris—pieces of 'junk' that orbit the earth, with the potential to cause serious damage if they collide with operational units, including the ISS. (31 words)
cn: 作者提出的最大担忧是太空碎片——绕地球运行的‘垃圾’碎片，如果它们与包括国际空间站在内的运行单元相撞，可能造成严重损害。

en: Currently, there aren't many CubeSats and they're tracked closely. (9 words)
cn: 目前，立方体卫星的数量不多，并且它们受到密切跟踪。

en: Yet as LEO opens up to more amateur satellites, they may pose an increasing threat. (15 words)
cn: 然而，随着低地球轨道向更多业余卫星开放，它们可能构成越来越大的威胁。

en: As the report authors point out, even near-misses might lead to the 'creation of a burdensome regulatory framework and affect the future disposition of science CubeSats.' (26 words)
cn: 正如报告作者指出的那样，即使是险撞也可能导致‘产生一个繁重的监管框架，并影响科学立方体卫星的未来配置’。

en: CubeSat researchers suggest that now's the time to ponder unexpected and unintended possible consequences of more people than ever having access to their own small slice of space. (28 words)
cn: 立方体卫星研究人员认为，现在是时候思考比以往任何时候都多的人能够进入自己那一小片太空所带来的意想不到的可能后果了。

en: In an era when you can simply buy a CubeSat kit off the shelf, how can we trust the satellites over our heads were developed with good intentions by people who knew what they were doing? (36 words)
cn: 在一个你可以直接从货架上购买立方体卫星套件的时代，我们怎么能相信我们头顶上的卫星是由那些知道自己在做什么的人出于善意开发的呢？

en: Some 'expert amateurs' in the satellite game could provide some inspiration for how to proceed responsibly. (16 words)
cn: 卫星领域的一些‘专业业余爱好者’可以为如何负责任地行事提供一些启示。

en: In 1969, the Radio Amateur Satellite Corporation (AMSAT) was created in order to foster ham radio enthusiasts' participation in space research and communication. (23 words)
cn: 1969年，业余无线电卫星公司（AMSAT）成立，旨在促进业余无线电爱好者参与太空研究和通信。

en: It continued the efforts, begun in 1961, by Project OSCAR—a U.S.-based group that built and launched the very first nongovernmental satellite just four years after Sputnik. (26 words)
cn: 它延续了OSCAR项目始于1961年的努力——OSCAR是一个总部位于美国的团体，在斯普特尼克号发射仅四年后就建造并发射了第一颗非政府卫星。

en: As an organization of volunteers, AMSAT was putting 'amateur' satellites in orbit decades before the current CubeSat craze. (18 words)
cn: 作为一个志愿者组织，AMSAT在当前的立方体卫星热潮之前几十年就已经将‘业余’卫星送入轨道。

en: And over time, its members have learned a thing or two about responsibility. (13 words)
cn: 随着时间的推移，其成员在责任方面学到了不少东西。

en: Here, open-source development has been a central principle. (8 words)
cn: 在这里，开源开发一直是一个核心原则。

en: Within the organization, AMSAT has a philosophy of open sourcing everything, making technical data on all aspects of their satellites fully available to everyone in the organization, and when possible, the public. (32 words)
cn: 在该组织内部，AMSAT奉行一切开源的理念，将其卫星各个方面的技术数据完全提供给组织内的每个人，并在可能的情况下向公众公开。

en: According to a member of the team responsible for FOX 1-A, AMSAT's first CubeSat, this means that there's no way to sneak something like explosives or an energy emitter into an amateur satellite when everyone has access to the designs and implementation. (42 words)
cn: 据负责AMSAT首颗立方体卫星FOX 1-A的团队成员称，这意味着当每个人都能接触到设计和实施细节时，就没有办法将炸药或能量发射器等物品偷偷放入业余卫星中。

en: However, they're more cautious about sharing information with nonmembers, as the organization guards against others developing the ability to hijack and take control of their satellites. (26 words)
cn: 然而，他们在与非成员分享信息方面更加谨慎，因为该组织防范他人发展出劫持和控制其卫星的能力。

en: This form of 'self-governance' is possible within long-standing amateur organizations that, over time, are able to build a sense of responsibility to community members, as well as society in general. (30 words)
cn: 这种形式的‘自治’在长期存在的业余组织中是可能的，这些组织随着时间的推移能够建立起对社区成员以及整个社会的责任感。

en: But what happens when new players emerge, who don't have deep roots within the existing culture? (16 words)
cn: 但当新的参与者出现，他们在现有文化中没有深厚根基时，会发生什么？

en: Hobbyists and students are gaining access to technologies without being part of a long-standing amateur establishment. (16 words)
cn: 爱好者和学生正在获得技术，而不属于长期存在的业余机构的一部分。

en: They're still constrained by funders, launch providers and a series of regulations—all of which rein in what CubeSat developers can and cannot do. (23 words)
cn: 他们仍然受到资助者、发射服务提供商和一系列法规的约束——所有这些都限制了立方体卫星开发者能做什么和不能做什么。

en: But there's a danger they're ill-equipped to think through potential unintended consequences. (12 words)
cn: 但存在一种危险，即他们没有足够的能力去充分考虑潜在的意外后果。

en: What these unintended consequences might be is admittedly far from clear. (11 words)
cn: 这些意外后果可能是什么，诚然还远不清楚。

en: Yet we know innovators can be remarkably creative with taking technologies in unexpected directions. (14 words)
cn: 但我们知道，创新者在将技术引向意想不到的方向方面可能非常有创造力。

en: Think of something as seemingly benign as the cellphone—we have microfinance and text-based social networking at one end of the spectrum, and improvised explosive devices at the other. (28 words)
cn: 想想像手机这样看似无害的东西——光谱的一端是小额信贷和基于文本的社交网络，另一端是简易爆炸装置。

en: This is where a culture of social responsibility around CubeSats becomes important—not simply to ensure that physical risks are minimized, but to engage with a much larger community in anticipating and managing less obvious consequences of the technology. (38 words)
cn: 这就是围绕立方体卫星建立社会责任文化变得重要的地方——不仅仅是确保物理风险最小化，而且要与更大的社区一起参与预测和管理这项技术不太明显的后果。

en: This is not an easy task. (6 words)
cn: 这不是一项容易的任务。

en: Yet the evidence from AMSAT and other areas of technology development suggests that responsible amateur communities can and do emerge around novel technologies. (23 words)
cn: 然而，来自AMSAT和其他技术发展领域的证据表明，负责任的业余爱好者社区能够并且确实在新兴技术周围出现。

en: The challenge here, of course, is ensuring that what an amateur community considers to be responsible, actually is. (18 words)
cn: 当然，这里的挑战是确保业余爱好者社区认为负责任的做法实际上确实如此。

en: Here's where there needs to be a much wider public conversation that extends beyond government agencies and scientific communities to include students, hobbyists, and anyone who may potentially stand to be affected by the use of CubeSat technology. (38 words)
cn: 这正是需要一场更广泛的公众对话的地方，这场对话应超越政府机构和科学界，涵盖学生、爱好者以及任何可能受到立方体卫星技术使用影响的人。

en: When I re-entered the full-time workforce a few years ago after a decade of solitary self-employment, there was one thing I was looking forward to the most: the opportunity to have work friends once again. (35 words)
cn: 几年前，在经历了十年的独自创业后，我重新进入全职职场时，最期待的一件事就是：再次拥有工作朋友的机会。

en: It wasn't until I entered the corporate world that I realized, for me at least, being friends with colleagues didn't emerge as a priority at all. (26 words)
cn: 直到我进入企业界，我才意识到，至少对我来说，与同事交朋友根本不是优先考虑的事情。

en: This is surprising when you consider the prevailing emphasis by scholars and trainers and managers on the importance of cultivating close interpersonal relationships at work. (25 words)
cn: 当你考虑到学者、培训师和管理者普遍强调在工作中培养亲密人际关系的重要性时，这令人惊讶。

en: So much research has explored the way in which collegial ties can help overcome a range of workplace issues affecting productivity and the quality of work output such as team-based conflict, jealousy, undermining, anger, and more. (36 words)
cn: 大量研究探索了同事关系如何帮助克服一系列影响生产率和工作产出质量的工作场所问题，如团队冲突、嫉妒、暗中破坏、愤怒等等。

en: Perhaps my expectations of lunches, water-cooler gossip and caring, deep-and-meaningful conversations were a legacy of the last time I was in that kind of office environment. (26 words)
cn: 也许我对午餐、茶水间八卦和关心、深入有意义的对话的期望，是我上次身处那种办公环境时留下的印记。

en: Whereas now, as I near the end of my fourth decade, I realize work can be fully functional and entirely fulfilling without needing to be best mates with the people sitting next to you. (34 words)
cn: 而现在，当我接近四十岁的尾声时，我意识到工作完全可以正常运转并完全令人满足，而无需与坐在你旁边的人成为最好的朋友。

en: In an academic analysis just published in the profoundly-respected Journal of Management, researchers have looked at the concept of 'indifferent relationships'. (21 words)
cn: 在刚刚发表在备受尊敬的《管理杂志》上的一篇学术分析中，研究人员研究了‘冷漠关系’的概念。

en: It's a simple term that encapsulates the fact that relationships at work can reasonably be non-intimate, inconsequential, unimportant and even, dare I say it, disposable or substitutable. (27 words)
cn: 这是一个简单的术语，概括了这样一个事实：工作中的关系可以合理地被看作是：非亲密的、无关紧要的、不重要的，甚至——我敢说——可抛弃的或可替代的。

en: Indifferent relationships are neither positive nor negative. (7 words)
cn: 冷漠关系既不是积极的，也不是消极的。

en: The limited research conducted thus far indicates they're especially dominant among those who value independence over cooperation, and harmony over confrontation. (21 words)
cn: 迄今为止进行的有限研究表明，它们在那些重视独立胜过合作、重视和谐胜过对抗的人中尤为突出。

en: Indifference is also the preferred option among those who are socially lazy. (12 words)
cn: 冷漠也是那些在社交上懒惰的人的首选。

en: Maintaining relationships over the long term takes effort. (8 words)
cn: 长期维持关系需要努力。

en: For some of us, too much effort. (7 words)
cn: 对我们中的一些人来说，是太多的努力。

en: As noted above, indifferent relationships may not always be the most helpful approach in resolving some of the issues that pop up at work. (24 words)
cn: 如上所述，冷漠关系并不总是解决工作中出现的一些问题的最有帮助的方法。

en: But there are nonetheless several empirically proven benefits. (8 words)
cn: 但尽管如此，还是有几个经过实证证明的好处。

en: One of those is efficiency. (5 words)
cn: 其中之一是效率。

en: Less time chatting and socializing means more time working and churning. (11 words)
cn: 少花时间聊天和社交意味着多花时间工作和产出。

en: The other is self-esteem. (4 words)
cn: 另一个是自尊。

en: As human beings, we're primed to compare ourselves to each other in what is an anxiety-inducing phenomenon. (17 words)
cn: 作为人类，我们天生就会在一种引发焦虑的现象中相互比较。

en: Apparently, we look down on acquaintances more so than friends. (10 words)
cn: 显然，我们更看不起熟人，而不是朋友。

en: Since the former is most common among those inclined towards indifferent relationships, their predominance can bolster individuals' sense of self-worth. (20 words)
cn: 由于前者在倾向于冷漠关系的人中最为常见，它们的普遍性可以增强个人的自我价值感。

en: Ego aside, a third advantage is that the emotional neutrality of indifferent relationships has been found to enhance critical evaluation, to strengthen one's focus on task resolution, and to gain greater access to valuable information. (35 words)
cn: 抛开自我不谈，第三个优势是，冷漠关系的情感中立性已被发现能增强批判性评估，加强人们对任务解决的专注，并更容易获取有价值的信息。

en: None of that might be as fun as after-work socializing but, hey, I'll take it anyway. (16 words)
cn: 这些可能都没有下班后的社交活动那么有趣，但是，嘿，我还是会接受的。

en: In a few decades, artificial intelligence (AI) will surpass many of the abilities that we believe make us special. (19 words)
cn: 在几十年内，人工智能将超越我们认为是使我们独特的能力中的许多项。

en: This is a grand challenge for our age and it may require an 'irrational' response. (15 words)
cn: 这是我们这个时代的一项重大挑战，它可能需要一种‘非理性’的回应。

en: One of the most significant pieces of news from the US in early 2017 was the efforts of Google to make autonomous driving a reality. (25 words)
cn: 2017年初来自美国的最重要新闻之一，就是谷歌为实现自动驾驶所做的努力。

en: According to a report, Google's self-driving cars clocked 1,023,330 km, and required human intervention 124 times. (16 words)
cn: 根据一份报告，谷歌的自动驾驶汽车行驶了1,023,330公里，需要人工干预124次。

en: That is one intervention about every 8,047 km of autonomous driving. (11 words)
cn: 这意味着大约每行驶8,047公里就需要一次干预。

en: But even more impressive is the progress in just a single year: human interventions fell from 0.8 times per thousand miles to 0.2, a 400% improvement. (26 words)
cn: 但更令人印象深刻的是仅在一年内取得的进展：人工干预从每千英里0.8次下降到0.2次，提高了400%。

en: With such progress, Google's cars will easily surpass my own driving ability later this year. (15 words)
cn: 有了这样的进展，谷歌的汽车将在今年晚些时候轻松超过我自己的驾驶能力。

en: Driving once seemed to be a very human skill. (9 words)
cn: 驾驶曾经似乎是一种非常人类化的技能。

en: But we said that about chess, too. (7 words)
cn: 但我们以前也这样说过国际象棋。

en: Then a computer beat the human world champion, repeatedly. (9 words)
cn: 然后计算机反复击败了人类世界冠军。

en: The board game Go took over from chess as a new test for human thinking in 2016, when a computer beat one of the world's leading professional Go players. (29 words)
cn: 2016年，围棋从国际象棋手中接过了作为人类思维新测试的接力棒，当时一台计算机击败了世界顶尖职业围棋选手之一。

en: With computers conquering what used to be deeply human tasks, what will it mean in the future to be human? (20 words)
cn: 随着计算机攻克了曾经被认为是深度人类任务的工作，未来成为人类意味着什么？

en: I worry about my six-year-old son. (6 words)
cn: 我为我六岁的儿子担心。

en: What will his place be in a world where machines beat us in one area after another? (17 words)
cn: 在一个机器在一个又一个领域击败我们的世界里，他的位置在哪里？

en: He'll never calculate faster, never drive better, or even fly more safely. (12 words)
cn: 他永远不会计算得更快，永远开得更好，甚至飞得更安全。

en: Actually, it all comes down to a fairly simple question: What's so special about us? (15 words)
cn: 实际上，这一切都归结为一个相当简单的问题：我们有什么特别之处？

en: It can't be skills like arithmetic, which machines already excel in. (11 words)
cn: 不可能是像算术这样的技能，机器在这方面已经很擅长了。

en: So far, machines have a pretty hard time emulating creativity, arbitrary enough not to be predicted by a computer, and yet more than simple randomness. (25 words)
cn: 到目前为止，机器在模仿创造力方面还相当困难，创造力足够任意，以至于计算机无法预测，但又不仅仅是简单的随机性。

en: Perhaps, if we continue to improve information-processing machines, we'll soon have helpful rational assistants. (14 words)
cn: 也许，如果我们继续改进信息处理机器，我们很快就会有有用的理性助手。

en: So we must aim to complement the rationality of the machine, rather than to compete with it. (17 words)
cn: 因此，我们的目标必须是补充机器的理性，而不是与之竞争。

en: If I'm right, we should foster a creative spirit because a dose of illogical creativity will complement the rationality of the machine. (22 words)
cn: 如果我是对的，我们应该培养一种创造精神，因为一点不合逻辑的创造力将补充机器的理性。

en: Unfortunately, however, our education system has not caught up to the approaching reality. (13 words)
cn: 然而，不幸的是，我们的教育体系还没有跟上即将到来的现实。

en: Indeed, our schools and universities are structured to mould pupils to be mostly obedient servants of rationality, and to develop outdated skills in interacting with outdated machines. (27 words)
cn: 事实上，我们的学校和大学的结构是为了将学生塑造成基本上是理性的顺从仆役，并培养与过时机器互动的过时技能。

en: We need to help our children learn how to best work with smart computers to improve human decision-making. (18 words)
cn: 我们需要帮助我们的孩子学习如何最好地与智能计算机合作，以改善人类的决策。

en: But most of all we need to keep the long-term perspective in mind: that even if computers will outsmart us, we can still be the most creative. (27 words)
cn: 但最重要的是，我们需要牢记长期的观点：即使计算机比我们更聪明，我们仍然可以是最有创造力的。

en: Because if we aren't, we won't be providing much value in future ecosystems, and that may put in question the foundation for our existence. (24 words)
cn: 因为如果我们不这样做，我们将不会在未来的生态系统中提供太多价值，而这可能会使我们的存在基础受到质疑。

en: When considering risk factors associated with serious chronic diseases, we often think about health indicators such as cholesterol, blood pressure, and body weight. (23 words)
cn: 在考虑与严重慢性疾病相关的风险因素时，我们通常会想到胆固醇、血压和体重等健康指标。

en: But poor diet and physical inactivity also each increase the risk of heart disease and have a role to play in the development of some cancers. (26 words)
cn: 但不良饮食和缺乏身体活动也各自会增加心脏病的风险，并在某些癌症的发展中起作用。

en: Perhaps worse, the detrimental effects of an unhealthy diet and insufficient exercise are not limited to your body. (18 words)
cn: 也许更糟糕的是，不健康饮食和缺乏锻炼的有害影响并不局限于你的身体。

en: Recent research has also shown that indulging in a high-fat and high-sugar diet may have negative effects on your brain, causing learning and memory deficits. (25 words)
cn: 最近的研究还表明，沉迷于高脂肪和高糖饮食可能会对你的大脑产生负面影响，导致学习和记忆缺陷。

en: Studies have found obesity is associated with impairments in cognitive functioning, as assessed by a range of learning and memory tests, such as the ability to remember a list of words presented some minutes or hours earlier. (37 words)
cn: 研究发现，肥胖与认知功能受损有关，这通过一系列学习和记忆测试来评估，例如记住几分钟或几小时前呈现的一列单词的能力。

en: There is also a growing body of evidence that diet-induced cognitive impairments can emerge rapidly—within weeks or even days. (19 words)
cn: 还有越来越多的证据表明，饮食引起的认知障碍可能在数周甚至数天内迅速出现。

en: For example, one study found healthy adults assigned to a high-fat diet for five days showed impaired attention, memory, and mood compared with a low-fat diet control group. (28 words)
cn: 例如，一项研究发现，与低脂饮食对照组相比，被分配到高脂饮食五天的健康成年人表现出注意力、记忆力和情绪受损。

en: Another study also found eating a high-fat and high-sugar breakfast each day for as little as four days resulted in problems with learning and memory similar to those observed in overweight and obese individuals. (34 words)
cn: 另一项研究还发现，每天吃高脂肪和高糖早餐，仅需四天，就会导致学习和记忆问题，与在超重和肥胖个体中观察到的问题相似。

en: Body weight was not hugely different between the groups eating a healthy diet and those on high fat and sugar diets. (21 words)
cn: 健康饮食组与高脂肪和高糖饮食组之间的体重并没有很大差异。

en: So this shows negative consequences of poor dietary intake can occur even when body weight has not changed conspicuously. (19 words)
cn: 因此，这表明即使在体重没有明显变化的情况下，不良饮食摄入也可能产生负面后果。

en: Thus, body weight is not always the best indicator of health and a thin person still needs to eat well and exercise regularly. (23 words)
cn: 因此，体重并不总是健康的最佳指标，瘦人仍然需要吃得好并定期锻炼。

en: Have young people never had it so good? (8 words)
cn: 年轻人从未有过这么好的条件吗？

en: Or do they face more challenges than any previous generation? (10 words)
cn: 还是他们比任何前一代人面临更多的挑战？

en: Our current era in the West is one of high wealth. (11 words)
cn: 我们西方当前的时代是一个高财富的时代。

en: This means minors enjoy material benefits and legal protections that would have been the envy of those living in the past. (21 words)
cn: 这意味着未成年人享有物质利益和法律保护，这些会让过去的人羡慕不已。

en: But there is an increasing suspicion that all is not well for our youth. (14 words)
cn: 但越来越多的人怀疑，我们的年轻人并不一切都好。

en: And one of the most popular explanations, among some experts and the popular media, is that excessive 'screen time' is to blame. (22 words)
cn: 在一些专家和大众媒体中，最流行的解释之一是，过度的‘屏幕时间’是罪魁祸首。

en: This refers to all the attention young people devote to their phones, tablets and laptops. (15 words)
cn: 这指的是年轻人投入到手机、平板电脑和笔记本电脑上的所有注意力。

en: However, this is a contentious theory and such claims have been treated skeptically by some scholars based on their reading of the relevant data. (24 words)
cn: 然而，这是一个有争议的理论，一些学者根据他们对相关数据的解读，对此类说法持怀疑态度。

en: Now a new study has provided another contribution to the debate, uncovering strong evidence that adolescent wellbeing in the United States really is experiencing a decline and arguing that the most likely cause is the electronic riches we have given them. (41 words)
cn: 现在，一项新的研究为这场辩论提供了另一个贡献，发现了强有力的证据，表明美国青少年的幸福感确实在下降，并认为最可能的原因是我们给予他们的电子财富。

en: The background to this is that from the 1960s into the early 2000s, measures of average wellbeing went up in the US. (22 words)
cn: 其背景是，从20世纪60年代到21世纪初，美国的平均幸福感指标一直在上升。

en: This was especially true for younger people. (7 words)
cn: 对年轻人来说尤其如此。

en: It reflected the fact that these decades saw a climb in general standards of living and avoidance of mass societal traumas like full-scale war or economic deprivation. (27 words)
cn: 这反映了这样一个事实：这几十年中，总体生活水平提高，并且避免了大规模社会创伤，如全面战争或经济匮乏。

en: However, the 'screen time' hypothesis, advanced by researchers such as Jean Twenge, is that electronic devices and excessive time spent online may have reversed these trends in recent years, causing problems for young people's psychological health. (36 words)
cn: 然而，由珍·特温格等研究人员提出的‘屏幕时间’假说认为，电子设备和过度的上网时间可能在近年来逆转了这些趋势，给年轻人的心理健康带来了问题。

en: To investigate, Twenge and her colleagues dived into the 'Monitoring the Future' dataset based on annual surveys of American school students from grades 8, 10, and 12 that started in 1991. (31 words)
cn: 为了进行调查，特温格和她的同事们深入研究了‘监测未来’数据集，该数据集基于1991年开始的对美国8年级、10年级和12年级学生的年度调查。

en: In total, 1.1 million young people answered various questions related to their wellbeing. (13 words)
cn: 总共有110万年轻人回答了与他们的幸福感相关的各种问题。

en: Twenge's team's analysis of the answers confirmed the earlier, well-established wellbeing climb, with scores rising across the 1990s, and into the later 2000s. (23 words)
cn: 特温格团队对这些答案的分析证实了早期确立的幸福感上升趋势，得分在20世纪90年代及21世纪后期一直在上升。

en: This was found across measures like self-esteem, life satisfaction, happiness and satisfaction with individual domains like job, neighborhood, or friends. (20 words)
cn: 这在自尊、生活满意度、幸福感和对工作、邻里或朋友等个人领域的满意度等指标上都有体现。

en: But around 2012 these measures started to decline. (8 words)
cn: 但在2012年左右，这些指标开始下降。

en: This continued through 2016, the most recent year for which data is available. (13 words)
cn: 这种情况一直持续到2016年，这是有数据可用的最近一年。

en: Twenge and her colleagues wanted to understand why this change in average wellbeing occurred. (14 words)
cn: 特温格和她的同事们想了解为什么平均幸福感会发生这种变化。

en: However, it is very hard to demonstrate causes using non-experimental data such as this. (14 words)
cn: 然而，使用这样的非实验数据来证明因果关系是非常困难的。

en: In fact, when Twenge previously used this data to suggest a screen time effect, some commentators were quick to raise this problem. (22 words)
cn: 事实上，当特温格之前用这些数据来表明屏幕时间效应时，一些评论员很快就提出了这个问题。

en: They argued that her causal-sounding claims rested on correlational data, and that she had not adequately accounted for other potential causal factors. (22 words)
cn: 他们认为她听起来像因果关系的说法建立在相关性数据之上，而且她没有充分考虑其他潜在的因果因素。

en: This time around, Twenge and her team make a point of saying that they are not trying to establish causes as such, but that they are assessing the plausibility of potential causes. (32 words)
cn: 这一次，特温格和她的团队特意表示，他们并不是在试图建立因果关系本身，而是在评估潜在原因的合理性。

en: First, they explain that if a given variable is playing a role in affecting wellbeing, then we should expect any change in that variable to correlate with the observed changes in wellbeing. (32 words)
cn: 首先，他们解释说，如果某个变量在影响幸福感方面发挥作用，那么我们应该预期该变量的任何变化都与观察到的幸福感变化相关。

en: If not, it is not plausible that the variable is a causal factor. (13 words)
cn: 如果不是，那么该变量是因果因素的说法就不合理。

en: So the researchers looked at time spent in a number of activities that could plausibly be driving the wellbeing decline. (20 words)
cn: 因此，研究人员考察了在若干可能推动幸福感下降的活动上花费的时间。

en: Less sport, and fewer meetings with peers correlated with lower wellbeing, as did less time reading print media and, surprisingly, less time doing homework. (24 words)
cn: 较少的运动和较少的与同龄人见面与较低的幸福感相关，阅读印刷媒体时间减少和——令人惊讶的是——做家庭作业时间减少也是如此。

en: This last finding would appear to contradict another popular hypothesis that it is our burdening of students with assignments that is causing all the problems. (25 words)
cn: 这最后一项发现似乎与另一个流行的假设相矛盾，即我们给学生布置过多的作业才是造成所有问题的原因。

en: In addition, more TV watching and more electronic communication both correlated with lower wellbeing. (14 words)
cn: 此外，更多的电视观看和更多的电子通信都与较低的幸福感相关。

en: All these effects held true for measures of happiness, life satisfaction and self-esteem, with the effects stronger in the 8th and 10th-graders. (22 words)
cn: 所有这些效应在幸福、生活满意度和自尊的测量上都成立，并且在8年级和10年级学生中效应更强。

en: Next, Twenge's team dug a little deeper into the data on screen time. (13 words)
cn: 接下来，特温格的团队更深入地研究了屏幕时间的数据。

en: They found that adolescents who spent a very small amount of time on digital devices—a couple of hours a week—had the highest wellbeing. (23 words)
cn: 他们发现，在数字设备上花费极少时间——每周几个小时——的青少年的幸福感最高。

en: Their wellbeing was even higher than those who never used such devices. (12 words)
cn: 他们的幸福感甚至高于那些从未使用过此类设备的人。

en: However, higher doses of screen time were clearly associated with lower happiness. (12 words)
cn: 然而，更多的屏幕时间显然与较低的幸福感相关。

en: Those spending 10-19 hours per week on their devices were 41 percent more likely to be unhappy than lower-frequency users. (20 words)
cn: 那些每周花10-19小时在设备上的人比低频率用户不快乐的可能性高出41%。

en: Those who used such devices 40 hours a week or more (one in ten teenagers) were twice as likely to be unhappy. (22 words)
cn: 那些每周使用此类设备40小时或以上（十分之一的青少年）不快乐的可能性是前者的两倍。

en: The data was slightly complicated by the fact that there was a tendency for kids who were social in the real world to also use more online communication, but by bracketing out different cases it became clear that the real-world sociality component correlated with greater wellbeing, whereas greater time on screens or online only correlated with poorer wellbeing. (58 words)
cn: 数据因现实世界中善于社交的孩子也更倾向于使用更多在线交流这一事实而略显复杂，但通过排除不同的情况，很明显现实世界的社交成分与更高的幸福感相关，而更多的屏幕或在线时间则仅与较差的幸福感相关。

en: So far, so plausible. (4 words)
cn: 到目前为止，还算合理。

en: But the next question is, are the drops in average wellbeing happening at the same time strands toward increased electronic device usage? (22 words)
cn: 但下一个问题是，平均幸福感的下降是否与电子设备使用量的增加同时发生？

en: It looks like it—after all, 2012 was the tipping point when more than half of Americans began owning smartphones. (19 words)
cn: 看起来确实如此——毕竟，2012年是超过半数美国人开始拥有智能手机的转折点。

en: Twenge and her colleagues also found that across the key years of 2013-16, wellbeing was indeed lowest in years where adolescents spent more time online, on social media, and reading news online, and when more youth in the United States had smartphones. (42 words)
cn: 特温格和她的同事们还发现，在2013-16年的关键年份中，幸福感在青少年花更多时间上网、使用社交媒体和在线阅读新闻，以及美国更多年轻人拥有智能手机的年份确实最低。

en: And in a second analysis, they found that where technology went, dips in wellbeing followed. (15 words)
cn: 在第二次分析中，他们发现，技术到哪里，幸福感的下降就跟到哪里。

en: For instance, years with a larger increase in online usage were followed by years with lower wellbeing, rather than the other way around. (23 words)
cn: 例如，在线使用量增长较大的年份之后是幸福感较低的年份，而不是相反。

en: This does not prove causality, but is consistent with it. (10 words)
cn: 这并不能证明因果关系，但与其一致。

en: Meanwhile, TV use did not show this tracking. (8 words)
cn: 同时，电视使用量并未显示出这种追踪关系。

en: TV might make you less happy, but this is not what seems to be driving the recent declines in young people's average happiness. (23 words)
cn: 看电视可能会让你不那么快乐，但这似乎不是导致近期年轻人平均幸福感下降的原因。

en: A similar but reversed pattern was found for the activities associated with greater wellbeing. (14 words)
cn: 在与更高幸福感相关的活动中发现了类似但相反的模式。

en: For example, years when people spent more time with friends were better years for wellbeing (and followed by better years). (20 words)
cn: 例如，人们花更多时间与朋友在一起的年份是幸福感更好的年份（并且随后是更好的年份）。

en: Sadly, the data also showed face-to-face socializing and sports activity had declined over the period covered by the survey. (19 words)
cn: 遗憾的是，数据还显示，在调查涵盖的时期内，面对面的社交活动和体育活动有所减少。

en: There is another explanation that Twenge and her colleagues wanted to address: the impact of the great recession of 2007-2009, which hit a great number of American families and might be affecting adolescents. (33 words)
cn: 特温格和她的同事们还想探讨另一种解释：2007-2009年大衰退的影响，这场衰退重创了许多美国家庭，并可能正在影响青少年。

en: The dataset they used did not include economic data, so instead the researchers looked at whether the 2013-16 wellbeing decline was tracking economic indicators. (24 words)
cn: 他们使用的数据集不包括经济数据，因此研究人员转而考察2013-16年的幸福感下降是否与经济指标同步。

en: They found some evidence that some crude measures, like income inequality, correlated with changes in wellbeing, but economic measures with a more direct impact, like family income and unemployment rates (which put families into difficulties), had no relationship with wellbeing. (40 words)
cn: 他们发现一些证据表明，一些粗略的指标，如收入不平等，与幸福感的变化相关，但具有更直接影响的经济指标，如家庭收入和失业率（使家庭陷入困境），与幸福感没有关系。

en: The researchers also note that the recession hit some years before we see the beginning of the wellbeing drop, and before the steepest wellbeing decline, which occurred in 2013. (29 words)
cn: 研究人员还指出，经济衰退发生在幸福感开始下降的几年前，也发生在2013年最急剧的幸福感下降之前。

en: The researchers conclude that electronic communication was the only adolescent activity that increased at the same time psychological wellbeing declined. (20 words)
cn: 研究人员得出结论，电子通信是唯一一项在心理健康下降的同时增加的青少年活动。

en: I suspect that some experts in the field will be keen to address alternative explanations, such as unassessed variables playing a role in the wellbeing decline. (26 words)
cn: 我怀疑该领域的一些专家会热衷于探讨其他解释，例如未经评估的变量在幸福感下降中发挥作用。

en: But the new work does go further than previous research and suggests that screen time should still be considered a potential barrier to young people's flourishing. (26 words)
cn: 但这项新研究确实比以往的研究更进一步，并表明屏幕时间仍应被视为年轻人茁壮成长的潜在障碍。

en: The dangerous thing about lying is people don't understand how the act changes us, says Dan Ariely, behavioural psychologist at Duke University. (22 words)
cn: 杜克大学行为心理学家丹·艾瑞里说：‘说谎的危险之处在于人们不了解这种行为如何改变我们。’

en: Psychologists have documented children lying as early as the age of two. (12 words)
cn: 心理学家已经记录到儿童早在两岁时就开始说谎。

en: Some experts even consider lying a developmental milestone, like crawling and walking, because it requires sophisticated planning, attention and the ability to see a situation from someone else's perspective to manipulate them. (32 words)
cn: 一些专家甚至将说谎视为发展的里程碑，就像爬行和走路一样，因为它需要周密的计划、注意力以及从他人角度看待情况以操纵他们的能力。

en: But, for most people, lying gets limited as we develop a sense of morality and the ability to self-regulate. (19 words)
cn: 但对大多数人来说，随着我们发展出道德感和自我调节能力，说谎会受到限制。

en: Harvard cognitive neuroscientist Joshua Greene says, for most of us, lying takes work. (13 words)
cn: 哈佛大学认知神经科学家约书亚·格林说，对我们大多数人来说，说谎需要费功夫。

en: In studies, he gave subjects a chance to deceive for monetary gain while examining their brains in a functional MRI machine, which maps blood flow to active parts of the brain. (31 words)
cn: 在研究中，他给受试者一个机会为了金钱利益而欺骗，同时用功能性磁共振成像机检查他们的大脑，该机器可以绘制流向大脑活跃部分的血流图。

en: Some people told the truth instantly and instinctively. (8 words)
cn: 有些人本能地立即说出真相。

en: But others opted to lie, and they showed increased activity in their frontal parietal control network, which is involved in difficult or complex thinking. (24 words)
cn: 但其他人选择说谎，他们的额顶控制网络活动增加，该网络参与困难或复杂的思考。

en: This suggests that they were deciding between truth and dishonesty—and ultimately opting for the latter. (15 words)
cn: 这表明他们在真实与不诚实之间做出决定——并最终选择了后者。

en: For a follow-up analysis, he found that people whose neural reward centers were more active when they won money were also more likely to be among the group of liars—suggesting that lying may have to do with the inability to resist temptation. (42 words)
cn: 在后续分析中，他发现那些在赢钱时神经奖赏中枢更活跃的人也更容易成为说谎者群体的一员——这表明说谎可能与无法抵制诱惑有关。

en: External conditions also matter in terms of when and how often we lie. (13 words)
cn: 外部条件也影响我们何时以及多久说谎。

en: We are more likely to lie, when we are able to rationalise it, when we are stressed and fatigued or see others being dishonest. (24 words)
cn: 当我们能够将其合理化、当我们感到压力和疲劳或看到他人不诚实时，我们更有可能说谎。

en: And we are less likely to lie when we have moral reminders or when we think others are watching. (19 words)
cn: 而当我们有道德提醒或认为他人在关注时，我们不太可能说谎。

en: We as a society need to understand that, when we don't punish lying, we increase the probability it will happen again, Ariely says. (23 words)
cn: 艾瑞里说：‘我们作为一个社会需要明白，当不惩罚说谎时，我们就增加了它再次发生的可能性。’

en: In a 2016 study published in the journal Nature Neuroscience, Ariely and colleagues showed how dishonesty alters people's brains, making it easier to tell lies in the future. (28 words)
cn: 在2016年发表于《自然·神经科学》杂志的一项研究中，艾瑞里和同事们展示了不诚实如何改变人们的大脑，使将来更容易说谎。

en: When people uttered a falsehood, the scientists noticed a burst of activity in their amygdala. (15 words)
cn: 当人们说出谎言时，科学家注意到他们的杏仁核出现一阵活动。

en: The amygdala is a crucial part of the brain that produces fear, anxiety and emotional responses—including that sinking, guilty feeling you get when you lie. (25 words)
cn: 杏仁核是大脑中产生恐惧、焦虑和情绪反应的关键部分——包括你说谎时那种沉重、内疚的感觉。

en: But when scientists had their subjects play a game in which they won money by deceiving their partner, they noticed the negative signals from the amygdala began to decrease. (29 words)
cn: 但当科学家让受试者玩一个通过欺骗伙伴赢钱的游戏时，他们注意到来自杏仁核的负面信号开始减少。

en: Not only that, but when people faced no consequences for dishonesty, their falsehood tended to get even more sensational. (19 words)
cn: 不仅如此，当人们的不诚实没有面临后果时，他们的谎言往往会变得更加耸人听闻。

en: This means that if you give people multiple opportunities to lie for their own benefit, they start with little lies which get bigger over time. (25 words)
cn: 这意味着如果你给人们多次机会为了自己的利益而说谎，他们会从小谎开始，随着时间的推移谎言会越来越大。

en: Here's how the Pacific Northwest is preparing for 'The Big One'. (11 words)
cn: 以下是太平洋西北地区如何为‘大地震’做准备。

en: It's the mother of all disaster drills for what could be the worst disaster in American history. (17 words)
cn: 这是可能是美国历史上最严重灾难的所有灾难演习之母。

en: California has spent years preparing for 'The Big One'—the inevitable earthquake that will undoubtedly unleash all kinds of havoc along the famous San Andreas fault. (25 words)
cn: 加利福尼亚州多年来一直在为‘大地震’做准备——这场不可避免的地震无疑会在著名的圣安德烈亚斯断层沿线造成各种破坏。

en: But what if the fault that runs along the Pacific Northwest delivers a gigantic earthquake of its own? (18 words)
cn: 但如果沿太平洋西北地区延伸的断层自己发生一次巨大的地震呢？

en: If the people of the Cascadia region have anything to do with it, they won't be caught unawares. (18 words)
cn: 如果卡斯卡迪亚地区的人们对此有所行动，他们不会措手不及。

en: The region is engaged in a multi-day earthquake-and-tsunami drill involving around 20,000 people. (13 words)
cn: 该地区正在进行一场为期多天的地震和海啸演习，约有2万人参加。

en: The Cascadia Rising drill gives area residents and emergency responders a chance to practice what to do in case of a 9.0 magnitude earthquake and tsunami along one of the nation's dangerous—and underestimated—faults. (33 words)
cn: ‘卡斯卡迪亚崛起’演习让该地区居民和应急响应人员有机会练习在发生9.0级地震和海啸时如何应对——该地震带是美国最危险且被低估的断层之一。

en: The Cascadia Earthquake Zone is big enough to compete with San Andreas (it's been called the most dangerous fault in America), but it's much lesser known than its California cousin. (30 words)
cn: 卡斯卡迪亚地震带大到足以与圣安德烈亚斯断层相媲美（它被称为美国最危险的断层），但它的知名度远低于加利福尼亚的同类。

en: Nearly 700 miles long, the earthquake zone is located by the North American Plate off the coast of Pacific British Columbia, Washington, Oregon and Northern California. (26 words)
cn: 该地震带近700英里长，位于太平洋不列颠哥伦比亚省、华盛顿州、俄勒冈州和北加利福尼亚州海岸外的北美板块附近。

en: Cascadia is what's known as a 'megathrust' fault. (8 words)
cn: 卡斯卡迪亚就是所谓的‘巨型逆冲’断层。

en: Megathrusts are created in earthquake zones—land plate boundaries where two plates converge. (12 words)
cn: 巨型逆冲断层产生于地震带——两个板块汇聚的陆地板块边界。

en: In the areas where one plate is beneath another, stress builds up over time. (14 words)
cn: 在一个板块位于另一个板块下方的区域，压力会随着时间的推移而积累。

en: During a megathrust event, all of that stress releases and some of the world's most powerful earthquakes occur. (18 words)
cn: 在巨型逆冲事件中，所有压力都会释放，并发生一些世界上最强烈的地震。

en: Remember the 9.1 earthquake and tsunami in the Indian Ocean off Sumatra in 2004? (14 words)
cn: 还记得2004年苏门答腊附近印度洋的9.1级地震和海啸吗？

en: It was caused by a megathrust event as the India plate moved beneath the Burma micro-plate. (16 words)
cn: 那是由巨型逆冲事件引起的，因为印度板块移动到缅甸微板块下方。

en: The last time a major earthquake occurred along the Cascadia fault was in 1700, so officials worry that another event could occur any time. (24 words)
cn: 卡斯卡迪亚断层上次发生大地震是在1700年，因此官员们担心另一次地震随时可能发生。

en: To prevent that event from becoming a catastrophe, first responders will join members of the public in rehearsals that involve communication, evacuation, search and rescue, and other scenarios. (28 words)
cn: 为了防止该事件演变成灾难，急救人员将与公众一起参加涉及通信、疏散、搜救和其他情景的演习。

en: Thousands of casualties are expected if a 9.0 earthquake were to occur. (12 words)
cn: 如果发生9.0级地震，预计会有数千人伤亡。

en: First, the earthquake would shake metropolitan areas including Seattle and Portland. (11 words)
cn: 首先，地震会震动包括西雅图和波特兰在内的大都市地区。

en: This could trigger a tsunami that would create havoc along the coast. (12 words)
cn: 这可能会引发海啸，在沿海地区造成严重破坏。

en: Not all casualties can necessarily be prevented—but by coordinating across local, state, and even national borders, officials hope that the worst-case scenario can be averted. (25 words)
cn: 并非所有伤亡都一定能预防——但通过在地方、州甚至国家边界之间进行协调，官员们希望最坏的情况可以避免。

en: On the exercise's website, officials explain that the report they prepare during this rehearsal will inform disaster management for years to come. (22 words)
cn: 在演习网站上，官员们解释说，他们在这次演习期间准备的报告将为未来几年的灾害管理提供信息。

en: For hundreds of thousands of Cascadia residents, 'The Big One' isn't a question of if, only when. (17 words)
cn: 对数十万卡斯卡迪亚居民来说，‘大地震’不是是否会发生的问题，只是时间问题。

en: And it's never too early to get ready for the inevitable. (11 words)
cn: 为不可避免的事情做准备，越早越好。

en: The persistent haze over many of our cities is a reminder of the polluted air that we breathe. (18 words)
cn: 许多城市持续的雾霾提醒我们，我们呼吸的空气受到了污染。

en: Over 80% of the world's urban population is breathing air that fails to meet World Health Organisation guidelines, and an estimated 4.5 million people died prematurely from outdoor air pollution in 2015. (32 words)
cn: 世界上超过80%的城市人口呼吸的空气质量未能达到世界卫生组织的标准，据估计，2015年有450万人因室外空气污染而过早死亡。

en: Globally, urban populations are expected to double in the next 40 years, and an extra 2 billion people will need new places to live, as well as services and ways to move around their cities. (35 words)
cn: 在全球范围内，城市人口预计在未来40年内将翻倍，额外的20亿人将需要新的居住场所，以及城市内的服务和交通方式。

en: What is more important, the decisions that we make now about the design of our cities will determine the everyday lives and health of the coming generations. (27 words)
cn: 更重要的是，我们现在对城市设计所做的决定将决定子孙后代的日常生活和健康。

en: So what would a smog-free, or at least low-pollution, city be like? (12 words)
cn: 那么，一个无雾霾，或者至少是低污染的城市会是什么样子呢？

en: Traffic has become synonymous with air pollution, and many countries intend to ban the sale of petrol and diesel cars in the next two decades. (25 words)
cn: 交通已成为空气污染的同义词，许多国家计划在未来二十年禁止销售汽油和柴油汽车。

en: But simply switching to electric cars will not mean pollution-free cities. (11 words)
cn: 但仅仅转向电动汽车并不意味着城市无污染。

en: The level of emissions they cause will depend on how the electricity to run them is generated, while brakes, tyres and roads all create tiny airborne particles as they wear out. (31 words)
cn: 它们造成的排放水平将取决于运行它们的电力是如何产生的，同时刹车、轮胎和道路在磨损时都会产生微小的空气悬浮颗粒。

en: Across the developed world, car use is in decline as more people move to city centres, while young people especially are opting for other means of travel. (27 words)
cn: 在整个发达国家，随着越来越多的人搬到市中心，汽车使用量正在下降，而年轻人尤其倾向于选择其他出行方式。

en: Researchers are already asking if motor vehicle use has reached its peak and will decline, but transport planners have yet to catch up with this trend, instead of laying new roads to tackle traffic jams. (35 words)
cn: 研究人员已经在质疑机动车使用量是否已经达到顶峰并将下降，但交通规划者尚未跟上这一趋势，仍在铺设新道路来解决交通拥堵问题。

en: As users of London's orbital M25 motorway will know, new roads rapidly fill with more traffic. (16 words)
cn: 正如伦敦M25环城高速公路的使用者所知，新道路很快就会被更多的车辆填满。

en: In the US, studies have shown that doubling the size of a road can simply double the traffic, taking us back to the starting point. (25 words)
cn: 在美国，研究表明，将道路规模扩大一倍只会使交通量翻倍，让我们回到起点。

en: The marketing is enticing: Get stronger muscles and healthier bodies with minimal effort by adding protein powder to your morning shake or juice drink. (24 words)
cn: 营销宣传很诱人：通过在早晨的奶昔或果汁饮料中添加蛋白粉，以最小的努力获得更强壮的肌肉和更健康的身体。

en: Or grab a protein bar at lunch or for a quick snack. (12 words)
cn: 或者在午餐时或作为快速零食拿一根蛋白棒。

en: Today, you can find protein supplements everywhere—online, at the pharmacy, grocery store, or health food store. (16 words)
cn: 如今，你可以在任何地方找到蛋白质补充剂——网上、药店、杂货店或健康食品店。

en: They come in powders, pills, and bars. (7 words)
cn: 它们有粉末、药丸和棒状形式。

en: With more than $12 billion in sales this year, the industry is booming and, according to the market research company, Grand View Research, is on track to sell billions more by 2025. (32 words)
cn: 今年销售额超过120亿美元，该行业正在蓬勃发展，根据市场研究公司Grand View Research的数据，到2025年销售额还将再增加数十亿美元。

en: But do we really need all this supplemental protein? (9 words)
cn: 但我们真的需要所有这些额外的蛋白质吗？

en: It depends. (2 words)
cn: 这取决于情况。

en: There are pros, cons and some ho-hums to consider. (9 words)
cn: 有优点、缺点和一些平淡无奇之处需要考虑。

en: For starters, protein is critical for every cell in our body. (11 words)
cn: 首先，蛋白质对我们身体的每个细胞都至关重要。

en: It helps build nails, hair, bones, and muscles. (8 words)
cn: 它有助于构建指甲、头发、骨骼和肌肉。

en: It can also help you feel fuller longer than eating foods without protein. (13 words)
cn: 与不含蛋白质的食物相比，它还能让你更长时间保持饱腹感。

en: And, unlike nutrients that are found only in a few foods, protein is pretty much ubiquitous. (16 words)
cn: 而且，与仅在少数食物中发现的营养素不同，蛋白质几乎无处不在。

en: The typical American diet is a lot higher in protein than a lot of us think, says registered dietitian Angela Pipitone with Johns Hopkins McKusick-Nathans Institute of Genetic Medicine. (29 words)
cn: 约翰霍普金斯大学麦库西克-内森斯遗传医学研究所的注册营养师安吉拉·皮皮托内说：‘典型的美国饮食中的蛋白质含量比我们很多人想象的要高得多。’

en: She says it's in foods many of us expect, such as beef, chicken, and other types of meat and dairy. (20 words)
cn: 她说它存在于我们许多人期望的食物中，如牛肉、鸡肉和其他类型的肉类和奶制品。

en: But it's also in foods that may not come immediately to mind like vegetables, fruit, beans and grains. (18 words)
cn: 但它也存在于我们可能不会立即想到的食物中，如蔬菜、水果、豆类和谷物。

en: The U.S. government's recommended daily allowance (RDA) for the average adult is 50 to 60 grams of protein a day. (20 words)
cn: 美国政府建议普通成年人的每日摄入量为每天50至60克蛋白质。

en: This may sound like a lot, but Pipitone says: 'We get bits of protein here and there and that really adds up throughout the day.' (25 words)
cn: 这听起来可能很多，但皮皮托内说：‘我们到处都能摄入少量蛋白质，一天下来真的就积累起来了。’

en: Take, for example, breakfast. (4 words)
cn: 以早餐为例。

en: If you ate two eggs topped with a little bit of cheese and an orange on the side, you already have 22 grams of protein. (25 words)
cn: 如果你吃了两个鸡蛋，上面加一点奶酪，旁边还有一个橙子，你已经摄入了22克蛋白质。

en: Each egg gives you 7 grams; the cheese gives you around 6 grams and the orange — about 2 grams. (20 words)
cn: 每个鸡蛋给你7克；奶酪给你大约6克，橙子大约2克。

en: Add a lunch of chicken, rice, and broccoli, and you are already over the recommended 50 grams. (17 words)
cn: 再加上一顿有鸡肉、米饭和西兰花的午餐，你就已经超过了建议的50克。

en: You can get enough protein and meet the RDA before you even get to dinner, says Pipitone. (17 words)
cn: 皮皮托内说：‘你甚至可以在吃晚餐之前就获得足够的蛋白质并达到每日建议摄入量。’

en: So if it's so easy to get your protein in food, why add more in the form of powders, snack bars or a boost at your local juice bar? (29 words)
cn: 所以，如果从食物中获取蛋白质如此容易，为什么还要以粉末、零食棒或当地果汁吧的蛋白补充剂形式额外添加呢？

en: No need to, says Pipitone because, in fact, most of us already get enough protein in our diet. (18 words)
cn: 皮皮托内说没有必要，因为事实上，我们大多数人已经在饮食中摄入了足够的蛋白质。

en: Whole foods are always the best option rather than adding supplements, she says, noting the FDA does not regulate supplements as stringently as foods or drugs, so there could be less protein, more sugar, and some additives you wouldn't expect, such as caffeine and even steroids. (46 words)
cn: 她说：‘天然食品总是最好的选择，而不是添加补充剂。’并指出美国食品药品监督管理局对补充剂的监管不如对食品或药品严格，因此可能会有更少的蛋白质、更多的糖分，以及一些你意想不到的添加剂，如咖啡因甚至类固醇。

en: If you are considering a supplement, read the list of ingredients, she says although this is not always foolproof. (19 words)
cn: 她说，如果你在考虑补充剂，请阅读成分列表，尽管这并不总是万无一失的。

en: I've seen very expensive protein supplements that claim to be high quality but they might not really be beneficial for the average healthy adult, she says. (26 words)
cn: 她说：‘我见过非常昂贵的蛋白质补充剂，声称质量很高，但它们可能并不真正对普通健康成年人有益。’

en: It could just be a waste of money. (8 words)
cn: ‘这可能只是浪费钱。’

en: But there are certain situations that do warrant extra protein. (10 words)
cn: 但在某些情况下确实需要额外摄入蛋白质。

en: Anytime you're in an anabolic state or building muscle, Pipitone says, such as if you're an extreme endurance athlete, training for a marathon, or you're a body builder. (28 words)
cn: 皮皮托内说：‘任何时候当你处于合成代谢状态或正在增肌时，’比如你是一名极限耐力运动员、为马拉松训练，或者你是一名健美运动员。

en: If you're moderately exercising for 150 minutes a week, as the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends, or less than that, you're probably not an extreme athlete. (28 words)
cn: 如果你按照疾病控制与预防中心的建议每周适度运动150分钟，或者更少，你可能不是极限运动员。

en: Extreme athletes expend lots of energy breaking down and repairing and building muscles. (13 words)
cn: 极限运动员消耗大量能量来分解、修复和构建肌肉。

en: Protein can give them the edge they need to speed along that process. (13 words)
cn: 蛋白质可以给他们提供加速这一过程所需的优势。

en: Vegans can benefit from protein supplements since they do not eat animal-based protein sources like meat, dairy, or eggs. (19 words)
cn: 纯素食者可以从蛋白质补充剂中受益，因为他们不吃肉类、奶制品或鸡蛋等动物性蛋白质来源。

en: And, for someone always on-the-go who may not have time for a meal, a protein snack bar can be a good option for occasional meal replacement. (26 words)
cn: 而且，对于总是忙碌可能没有时间吃饭的人来说，蛋白质零食棒可以作为偶尔代餐的不错选择。

en: Also, individuals recovering from surgery or an injury can also benefit from extra protein. (14 words)
cn: 此外，从手术或受伤中恢复的人也可以从额外蛋白质中受益。

en: So, too, can older people. (5 words)
cn: 老年人也同样如此。

en: At around age 60, 'muscles really start to break down,' says Kathryn Starr, an aging researcher at Duke University School of Medicine, 'and because of that, in addition to the fact that as we get older our body's ability to break down protein is reduced, the protein needs of an older adult actually increases.' (54 words)
cn: 杜克大学医学院的衰老研究员凯瑟琳·斯塔尔说：‘大约在60岁时，肌肉真的开始衰退，’‘正因为如此，再加上随着年龄增长我们身体分解蛋白质的能力下降，老年人的蛋白质需求实际上在增加。’

en: In fact, along with her colleague Connie Bales, Starr recently conducted a small study that found that adding extra protein foods to the diet of obese older individuals who were trying to lose weight strengthened their muscles. (37 words)
cn: 事实上，斯塔尔和她的同事康妮·贝尔斯最近进行了一项小型研究，发现在试图减肥的肥胖老年人的饮食中添加额外的蛋白质食物增强了他们的肌肉。

en: Participants in the study were separated into two groups—one group was asked to eat 30 grams of protein per meal in the form of whole foods. (26 words)
cn: 研究参与者被分为两组——一组被要求每餐以天然食物的形式摄入30克蛋白质。

en: That meant they were eating 90 grams of protein a day. (11 words)
cn: 这意味着他们每天摄入90克蛋白质。

en: The other group—the control group—was put on a typical low-calorie diet with about 50 to 60 grams of protein a day. (21 words)
cn: 另一组——对照组——采用典型的低热量饮食，每天摄入约50至60克蛋白质。

en: After six months, researchers found the high protein group had significantly improved their muscle function—almost twice as much as the control group. (22 words)
cn: 六个月后，研究人员发现高蛋白组的肌肉功能显著改善——几乎是对照组的两倍。

en: They were able to walk faster, had improved balance, and were also able to get up out of a chair faster than the control group, Starr says. (27 words)
cn: 斯塔尔说：‘他们能够走得更快，平衡能力有所改善，并且从椅子上站起来的速度也比对照组快。’

en: All 67 participants were over 60 years of age, and both groups lost about the same amount of weight. (19 words)
cn: 所有67名参与者都超过60岁，两组减掉的体重差不多。

en: Starr is now looking into whether high-protein diets also improve the quality of the muscle itself in seniors. (18 words)
cn: 斯塔尔现在正在研究高蛋白饮食是否也能改善老年人肌肉本身的质量。

en: She's using CT scans to measure muscle size and fat, and comparing seniors on a high-protein diet to those on regular diets. (22 words)
cn: 她正在使用CT扫描来测量肌肉大小和脂肪，并将高蛋白饮食的老年人对比常规饮食的老年人。

en: She says her findings should be available in a couple of months. (12 words)
cn: 她说她的研究结果应该会在几个月后公布。

en: In the meantime, 70-year-old Corliss Keith, who was in the high protein group in Starr's latest study, says she feels a big difference. (23 words)
cn: 与此同时，70岁的科利斯·基思——斯塔尔最新研究中高蛋白组的成员——说她感觉有很大的不同。

en: I feel excellent, she says, I feel like I have a different body, I have more energy, I'm stronger. (19 words)
cn: 她说：‘我感觉非常好，我觉得我有了一个不同的身体，我更有活力，更强壮了。’

en: She says she is able to take Zumba exercise classes three times a week, work out on the treadmill and take long, brisk walks. (24 words)
cn: 她说她现在每周能上三次尊巴健身课，在跑步机上锻炼，还能进行长时间的快走。

en: Keith also lost more than 15 pounds. (7 words)
cn: 基思还减掉了超过15磅。

en: I'm a fashionable person, so now I'm back in my three-inch heels, she says. (14 words)
cn: 她说：‘我是一个时尚的人，所以现在我又穿回了三英寸的高跟鞋。’

en: As people age, researcher Starr says muscle strength is key to helping them stay strong and continue living on their own in their own home. (25 words)
cn: 研究人员斯塔尔说，随着年龄增长，肌肉力量是帮助老年人保持强壮并继续独立生活在自己家中的关键。

en: I feel very much alive now, says Keith, I feel like I could stay by myself until I'm 100. (19 words)
cn: 基思说：‘我现在感觉非常有活力，我觉得我可以独自生活到100岁。’

en: But can people overdo protein? (5 words)
cn: 但人们会过量摄入蛋白质吗？

en: Pipitone says you do have to be careful. (8 words)
cn: 皮皮托内说你确实需要小心。

en: Too much protein can cause nausea, cramps, headaches, fatigue, and bloating. (11 words)
cn: 过多的蛋白质会导致恶心、痉挛、头痛、疲劳和腹胀。

en: Dehydration is also a risk when you eat too much protein. (11 words)
cn: 当你摄入过多蛋白质时，脱水也是一种风险。

en: Pipitone says if you increase protein, you also have to increase your fluid intake. (14 words)
cn: 皮皮托内说如果你增加蛋白质摄入量，你也必须增加液体摄入量。

en: I always tell people to make sure they're drinking enough fluids, which for the average person is 60 to 70 ounces a day, which translates into eight 8-ounce glasses of water or liquid per day. (35 words)
cn: ‘我总是告诉人们要确保摄入足够的液体，’对普通人来说每天是60到70盎司，相当于每天八杯8盎司的水或液体。

en: There have been some indications that extra protein makes the kidneys work harder which could be problematic for individuals with a history of kidney disease and for them, the supplements may increase the risk of kidney stones, she says. (39 words)
cn: 她说：‘有一些迹象表明，额外的蛋白质会使肾脏工作更费力，这对有肾脏病史的人来说可能是有问题的，对他们来说，补充剂可能会增加肾结石的风险。’

en: Bottom Line: if you think you need more protein in your diet, consider these questions: Are you an extreme athlete; are you recovering from injury or surgery; or are you 60 years or older? (34 words)
cn: 底线是：如果你认为你的饮食中需要更多蛋白质，考虑这些问题：你是极限运动员吗；你正在从受伤或手术中恢复吗；或者你60岁或以上吗？

en: If so, adding high protein foods like eggs and meat products to your diet can be beneficial. (17 words)
cn: 如果是这样，在饮食中添加鸡蛋和肉类产品等高蛋白食物可能是有益的。

en: And, if you're not sure, it is always a good idea to check with your primary care provider. (18 words)
cn: 而且，如果你不确定，咨询你的初级保健提供者总是一个好主意。

en: Last year, a child was born at a hospital in the UK with her heart outside her body. (18 words)
cn: 去年，一个婴儿在英国一家医院出生，她的心脏长在身体外面。

en: Few babies survive this rare condition, and those who do must endure numerous operations and are likely to have complex needs. (21 words)
cn: 很少有婴儿在这种罕见的情况下存活下来，而那些存活下来的婴儿必须忍受多次手术，并可能有复杂的需求。

en: When her mother was interviewed, three weeks after her daughter's birth, she was asked if she was prepared for what might be a daunting task caring for her. (28 words)
cn: 当她的母亲在女儿出生三周后接受采访时，她被问及是否准备好面对照顾女儿这一可能令人生畏的任务。

en: She answered without hesitation that, as far as she was concerned, this would be a 'privilege'. (16 words)
cn: 她毫不犹豫地回答说，就她而言，这将是一种‘荣幸’。

en: Rarely has there been a better example of the power of attitude, one of our most powerful psychological tools. (19 words)
cn: 很少有比这更好的例子来说明态度的力量——态度是我们最强大的心理工具之一。

en: Our attitudes allow us to turn mistakes into opportunities, and loss into the chance for new beginnings. (17 words)
cn: 我们的态度使我们能够将错误转化为机会，将损失转化为新的开始。

en: An attitude is a settled way of thinking, feeling and/or behaving towards particular objects, people, events or ideologies. (18 words)
cn: 态度是一种对特定对象、人、事件或意识形态的固定的思考、感受和/或行为方式。

en: We use our attitudes to filter, interpret and react to the world around us. (14 words)
cn: 我们用态度来过滤、解读和回应周围的世界。

en: You weren't born with attitudes; rather they are all learned, and this happens in a number of ways. (18 words)
cn: 你不是生来就带有态度的；相反，它们都是后天习得的，并且通过多种方式形成。

en: The most powerful influences occur during early childhood and include both what happened to you directly, and what those around you did and said in your presence. (27 words)
cn: 最强大的影响发生在幼儿时期，包括直接发生在你身上的事，以及你周围的人在你在场时做的和说的。

en: As you acquire a distinctive identity your attitudes are further refined by the behavior of those with whom you identify—your family, those of your gender and culture, and the people you admire, even though you may not know them personally. (40 words)
cn: 随着你获得独特的身份认同，你的态度会进一步被你认同的人的行为所完善——你的家庭、与你性别和文化相同的人，以及你钦佩的人，即使你可能并不认识他们本人。

en: Friendships and other important relationships become increasingly important, particularly during adolescence. (11 words)
cn: 友谊和其他重要关系变得越来越重要，尤其是在青春期。

en: About that same time and throughout adulthood, the information you receive, especially when ideas are repeated in association with goals and achievements you find attractive, also refines your attitudes. (29 words)
cn: 大约在同一时期以及整个成年期，你所接收的信息——特别是当观点与你认为有吸引力的目标和成就相关联并被重复时——也会完善你的态度。

en: Many people assume that our attitudes are internally consistent, that is, the way you think and feel about someone or something predicts your behavior towards them. (26 words)
cn: 许多人认为我们的态度是内在一致的，也就是说，你对某人或某事的想法和感受预示了你对他们的行为。

en: However, many studies have found that feelings and thoughts don't necessarily predict behavior. (13 words)
cn: 然而，许多研究发现，感受和想法并不一定能预测行为。

en: In general, your attitudes will be internally consistent only when the behavior is easy, and when those around you hold similar beliefs. (22 words)
cn: 一般来说，只有当行为容易做到，并且当你周围的人持有相似信念时，你的态度才会在内部保持一致。

en: That's why, for example, many say they believe in the benefits of recycling or exercise, but don't behave in line with their views, because it takes awareness, effort and courage to go beyond merely stating that you believe something is a good idea. (43 words)
cn: 这就是为什么，例如，许多人说他们相信回收或锻炼的好处，但行为却不符合他们的观点，因为仅仅说某件事是个好主意是不够的，还需要意识、努力和勇气。

en: One of the most effective ways to change an attitude is to start behaving as if you already feel and think the way you'd prefer to. (26 words)
cn: 改变态度最有效的方法之一就是开始表现得好像你已经有了理想中的感受和想法。

en: Take some time to reflect on your attitudes, to think about what you believe and why. (16 words)
cn: 花些时间反思你的态度，思考你相信什么以及为什么。

en: Is there anything you consider a burden rather than a privilege? (11 words)
cn: 是否有任何你认为是负担而不是荣幸的事情？

en: If so, start behaving—right now—as if the latter is the case. (11 words)
cn: 如果是这样，现在就开始表现得好像后者才是事实。

en: Industrial fishing for krill in the unspoilt waters around Antarctica is threatening the future of one of the world's last great wildernesses, according to a new report. (27 words)
