en: On days when you're really reluctant to brave the world, Draper suggests selecting sentimental items of clothing, such as ones you wore on a special day, or given to you by a loved one, as clothes with fond associations can help you tap into constructive emotions. (46 words)
cn: 当你真的不愿意面对这个世界的时候，德雷珀建议选择有纪念意义的衣物，比如你在特殊日子穿过的，或者心爱之人送给你的，因为带有美好回忆的衣服可以帮助你激发积极的情感。

en: A recent analysis found that most research mischaracterizes the relationship between music and skills enhancement. (15 words)
cn: 最近的一项分析发现，大多数研究错误地描述了音乐与技能提升之间的关系。

en: In 2004, a paper appeared in the journal Psychological Science, titled 'Music Lessons Enhance IQ.' (15 words)
cn: 2004年，《心理科学》杂志上发表了一篇题为《音乐课提高智商》的论文。

en: The author, composer and psychologist Glenn Schellenberg had conducted an experiment with 144 children randomly assigned to four groups: one learned the keyboard for a year, one took singing lessons, one joined an acting class, and a control group had no extracurricular training. (43 words)
cn: 作者、作曲家和心理学家格伦·舍伦贝格对144名儿童进行了一项实验，将他们随机分为四组：一组学习了一年的键盘，一组上歌唱课，一组参加表演班，对照组没有课外训练。

en: The IQ of the children in the two musical groups rose by an average of seven points in the course of a year; those in the other two groups gained an average of 4.3 points. (35 words)
cn: 两个音乐组儿童的智商在一年中平均提高了7分；另外两组的儿童平均提高了4.3分。

en: Schellenberg had long been skeptical of the science supporting claims that music education enhances children's abstract reasoning, math, or language skills. (21 words)
cn: 舍伦贝格长期以来一直对支持音乐教育能提高儿童抽象推理、数学或语言技能这一说法的科学依据持怀疑态度。

en: If children who play the piano are smarter, he says, it doesn't necessarily mean they are smarter because they play the piano. (22 words)
cn: 他说，如果弹钢琴的孩子更聪明，这并不一定意味着他们因为弹钢琴而更聪明。

en: It could be that the youngsters who play the piano also happen to be more ambitious or better at focusing on a task. (23 words)
cn: 也可能是弹钢琴的年轻人碰巧更有抱负或更擅长专注于一项任务。

en: Correlation, after all, does not prove causation. (7 words)
cn: 毕竟，相关性并不能证明因果关系。

en: The 2004 paper was specifically designed to address those concerns. (10 words)
cn: 2004年的论文正是为了解决这些担忧而设计的。

en: And as a passionate musician, Schellenberg was delighted when he turned up credible evidence that music has transfer effects on general intelligence. (22 words)
cn: 作为一名充满激情的音乐家，舍伦贝格在找到可信证据证明音乐对一般智力有迁移效应时感到非常高兴。

en: But nearly a decade later, in 2013, the Education Endowment Foundation funded a bigger study with more than 900 students. (20 words)
cn: 但近十年后的2013年，教育捐赠基金会资助了一项规模更大的研究，涉及900多名学生。

en: That study failed to confirm Schellenberg's findings, producing no evidence that music lessons improved math and literacy skills. (18 words)
cn: 该研究未能证实舍伦贝格的发现，没有产生任何证据表明音乐课能提高数学和读写能力。

en: Schellenberg took that news in stride while continuing to cast a skeptical eye on the research in his field. (19 words)
cn: 舍伦贝格从容地接受了这一消息，同时继续对他所在领域的研究持怀疑态度。

en: Recently, he decided to formally investigate just how often his fellow researchers in psychology and neuroscience make what he believes are erroneous—or at least premature—causal connections between music and intelligence. (30 words)
cn: 最近，他决定正式调查他的心理学和神经科学同行们究竟有多频繁地在他认为是错误的——或至少是过早的——音乐与智力之间的因果关系上做出断言。

en: His results, published in May, suggest that many of his peers do just that. (14 words)
cn: 他于5月发表的结果表明，他的许多同行正是这样做的。

en: For his recent study, Schellenberg asked two research assistants to look for correlational studies on the effects of music education. (20 words)
cn: 在他最近的研究中，舍伦贝格要求两名研究助理寻找关于音乐教育效果的相关性研究。

en: They found a total of 114 papers published since 2000. (10 words)
cn: 他们找到了自2000年以来发表的共114篇论文。

en: To assess whether the authors claimed any causation, researchers then looked for telltale verbs in each paper's title and abstract, verbs like 'enhance,' 'promote,' 'facilitate,' and 'strengthen.' (27 words)
cn: 为了评估作者是否声称了任何因果关系，研究人员随后在每篇论文的标题和摘要中寻找一些能说明问题的动词，如‘增强’、‘促进’、‘推动’和‘加强’。

en: The papers were categorized as neuroscience if the study employed a brain imaging method like magnetic resonance, or if the study appeared in a journal that had 'brain,' 'neuroscience,' or a related term in its title. (36 words)
cn: 如果研究使用了磁共振等脑成像方法，或者研究发表在标题中含有‘脑’、‘神经科学’或相关术语的期刊上，则这些论文被归类为神经科学。

en: Otherwise the papers were categorized as psychology. (7 words)
cn: 否则，论文被归类为心理学。

en: Schellenberg didn't tell his assistants what exactly he was trying to prove. (12 words)
cn: 舍伦贝格没有告诉他的助手他到底想证明什么。

en: After computing their assessments, Schellenberg concluded that the majority of the articles erroneously claimed that music training had a causal effect. (21 words)
cn: 在计算了他们的评估后，舍伦贝格得出结论，大多数文章错误地声称音乐训练有因果效应。

en: The overselling, he also found, was more prevalent among neuroscience studies, three quarters of which mischaracterized a mere association between music training and skills enhancement as a cause-and-effect relationship. (29 words)
cn: 他还发现，过度宣传在神经科学研究中更为普遍，其中四分之三的研究错误地将音乐训练与技能提升之间的单纯关联描述为因果关系。

en: This may come as a surprise to some. (8 words)
cn: 这可能会让一些人感到惊讶。

en: Psychologists have been battling charges that they don't do 'real' science for some time—in large part because many findings from classic experiments have proved unreproducible. (25 words)
cn: 心理学家们一段时间以来一直在应对他们不做‘真正’科学的指控——在很大程度上是因为经典实验的许多发现已被证明无法重现。

en: Neuroscientists, on the other hand, armed with brain scans and EEGs, have not been subject to the same degree of critique. (21 words)
cn: 另一方面，拥有脑扫描和脑电图工具的神经科学家则没有受到同样程度的批评。

en: To argue for a cause-and-effect relationship, scientists must attempt to explain why and how a connection could occur. (18 words)
cn: 为了论证因果关系，科学家必须尝试解释这种联系为什么以及如何会发生。

en: When it comes to transfer effects of music, scientists frequently point to brain plasticity—the fact that the brain changes according to how we use it. (25 words)
cn: 当谈到音乐的迁移效应时，科学家经常提到大脑可塑性——即大脑会根据我们使用它的方式而改变这一事实。

en: When a child learns to play the violin, for example, several studies have shown that the brain region responsible for the fine motor skills of the left hand's fingers is likely to grow. (33 words)
cn: 例如，当孩子学习拉小提琴时，几项研究表明负责左手手指精细运动技能的大脑区域可能会增大。

en: And many experiments have shown that musical training improves certain hearing capabilities, like filtering voices from background noise or distinguishing the difference between the consonants 'b' and 'g'. (28 words)
cn: 许多实验也表明，音乐训练能提高某些听觉能力，比如从背景噪音中过滤人声，或区分辅音‘b’和‘g’之间的差异。

en: But Schellenberg remains highly critical of how the concept of plasticity has been applied in his field. (17 words)
cn: 但舍伦贝格对其领域中可塑性概念的应用方式仍然持高度批评态度。

en: Plasticity has become an industry of its own, he wrote in his May paper. (14 words)
cn: 他在5月的论文中写道：‘可塑性已经成为一个独立的产业。’

en: Practice does change the brain, he allows, but what is questionable is the assertion that these changes affect other brain regions, such as those responsible for spatial reasoning or math problems. (31 words)
cn: 他承认练习确实会改变大脑，但值得质疑的是这些变化会影响其他大脑区域的断言，比如负责空间推理或数学问题的区域。

en: Neuropsychologist Lutz Jancke agrees. (4 words)
cn: 神经心理学家卢茨·扬克表示赞同。

en: Most of these studies don't allow for causal inferences, he said. (11 words)
cn: 他说：‘这些研究大多不允许进行因果推断。’

en: For over two decades, Jancke has researched the effects of music lessons, and like Schellenberg, he believes that the only way to truly understand their effects is to run longitudinal studies. (31 words)
cn: 二十多年来，扬克一直在研究音乐课的效果，和舍伦贝格一样，他认为真正理解其效果的唯一方法是进行纵向研究。

en: In such studies, researchers would need to follow groups of children with and without music lessons over a long period of time—even if the assignments are not completely random. (29 words)
cn: 在这类研究中，研究人员需要长期跟踪有音乐课和没有音乐课的儿童群体——即使分配不是完全随机的。

en: Then they could compare outcomes for each group. (8 words)
cn: 然后他们可以比较每组的结果。

en: Some researchers are starting to do just that. (8 words)
cn: 一些研究人员正在开始这样做。

en: The neuroscientist Peter Schneider from Heidelberg University in Germany, for example, has been following a group of children for ten years now. (22 words)
cn: 例如，德国海德堡大学的神经科学家彼得·施奈德已经跟踪一组儿童长达十年。

en: Some of them were handed musical instruments and given lessons through a school-based program in the Ruhr region of Germany called Jedem Kind ein Instrument, or 'an instrument for every child,' which was carried out with government funding. (38 words)
cn: 其中一些孩子通过德国鲁尔地区一个名为‘每个孩子一件乐器’的学校项目获得了乐器并接受了课程，该项目由政府资助。

en: Among these children, Schneider has found that those who were enthusiastic about music and who practiced voluntarily showed improvements in hearing ability, as well as in more general competencies, such as the ability to concentrate. (35 words)
cn: 在这些孩子中，施奈德发现那些对音乐充满热情并自愿练习的孩子在听力能力以及更广泛的能力（如集中注意力的能力）上都有所提高。

en: To establish whether effects such as improved concentration are caused by music participation itself, and not by investing time in an extracurricular activity of any kind, Assal Habibi, a psychology professor at the University of Southern California, is conducting a five-year longitudinal study with children from low-income communities in Los Angeles. (51 words)
cn: 为了确定诸如注意力提高等效果是否由音乐参与本身引起，而不是由花时间参加任何一种课外活动引起，南加州大学心理学教授阿萨尔·哈比比正在对洛杉矶低收入社区的儿童进行一项为期五年的纵向研究。

en: The youngsters fall into three groups: those who take after-school music, those who do after-school sports, and those with no structured after-school program at all. (25 words)
cn: 这些年轻人分为三组：参加课后音乐课的、参加课后体育活动的，以及完全没有结构化课后活动的。

en: After two years, Habibi and her colleagues reported seeing structural changes in the brains of the musically trained children, both locally and in the pathways connecting different parts of the brain. (31 words)
cn: 两年后，哈比比和她的同事报告说，他们观察到接受音乐训练的儿童大脑中出现了结构变化，既在局部区域，也在连接大脑不同部分的通路中。

en: That may seem compelling, but Habibi's children were not selected randomly. (11 words)
cn: 这看起来可能很有说服力，但哈比比研究的儿童并非随机挑选的。

en: Did the children who were drawn to music perhaps have something in them from the start that made them different but eluded the brain scanners? (25 words)
cn: 那些被音乐吸引的孩子们是否从一开始就有什么东西使他们与众不同，但却逃过了脑部扫描仪的检测？

en: As somebody who started taking piano lessons at the age of five and got up every morning at seven to practice, that experience changed me and made me part of who I am today, Schellenberg said. (36 words)
cn: 舍伦贝格说：‘作为一个五岁开始学钢琴、每天早上七点起床练习的人，那段经历改变了我，塑造了今天的我。’

en: The question is whether those kinds of experiences do so systematically across individuals and create exactly the same changes. (19 words)
cn: ‘问题是，这类经历是否在不同个体身上系统地产生作用，并产生完全相同的改变。’

en: And I think that is that huge leap of faith. (10 words)
cn: ‘我认为那是巨大的信念飞跃。’

en: Did he have a hidden talent that others didn't have? (10 words)
cn: 他是否拥有别人没有的隐藏天赋？

en: Or more endurance than his peers? (6 words)
cn: 或者比同龄人更有耐力？

en: Music researchers tend, like Schellenberg, to be musicians themselves, and as he noted in his recent paper, 'the idea of positive cognitive and neural side effects from music training (and other pleasurable activities) is inherently appealing.' (36 words)
cn: 音乐研究人员往往和舍伦贝格一样，本身就是音乐家，正如他在最近的论文中指出的那样：‘音乐训练（和其他愉悦活动）带来的积极认知和神经副作用的想法本身就很吸引人。’

en: He also admits that if he had children of his own, he would encourage them to take music lessons and go to university. (23 words)
cn: 他还承认，如果他有自己的孩子，他会鼓励他们上音乐课和上大学。

en: I would think that it makes them better people, more critical, just wiser in general, he said. (17 words)
cn: 他说：‘我认为这会让他们成为更好的人，更具批判性，总的来说也更明智。’

en: But those convictions should be checked at the entrance to the lab, he added. (14 words)
cn: 但他补充说，这些信念应该在进入实验室时就被检查。

en: Otherwise, the work becomes religion or faith. (7 words)
cn: 否则，工作就会变成宗教或信仰。

en: You have to let go of your faith if you want to be a scientist. (15 words)
cn: 如果你想成为一名科学家，你就必须放弃你的信仰。

en: The trend toward rationality and enlightenment was endangered long before the advent of the World Wide Web. (17 words)
cn: 早在万维网出现之前，走向理性和启蒙的趋势就已受到威胁。

en: As Neil Postman noted in his 1985 book Amusing Ourselves to Death, the rise of television introduced not just a new medium but a new discourse: a gradual shift from a typographic culture to a photographic one, which in turn meant a shift from rationality to emotions, exposition to entertainment. (50 words)
cn: 正如尼尔·波兹曼在他1985年的著作《娱乐至死》中指出的那样，电视的兴起不仅引入了一种新媒介，还引入了一种新的话语方式：从印刷文化逐渐转向图像文化，这反过来又意味着从理性转向情感，从阐述转向娱乐。

en: In an image-centered and pleasure-driven world, Postman noted, there is no place for rational thinking, because you simply cannot think with images. (22 words)
cn: 波兹曼指出，在一个以图像为中心、以快乐为驱动的世界里，没有理性思考的空间，因为你根本无法用图像思考。

en: It is text that enables us to 'uncover lies, confusions and overgeneralizations, and to detect abuses of logic and common sense. (21 words)
cn: 正是文字使我们能够‘揭露谎言、混淆和过度概括，并发现滥用逻辑和常识的情况’。

en: It also means to weigh ideas, to compare and contrast assertions, to connect one generalization to another.' (17 words)
cn: ‘这也意味着权衡各种观点，比较和对照各种论断，将一个概括与另一个概括联系起来。’

en: The dominance of television was not confined to our living rooms. (11 words)
cn: 电视的主导地位并不局限于我们的客厅。

en: It overturned all of those habits of mind, fundamentally changing our experience of the world, affecting the conduct of politics, religion, business, and culture. (24 words)
cn: 它颠覆了所有这些思维习惯，从根本上改变了我们对世界的体验，影响了政治、宗教、商业和文化的运行方式。

en: It reduced many aspects of modern life to entertainment, sensationalism, and commerce. (12 words)
cn: 它将现代生活的许多方面简化为娱乐、煽情和商业。

en: Americans don't talk to each other, we entertain each other, Postman wrote. (12 words)
cn: 波兹曼写道：‘美国人不互相交谈，而是互相娱乐。’

en: They don't exchange ideas, they exchange images. (7 words)
cn: ‘他们不交换思想，他们交换图像。’

en: They do not argue with propositions, they argue with good looks, celebrities and commercials.' (14 words)
cn: ‘他们不用命题来争论，他们用美貌、名人和广告来争论。’

en: At first, the web seemed to push against this trend. (10 words)
cn: 起初，网络似乎是在反对这一趋势。

en: When it emerged towards the end of the 1980s as a purely text-based medium, it was seen as a tool to pursue knowledge, not pleasure. (25 words)
cn: 当它在20世纪80年代末作为一种纯文本媒介出现时，它被视为追求知识而非娱乐的工具。

en: Reason and thought were most valued in this garden—all derived from the project of the Enlightenment. (16 words)
cn: 在这个园地里，理性和思想最受重视——这一切都源于启蒙运动的规划。

en: Universities around the world were among the first to connect to this new medium, which hosted discussion groups, informative personal or group blogs, electronic magazines, and academic mailing lists and forums. (31 words)
cn: 世界各地的大学是最早连接到这种新媒介的机构之一，这种媒介承载着讨论组、信息丰富的个人或团体博客、电子杂志以及学术邮件列表和论坛。

en: It was an intellectual project, not about commerce or control, created in a scientific research center in Switzerland. (18 words)
cn: 这是一个知识性的项目，与商业或控制无关，是在瑞士的一个科学研究中心创建的。

en: And for more than a decade, the web created an alternative space that threatened television's grip on society. (18 words)
cn: 十多年来，网络创造了一个替代性空间，威胁到了电视对社会的掌控。

en: Social networks, though, have since colonized the web for television's values. (11 words)
cn: 然而，社交网络此后用电视的价值观占领了网络。

en: From Facebook to Instagram, the medium refocuses our attention on videos and images, rewarding emotional appeals—'like' buttons—over rational ones. (19 words)
cn: 从Facebook到Instagram，这些媒介将我们的注意力重新集中在视频和图像上，奖励情感诉求——‘点赞’按钮——而非理性的诉求。

en: Instead of a quest for knowledge, it engages us in an endless zest for instant approval from an audience, for which we are constantly but unconsciously performing. (27 words)
cn: 它不是让我们追求知识，而是让我们沉浸在对观众即时认可的无限热情中，为此我们不断地、无意识地表演。

en: It's telling that, while Google began life as a PhD thesis, Facebook started as a tool to judge classmates' appearances. (20 words)
cn: 具有说明意义的是，虽然Google始于一篇博士论文，但Facebook最初是作为评判同学外貌的工具。

en: It reduces our curiosity by showing us exactly what we already want and think, based on our profiles and preferences. (20 words)
cn: 它根据我们的个人资料和偏好，准确地向我们展示我们已经想要和思考的内容，从而削弱了我们的好奇心。

en: The Enlightenment's motto of 'Dare to know' has become 'Dare not to care to know.' (15 words)
cn: 启蒙运动的座右铭‘敢于知道’已经变成了‘不敢在乎知道’。

en: According to a recent study, a small but growing proportion of the workforce is affected to some degree by a sense of entitlement. (23 words)
cn: 根据最近的一项研究，一小部分但不断增长的劳动力在某种程度上受到了特权感的影响。

en: Work is less about what they can contribute but more about what they can take. (15 words)
cn: 工作不再是他们能贡献什么，而是他们能获取什么。

en: It can lead to workplace dysfunction and diminish their own job satisfaction. (12 words)
cn: 这会导致工作场所的功能失调，并降低他们自己的工作满意度。

en: I'm not referring to employees who are legitimately dissatisfied with their employment conditions due to, say, being denied fair pay or flexible work practices. (24 words)
cn: 我不是指那些因为被拒绝公平薪酬或灵活工作安排等而对工作条件有正当不满的员工。

en: I'm talking about those who consistently believe they deserve special treatment and generous rewards. (14 words)
cn: 我指的是那些始终认为自己应该得到特殊待遇和丰厚回报的人。

en: It's an expectation that exists irrespective of their abilities or levels of performance. (13 words)
cn: 这是一种期望，与他们的能力或表现水平无关。

en: As a result of that discrepancy between the privileges they feel they're owed and their inflated sense of self-worth, they don't work as hard for their employer. (27 words)
cn: 由于他们觉得自己应得的特权与膨胀的自我价值感之间的差距，他们不会为雇主那么努力地工作。

en: They prefer instead to slack off. (6 words)
cn: 他们反而更愿意偷懒。

en: It's a tendency which many scholars believe begins in childhood due to parents who overindulge their kids. (17 words)
cn: 许多学者认为，这种倾向始于童年，因为父母过度溺爱孩子。

en: This thereby leads them to expect the same kind of spoilt treatment throughout their adult lives. (16 words)
cn: 这进而导致他们在整个成年生活中都期望得到同样的娇惯待遇。

en: And yet despite how these employees feel, it's obviously important for their manager to nonetheless find out how to keep them motivated. (22 words)
cn: 然而，尽管这些员工有这些感受，但他们的经理仍然需要找到如何保持他们积极性的方法，这显然很重要。

en: And, by virtue of that heightened motivation, to perform well. (10 words)
cn: 并且，通过这种增强的积极性，让他们表现良好。

en: The research team from several American universities surveyed more than 240 individuals. (12 words)
cn: 来自几所美国大学的研究团队调查了240多人。

en: They sampled managers as well as team members. (8 words)
cn: 他们对经理和团队成员都进行了抽样调查。

en: Employee entitlement was measured by statements such as 'I honestly feel I'm just more deserving than others.' (17 words)
cn: 员工的特权感通过诸如‘我真的觉得自己比别人更值得’之类的陈述来衡量。

en: The respondents had to rate the extent of their agreement. (10 words)
cn: 受访者必须对他们的同意程度进行评分。

en: Employee engagement, meanwhile, was assessed with statements like 'I really throw myself into my work.' (15 words)
cn: 同时，员工敬业度通过‘我真的全身心投入工作’等陈述来评估。

en: The findings revealed ethical leadership is precisely what alleviates the negative effects of employee entitlement. (15 words)
cn: 研究结果表明，道德领导正是减轻员工特权感负面影响的因素。

en: That's because rather than indulging employees or neglecting them, ethical leaders communicate very direct and clear expectations. (17 words)
cn: 这是因为，道德领导者不会纵容员工或忽视他们，而是会传达非常直接和明确的期望。

en: They also hold employees accountable for their behaviors and are genuinely committed to doing the right thing. (17 words)
cn: 他们还要求员工为自己的行为负责，并真诚地致力于做正确的事情。

en: Additionally, these leaders are consistent in their standards. (8 words)
cn: 此外，这些领导者的标准是一致的。

en: They're also less likely to deviate in how they treat employees. (11 words)
cn: 他们也不太可能在对待员工的方式上有所偏差。

en: This means, when confronted by an entitled team member, an ethical leader is significantly disinclined to accommodate their demands. (19 words)
cn: 这意味着，当面对一个有特权感的团队成员时，道德领导者非常不愿意迁就他们的要求。

en: He or she will instead point out, constructively and tactfully, exactly how their inflated sense of deservingness is somewhat distorted. (20 words)
cn: 相反，他或她会以建设性和巧妙的方式指出，他们膨胀的应得感在哪些方面是有些扭曲的。

en: They'd then go further to explain the specific, and objective, criteria the employee must meet to receive their desired rewards. (20 words)
cn: 然后他们会进一步解释员工必须满足的具体、客观的标准，才能获得他们想要的回报。

en: This shift away from unrealistic expectations is successful because entitled employees feel more confident that ethical leaders will deliver on their promises. (22 words)
cn: 这种脱离不切实际期望的转变之所以成功，是因为有特权感的员工更有信心，相信道德领导者会兑现他们的承诺。

en: This occurs because they're perceived to be fair and trustworthy. (10 words)
cn: 这是因为他们被认为公平且值得信赖。

en: The researchers, however, exercise caution by warning no one single response is the perfect remedy. (15 words)
cn: 然而，研究人员保持谨慎，警告说没有哪一种单一回应是完美的补救措施。

en: But there's no denying ethical leadership is at least a critical step in the right direction. (16 words)
cn: 但不可否认，道德领导至少是朝着正确方向迈出的关键一步。

en: The economist J. K. Galbraith once wrote, 'Faced with a choice between changing one's mind and proving there is no need to do so, almost everyone gets busy with the proof.' (31 words)
cn: 经济学家J·K·加尔布雷思曾写道：‘面对改变主意和证明没有必要改变主意之间的选择，几乎每个人都会忙于证明。’

en: Leo Tolstoy was even bolder: 'The most difficult subjects can be explained to the most slow-witted man if he has not formed any idea of them already; but the simplest thing cannot be made clear to the most intelligent man if he is firmly persuaded that he knows already, without a shadow of a doubt, what is laid before him.' (60 words)
cn: 列夫·托尔斯泰更大胆：‘最困难的课题可以解释给最迟钝的人，如果他还没有形成任何关于它们的想法；但最简单的事情也无法让最聪明的人明白，如果他坚信自己已经毫无疑问地知道了摆在他面前的是什么。’

en: What's going on here? (4 words)
cn: 这到底是怎么回事？

en: Why don't facts change our minds? (6 words)
cn: 为什么事实不能改变我们的想法？

en: And why would someone continue to believe a false or inaccurate idea anyway? (13 words)
cn: 而且，为什么有人会继续相信一个错误或不准确的想法呢？

en: How do such behaviors serve us? (6 words)
cn: 这种行为对我们有什么好处？

en: Humans need a reasonably accurate view of the world in order to survive. (13 words)
cn: 人类需要相当准确的世界观才能生存。

en: If your model of reality is wildly different from the actual world, then you struggle to take effective actions each day. (21 words)
cn: 如果你的现实模型与实际世界大相径庭，那么你每天都会难以采取有效的行动。

en: However, truth and accuracy are not the only things that matter to the human mind. (15 words)
cn: 然而，真理和准确性并不是对人类心智重要的唯一事物。

en: Humans also seem to have a deep desire to belong. (10 words)
cn: 人类似乎也有一种深切的归属感渴望。

en: In Atomic Habits, I wrote, 'Humans are herd animals. (9 words)
cn: 在《原子习惯》一书中，我写道：‘人类是群居动物。’

en: We want to fit in, to bond with others, and to earn the respect and approval of our peers. (19 words)
cn: ‘我们想要融入群体，与他人建立联系，并赢得同龄人的尊重和认可。’

en: Such inclinations are essential to our survival. (7 words)
cn: ‘这种倾向对我们的生存至关重要。’

en: For most of our evolutionary history, our ancestors lived in tribes. (11 words)
cn: ‘在我们进化史的大部分时间里，我们的祖先生活在部落中。’

en: Becoming separated from the tribe—or worse, being cast out—was a death sentence.' (12 words)
cn: ‘与部落分离——或者更糟，被驱逐出去——就等于被判死刑。’

en: Understanding the truth of a situation is important, but so is remaining part of a tribe. (16 words)
cn: 理解情况的真相很重要，但留在部落中也同样重要。

en: While these two desires often work well together, they occasionally come into conflict. (13 words)
cn: 虽然这两种愿望通常能够很好地协同作用，但它们偶尔也会发生冲突。

en: In many circumstances, social connection is actually more helpful to your daily life than understanding the truth of a particular fact or idea. (23 words)
cn: 在许多情况下，社会联系实际上比理解某个特定事实或想法的真相对你的日常生活更有帮助。

en: The Harvard psychologist Steven Pinker put it this way: 'People are embraced or condemned according to their beliefs, so one function of the mind may be to hold beliefs that bring the belief-holder the greatest number of allies, protectors, or disciples, rather than beliefs that are most likely to be true.' (51 words)
cn: 哈佛大学心理学家史蒂芬·平克是这样说的：‘人们根据他们的信仰被接纳或谴责，所以心智的一个功能可能是持有能带给信仰者最多盟友、保护者或信徒的信仰，而不是最可能真实的信仰。’

en: We don't always believe things because they are correct. (9 words)
cn: 我们并不总是因为事物是正确的才相信它们。

en: Sometimes we believe things because they make us look good to the people we care about. (16 words)
cn: 有时我们相信某件事是因为它们让我们在我们关心的人面前看起来很好。

en: I thought Kevin Simler put it well when he wrote, 'If a brain anticipates that it will be rewarded for adopting a particular belief, it's perfectly happy to do so, and doesn't much care where the reward comes from—whether it's pragmatic (better outcomes resulting from better decisions), social (better treatment from one's peers), or some mix of the two.' (59 words)
cn: 我认为凯文·西姆勒说得很好，他写道：‘如果大脑预期采用某种特定信念会得到回报，它很乐意这样做，并且不太关心回报来自哪里——无论是实用主义的（更好的决策带来更好的结果）、社会性的（来自同龄人更好的待遇），还是两者的某种混合。’

en: False beliefs can be useful in a social sense even if they are not useful in a factual sense. (19 words)
cn: 错误的信念在社会意义上有用，即使它们在事实意义上没有用。

en: For lack of a better phrase, we might call this approach 'factually false, but socially accurate.' (16 words)
cn: 由于缺乏更好的说法，我们可以称这种方法为‘事实错误，但社会准确’。

en: When we have to choose between the two, people often select friends and family over facts. (16 words)
cn: 当我们必须在两者之间做出选择时，人们往往选择朋友和家人而非事实。

en: This insight not only explains why we might hold our tongue at a dinner party or look the other way when our parents say something offensive, but also reveals a better way to change the minds of others. (38 words)
cn: 这一洞见不仅解释了为什么我们可能会在晚宴上保持沉默，或者在父母说了一些冒犯性的话时视而不见，而且还揭示了一种改变他人想法的更好方法。

en: Convincing someone to change their mind is really the process of convincing them to change their tribe. (17 words)
cn: 说服某人改变主意实际上就是说服他们改变部落的过程。

en: If they abandon their beliefs, they run the risk of losing social ties. (13 words)
cn: 如果他们放弃自己的信仰，他们就有失去社会关系的风险。

en: You can't expect someone to change their mind if you take away their community too. (15 words)
cn: 如果你也带走了他们的社群，你就不能指望某人改变主意。

en: You have to give them somewhere to go. (8 words)
cn: 你必须给他们一个去处。

en: Nobody wants their worldview torn apart if loneliness is the outcome. (11 words)
cn: 如果结果是孤独，没有人希望自己的世界观被撕裂。

en: The way to change people's minds is to become friends with them, to integrate them into your tribe, to bring them into your circle. (24 words)
cn: 改变人们想法的方法是和他们成为朋友，把他们融入你的部落，把他们带入你的圈子。

en: Now, they can change their beliefs without the risk of being abandoned socially. (13 words)
cn: 现在，他们可以在没有社会遗弃风险的情况下改变自己的信仰。

en: Perhaps it is not difference, but distance, that breeds tribalism and hostility. (12 words)
cn: 也许滋生部落主义和敌意的不是差异，而是距离。

en: As proximity increases, so does understanding. (6 words)
cn: 随着距离的拉近，理解也在增加。

en: I am reminded of Abraham Lincoln's quote, 'I don't like that man. (12 words)
cn: 我想起了亚伯拉罕·林肯的名言：‘我不喜欢那个人。’

en: I must get to know him better.' (7 words)
cn: ‘我必须更好地了解他。’

en: Facts don't change our minds. (5 words)
cn: 事实不会改变我们的想法。

en: Friendship does. (2 words)
cn: 友谊才能。

en: Years ago, Ben Casnocha mentioned an idea to me that I haven't been able to shake: The people who are most likely to change our minds are the ones we agree with on 98 percent of topics. (37 words)
cn: 多年前，本·卡斯诺查向我提出了一个我一直无法释怀的想法：最可能改变我们想法的是那些我们在98%的话题上都持相同观点的人。

en: If someone you know, like, and trust believes a radical idea, you are more likely to give it merit, weight, or consideration. (22 words)
cn: 如果你认识、喜欢和信任的人相信一个激进的想法，你更可能给予它价值、重视或考虑。

en: You already agree with them in most areas of life. (10 words)
cn: 你在生活的大多数领域已经与他们意见一致。

en: Maybe you should change your mind on this one too. (10 words)
cn: 也许你也应该在这个问题上改变主意。

en: But if someone wildly different than you proposes the same radical idea, well, it's easy to dismiss them as nuts. (20 words)
cn: 但如果一个与你截然不同的人提出同样的激进想法，那么，很容易把他们当作疯子而不予理会。

en: One way to visualize this distinction is by mapping beliefs on a spectrum. (13 words)
cn: 将这种区别可视化的一种方法是将信念映射在一个光谱上。

en: If you divide this spectrum into 10 units and you find yourself at Position 7, then there is little sense in trying to convince someone at Position 1. (28 words)
cn: 如果你把这个光谱分成10个单位，而你发现自己处于位置7，那么试图说服位置1的人就没有多大意义了。

en: The gap is too wide. (5 words)
cn: 差距太大了。

en: When you're at Position 7, your time is better spent connecting with people who are at Positions 6 and 8, gradually pulling them in your direction. (26 words)
cn: 当你处于位置7时，你的时间最好花在与位置6和8的人建立联系上，逐渐把他们拉向你的方向。

en: The most heated arguments often occur between people on opposite ends of the spectrum, but the most frequent learning occurs from people who are nearby. (25 words)
cn: 最激烈的争论往往发生在光谱两端的人之间，但最频繁的学习来自附近的人。

en: The closer you are to someone, the more likely it becomes that the one or two beliefs you don't share will bleed over into your own mind and shape your thinking. (31 words)
cn: 你离某人越近，你们没有共享的一两个信念就越有可能渗透到你的脑海中并塑造你的思维。

en: The further away an idea is from your current position, the more likely you are to reject it outright. (19 words)
cn: 一个想法离你当前位置越远，你就越有可能直接拒绝它。

en: When it comes to changing people's minds, it is very difficult to jump from one side to another. (18 words)
cn: 当涉及到改变人们的想法时，从一边跳到另一边是非常困难的。

en: You can't jump down the spectrum. (6 words)
cn: 你不能在光谱上跳跃。

en: You have to slide down it. (6 words)
cn: 你必须沿着它滑下去。

en: Any idea that is sufficiently different from your current worldview will feel threatening. (13 words)
cn: 任何与你当前世界观差异足够大的想法都会让人感到威胁。

en: And the best place to ponder a threatening idea is in a non-threatening environment. (14 words)
cn: 而思考一个具有威胁性的想法的最佳场所是在一个没有威胁的环境中。

en: As a result, books are often a better vehicle for transforming beliefs than conversations or debates. (16 words)
cn: 因此，书籍通常是比对话或辩论更好的改变信念的载体。

en: In conversation, people have to carefully consider their status and appearance. (11 words)
cn: 在对话中，人们必须仔细考虑自己的地位和形象。

en: They want to save face and avoid looking stupid. (9 words)
cn: 他们想要保全面子，避免看起来很愚蠢。

en: When confronted with an uncomfortable set of facts, the tendency is often to double down on their current position rather than publicly admit to being wrong. (26 words)
cn: 当面对一组令人不快的事实时，人们往往倾向于加倍坚持自己目前的立场，而不是公开承认错误。

en: Books resolve this tension. (4 words)
cn: 书籍解决了这种紧张关系。

en: With a book, the conversation takes place inside someone's head and without the risk of being judged by others. (19 words)
cn: 有了书，对话发生在某人的头脑中，没有被人评判的风险。

en: It's easier to be open-minded when you aren't feeling defensive. (10 words)
cn: 当你不感到防御时，更容易保持开放的心态。

en: There is another reason bad ideas continue to live on, which is that people continue to talk about them. (19 words)
cn: 坏想法继续存在的另一个原因是人们继续谈论它们。

en: Silence is death for any idea. (6 words)
cn: 沉默对任何想法来说都是死亡。

en: An idea that is never spoken or written down dies with the person who conceived it. (16 words)
cn: 一个从未被说出或写下的想法会随着构思它的人一起消亡。

en: Ideas can only be remembered when they are repeated. (9 words)
cn: 想法只有在被重复时才能被记住。

en: They can only be believed when they are repeated. (9 words)
cn: 它们只有在被重复时才能被相信。

en: I have already pointed out that people repeat ideas to signal they are part of the same social group. (19 words)
cn: 我已经指出，人们重复想法是为了表明他们是同一社会群体的一部分。

en: But here's a crucial point most people miss: People also repeat bad ideas when they complain about them. (18 words)
cn: 但这里有一个大多数人忽略的关键点：人们在抱怨坏想法时也在重复它们。

en: Before you can criticize an idea, you have to reference that idea. (12 words)
cn: 在你批评一个想法之前，你必须先提及那个想法。

en: You end up repeating the ideas you're hoping people will forget—but, of course, people can't forget them because you keep talking about them. (23 words)
cn: 你最终会重复你希望人们忘记的想法——但当然，人们无法忘记它们，因为你一直在谈论它们。

en: The more you repeat a bad idea, the more likely people are to believe it. (15 words)
cn: 你重复一个坏想法的次数越多，人们就越有可能相信它。

en: Let's call this phenomenon Clear's Law of Recurrence: The number of people who believe an idea is directly proportional to the number of times it has been repeated during the last year—even if the idea is false. (37 words)
cn: 让我们称这种现象为‘克利尔重复定律’：相信某个想法的人数与它在过去一年中被重复的次数成正比——即使这个想法是错误的。

en: The subject of automation and its role in our economy has taken hold in American public discourse. (17 words)
cn: 自动化及其在经济中的作用这一话题已经在美国公众讨论中占据了一席之地。

en: Technology broadly and automation specifically are dramatically reshaping the way we work. (12 words)
cn: 广义上的技术，特别是自动化，正在极大地重塑我们的工作方式。

en: And we need to have a plan for what's still to come. (12 words)
cn: 我们需要为未来做好准备。

en: We don't have to look further than our own communities to see the devastating impact of automation. (17 words)
cn: 我们不必看得太远，只看自己的社区就能看到自动化的毁灭性影响。

en: From automated warehouses to cashierless grocery stores to neighborhood libraries that offer self-checkout lanes instead of employing real people—automation is increasingly replacing jobs and leaving too few good new jobs behind. (31 words)
cn: 从自动化仓库到无人收银杂货店，再到提供自助结账通道而非雇用真人的社区图书馆——自动化正日益取代工作岗位，留下的好新工作岗位太少。

en: The statistics in manufacturing are staggering. (6 words)
cn: 制造业的统计数据令人震惊。

en: Despite the widespread fears about trade, a recent report showed that just 13 percent of jobs lost in manufacturing are due to trade—the rest of the losses have been due to advances in technology. (34 words)
cn: 尽管人们对贸易普遍存在担忧，但最近的一份报告显示，制造业流失的工作岗位中只有13%是由于贸易造成的——其余损失是由于技术进步造成的。

en: That is why more people are criticizing the ever-increasing role of technology in our economy. (15 words)
cn: 这就是为什么越来越多的人在批评技术在我们经济中日益增长的作用。

en: Our country is manufacturing more than ever before, but we are doing it with fewer workers. (16 words)
cn: 我们的国家正在生产比以往任何时候都多的产品，但我们正在用更少的工人来完成。

en: However, it's not just factories that are seeing losses—software and information technology are also having a dramatic impact on jobs most people think are secure from the forces of a rapidly-changing economy. (32 words)
cn: 然而，不仅仅是工厂正在遭受损失——软件和信息技术也对大多数人认为在快速变化的经济中安全的工作产生了巨大影响。

en: Something transformative is happening in America that is having an adverse effect on American families. (15 words)
cn: 美国正在发生某种变革性的事情，这对美国家庭产生了不利影响。

en: Whether policymakers and politicians admit it or not, workers have made clear their feelings about their economic insecurity and desire to keep good jobs in America. (26 words)
cn: 无论政策制定者和政客们承认与否，工人们已经清楚地表达了他们对经济不安全的感受以及在美国保留好工作的愿望。

en: So why are people so insistent on ignoring the perils of automation? (12 words)
cn: 那么，为什么人们如此坚持忽视自动化的危险呢？

en: They are failing to look ahead at a time when planning for the future is more important than ever. (19 words)
cn: 他们未能在规划未来比以往任何时候都更重要的时刻向前看。

en: Resisting automation is futile: it is as inevitable as industrialization was before it. (13 words)
cn: 抵制自动化是徒劳的：它就像之前的工业化一样不可避免。

en: I sincerely hope that those who assert that automation will make us more effective and pave the way for new occupations are right, but the reality of automation's detrimental effects on workers makes me skeptical. (35 words)
cn: 我真诚地希望那些断言自动化将使我们更有效率并为新职业铺平道路的人是正确的，但自动化对工人的有害影响的现实使我一直持怀疑态度。

en: No one can currently say where the new jobs are coming from or when, and any sensible company or country should prepare for all alternatives. (25 words)
cn: 目前没有人能说出新工作岗位来自哪里或何时出现，任何明智的公司或国家都应该为所有可能性做好准备。

en: I'm not overstating the danger: look at what's happened to the labor force. (13 words)
cn: 我并没有夸大危险：看看劳动力发生了什么。

en: According to economic research, one in six working-age men, 25—54, doesn't have a job. (14 words)
cn: 根据经济研究，25至54岁的劳动年龄男性中，每六人就有一人没有工作。

en: Fifty years ago, nearly 100 percent of men that age were working. (12 words)
cn: 五十年前，这个年龄段的男性几乎百分之百都在工作。

en: Women's labor force participation, meanwhile, has slipped back to the level it was at in the late 1980s. (18 words)
cn: 与此同时，女性的劳动力参与率已经下滑到20世纪80年代末的水平。

en: American families and prominent business leaders are aware that there's a big problem with automation. (15 words)
cn: 美国家庭和知名商界领袖都意识到自动化存在一个大问题。

en: The value of a college degree is diminishing, and our upward mobility is declining. (14 words)
cn: 大学学位的价值正在下降，我们的向上流动性也在下降。

en: If we want an economy that allows everyone to be economically secure, we need to start thinking about how we can rightfully address automation. (24 words)
cn: 如果我们想要一个让每个人都能获得经济保障的经济，我们就需要开始思考如何正确地应对自动化。

en: Look at the people around you. (6 words)
cn: 看看你周围的人。

en: Some are passive, others more aggressive. (6 words)
cn: 有些人是被动的，另一些人则更积极进取。

en: Some work best alone, others crave companionship. (7 words)
cn: 有些人独自工作效果最好，另一些人则渴望陪伴。

en: We easily recognize that there is great variation among the individuals who live near us. (15 words)
cn: 我们很容易认识到，住在我们附近的人之间存在着很大的差异。

en: Yet, when we speak of people from elsewhere, we seem to inevitably characterize them based on their country of origin. (20 words)
cn: 然而，当我们谈论来自其他地方的人时，我们似乎不可避免地根据他们的国籍来对他们进行定性。

en: Statistics specialists, when they speak of national averages, often make the same mistake. (13 words)
cn: 统计专家在谈论全国平均水平时，往往犯同样的错误。

en: Newly published research shows how erroneous such overviews are. (9 words)
cn: 新发表的研究表明，这种概览是多么错误。

en: Three researchers analyzed decades of values-based surveys and found that only between 16% and 21% of the variation in cultural values could be explained by differences between countries. (28 words)
cn: 三位研究人员分析了数十年的基于价值观的调查，发现文化价值观的差异中只有16%到21%可以用国家之间的差异来解释。

en: In other words, the vast majority of what makes us culturally distinct from one another has nothing to do with our homeland. (22 words)
cn: 换句话说，使我们文化上彼此区别的绝大多数因素与我们的祖国无关。

en: To determine what factors really are associated with culture, the authors combined data from 558 prior surveys that each measured one or more of Hofstede's cultural dimensions. (27 words)
cn: 为了确定哪些因素真正与文化相关，作者合并了558项先前调查的数据，这些调查分别测量了霍夫斯泰德文化维度中的一个或多个。

en: These are traits, such as individualism and masculinity, that describe work-related cultural values. (13 words)
cn: 这些是描述与工作相关的文化价值观的特征，如个人主义和男性气质。

en: They are not a measure of visible cultural traits, such as food or dress. (14 words)
cn: 它们不是对可见文化特征（如食物或服饰）的衡量。

en: Though the validity of Hofstede's dimensions has been questioned, they have the singular benefit of having been in use for decades, which allows for historical and international comparisons. (28 words)
cn: 尽管霍夫斯泰德维度的有效性受到质疑，但它们有一个独特的好处，即已经使用了数十年，这允许进行历史和跨国际的比较。

en: The researchers found that both demographic factors, such as age, and environmental factors, such as long-term unemployment rates, were more correlated with cultural values than nationality. (26 words)
cn: 研究人员发现，人口因素（如年龄）和环境因素（如长期失业率）与文化价值观的相关性都高于国籍。

en: Occupation and social economic status were the most strongly correlated, suggesting that our values are more economically driven than we usually give them credit for. (25 words)
cn: 职业和社会经济地位的相关性最强，这表明我们的价值观比我们通常认为的更多地受经济驱动。

en: The evidence implies that people with similar jobs and incomes are more culturally alike, regardless of where they live. (19 words)
cn: 证据表明，具有相似工作和收入的人在文化上更相似，无论他们住在哪里。

en: Vas Taras, the lead author of the study, puts it this way: 'Tell me how much you make and I will make a pretty accurate prediction about your cultural values. (30 words)
cn: 该研究的主要作者瓦斯·塔拉斯是这样说的：‘告诉我你赚多少钱，我就能对你的文化价值观做出相当准确的预测。’

en: Tell me what your nationality is and I probably will make a wrong prediction.' (14 words)
cn: ‘告诉我你的国籍，我很可能会做出错误的预测。’

en: Taras says our erroneous belief that countries are cultures has caused businesses to teach their employees useless or even harmful ways of interacting with their international peers. (27 words)
cn: 塔拉斯说，我们认为国家就是文化的错误信念导致企业向员工传授与国际化同行互动的无用甚至有害的方式。

en: Chinese and American lawyers might be trained to interact based on the assumption that the Chinese person is less individualistic, even though their similar social economic situations make it probable they are actually quite alike in that regard. (38 words)
cn: 中国和美国律师可能会接受基于中国人较少个人主义的假设的互动培训，尽管他们相似的社会经济状况使得他们在这一方面实际上很可能非常相似。

en: The country, as the unit of authority, is often a convenient way of generalizing about a population. (17 words)
cn: 国家作为权威单位，通常是对人口进行概括的一种便捷方式。

en: However, our focus on countries can mask broad variations within them. (11 words)
cn: 然而，我们对国家的关注可能会掩盖国家内部的广泛差异。

en: In the majority of cases we would be better off identifying people by the factors that constrain their lives, like income, rather than by the lines surrounding them on a map. (31 words)
cn: 在大多数情况下，我们最好根据限制他们生活的因素（如收入）来识别人们，而不是根据地图上围绕他们的线条。

en: The city of Bath was founded by the Romans almost two thousand years ago. (14 words)
cn: 巴斯城由罗马人建于近两千年前。

en: It has been famous for its aesthetically pleasing architecture and healing thermal springs ever since. (15 words)
cn: 从此，它便以其赏心悦目的建筑和具有疗效的温泉而闻名。

en: There are three hot springs in Bath; one is the King's Spring, upon which the Roman Baths and a temple were constructed. (22 words)
cn: 巴斯有三处温泉；一处是国王泉，罗马浴场和一座神庙就建在其上。

en: The other two are the Cross Spring and the Hetling Spring, close to each other in Hot Bath Street. (19 words)
cn: 另外两处是十字泉和海特灵泉，在热浴街彼此相邻。

en: Although Bath is principally known as a Roman and Georgian city, many people came in the intervening centuries to make use of the natural waters. (25 words)
cn: 尽管巴斯主要作为罗马和乔治亚时期的城市而闻名，但在其间的几个世纪里，许多人前来利用这里的天然泉水。

en: While the Georgians made 'taking the waters' or bathing particularly fashionable, it was previous generations who paved the way, creating greater interest in Bath and its springs. (27 words)
cn: 虽然乔治亚人使‘泡温泉’或洗浴变得特别时尚，但却是前几代人铺平了道路，引发了人们对巴斯及其温泉的更大兴趣。

en: Charles II, desperate for an heir and unable to produce a legitimate son, came to Bath to take the waters in the hope that their magical powers would do something to remedy the situation. (34 words)
cn: 查理二世迫切渴望一个继承人，却无法生下一个合法的儿子，于是他来到巴斯泡温泉，希望泉水的神奇力量能扭转局面。

en: Craving for a male heir, James and Mary both came to Bath and soon after produced a son, which bred many conspiracy theories about who was the real father of their offspring. (32 words)
cn: 詹姆斯和玛丽都渴望一个男性继承人，他们双双来到巴斯，不久便生下一个儿子，这引发了诸多关于他们后代亲生父亲是谁的阴谋论。

en: Regardless, the 'miracle' created something of a boom in tourism for Bath and once Queen Anne had paid a visit in 1702, sealing it as the place to be, the whole nation flocked to the city. (36 words)
cn: 尽管如此，这一‘奇迹’为巴斯的旅游业带来了一定的繁荣，而且当安妮女王于1702年造访此地，将其确认为必到之处后，全国人都涌向了这座城市。

en: Afterwards, the spas in Bath continued to go in and out of fashion for more than 150 years until they closed completely. (22 words)
cn: 此后，巴斯的矿泉疗养浴场时兴时衰，持续了150多年，直到完全关闭。

en: The new Bath Spa, which opened in 2006, incorporates modern architecture with the ancient spring, now the New Royal Bath. (20 words)
cn: 2006年开放的新巴斯温泉浴场，将现代建筑与古老的泉水融为一体，即现在的新皇家浴场。

en: Fazila is a young woman that has been dealing with eczema, a common skin condition, for the past five years, but never got it treated. (25 words)
cn: 法齐拉是一位年轻女性，过去五年来一直患有湿疹（一种常见的皮肤病），但从未接受过治疗。

en: The nearest hospital is an hour away, by boat and bus, and her skin condition didn't seem serious enough to make the trek, so she ignored it- until a new technology brought the doctor to her. (36 words)
cn: 最近的医院也要乘船和公共汽车一个小时的路程，而她的皮肤病似乎并不严重到值得长途跋涉，所以她一直没管——直到一项新技术把医生带到了她面前。

en: Fazila lives on one of the remote river islands in northern Bangladesh. (12 words)
cn: 法齐拉住在孟加拉国北部的一个偏远河岛上。

en: These islands are low-lying, temporary sand islands that are continuously formed and destroyed through sand buildup and erosion. (18 words)
cn: 这些岛屿是低洼的临时沙岛，通过泥沙堆积和侵蚀不断形成和消失。

en: They are home to over six million people, who face repeated displacement from flooding and erosion- which may be getting worse because of climate change-and a range of health risks, including poor nutrition, malaria and other water-borne diseases. (38 words)
cn: 这些岛屿是六百多万人的家园，他们面临着洪水和水土流失带来的反复流离失所——气候变化可能使情况更加恶化——以及一系列健康风险，包括营养不良、疟疾和其他水源性疾病。

en: The most dangerous thing for these remote island dwellers is land erosion. (12 words)
cn: 对这些偏远岛屿居民来说，最危险的是水土流失。

en: The second is lack of access to medical supplies and doctors. (11 words)
cn: 其次是缺乏医疗用品和医生。

en: There are no doctors within miles, and while child mortality and maternal death have gone down in the rest of the country, this is not the case for the islands. (30 words)
cn: 方圆数英里内没有医生，尽管该国其他地区的儿童死亡率和孕产妇死亡率有所下降，但这些岛屿的情况并非如此。

en: The medical situation is so bad that it really takes away from the quality of their life. (17 words)
cn: 医疗状况如此糟糕，以至于严重影响了他们的生活质量。

en: Yet for many island inhabitants——some of Bangladesh's poorest- paying for health care is a costly ordeal. (16 words)
cn: 然而，对许多岛屿居民——其中一些是孟加拉国最贫穷的人——来说，支付医疗费用是一笔昂贵的苦差事。

en: Victims of erosion lose their houses, agricultural land and jobs as farmers, fishermen and day laborers. (16 words)
cn: 水土流失的受害者失去了他们的房屋、农田以及作为农民、渔民和日工的工作。

en: Though government hospitals are free, many people hesitate to go, citing long commutes, endless lines and questionable diagnoses. (18 words)
cn: 虽然公立医院是免费的，但许多人犹豫是否要去，理由是路途遥远、排队无休止以及诊断不可靠。

en: For convenience's sake, one-third of rural households visit unqualified village doctors, who rely on unscientific methods of treatment, according to a 2016 study in the peer-reviewed journal Global Health Action. (30 words)
cn: 根据同行评审期刊《全球健康行动》2016年的一项研究，为方便起见，三分之一的农村家庭会去拜访不合格的乡村医生，这些医生依赖不科学的治疗方法。

en: On the islands, there's even a colloquial expression for the idea of making medical care your lowest priority: It's known as 'rog pushai rakha' in Bengali, which roughly translates to 'stockpiling their diseases'--waiting to seek medical attention until a condition becomes extremely serious. (43 words)
cn: 在这些岛屿上，甚至有一个口头表达来形容把医疗放在最低优先级的想法：在孟加拉语中被称为“rog pushai rakha”，大致翻译为“囤积疾病”——等到病情变得极其严重时才去就医。

en: Now, a new virtual medical service called Teledaktar (TD) is trying to make health care more easily accessible. (18 words)
cn: 如今，一项名为“远程医生”（TD）的新型虚拟医疗服务正试图使医疗保健更加便利。

en: Every week, TD's medical operators travel to the islands by boat, carrying a laptop, a portable printer for prescriptions and tools to run basic medical screenings such as blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature and weight. (36 words)
cn: 每周，TD的医疗操作员都会乘船前往这些岛屿，携带一台笔记本电脑、一台用于打印处方的便携式打印机以及进行基本医疗筛查（如血压、血糖、体温和体重）的工具。

en: They choose an area of the island with the best Internet reception and set up a makeshift medical center which consists of plastic stools and small tables borrowed from the locals' homes, a tent in case of rain and a sheet that is strung up to give the patients privacy during their session. (53 words)
cn: 他们选择岛上网络信号最好的区域，搭建一个临时医疗中心，包括从当地人家中借来的塑料凳和小桌子、防雨帐篷以及拉起的布帘，以便在就诊时为患者提供隐私。

en: Launched in October 2018, TD has eight centers in towns and villages across rural Bangladesh and on three islands. (19 words)
cn: TD于2018年10月启动，在孟加拉国农村地区的城镇和村庄以及三个岛屿上设有八个中心。

en: It is funded by a nonprofit organization founded by Bangladeshi entrepreneurs, finance and technology professionals. (15 words)
cn: 它由孟加拉国企业家、金融和技术专业人士创立的一个非营利组织资助。

en: Inside the center, the laptop screen lights up to reveal Dr. Tina Mustahid, TD's head physician, live-streamed from the capital city of Dhaka for free remote medical consultations. (28 words)
cn: 在中心内，笔记本电脑屏幕亮起，显示出TD的首席医师蒂娜·穆斯塔希德医生，她从首都达卡进行直播，提供免费远程医疗咨询。

en: Affectionately called Doctor Apa— 'older sister' in Bengali- by her patients, she is one of three volunteer doctors at TD. (20 words)
cn: 患者亲切地称她为“阿帕医生”——孟加拉语意为“姐姐”——她是TD的三名志愿医生之一。

en: 'I diagnose them through conversation,' says Dr. Mustahid. (8 words)
cn: 穆斯塔希德医生说：“我通过对话来诊断他们。”

en: 'Sometimes it's really obvious things that local doctors don't have the patience to talk through with their patients. (18 words)
cn: “有时候，当地医生没有耐心与患者详细沟通的问题其实非常明显。”

en: For example, a common complaint mothers come in with is that their children refuse to eat their meals. (18 words)
cn: 例如，母亲们经常来抱怨的一个问题是她们的孩子不肯吃饭。

en: The mothers are concerned they are dealing with indigestion, but it's because they are feeding the children packaged chips which are cheap and convenient. (24 words)
cn: 母亲们担心孩子是消化不良，但实际上是因为她们给孩子吃的是便宜方便的包装薯片。

en: I tell them it is ruining their appetite and ask them to cut back on unhealthy snacks.' (17 words)
cn: 我告诉他们这会破坏孩子的食欲，并让他们减少不健康的零食。”

en: Dr. Mustahid says building awareness about health and nutrition is important for island patients who are cut off from mainland resources. (21 words)
cn: 穆斯塔希德医生说，对与大陆资源隔绝的岛屿患者来说，建立健康和营养意识很重要。

en: Even off the islands, Bangladesh faces a critical deficit of health services. (12 words)
cn: 即使不在岛屿上，孟加拉国也面临着严重的医疗服务短缺。

en: The country has half the doctors-per-person ratio recommended by the World Health Organization: roughly one doctor per 2,000 people, instead of one doctor per 1,000 people. (26 words)
cn: 该国的医生与人口之比只有世界卫生组织建议的一半：大约每2,000人有一名医生，而不是每1,000人有一名医生。

en: And of those physicians, many are concentrated in cities: 70% of the country's population live in rural areas, yet less than 20% of health workers practice there. (27 words)
cn: 而这些医生中，许多集中在城市：该国70%的人口生活在农村地区，但只有不到20%的卫生工作者在那里执业。

en: Over 70% of TD's 3,000 patients are female, in part because many are not comfortable speaking with local doctors who tend to be male. (24 words)
cn: TD的3,000名患者中，超过70%是女性，部分原因是许多人不习惯与往往是男性的当地医生交谈。

en: The rural women are mostly not literate or confident enough to travel on their own to the nearest town to visit medical facilities. (23 words)
cn: 农村妇女大多没有文化，也没有足够的信心独自前往最近的城镇就医。

en: Many have spent their entire lives rebuilding their homes when the islands flood. (13 words)
cn: 许多人一生都在岛屿洪水时重建家园。

en: Early marriage and young motherhood, which are prevalent in these parts of Bangladesh, also contribute to the early onset of health problems. (22 words)
cn: 在孟加拉国这些地区盛行的早婚和早育，也导致了健康问题的早期出现。

en: For most TD patients on the islands, Dr. Mustahid is the first big-city doctor that they've ever consulted. (18 words)
cn: 对岛上大多数TD患者来说，穆斯塔希德医生是他们咨询过的第一位大城市医生。

en: TD doctors are not meant to treat serious illnesses or conditions that require a doctor to be physically present, such as pregnancy. (22 words)
cn: TD医生并不治疗需要医生亲自在场的严重疾病或状况，例如妊娠。

en: But they can write prescriptions, diagnose common ailments—including digestive issues, joint pain, skin diseases, fever and the common cold—and refer patients to doctors at local hospitals. (26 words)
cn: 但他们可以开处方、诊断常见疾病——包括消化问题、关节疼痛、皮肤病、发烧和普通感冒——并将患者转诊给当地医院的医生。

en: The visit is also an opportunity for the patients, especially women, to air their concerns about aging, motherhood and reproductive health according to Dr. Mustahid. (25 words)
cn: 据穆斯塔希德医生说，就诊也是患者，尤其是女性，表达对衰老、母职和生殖健康担忧的机会。

en: The doctors also offer health, dietary and lifestyle advice where necessary, including insight on everything from recognizing postnatal depression to daily exercise. (22 words)
cn: 医生们还在必要时提供健康、饮食和生活方式建议，包括从识别产后抑郁症到日常锻炼等方方面面的见解。

en: Dr. Mustahid regularly recommends her patients to take a daily thirty-minute morning walk before the sun gets too intense. (19 words)
cn: 穆斯塔希德医生定期建议她的患者在阳光变得过于强烈之前，每天进行三十分钟的晨间散步。

en: After a few sessions about general health issues Fazila finally opened up about something else that was bothering her: her persistent skin condition. (23 words)
cn: 在几次关于一般健康问题的就诊后，法齐拉终于敞开心扉，谈到了困扰她的另一件事：她持续的皮肤病。

en: It can get expensive to travel to the doctor, so usually the women living on the islands describe their illness to their husbands. (23 words)
cn: 去看医生可能花费不菲，所以通常岛上的妇女会向丈夫描述自己的病情。

en: The husbands then go to the pharmacy, try to describe the issue and return home with some random medicines. (19 words)
cn: 然后丈夫们去药店，试着描述问题，然后带着一些随意买的药回家。

en: Nothing worked for Fazila until she started seeing Dr. Apa. (10 words)
cn: 法齐拉直到开始看阿帕医生，才有所好转。

en: Other nonprofits are also starting to provide health services on the islands. (12 words)
cn: 其他非营利组织也开始在岛上提供医疗服务。

en: A local non-governmental organization called Friendship operates floating boat hospitals that provide health services to islands all over Bangladesh, docking at each for two months at a time. (28 words)
cn: 一个名为“友谊”的当地非政府组织运营着浮动船医院，为孟加拉国各地的岛屿提供医疗服务，每次在每个岛屿停靠两个月。

en: Friendship also runs satellite clinics in which one doctor and one clinic aide who are residents of the community disperse health and hygiene information. (24 words)
cn: “友谊”组织还运营卫星诊所，由一名医生和一名来自社区的诊所助理传播健康和卫生信息。

en: TD still has a few major challenges. (7 words)
cn: TD仍然面临一些重大挑战。

en: Many residents complain the medicines they are prescribed are sometimes unaffordable, but the government isn't doing enough for them. (19 words)
cn: 许多居民抱怨他们被开的药有时负担不起，但政府为他们做得不够。

en: Patients often ask why the medicine isn't free along with the consultation from the doctors. (15 words)
cn: 患者经常问为什么药物不能和医生的咨询一样免费。

en: The organizations are linked to local pharmacies and offer discounts to the patients and make sure to prescribe the most cost-effective brands, but still many residents can't afford even that. (30 words)
cn: 这些组织与当地药店有联系，为患者提供折扣，并确保开具最具成本效益的品牌药物，但即便如此，许多居民仍然负担不起。

en: Nevertheless, TD's remote consultations seem to be popular: Of 3,000 patients, at least 200 have returned for follow-ups, according to TD. (21 words)
cn: 尽管如此，TD的远程咨询似乎很受欢迎：据TD称，在3,000名患者中，至少有200人已回来进行复诊。

en: The reason, explains one resident, might be the simple gesture of treating the island inhabitants with respect. (17 words)
cn: 一位居民解释说，原因可能是尊重岛上居民这一简单的举动。

en: 'Dr. Apa is patient,' he says, 'At government hospitals, the doctors treat us very badly, but here they listen to us, I can repeat myself many times and no one gets annoyed.' (32 words)
cn: 他说：“阿帕医生很有耐心。在公立医院，医生对我们很不好，但在这里他们会倾听我们的诉说，我可以重复很多次，没人会生气。”

en: Selective colleges and universities in the U.S. are under fire for being too elite and too expensive, and for not training graduates for the world of work. (27 words)
cn: 美国选择性大学因过于精英化、学费过高以及未能培养毕业生适应职场而受到抨击。

en: Such charges ignore the fact that these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work, for thoughtful engagement in civic life, for lifelong learning, and for understanding the world and those with whom they live. (37 words)
cn: 这些指责忽视了这样一个事实：这些学校继续培养学生为工作成功、对公民生活的深思熟虑参与、终身学习以及理解世界和与他们共同生活的人做好准备。

en: These colleges and universities must be doing something right. (9 words)
cn: 这些学院和大学必定在某些方面做得不错。

en: Applications are at record highs, and their financial aid programs make them more accessible than ever. (16 words)
cn: 申请人数创历史新高，而他们的经济援助计划使它们比以往任何时候都更加容易入学。

en: This model of education has long played a central role in creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation. (19 words)
cn: 这种教育模式长期以来在创造机会、推动经济增长和刺激创新方面发挥了核心作用。

en: Yet, there is growing skepticism about the value of this model. (11 words)
cn: 然而，人们对此模式的价值越来越怀疑。

en: The recent tax reform bill is a wake-up call that our strongest colleges and universities are under assault by some in government. (22 words)
cn: 最近的税改法案敲响了警钟，表明我们最强大的大学正受到政府中一些人的攻击。

en: The initial proposals would have made education unaffordable for many by taxing tuition waivers for graduate students and ending deductions for student loan interest. (24 words)
cn: 最初的提案将对研究生学费减免征税并终止学生贷款利息扣除，这将使许多人无法负担教育费用。

en: Thankfully, these provisions were ultimately stripped from the bill, but lawmakers let stand a new tax on the investment income of some colleges and universities. (25 words)
cn: 值得庆幸的是，这些条款最终从法案中被删除，但立法者保留了对部分大学投资收益征收新税的规定。

en: While these attacks are motivated by misguided ideas, we need to do a better job of explaining why these claims are false and why what we do is valuable. (29 words)
cn: 虽然这些攻击是受错误观念驱使，但我们需要更好地解释为什么这些说法是错误的，以及我们所做的事情为什么有价值。

en: We cannot take for granted that any of this is obvious. (11 words)
cn: 我们不能想当然地认为这一切都是显而易见的。

en: It is often said that elite colleges and universities do not train students, particularly those who study the liberal arts, for the workforce. (23 words)
cn: 人们常说，精英大学不培养学生（尤其是文科学生）为就业做准备。

en: But this can be refuted by scholarly research. (8 words)
cn: 但这可以通过学术研究予以驳斥。

en: The data are clear: a liberal arts education is great career preparation, both for excellent lifetime earnings and for satisfaction with the work. (23 words)
cn: 数据很清楚：文科教育是很好的职业准备，无论是对于获得优异的终身收入还是对工作的满意度。

en: This education develops the skills of critical thinking, rigorous analysis of data and facts, communication with the written and spoken word, understanding of cultural differences and issues, and the ability to keep learning. (33 words)
cn: 这种教育培养了批判性思维、对数据和事实的严谨分析、书面和口头沟通、理解文化差异和问题以及持续学习的能力。

en: In fact, liberal arts graduates do extremely well in every imaginable field. (12 words)
cn: 事实上，文科毕业生在每一个能想到的领域都表现得非常出色。

en: Access to an education at selective colleges and universities is now more available than ever to low-and middle-income families. (19 words)
cn: 如今，低收入和中等收入家庭获得选择性大学教育的机会比以往任何时候都多。

en: We have built endowments from donations by alumni and parents who understand and appreciate our mission to provide access and opportunity, and a significant portion of the returns from these endowments is used to fund financial aid. (37 words)
cn: 我们从校友和家长的捐赠中建立了捐赠基金，他们理解并赞赏我们提供入学机会的使命，而这些捐赠基金收益的很大一部分用于资助经济援助。

en: Ironically, the new tax on endowments drains financial aid funds from the very schools most able to offer opportunity to those who have earned a spot but cannot otherwise afford this education. (32 words)
cn: 具有讽刺意味的是，对捐赠基金征收新税，恰恰从那些最有能力为获得入学资格但无力承担教育费用的人提供机会的学校抽走了经济援助资金。

en: Beyond the virtue of access to those who have earned a place at these schools, the diversity of economic backgrounds enhances the education and experience of all of our students. (30 words)
cn: 除了为获得入学资格的人提供机会这一美德之外，经济背景的多样性也提升了我们所有学生的教育和体验。

en: When a group of Australians was asked why they believed climate change was not happening, about 36% said it was 'common sense', according to a report published last year by the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organization. (37 words)
cn: 根据澳大利亚联邦科学与工业研究组织去年发布的一份报告，当一组澳大利亚人被问及为什么他们认为气候变化没有发生时，约36%的人说这是‘常识’。

en: This was the most popular reason for their opinion, with only 11% saying their belief that climate change was not happening was based on scientific research. (26 words)
cn: 这是他们观点中最常见的理由，只有11%的人表示他们相信气候变化没有发生是基于科学研究。

en: But what do we mean by an appeal to common sense? (11 words)
cn: 但我们所说的诉诸常识是什么意思呢？

en: Presumably it's an appeal to rationality of some sort that forms the basis of more complex reasoning. (17 words)
cn: 大概是对某种理性的诉求，这种理性构成了更复杂推理的基础。

en: The appeal to common sense, however, is usually nothing more than an appeal to thinking that just feels right, but what feels right to one person may not feel right to another. (32 words)
cn: 然而，诉诸常识通常不过是对感觉正确的思考的诉求，但一个人感觉正确的东西对另一个人可能并不正确。

en: Whether it feels right is usually a reflection of the world view and ideologies we have internalised, and that frames how we interact with new ideas. (26 words)
cn: 它是否感觉正确，通常反映了我们内化的世界观和意识形态，而这塑造了我们与新观点互动的方式。

en: When new ideas are in accord with what we already believe, they are more readily accepted. (16 words)
cn: 当新观点与我们已有信念一致时，它们更容易被接受。

en: When they are not, they, and the arguments that lead to them, are more readily rejected. (16 words)
cn: 当它们不一致时，它们以及导致它们的论据就更容易被拒绝。

en: We often mistake this automatic compatibility testing of new ideas with existing beliefs as an application of common sense, but, in reality, it is more about judging than thinking. (29 words)
cn: 我们常常将这种新观点与现有信念的自动兼容性测试误认为是常识的应用，但实际上，这更像是判断而非思考。

en: As Nobelist Daniel Kahneman notes in Thinking, Fast and Slow, when we arrive at conclusions in this way, the outcomes also feel true, regardless of whether they are. (28 words)
cn: 正如诺贝尔奖得主丹尼尔·卡尼曼在《思考，快与慢》中指出的那样，当我们以这种方式得出结论时，结果也会让人感觉是真实的，无论它们是否真实。

en: We are not psychologically well equipped to judge our own thinking. (11 words)
cn: 我们在心理上并不具备判断自己思维的能力。

en: We are also highly susceptible to a range of cognitive biases such as giving preference to the first things that come to mind when making decisions or giving weight to evidence. (31 words)
cn: 我们还极易受到一系列认知偏见的影响，例如在做决策时优先考虑首先想到的事情或赋予证据权重。

en: One way we can check our internal biases and inconsistencies is through the social verification of knowledge, in which we test our ideas in a rigorous and systematic way to see if they make sense not just to us, but to other people. (43 words)
cn: 我们可以通过知识的社会验证来检查我们内部的偏见和不一致之处，即以严谨和系统的方式检验我们的观点，看看它们是否不仅对我们自己有意义，而且对他人也有意义。

en: The outstanding example of this socially shared cognition is science. (10 words)
cn: 这种社会共享认知的突出例子就是科学。

en: That does not mean that individuals are not capable of excellent thinking, nor does it mean no individual is rational. (20 words)
cn: 这并不意味着个人没有出色的思考能力，也不意味着没有个人是理性的。

en: But the extent to which individuals can do this on their own is a function of how well integrated they are with communities of systematic inquiry in the first place. (30 words)
cn: 但是个人能独自做到这一点的程度，首先取决于他们与系统性探究的群体融合得有多好。

en: You can't learn to think well by yourself. (8 words)
cn: 你无法独自学会良好的思考。

en: In matters of science at least, those who value their common sense over methodological, collaborative investigation imagine themselves to be more free in their thinking, unbound by involvement with the group, but in reality they are tightly bound by their capabilities and perspectives. (43 words)
cn: 至少在科学问题上，那些将常识置于方法论和合作调查之上的人想象自己思维更自由，不受群体参与的束缚，但实际上他们被自己的能力和视角紧紧束缚着。

en: We are smarter together than we are individually, and perhaps that's just common sense. (14 words)
cn: 我们在一起比单独更聪明，也许这本身就是常识。

en: Thinking kind thoughts about yourself and your loved ones can prove beneficial for your overall wellbeing, empirical evidence has shown. (20 words)
cn: 实证证据表明，对自己和你所爱的人心存善念，对你的整体健康有益。

en: Researchers carried out an investigation to explore the correlation between having kind thoughts and a person's psychological state. (18 words)
cn: 研究人员进行了一项调查，以探究心存善念与人的心理状态之间的相关性。

en: For the study, five groups of participants were presented with a different set of audio instructions, some of which encouraged the participants to think amiably about themselves and others which persuaded them to think in a self-critical manner. (38 words)
cn: 在这项研究中，五组参与者分别听取了不同的音频指令，其中一些鼓励参与者友善地看待自己，而另一些则说服他们以自我批评的方式思考。

en: After listening to the audio instructions, the participants were asked to answer a series of questions. (16 words)
cn: 听完音频指令后，参与者被要求回答一系列问题。

en: These included whether they felt agitated, how likely they were to show kindness to themselves and how connected they felt to other individuals. (23 words)
cn: 这些问题包括他们是否感到焦虑、他们对自己表现出善意的可能性有多大，以及他们感觉与他人有多亲近。

en: The participants who were instructed to think kindly about themselves were more likely to exhibit a bodily response associated with being relaxed and feeling safe. (25 words)
cn: 那些被指示善待自己的参与者更有可能表现出与放松和安全感相关的身体反应。

en: Their heart rates also dropped, which is a healthy sign of a heart that can respond flexibly to situations. (19 words)
cn: 他们的心率也下降了，这是心脏能够灵活应对各种情况的健康标志。

en: Yet, conversely, those who listened to the critical audio clips were noted as having a higher heart rate and sweat response afterwards, both of which signify feelings of threat and distress. (31 words)
cn: 然而，相反地，那些听了批评性音频片段的人随后心率和出汗反应都更高，这两者都预示着威胁和痛苦的感觉。

en: Having the ability to switch off the body's natural threat response can boost a person's immune system. (17 words)
cn: 能够关闭身体的自然威胁反应可以增强人的免疫系统。

en: This, in turn, gives them a greater likelihood of recovering quickly from illness. (13 words)
cn: 这反过来又使他们更有可能从疾病中迅速康复。

en: These findings help us to further understand some of our clinical trials research findings, where we show that individuals with recurrent depression benefit particularly from self-awareness-based cognitive therapy. (28 words)
cn: 这些发现帮助我们进一步理解了我们的一些临床试验研究结果，其中我们表明，患有复发性抑郁症的人尤其能从基于自我意识的认知疗法中获益。

en: They essentially learn to become more sympathetic to themselves. (9 words)
cn: 他们本质上是学会了对自己更加有同情心。

en: The sense is that for people prone to depression, meeting their negative thoughts and feelings with compassion is a radically different way; that these thoughts are not facts. (28 words)
cn: 其意义在于，对于容易抑郁的人来说，以同情心对待自己的消极想法和感受是一种根本不同的方式；即这些想法并非事实。

en: It introduces a different way of being and knowing that is quite transformative for many people. (16 words)
cn: 它引入了一种不同的存在和认知方式，对许多人来说具有相当大的变革性。

en: In the long view, the human relationship with forests has been one of brutal destruction, but even it carries elements of slow hope. (23 words)
cn: 从长远来看，人类与森林的关系一直是一种残酷的破坏关系，但即便如此，其中也包含着缓慢希望的因素。

en: In the Middle Ages, there was no shortage of timber in most parts of the world, and few saw cutting down forests as a problem. (25 words)
cn: 在中世纪，世界大部分地区并不缺乏木材，很少有人把砍伐森林看作一个问题。

en: Yet in 1548 the people of Venice estimated that an important timber supply would last only 30 years at their current rate of usage- but different forest management would make it possible to meet the demand for many centuries to come. (41 words)
cn: 然而在1548年，威尼斯人估计按照他们目前的使用速度，一项重要的木材供应只能维持30年——但不同的森林管理方式将使未来许多个世纪的需求得到满足成为可能。

en: The idea of preserving resources came out of a concern for the future: a fear of using up resources faster than they could be replenished. (25 words)
cn: 保护资源的想法源于对未来的担忧：担心资源消耗的速度超过其补充的速度。

en: Economic interests were at the core of this understanding of trees and forests. (13 words)
cn: 经济利益是这种对树木和森林理解的核心。

en: It would take more than three centuries before scientists began to understand that timber production is not the only, and possibly not the most important, function of forests. (28 words)
cn: 花了三个多世纪的时间，科学家们才开始认识到木材生产并非森林唯一的功能，甚至可能不是最重要的功能。

en: The late 19th and early 20th century saw an increasing recognition that forests serve as habitats for countless animal and plant species that all rely on each other. (28 words)
cn: 19世纪末20世纪初，人们越来越认识到森林是无数相互依存的动植物的栖息地。

en: They take over protective functions against soil erosion and landslides; they make a significant contribution to the water balance as they prevent surface runoff; they filter dirt particles, greenhouse gases and radioactive substances from the air; they produce oxygen; they provide spaces for recreation and they preserve historic and prehistoric remains. (51 words)
cn: 它们承担着防止水土流失和滑坡的保护功能；它们通过防止地表径流对水平衡做出重大贡献；它们过滤空气中的灰尘颗粒、温室气体和放射性物质；它们产生氧气；它们提供休闲空间，并保护历史和史前遗迹。

en: As a result, forests around the world have been set aside as parks or wilderness areas. (16 words)
cn: 因此，世界各地的森林都被划为公园或荒野地区。

en: Recent years have seen a big change in our view of forests. (12 words)
cn: 近年来，我们对森林的看法发生了巨大的变化。

en: Peter Wohlleben's book The Hidden Life of Trees (2015), an international bestseller, suggests that trees can warn each other of danger through a 'wood wide web' of roots and fungi. (30 words)
cn: 彼得·沃莱本的《树的隐秘生活》（2015年）是一本国际畅销书，书中指出树木可以通过根系和真菌构成的‘木材万维网’互相警告危险。

en: They support each other through sharing of nutrients and information, and they even keep ancient stumps alive by feeding them solutions of sugars. (23 words)
cn: 它们通过分享营养和信息来相互支持，甚至通过给古老的树桩输送糖溶液来维持其生命。

en: Such insights have made us aware of deep ecological relationships between humans and the more-than-human world. (16 words)
cn: 这些见解使我们认识到人类与超越人类的世界之间深层的生态关系。

en: Awareness of ecologies is a recent phenomenon. (7 words)
cn: 对生态学的认识是最近才出现的现象。

en: It was not until the 1940s that the concept of the 'environment' embracing all living and nonliving things developed. (19 words)
cn: 直到20世纪40年代，涵盖所有生物和非生物的事物的‘环境’概念才发展起来。

en: In the 1970s, the term 'environment' gained currency, becoming widely adopted in the English and Romance languages, and as 'Umwelt' ('surrounding world') in German. (24 words)
cn: 在20世纪70年代，‘环境’一词开始流行，在英语和罗曼语系中被广泛采用，在德语中则成为‘Umwelt’（‘周围世界’）。

en: The emergence of the idea led to the rise of environmental agencies, regulations and environmental studies, and to environmental science as new, integrated academic disciplines. (25 words)
cn: 这一观念的出现导致了环境机构、法规和环境研究的兴起，并促使环境科学成为新的综合型学科。

en: It was in 1956 that the very first bachelor of science in environmental studies was awarded, at the State University of New York College of Forestry at Syracuse. (28 words)
cn: 正是在1956年，纽约州立大学锡拉丘兹林学院授予了第一个环境研究理学学士学位。

en: Since the 1970s- with the rise of 'environmentalism'- environmental studies programmes have sprung up at hundreds of universities. (18 words)
cn: 自20世纪70年代以来——随着‘环保主义’的兴起——环境研究项目在数百所大学中如雨后春笋般涌现。

en: There is (slow) hope in the fact that scholars from many different disciplines have adopted the term 'environment' over the past decades. (22 words)
cn: 在过去的几十年里，来自许多不同学科的学者都采用了‘环境’一词，这带来（缓慢的）希望。

en: They are exploring intricate connections within and between complex ecologies, as well as the impact that human environment-making (through techno-industrial, economic and other manipulative developments) has had on the biosphere. (30 words)
cn: 他们正在探索复杂生态系统内部及之间错综复杂的联系，以及人类环境营造（通过技术工业、经济和其他操控性发展）对生物圈的影响。

en: The rise of the idea of the environment and a scholarly understanding of ecological processes has influenced new technologies and also politics. (22 words)
cn: 环境观念的兴起以及对生态过程的学术理解影响了新技术，也影响了政治。

en: We have come to ask questions about vulnerability and risk, world ecologies, and the relationship between nature and power. (19 words)
cn: 我们开始提出关于脆弱性和风险、世界生态以及自然与权力之间关系的问题。

en: The search for an adequate response to climate change occupies centre stage in international diplomacy. (15 words)
cn: 寻找应对气候变化的适当方法在国际外交中占据中心地位。

en: Social and environmental activists, scientists and indigenous groups have called the Paris Agreement of the United Nations Climate Change Conference in December 2015 insufficient, weak, or compromised. (27 words)
cn: 社会和环境活动家、科学家和原住民团体称2015年12月联合国气候变化大会的《巴黎协定》不充分、软弱或打了折扣。

en: To some extent, they are right: climate change has already destroyed tens of thousands of livelihoods, and the situation will worsen in the near future for millions of mostly poorer people, who will join the ranks of those who have already been displaced by climate change and extreme weather events. (50 words)
cn: 在某种程度上，他们是对的：气候变化已经摧毁了数万人的生计，而且在不久的将来，数百万主要是贫困人口的情况将会恶化，他们将加入那些已经被气候变化和极端天气事件流离失所者的行列。

en: But the Paris Conference nevertheless marked a historic step toward the recognition of the need for action on climate change, the cutting of carbon emissions, and world cooperation. (28 words)
cn: 但巴黎会议仍然标志着在承认需要采取气候变化行动、削减碳排放和世界合作方面迈出了历史性的一步。

en: There were 195 nations that came to the table in Paris and agreed to limits on emissions. (17 words)
cn: 有195个国家来到巴黎的谈判桌前，同意限制排放。

en: Historically, nothing comparable had happened prior to this. (8 words)
cn: 从历史上看，在此之前没有发生过类似的事情。

en: Before the 20th century, a handful of scientists had been interested in the theoretical relationship between greenhouse gases and climate change, but only the empirical evidence accumulated since the late 20th century established a clear connection between the burning of fossil fuels and a vastly accelerated rise in global temperatures. (50 words)
cn: 在20世纪之前，只有少数科学家对温室气体与气候变化之间的理论关系感兴趣，但直到20世纪后期积累的经验证据才确立了化石燃料燃烧与全球气温急剧加速上升之间的明确联系。

en: The current crisis is not the first that humans have encountered, and a look at the struggles with pollution in recent history reveals transformations that once seemed unimaginable. (28 words)
cn: 当前的危机并非人类遭遇的第一次，回顾近代史上与污染的斗争，可以发现曾经看似不可想象的转变。

en: The 'London fog' that came to define the capital through British novels and thrillers is in reality smog or smoke, a legacy of industrialisation. (24 words)
cn: 通过英国小说和惊悚小说成为首都标志的‘伦敦雾’，实际上是烟雾，是工业化的遗留物。

en: After a century of ignorance, London was hit by the Great Smog of December 1952- the worst air-pollution event in the history of the United Kingdom which caused the deaths of approximately 12,000 people. (34 words)
cn: 在一个世纪的忽视之后，伦敦遭遇了1952年12月的大雾霾——这是英国历史上最严重的空气污染事件，造成约12,000人死亡。

en: Shortly thereafter, public initiatives and political campaigns led to strict regulations and new laws, including the Clean Air Act (1956). (20 words)
cn: 此后不久，公众倡议和政治运动导致了严格的法规和新法律的出台，包括《清洁空气法案》（1956年）。

en: Today, London has effectively reduced traffic emissions through the introduction of a Congestion Charge Zone in 2003, and an Ultra Low Emission Zone in 2019. (25 words)
cn: 如今，伦敦通过2003年引入拥堵收费区和2019年引入超低排放区，有效减少了交通排放。

en: Scientific evidence that we are living in an era of climate change, resource exhaustion and potential ecological disaster is overwhelming. (20 words)
cn: 我们正生活在一个气候变化、资源枯竭和潜在生态灾难时代的科学证据是压倒性的。

en: How do we motivate a public exhausted by never-ending scenarios of doom and disaster, when the challenges seem so huge and so impossible to solve? (25 words)
cn: 当挑战如此巨大、似乎无法解决时，我们如何激励那些被永无止境的厄运和灾难场景所困扰的公众？

en: Statistics about extinction and the gloom of decline will not in themselves get us out of our often self-created ecological traps: instead, they are more likely to result in paralysis and inaction. (32 words)
cn: 关于灭绝和衰退阴霾的统计数据本身并不能让我们走出我们常常自己制造的生态陷阱；相反，它们更有可能导致瘫痪和无所作为。

en: We need stories and histories of change and transformation: ecological stories that make us confront the fact that human power is potentially destructive, and that the survival of our species on this planet depends on the preservation of soil and water, and the habitats and ecological systems. (47 words)
cn: 我们需要关于变化和转型的故事和历史：那些让我们直面人类力量具有潜在破坏性这一事实的生态故事，以及我们物种在这个星球上的生存依赖于土壤和水、栖息地和生态系统的保护。

en: It is time that we showed successes and accelerations in ecological awareness, action and restoration: stories that include past successes and future visions about the rise of urban gardening and of renaturalised riverscapes, of successful protests against polluted air and water, of the rise of regional markets and slow food, and the planting of trees around the globe, of initiatives and enterprises that work towards ecological restoration. (67 words)
cn: 现在是时候展示我们在生态意识、行动和恢复方面的成功和加速了：这些故事包括过去的成功和未来的愿景——关于城市园艺和河流景观自然化的兴起、反对污染空气和水的成功抗议、区域市场和慢食的兴起、全球植树造林、以及致力于生态恢复的倡议和企业。

en: The reality of ecological curses seems far greater than the power of the hopes left at the bottom of Pandora's box. (21 words)
cn: 生态诅咒的现实似乎远大于留在潘多拉魔盒底部的希望的力量。

en: But if we believe that nothing can be changed, then we are giving up our opportunity to act. (18 words)
cn: 但如果我们相信什么都无法改变，那么我们就在放弃行动的机会。

en: Today's saving powers will not come from a deus ex machina. (11 words)
cn: 今天的拯救力量不会来自解围之神。

en: In an ever-more complex and synthetic world, our saving powers won't come from a single source, and certainly not from a too-big-to-fail approach or from those who have been drawn into the whirlpool of our age of speed. (38 words)
cn: 在一个日益复杂和综合的世界中，我们的拯救力量不会来自单一来源，当然也不会来自‘大到不能倒’的方法，也不会来自那些被卷入我们高速时代漩涡中的人。

en: Hope can work as a wake-up call. (7 words)
cn: 希望可以起到警钟的作用。

en: It acknowledges setbacks. (3 words)
cn: 它承认挫折。

en: The concept of slow hope suggests that we can't expect things to change overnight. (14 words)
cn: ‘缓慢希望’的概念表明我们不能指望事情一夜之间改变。

en: If the ever-faster exhaustion of natural resources (in ecological terms) and the 'shrinking of the present' (in social terms) are urgent problems of humans, then cutting down on exhaustive practices and working towards a 'stretching of the present' will be ways to move forward. (44 words)
cn: 如果自然资源日益加速的枯竭（从生态角度而言）和‘当下的缩小’（从社会角度而言）是人类紧迫的问题，那么减少消耗性行为并朝着‘延伸当下’的方向努力将是前进的方式。

en: Since American Idol star Taryn Southern started composing music with AI in 2017, musicians all over the world have begun wondering about the implications of AI and modern technology where music production is concerned. (34 words)
cn: 自从美国偶像明星塔琳·萨瑟恩于2017年开始用AI创作音乐以来，世界各地的音乐家们开始思考AI和现代技术在音乐制作方面的影响。

en: Using AI in the creation of music is perceived by some as a helpful tool and by others as almost 'the beginning of the end'. (25 words)
cn: 在音乐创作中使用AI，在一些人看来是一种有用的工具，而在另一些人看来几乎是‘终结的开始’。

en: In Taryn's case, AI software enabled her to communicate melodies and chords that she didn't know how to put together herself. (21 words)
cn: 在塔琳的案例中，AI软件使她能够表达她自己不知道如何组合的旋律和和弦。

en: The end product was therefore a collaborative effort, rather than a piece entirely produced by technology. (16 words)
cn: 因此，最终产品是合作的结果，而不是完全由技术产生的作品。

en: Taryn's story has a distinctly positive feel that highlights the advantages of using AI in music production. (17 words)
cn: 塔琳的故事有一种明显的积极感觉，突出了在音乐制作中使用AI的优势。

en: It can serve as a source of inspiration, and as an ideal jumping-off point should a musician be hit with writer's block. (22 words)
cn: 它可以作为灵感的来源，以及在音乐家遭遇创作瓶颈时的理想起点。

en: Contrary to seeing AI as a tool, some musicians consider it to be hugely detrimental to the music scene. (19 words)
cn: 与将AI视为工具相反，一些音乐家认为它对音乐界非常有害。

en: At the moment, because such technology is still so young, the music it's producing is not necessarily what we want to hear. (22 words)
cn: 目前，由于这项技术仍处于早期阶段，它产生的音乐不一定是我们需要听的。

en: In short, it's not of great quality. (7 words)
cn: 简而言之，它的质量并不高。

en: Those who have produced their own music, or even fans of authentic, artistic music, will also argue that a computer could never emulate the work (and human touch) of a true musician. (32 words)
cn: 那些自己创作过音乐的人，甚至是真实艺术音乐的歌迷，也会认为计算机永远无法模仿真正音乐家的作品（和人性的触感）。

en: Music has been an integral part of the story of humans for ages; in fact, the first known piece of music is believed to be around 3,400 years old. (29 words)
cn: 音乐长期以来一直是人类故事中不可或缺的一部分；事实上，已知的第一首音乐被认为大约有3,400年的历史。

en: Songs have long been used as a means of communicating messages and folk stories, covering everything from societal ethics to world history. (22 words)
cn: 歌曲长期以来一直被用作传达信息和民间故事的手段，涵盖从社会伦理到世界历史的一切内容。

en: Since many people see music as such an inherently human expression, it is often considered as too precious to impart to technology. (22 words)
cn: 由于许多人将音乐视为如此一种固有的人类表达方式，它通常被认为过于珍贵，不能传授给技术。

en: The thought of a computer generating a 'random' piece of music that hasn't been painstakingly created by an artist is almost seen as sacrilegious. (24 words)
cn: 计算机生成一首并非由艺术家精心创作的‘随机’音乐的想法，几乎被视为亵渎神圣。

en: Regardless of which side of the argument you fall on, it seems likely that the use of AI in music production will only become more frequent. (26 words)
cn: 无论你站在争论的哪一边，AI在音乐制作中的使用似乎只会越来越频繁。

en: Our modern world is preoccupied with technological advancements. (8 words)
cn: 我们的现代世界专注于技术进步。

en: Instead of shying away from the idea of this bleak future, the best approach to take is one of optimism and curiosity. (22 words)
cn: 与其回避这种黯淡未来的想法，最好的方法是采取乐观和好奇的态度。

en: While there are always bound to be stubborn old-school musicians who refuse to use tech, music producers should consider AI as something to be embraced. (25 words)
cn: 虽然总会有顽固的老派音乐家拒绝使用技术，但音乐制作人应该将AI视为值得拥抱的东西。

en: AI music software is still very much in its infancy, but with more investors interested in the development and outcomes of such technology, and considering the rapid growth rate of other tech advances in recent years, it's only a matter of time before AI-produced music is seen as the new norm. (51 words)
cn: AI音乐软件仍处于起步阶段，但随着越来越多的投资者对此类技术的开发和成果感兴趣，并考虑到近年来其他技术进步的快速增长速度，AI制作的音乐被视为新常态只是时间问题。

en: A few weeks ago, a well-meaning professor tried to explain the physiological process behind viruses and the human body in a tweet and was immediately criticized for a mistake in his information. (32 words)
cn: 几周前，一位善意的教授试图在推文中解释病毒和人体背后的生理过程，并立即因信息错误而受到批评。

en: He then issued an apology and deleted his erroneous tweet. (10 words)
cn: 随后他发表了道歉并删除了错误的推文。

en: Communicating science beyond the academic bubble is necessary to augmenting public understanding of health and environmental issues and helping individuals make well-informed personal decisions. (24 words)
cn: 在学术圈之外传播科学对于增进公众对健康和环境问题的理解以及帮助个人做出明智的个人决策是必要的。

en: However, scientists who engage in science communication must acknowledge that even in their area, their expertise is deep but narrow. (20 words)
cn: 然而，从事科学传播的科学家必须承认，即使在自己的领域，他们的专业知识也是深入但狭窄的。

en: They need to recognize the constraints in their own knowledge. (10 words)
cn: 他们需要认识到自身知识的局限性。

en: That is not to suggest that they only write or present on their own research, but rather, that they consult with an expert if the topic is outside of their discipline. (31 words)
cn: 这并不是说他们只撰写或展示自己的研究，而是说如果主题超出他们的学科范围，他们应该咨询专家。

en: Fact-checking with a scientist who works in the specialty will prevent the unintentional spread of misinformation, and the process of doing so may yield tiny pieces of interesting new information that can be incorporated. (34 words)
cn: 与该领域的科学家进行事实核查将防止无意中传播错误信息，而这样做的过程可能会产生一些有趣的新信息，可以纳入其中。

en: Some have argued that the public is not educated enough to understand scientific information, especially for any complex phenomena, but this is absurd. (23 words)
cn: 有些人认为公众没有受过足够的教育来理解科学信息，尤其是任何复杂现象，但这很荒谬。

en: Science instruction can be found at all levels of public education with most secondary schools offering classes on biology, physics, and chemistry. (22 words)
cn: 科学教育在各级公共教育中都有，大多数中学都开设生物学、物理学和化学课程。

en: If anything, social media has shown that the public craves knowledge based on a solid scientific foundation. (17 words)
cn: 如果说有什么的话，社交媒体表明公众渴望基于坚实科学基础的知识。

en: Even the public discourse that follows most scientific articles shows that online readers can understand even the most baffling of scientific principles. (22 words)
cn: 即使是大多数科学文章之后的公众讨论也表明，在线读者能够理解即使是最令人费解的科学原理。

en: It is equally imperative to emphasize that being an expert on a topic does not automatically make a scholar qualified to communicate it to a nonscientific audience. (27 words)
cn: 同样必须强调的是，成为某一主题的专家并不会自动使学者有资格向非科学受众传播该主题。

en: A number of scientists recently have been offering public-aimed explanations of scientific phenomena. (13 words)
cn: 最近许多科学家一直在提供面向公众的科学现象解释。

en: Even though they have appropriate credentials, they often do very little in the way of explaining. (16 words)
